# Mixed-effects, random-coefficient and repeated-measures models: trial-level details

Companion to [`findings.md`](findings.md). One section per census entry flagged by a keyword search of `census/census.md`, in README order. Each section lists every mixed-effects, random-coefficient, repeated-measures or GEE analysis found in the README entry and in the FDA reviews, SAPs, and publications linked from it.

Provenance tags: `[README]` census entry; `[SAP]`/`[Protocol]` sponsor document posted on ClinicalTrials.gov; `[StatR]` FDA Statistical Review; `[MDR]`/`[IR]`/`[IntegratedR]` FDA Multi-Discipline or Integrated Review; `[MedR]` FDA Medical Review; `[Pub]` journal publication. Page numbers are PDF page indices and may be off by about one from the printed page. Fields reading *Not stated* were not found in any source consulted.

Each entry ends with **Verbatim specification excerpts**: passages copied from the source documents that state the model terms, covariance structure, df and estimation method, missing-data handling, software/SAS code, and FDA reviewer critiques, grouped by model. Each quote was checked against the downloaded PDF text. Quotes that could only be matched in part (because they span a page break or table) are marked. Page numbers in the excerpts are PDF page indices, which can differ from the printed page numbers (sometimes by many pages, e.g. when a review is appended to another document). `[...]` marks omitted text, usually running page headers or footers.

### blinatumomab (Blincyto) — BLA 125557

Therapeutic area: Oncology. Sponsor: Amgen, Inc.. Approval year: 2014.

Note: No patient-level mixed model in pivotal MT103-211 (single-arm, exact binomial CI). The only mixed-effects usage is a study-level model-based meta-analysis of historical data (Studies 118427/119834). No protocol/SAP posted.

#### Model 1: Historical CR rate, duration of CR, OS under existing salvage therapy (projected comparison vs blinatumomab) (supportive (historical-control justification of 30% threshold))

- Trial: Studies 118427/119834 (model-based meta-analysis of historical literature; supports pivotal MT103-211, NCT01466179)
- Endpoint / timepoint: Historical CR rate, duration of CR, OS under existing salvage therapy (projected comparison vs blinatumomab)
- Role: supportive (historical-control justification of 30% threshold)
- Model family: other: study-level mixed-effects model-based meta-analysis (meta-regression on published summary data)
- Response: Study-level summary CR proportion, DCR, OS from 24 published studies (1995-2012), ~4058 patients [StatR p.21]
- Fixed effects: 'available covariate information' (unspecified) [StatR p.21]
- Random effects: Not stated (study-level random effects implied by 'mixed-effects models')
- Covariance: Not stated
- Covariance fallback: Not stated
- Denominator df: Not stated
- Estimation: Not stated
- Time coding: Not stated
- Estimand / contrast: Not stated
- Missing data: Not stated
- MNAR sensitivity: Not stated
- Software: Not stated
- Results: Projected blinatumomab vs existing therapy: CR 33% vs 12%; median DCR 8.5 vs 4.8 mo; median OS 6.3 vs 4.3 mo [StatR p.21]
- FDA comments: Reviewer found the historical studies supportive of CR rate not exceeding 30% under existing therapy, noting the historical CR estimate is likely an over-estimate (may include CRi/CRp) [StatR p.21-22]
- Spec source: StatR verbatim (brief)

#### Verbatim specification excerpts

##### Model 1: Historical CR rate, duration of CR, OS under existing salvage therapy (projected comparison vs blinatumomab) (supportive (historical-control justification of 30% threshold))

> "In addition, the Applicant conducted a model-based meta-analysis (Studies 118427 and 119834) of historical data to project the effect of blinatumomab relative to existing therapies. Study 118427 developed mixed-effects models using summary results and available covariate information in 4058 relapsed/refractory ALL patients from 24 clinical studies published between 1995 and 2012. Study 119834 then used the developed models to project the effect of blinatumomab relative to existing salvage therapies for proportion of complete hematological remission (CR), duration of CR (DCR), and overall survival (OS) in relapsed/refractory ALL subjects. The projected results for blinatumomab versus existing therapies, as if they were compared in the same trials, are the flowing:  CR rate: 33% versus 12%  Median DCR: 8.5 months versus 4.8 months  Median OS: 6.3 months versus 4.3 months"
>
> — FDA Statistical Review, PDF p. 22 (https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2014/125557Orig1s000StatR.pdf)

> "This review finds the Applicant’s historical studies to be supportive of the complete remission rate not exceeding 30% in relapsed/refractory ALL subjects receiving existing salvage therapies, for the following reasons: 1. The estimated CR rate in patients receiving existing therapies is likely an over-estimation a. The estimated CR rate used all complete remissions reported by study groups, and may have included other additional subcategories such as complete response incomplete (CRi) and complete response without platelet recovery (CRp)."
>
> — FDA Statistical Review, PDF p. 23 (https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2014/125557Orig1s000StatR.pdf)

### Neratinib (Nerlynx) — NDA 208051

Therapeutic area: Oncology. Sponsor: Puma Biotechnology, Inc.. Approval year: 2017.

Note: README 'repeated-measures ANCOVA' is imprecise: primary QoL analysis was per-visit ANCOVA; mixed model was a sensitivity analysis. ExteNET has no posted protocol/SAP. PopPK (random effects on CL/F etc.) out of scope.

#### Model 1: Change from baseline in FACT-B (subscales and totals: FACT-G, FACT-B, TOI-PFB, TOI-ESB) and EQ-5D index/health state; assessed baseline, months 1, 3, 6, 9, 12 (sensitivity (to per-visit ANCOVA) for exploratory QoL endpoints)

- Trial: ExteNET (NCT00878709)
- Endpoint / timepoint: Change from baseline in FACT-B (subscales and totals: FACT-G, FACT-B, TOI-PFB, TOI-ESB) and EQ-5D index/health state; assessed baseline, months 1, 3, 6, 9, 12
- Role: sensitivity (to per-visit ANCOVA) for exploratory QoL endpoints
- Model family: MMRM
- Response: Change from baseline
- Fixed effects: treatment arm, visit, treatment-by-visit interaction, baseline assessment [MDR p.99]
- Random effects: none (covariance via R-matrix only)
- Covariance: Unstructured [MDR p.99]
- Covariance fallback: Not stated
- Denominator df: Not stated
- Estimation: Not stated
- Time coding: categorical (visit)
- Estimand / contrast: Between-arm difference in change from baseline by visit
- Missing data: MAR assumed for missing post-baseline assessments; patients missing baseline excluded; no imputation in primary per-visit ANCOVA [MDR p.99]
- MNAR sensitivity: None
- Software: Not stated
- Results: Not stated numerically; Applicant stated ANCOVA and mixed-model results consistent with descriptive results (early decrement ~month 1 on neratinib, shrinking from month 3); differences not considered clinically meaningful [MDR p.100]
- FDA comments: FDA focused its own analysis on FACT-B Physical Well-Being (descriptive mean change: ~2.5 pt worse on neratinib at month 1, ~1 pt from month 3); criticized FACT-B total as mixing distal concepts and lacking diarrhea item; completion >69% even ignoring Amendment 9 [MDR p.99-101]

- Fixed effects: treatment, baseline score [MDR p.82 and p.99]
- Random effects: Not stated

- Covariance fallback: Not stated
- Denominator df: Not stated
- Estimation: Not stated
- Time coding: Not stated
- Estimand / contrast: Not stated
- Missing data: Not stated
- MNAR sensitivity: Not stated
- Software: Not stated
- Results: Not stated
- FDA comments: README 'repeated-measures ANCOVA' label is inaccurate: MDR describes ANCOVA at each visit; only the sensitivity analysis was a repeated-measures mixed model
- Spec source: MDR verbatim

#### Verbatim specification excerpts

##### Model 1: Change from baseline in FACT-B (subscales and totals: FACT-G, FACT-B, TOI-PFB, TOI-ESB) and EQ-5D index/health state; assessed baseline, months 1, 3, 6, 9, 12 (sensitivity (to per-visit ANCOVA) for exploratory QoL endpoints)

> "The Applicant also planned for a sensitivity analysis using a repeated measures mixed model approach with change from baseline as the response variable and treatment arm, visit, interaction of treatment arm and visit, and baseline assessment as the model fixed effects. Repeated measurements at different visits would be modeled via an unstructured covariance matrix and missing assessments post-baseline would be assumed missing at random."
>
> — FDA Multi-Discipline Review, PDF p. 100 (https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2017/208051Orig1s000MultidisciplineR.pdf)

> "The Applicant noted that analysis of covariance and mixed model results were consistent with the descriptive results. None of the differences between arms were thought to be clinically meaningful."
>
> — FDA Multi-Discipline Review, PDF p. 101 (https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2017/208051Orig1s000MultidisciplineR.pdf)

##### Model 2: Same QoL endpoints (README calls this 'repeated-measures ANCOVA') (primary QoL analysis)

> "For quality-of-life parameters, changes from baseline were compared between treatments using analysis of covariance (ANCOVA), with baseline score as a covariate. A repeated measures mixed model approach was used as a sensitivity analysis."
>
> — FDA Multi-Discipline Review, PDF p. 83 (https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2017/208051Orig1s000MultidisciplineR.pdf)

> "These quality of life measures were assessed at baseline, months 1, 3, 6, 9, and 12 (end of treatment). The Applicant planned to present descriptive statistics for each treatment arm for each of the FACT-B subscales and total scores (FACT-G, FACT-B, TOI-PFB, and TOI-ESB) and EQ-5D health index and health state score at each visit. These variables were also summarized by plotting mean score versus assessment visit, and change from baseline for each of these variables were compared between treatment arms at each visit using ANCOVA with baseline score as a covariate. Subjects with missing baseline assessments of FACT-B and EQ-5D were excluded from their respective analyses and missing values were not imputed."
>
> — FDA Multi-Discipline Review, PDF p. 100 (https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2017/208051Orig1s000MultidisciplineR.pdf)

Therapeutic area: Oncology. Sponsor: Kyowa Kirin, Inc.. Approval year: 2018.

FDA Table 16 differences are labeled 'Source: FDA statistical reviewer' without specifying the model.

#### Model 1: Skindex-29 total score, change from baseline through 6 months (key secondary (multiplicity-controlled with ORR-INV; 4 key secondaries))

- Endpoint / timepoint: Skindex-29 total score, change from baseline through 6 months
- Role: key secondary (multiplicity-controlled with ORR-INV; 4 key secondaries)

- Covariance: Unstructured [MDR p.50]
- Covariance fallback: 'In case of convergence problems, another variance-covariance structure will be considered ... determined after exploration of the observed correlation structure' (unspecified) [MDR p.50]; if residuals non-normal, Wilcoxon rank-sum instead [MDR p.51]
- Denominator df: Not stated

#### Verbatim specification excerpts

##### Model 1: Skindex-29 total score, change from baseline through 6 months (key secondary (multiplicity-controlled with ORR-INV; 4 key secondaries))

> "The treatment differences in the mean change of Skindex-29 score from baseline across each planned timepoint (end of cycle 1, cycle 3, cycle 5) up to 6 months of assessments will be tested using a repeated measures mixed effects model with time, region, disease type, disease stage, treatment, and time-by-treatment interaction as factors and baseline score as a covariate. Restricted Maximum Likelihood (REML) method will be used. An unstructured covariance matrix will be employed to model the correlation among repeated measurements. Appropriate contrasts will be used to determine the difference between the Vorinostat treatment group and the KW-0761 treatment group across the end of Cycles 1, 3, and 5. In case of convergence problems, another variance-covariance structure will be considered. The selection of any of these structures will be determined after exploration of the observed correlation structure. Least squares (LS) means, corresponding standard errors, 95% two-sided CIs will be presented"
>
> — FDA Multi-Discipline Review (Applicant SAP text quoted in §8.1), PDF p. 51 (https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2018/761051Orig1s000MultidisciplineR.pdf)

> "for the within-group change for odd cycles. For the between-treatment group comparison, the difference in LS means, corresponding standard errors, 95% two-sided CIs, and two-sided p-value will also be derived from this ANCOVA model and presented for the odd cycles. This mixed-effects model will also be used to compare the treatment differences in the mean changes in Skindex-29 score from baseline to each scheduled time point at end of cycle 1, cycle 3, and cycle 5. In addition to the Skindex-29 score, a Skindex score based on a subset of Skindex questions may be analyzed in a similar fashion. Standard model diagnostics will be performed to assess the validity of the proposed ANCOVA model. These diagnostics will include an examination of the residuals for normality and homoscedasticity as well as testing for the significance of the treatment by baseline interaction term. If the residuals are not normally distributed, then the analysis will be carried out using Wilcoxon rank sum test instead."
>
> — FDA Multi-Discipline Review (Applicant SAP text quoted in §8.1), PDF p. 52 (https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2018/761051Orig1s000MultidisciplineR.pdf)

> "Missing data for Skindex-29 and FACT-G will be handled according to the questionnaires’ scoring guidelines. For Skindex-29, if responses to more than 25% of items are missing overall, the Skindex-29 score will be treated as missing. If any scale has more than 25% of the responses missing, the scale score is missing. The scale scores are the average of the non-missing items in a given scale. For FACT-G, if more than 50% of the items are responded for a subscale, the subscale scores will be prorated by multiplying the sum of the subscale by the number of items in the subscale and then dividing by the number of items responded. The total FACT-G score will be scored only if the overall item response rate is greater than 80%. For EQ-5D-3L, the EQ-5D index score will be treated as missing if not all five descriptors are responded."
>
> — FDA Multi-Discipline Review (Applicant SAP text quoted in §8.1), PDF p. 52 (https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2018/761051Orig1s000MultidisciplineR.pdf)

> "Table 16 summarizes the mean change scores of the QoL assessments from baseline across 6-month (Cycle 7) assessment."
>
> — FDA Multi-Discipline Review, PDF p. 73 (https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2018/761051Orig1s000MultidisciplineR.pdf)

> "The results in Table 16 and the figures above suggest a benefit of mogamulizumab compared to vorinostat to variable degrees with different QoL assessments. However, there are concerns with missing data. Table 17 presents the completion rate of Skindex-29 total score, FACT-G total score, and EQ-5D-3L index score."
>
> — FDA Multi-Discipline Review, PDF p. 77 (https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2018/761051Orig1s000MultidisciplineR.pdf)

> "Due mainly to the large amount of missing data, including missing data by design (due to death, AE, disease progression) even at earlier time points, the Agency has concerns regarding the interpretability and meaningfulness of the PRO data. There are also limitations with the choice of QoL instrument."
>
> — FDA Multi-Discipline Review, PDF p. 82 (https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2018/761051Orig1s000MultidisciplineR.pdf)

##### Model 2: FACT-G total score, change from baseline through 6 months (key secondary (multiplicity-controlled with ORR-INV; 4 key secondaries))

Same quotes as Model 1 (the SAP applies the Skindex-29 methods to this endpoint).

> "The same methods described above for the analysis of change in Skindex-29 score will be performed for the analysis of change from baseline for the ends of cycle 1,3, and 5 in FACTG total score and EQ-5D-3L index score."
>
> — FDA Multi-Discipline Review (Applicant SAP text quoted in §8.1), PDF p. 52 (https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2018/761051Orig1s000MultidisciplineR.pdf)

##### Model 3: EQ-5D-3L index, change from baseline through 6 months (key secondary (multiplicity-controlled with ORR-INV; 4 key secondaries))

> "The same methods described above for the analysis of change in Skindex-29 score will be performed for the analysis of change from baseline for the ends of cycle 1,3, and 5 in FACTG total score and EQ-5D-3L index score."

- Role: secondary/exploratory PRO (no multiplicity control)
- Model family: MMRM / linear mixed-effects repeated-measures model
- Response: PRO score (change from baseline per MDR; SAP includes baseline as covariate)
- Fixed effects: treatment, randomization stratification factors (lung/liver metastases yes/no; prior CDK4/6 inhibitor yes/no), time, baseline value, treatment-by-time [SAP p.56-57]
- Random effects: Not stated (correlation modeled via within-patient matrix)
- Covariance: Unstructured first approach [SAP p.57]
- Covariance fallback: 'structure of the correlation matrix will be investigated and simplified using likelihood ratio tests if appropriate'; if no convergence, fewer time points may be included [SAP p.57]
- Denominator df: Not stated
- Estimation: Not stated
- Time coding: 'Time will be explored as both a continuous and categorical variable to assess the best model fit' (time = weeks since baseline) [SAP p.57]
- Estimand / contrast: Difference in LS means and 2-sided 95% CI at selected time points [SAP p.57]
- Missing data: Data on treatment and post-treatment follow-up until documented progression included; patients need evaluable baseline and >=1 post-baseline score [SAP p.57]
- MNAR sensitivity: Not stated
- Software: SAS v9.4 used elsewhere in SAP; not stated for this model
- Results: No numeric model results in MDR; Applicant: no clinically meaningful differences except slight delay in pain worsening (BPI-SF), EQ-5D maintained, trend to worse social functioning on alpelisib [MDR p.117]
- FDA comments: FDA disagreed with Applicant's PRO conclusions: no multiplicity control so exploratory; 'meaningful difference' language rejected; not powered for no-difference conclusion; cannot exclude detriment to QoL [MDR p.118]
- Spec source: SAP verbatim (posted Amendment 6, post-approval) + MDR summary

#### Verbatim specification excerpts

##### Model 1: Change from baseline in EORTC QLQ-C30 subscales, EQ-5D-5L VAS, BPI-SF over time (secondary/exploratory PRO (no multiplicity control))

> "A repeated measures model for longitudinal data will be used to compare the two treatment arms in sub-scales obtained from EORTC QLQ-C30 over time. This longitudinal model will include terms for treatment, the randomization stratification factors (presence of lung and/or liver metastases [yes versus no] and previous treatment with any CDK4/6 inhibitor [yes versus no]), time (duration in weeks counting from the time of baseline measurement to the time of a particular post baseline measurement) and baseline value as main effects, as well as an interaction term for treatment by time. Time will be explored as both a continuous and categorical variable to assess the best model fit. As a first approach, an unstructured correlation matrix will be used to model the correlation within patients. The structure of the correlation matrix will be investigated and simplified using likelihood ratio tests if appropriate. The differences in least square means between treatment and control group, and the corresponding 2-sided 95% CI at selected time points will be presented. Data collected under treatment (i.e. while the patient is treated) and during post-treatment follow-up up until documented progression will be included. If the model fit based on unblinded data does not achieve convergence then fewer time points for inclusion may be considered."
>
> — SAP (Amendment 6, posted on ClinicalTrials.gov), PDF p. 56 (https://cdn.clinicaltrials.gov/large-docs/18/NCT02437318/SAP_003.pdf)

> "Change from baseline in all subscales obtained from EORTC QLQ-C30, the VAS of EQ-5D-5L and BPI-SF were analyzed using a linear mixed effect model."
>
> — FDA Multi-Discipline Review, PDF p. 96 (https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2019/212526Orig1s000MultidisciplineR.pdf)

> "The FDA disagrees with the applicant’s conclusions regarding COA (PRO) endpoints. The PRO analyses with composite scores were not controlled for multiple comparisons, and therefore all of these analyses are considered exploratory."
>
> — FDA Multi-Discipline Review, PDF p. 119 (https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2019/212526Orig1s000MultidisciplineR.pdf)

> "The analysis of COA endpoints was not adequately powered to support a non-inferiority conclusion (i.e. a finding of no difference between the two arms). It is not possible to exclude a detrimental effect of alpelisib on global health status or quality of life for patients enrolled in the SOLAR-1 trial."
>
> — FDA Multi-Discipline Review, PDF p. 119 (https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2019/212526Orig1s000MultidisciplineR.pdf)

### pegulicianine (Lumisight) — NDA 214511

Therapeutic area: Oncology (imaging agent). Sponsor: Lumicell, Inc.. Approval year: 2024.

Note: README says 'exchangeable' working correlation; SAP says 'compound symmetry' (equivalent). GEE is marginal, not mixed-effects.

#### Model 1: Tissue-level sensitivity (performance goal >40%) (co-primary)

- Trial: CL0007 (NCT03686215), mITT 357 patients, 2346 tissue orientations
- Endpoint / timepoint: Tissue-level sensitivity (performance goal >40%)
- Role: co-primary
- Model family: GEE (marginal, not mixed-effects)
- Response: Binary LUMISIGHT-positive among standard-of-truth-positive tissues
- Fixed effects: intercept only (proportion estimate)
- Random effects: none (marginal model; clustering within patient handled by working correlation)
- Covariance: Compound symmetry (exchangeable) working correlation [SAP p.8-9]
- Covariance fallback: Not stated
- Denominator df: Not stated
- Estimation: GEE (PROC GENMOD), binomial GLM [SAP p.8]
- Time coding: n/a (clustered tissues, not longitudinal)
- Estimand / contrast: GEE-estimated sensitivity with two-sided 95% CI; success if lower bound > 40%; bootstrap (10,000 resamples of subjects) as alternative CI [SAP p.8-9]; sample size by simulation with ICC 0.22 [SAP p.9]
- Missing data: Not stated
- MNAR sensitivity: n/a
- Software: SAS PROC GENMOD [SAP p.8]
- Results: 49.1% (95% CI 36.4%, 61.9%) - FAILED (lower bound < 40%); 34/69 positives; FDA unadjusted 49.3% (38.0, 61.6) [MDR Table 52 p.109]
- FDA comments: FDA ran exploratory analysis assuming independence: 'results between GEE and FDA exploratory analyses are similar, suggesting that the correlation among tissues within patients appears low' [MDR p.109]; sensitivity endpoint missed but approval granted on totality
- Spec source: SAP verbatim (CL0007r08, 17-Nov-2021)

#### Model 2: Tissue-level specificity (performance goal >60%) (co-primary)

- Trial: CL0007 (NCT03686215), mITT 357 patients, 2346 tissue orientations
- Endpoint / timepoint: Tissue-level specificity (performance goal >60%)
- Role: co-primary
- Model family: GEE (marginal, not mixed-effects)
- Response: Binary LUMISIGHT-negative among standard-of-truth-negative tissues
- Fixed effects: intercept only
- Random effects: none (marginal model; clustering within patient handled by working correlation)
- Covariance: Compound symmetry (exchangeable) working correlation [SAP p.8-9]
- Covariance fallback: Not stated
- Denominator df: Not stated
- Estimation: GEE (PROC GENMOD), binomial GLM [SAP p.8]
- Time coding: n/a (clustered tissues, not longitudinal)
- Estimand / contrast: GEE-estimated specificity, lower 95% bound vs 60%
- Missing data: Not stated
- MNAR sensitivity: n/a
- Software: SAS PROC GENMOD [SAP p.8]
- Results: 86.5% (95% CI 84.5%, 88.3%) - met; 1940/2277; FDA unadjusted 85.2% (83.4, 86.6) [MDR Table 52]
- FDA comments: As above
- Spec source: SAP verbatim (CL0007r08, 17-Nov-2021)

#### Verbatim specification excerpts

##### Model 1: Tissue-level sensitivity (performance goal >40%) (co-primary)

> "Generalized Estimating Equation (GEE): This method is used to analyze correlated data which is modeled with generalized linear model having binomial link function, and including correlation cluster and matrix information (here within each subject). Procedure Genmod in SAS is used to apply this method (https://support.sas.com/rnd/app/stat/topics/gee/gee.pdf). This method with a compound symmetry working correlation structure, will be used to estimate sensitivity and specificity along with a 97.5% lower bounded one-sided confidence interval (CI) (* Tessa S. S. Genders, Sandra Spronk, Theo Stijnen, Ewout W. Steyerberg, Emmanuel Lesaffre, M. G. Myriam Hunink. Methods for Calculating Sensitivity and Specificity of Clustered Data: A TutorialRadiology: Volume 265 (3):910 (2012))."
>
> — SAP CL0007 (17NOV2021) §4.3, PDF p. 10 (https://cdn.clinicaltrials.gov/large-docs/15/NCT03686215/SAP_001.pdf)

> "Bootstrapping sampling method: This method is applied to sample the subjects with replacement at the same sample size of mITT for 10,000 rounds. The sampled subjects with corresponding imaging, and standard truth positive and negatives will be used to estimate the sensitivity and specificity. The median sensitivity and specificity will be used as the estimate from bootstrapping method. The 2.5% and 97.5% percentiles will be used as lower and upper bounds, respectively, for 95% confidence intervals."
>
> — SAP CL0007 (17NOV2021) §4.3, PDF p. 10 (https://cdn.clinicaltrials.gov/large-docs/15/NCT03686215/SAP_001.pdf)

> "To account for within-subject correlation, Generalized Estimating Equations (GEE), with a compound symmetry working correlation structure, will be used to estimate sensitivity and specificity along with an equi-tail 95% two-sided confidence interval (CI). The null hypothesis 𝐻 is rejected if the lower bound of the confidence interval for sensitivity is larger than the performance goal of 40%."
>
> — SAP CL0007 (17NOV2021) §4.3, PDF p. 10 (https://cdn.clinicaltrials.gov/large-docs/15/NCT03686215/SAP_001.pdf)

> "As sensitivity and specificity are estimated at the per tissue level, within subject correlation is considered for the sample size estimation."
>
> — SAP CL0007 (17NOV2021) §4.3, PDF p. 11 (https://cdn.clinicaltrials.gov/large-docs/15/NCT03686215/SAP_001.pdf)

> "Assuming 70 truth standard positive shaves, under the alternative hypothesis, using Generalized Estimating Equation (GEE) model with a compound symmetry working correlation structure, will have >90% power to show that the true sensitivity is > 40%."
>
> — SAP CL0007 (17NOV2021) §4.3, PDF p. 11 (https://cdn.clinicaltrials.gov/large-docs/15/NCT03686215/SAP_001.pdf)

> "Tissue-level sensitivity and specificity were evaluated for H0: sensitivity ≤ 40% versus H1: sensitivity > 40%, and for H0: specificity ≤ 60% versus H1: specificity > 60% using a generalized estimating equation (GEE) to account for correlation of tissues from the same patient at a 2-sided 5% significance level. Results of co-primary efficacy endpoints 2 and 3 are shown in Table 52. Tissue-level specificity exceeded the performance goal of 60% and tissue-level sensitivity did not meet the performance goal of 40%. The FDA statistics review team performed an exploratory analysis assuming tissues within a patient are independent. The results between GEE and FDA exploratory analyses are similar, suggesting that the correlation among tissues within patients appears low."
>
> — FDA Multi-Discipline Review, PDF p. 110 (https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2024/214511Orig1s000MultidisciplineR.pdf)

##### Model 2: Tissue-level specificity (performance goal >60%) (co-primary)

#### Verbatim specification excerpts

##### Model 1: Active ROM (affected joint, % of AMA reference), Week 25 (model timepoints Weeks 13, 25) (key secondary (hierarchical, after ORR RECIST and ORR TVS))

> "FDA agrees with the Applicant’s description of the statistical analysis plan for MOTION."
>
> — FDA Multi-Discipline Review, PDF p. 126 (https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2025/219304Orig1s000MultidisciplineR.pdf)

> "For the key secondary endpoints that are based on change from baseline assessments, mixed model for repeated measurements (MMRM) with the sandwich estimator to estimate the variance-covariance matrix was used. Each of these models included fixed effects for treatment group, timepoint, treatment group by timepoint interaction, stratification factors (region and tumor location), and the baseline value of the corresponding endpoint. The different timepoints that were included in the model specific to each endpoint are included in the below table."
>
> — FDA Multi-Discipline Review, PDF p. 126 (https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2025/219304Orig1s000MultidisciplineR.pdf)

> "The preponderance of missing data for the key secondary efficacy endpoints of active ROM, PROMIS-PF, Worst Stiffness NRS, and EQ-VAS were evaluated. If there was more than 10% of missing data at Week 25 in any of the endpoints, then the impact of the missing data was explored for that endpoint and included, but not limited to, the following analyses: x Multiple imputation based on randomized treatment to mimic missing at random x A Pattern Mixture Model approach where participants who discontinued treatment due to an AE on vimseltinib were imputed based on the missing not at random assumption and imputed as if they received placebo"
>
> — FDA Multi-Discipline Review, PDF p. 125 (https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2025/219304Orig1s000MultidisciplineR.pdf)

> "Note 1: Mean change from baseline was estimated from the MMRM for each corresponding endpoint. Baseline means presented include all participants and not only the ones with data at baseline and Week 25. Active ROM was normalized to the AMA reference standard."
>
> — FDA Multi-Discipline Review, PDF p. 142 (https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2025/219304Orig1s000MultidisciplineR.pdf)

> "Missing data sensitivity analysis of change from baseline in active ROM per American Medical Association standard, PROMIS-PF, Worst Stiffness NRS, and EQ-5D-5L VAS (with mixed model repeated measures [MMRM] model) using multiple imputation based on data from placebo was performed. The results demonstrate robustness to the conclusion that participants receiving vimseltinib had statistically significant greater improvement in active ROM, PROMIS-PF, Worst Stiffness NRS, and EQ-5D-5L VAS compared to those receiving placebo, regardless of the true underlying missing data mechanism (Table 32)."
>
> — FDA Multi-Discipline Review, PDF p. 146 (https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2025/219304Orig1s000MultidisciplineR.pdf)

> "The Applicant conducted additional sensitivity analysis (Table 32) to assess the impact of missing data in active ROM. In this sensitivity analysis, the missing data were imputed based on the mean value from patients who received placebo using multiple imputation. Based on this sensitivity analysis, the differences in LS mean change from baseline at Week 25 remained similar in magnitude for active ROM (difference in LS mean [95% CI] was 13.0% (2.7%, 23.3%). In addition to this, the Applicant performed additional sensitivity analyses using tipping point analyses to address the concern of informative missingness for the COA endpoints. The results of these sensitivity analysis along with the primary analysis are provided in the table below."
>
> — FDA Multi-Discipline Review, PDF p. 150 (https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2025/219304Orig1s000MultidisciplineR.pdf)

> "These sensitivity analyses support the primary analysis conclusions. The delta-adjusting pattern mixture model (PMM) analysis showed that the required penalty for loss of statistical significance was an average worsening of 24% points for patients with missing data in the vimseltinib arm. FDA concludes that the tipping point of 24% to be an extreme scenario and is unlikely."
>
> — FDA Multi-Discipline Review, PDF p. 151 (https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2025/219304Orig1s000MultidisciplineR.pdf)

#### Verbatim specification excerpts

##### Model 1: Change from baseline in HbA1c at last scheduled visit (sensitivity (FDA reviewer re-analysis; sponsor primary = ANCOVA-LOCF))

> "The sponsor’s primary analyses used an analysis of covariance (ANCOVA) method with the treatment and previous anti-diabetes therapy as fixed classification effects and baseline HbA1c as linear covariate on the full analysis set (FAS). The FAS was a subset of the treated set including all patients who had a baseline and at least one on-treatment HbA1c measurement available. The last observation carried forward method (LOCF) was applied to the FAS. For studies 18 and 50, the fixed effects in the statistical model alter as specified in the two trials."
>

#### Verbatim specification excerpts

##### Model 1: Change from baseline in HbA1c at Week 26 (52 for DIA3009/3015; 18 for DIA3008 substudies); also FPG (supportive/sensitivity (primary = ANCOVA-LOCF))

> "The sponsor’s pre-specified primary analysis of HbA1c used an analysis of covariance (ANCOVA) model using the last observation carried forward method (LOCF) for missing observations. In general, the ANCOVA model included terms for treatment and randomization stratification factor(s) (if applicable) as fixed effects and the corresponding baseline HbA1c value as a covariate. In Study DIA3004, an additional covariate of baseline eGFR was included in the model. Least-squares (LS) mean treatment differences between each canagliflozin group and the comparator (either placebo or active comparator) and their two-sided 95% confidence intervals (CI) were estimated from the model for each individual study."
>
> — FDA Statistical Review, PDF p. 76 (https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2013/204042Orig1s000StatR.pdf)

> "I performed supportive analysis using the Per Protocol analysis set. As an additional supportive analysis, change from baseline in HbA1c was analyzed using mixed model repeated measures (MMRM). The MMRM analysis was based on observed data and included the fixed, categorical effects of treatment, stratification factors, visit, and treatment-by-visit interaction as fixed effects and the corresponding baseline HbA1c value as a covariate. An unstructured covariance was used to model the within-patient errors."
>
> — FDA Statistical Review, PDF p. 76 (https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2013/204042Orig1s000StatR.pdf)

> "All superiority comparisons of canagliflozin 300 mg and 100 mg doses vs placebo in HbA1c change from baseline, the primary efficacy endpoint, were significant in all studies. The results were based on LOCF as the primary method for accounting for missing data. Analyses using MMRM were consistent with the primary results with LOCF."
>
> — FDA Statistical Review, PDF p. 70 (https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2013/204042Orig1s000StatR.pdf)

##### Model 2: Durability: HbA1c change from Week 26 to Week 104 (supportive/descriptive)

> "To assess the durability of glycemic control, a longitudinal profile of HbA1c would be presented by treatment group. The rates of HbA1c change from Week 26 to Week 104 would be estimated and the comparisons between each dose group of CANAGLIFLOZIN and glimepiride would be made. For supportive analysis, the estimates of treatment from mixed effect modeling for the change of HbA1c from Week 26 would be derived. A longitudinal plot of the estimates would be presented. The analysis of durability which involves comparing groups on changes of HbA1c after randomization from Week 26 to Week 104 would be considered as descriptive analyses only."
>
> — FDA Statistical Review, PDF p. 130 (https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2013/204042Orig1s000StatR.pdf)

### Alirocumab (Praluent) — BLA 125559

Therapeutic area: Cardiovascular / Metabolic. Sponsor: Sanofi-Aventis U.S. LLC / Regeneron. Approval year: 2015.

#### Model 1: Percent change in calculated LDL-C from baseline to Week 24 (primary (ITT estimand, ITT population))

- **Trial:** ODYSSEY program, 10 Phase 3 trials (FH I, FH II, HIGH FH, COMBO I, COMBO II, LONG TERM NCT01507831, OPTIONS I, OPTIONS II, ALTERNATIVE, MONO)
- **Endpoint/timepoint:** Percent change in calculated LDL-C from baseline to Week 24
- **Role:** primary (ITT estimand, ITT population)
- **Model family:** MMRM
- **Response:** Percent change from baseline in LDL-C [StatR p.19]
- **Fixed effects:** treatment, randomization strata, time point (up to week 52), treatment-by-time, strata-by-time, baseline LDL-C, baseline LDL-C-by-time [StatR p.19 verbatim: 'The model included the following variables as covariates: treatment, randomization strata, time point (up to week 52; see Table 3), treatment-by-time interaction, strata-by-time interaction, baseline LDL-C, and baseline LDL-C by time interaction.']
- **Random effects:** none stated (classic MMRM)
- **Covariance structure:** Not stated
- **Covariance fallback:** Not stated
- **Denominator df:** Satterthwaite [StatR p.19 verbatim: 'denominator degrees of freedom were estimated using Satterthwaite's approximation']
- **Estimation:** REML [StatR p.19 verbatim: 'Parameters were estimated using restricted maximum likelihood']
- **Time coding:** categorical visits (weeks 4, 8, 12, 16, 24, 36, 52 ... per trial schedule, Table 3) [StatR p.13]
- **Estimand / contrast:** LS-mean difference (alirocumab - control) in % change at Week 24; ITT estimand uses all data regardless of adherence; 99% CI (OPTIONS I) / 98.75% CI (OPTIONS II) [StatR Table 13]
- **Missing data / intercurrent events:** MAR, no imputation [StatR p.19: 'Missing LDL-C values were assumed to be missing at random (MAR) and were not imputed.']
- **MNAR sensitivity:** Pattern-mixture model with mixed imputation (100 imputed datasets, Rubin's rules): on-treatment missing values imputed under MAR; post-discontinuation (after last injection + 21 days) values imputed centered on patient's own baseline (return-to-baseline). Adopted as FDA-preferred analysis. Fit only for primary endpoint. [StatR p.20-21]
- **Software:** Not stated
- **Results:** Sponsor MMRM [StatR Table 13, p.34]: LONG TERM aliro 150 mg (n=1386 w/ wk24 data of N=1553) -61% vs placebo (n=708 of 788) +1%, diff -62% (95% CI -64, -59); FH I -58% (-63,-53); FH II -51% (-58,-45); HIGH FH -39% (-51,-27); COMBO I -46% (-52,-39); COMBO II vs ezetimibe -30% (-34,-25); ALTERNATIVE -30% (-36,-24); MONO -32% (-40,-23); OPTIONS II rosuva 20 mg stratum non-significant (-20%, 98.75% CI -46, 6; -25%, -51, 1). FDA PMM [Table 14, p.38]: LONG TERM -58% (-61,-56); FH I -56%; COMBO I -43%; attenuation 0-8 percentage points.
- **FDA comments:** Reviewer disputed MAR: 'given that treatment adherence is not accounted for in the MMRM, the MAR assumption is questionable and likely leads to an over-estimate of the ITT effect' [p.19]; mean profiles from Phase 2 and LONG TERM/COMBO I/II showed LDL-C rebound after stopping drug; PMM is 'the FDA's preferred analysis' [p.9]. Subgroup analyses also used MMRM (sponsor) [p.~50] and PMM (FDA).
- **Spec source:** StatR verbatim

#### Verbatim specification excerpts

##### Model 1: Percent change in calculated LDL-C from baseline to Week 24 (primary (ITT estimand, ITT population))

> "Analysis of the primary efficacy endpoint: Percent change in LDL-C from baseline to week 24 was analyzed using a mixed model for repeated measures (MMRM). The model included the following variables as covariates: treatment, randomization strata, time point (up to week 52; see Table 3), treatment-by-time interaction, strata-by-time interaction, baseline LDL-C, and baseline LDL-C by time interaction. Parameters were estimated using restricted maximum likelihood; denominator degrees of freedom were estimated using Satterthwaite’s approximation. Missing LDL-C values were assumed to be missing at random (MAR) and were not imputed."
>
> — FDA Statistical Review, p. 40 (https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2015/125559Orig1s000StatR.pdf)

> "In my opinion, given that treatment adherence is not accounted for in the MMRM, the MAR assumption is questionable and likely leads to an over-estimate of the ITT effect. The problem with assuming that the statistical behavior of the missing data is the same as the statistical behavior of the observed data (conditional on covariates and observed responses) is that those with data are systematically different than those without data. In particular, those with data were primarily on study drug, whereas those without data were primarily no longer receiving study drug. The distinction is important as the LDL-C reduction achieved while on study drug was not sustained after stopping treatment, suggesting an attenuation of the treatment effect. This trend was observed in two phase 2 studies (Figure 3 and Figure 4) that followed patients after a 12 week treatment period and in LONG TERM, COMBO I and COMBO II, which had a sizable number of patients followed after stopping drug early. Mean profile plots for these phase 3 trials are displayed in Figure 13 to Figure 15 in the Appendix."
>
> — FDA Statistical Review, p. 40 (https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2015/125559Orig1s000StatR.pdf)

> "Statistical approaches for the analysis of primary and key secondary efficacy endpoints were discussed in several correspondences between 2013 and 2014. For the applicant’s primary analysis model for the primary and several key secondary efficacy endpoints, FDA conveyed their concern that by ignoring treatment adherence when addressing missing data that the analysis may not provide a clinically meaningful estimate of the treatment effect. In response the applicants implemented as a sensitivity analysis a pattern mixture model to account for possible non-random missingness. This model was only fit for the primary efficacy endpoint, and is the FDA’s preferred analysis."
>
> — FDA Statistical Review, p. 30 (https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2015/125559Orig1s000StatR.pdf)

> "Preferred analysis of the primary efficacy endpoint: In response to the concerns shared with the applicant regarding the handling of missing data in the primary efficacy analysis, they proposed an alternative approach that likely gives a more accurate estimate of the ITT effect. The approach used a Pattern-Mixture Model (PMM) with mixed imputation in the randomized population. To account for the uncertainty in the missing data, missing values imputed using multiple imputation. A total of 100 imputed datasets were created. Results from the imputed datasets were combined using Rubin’s method. [...] In the PMM different imputation strategies were applied to missing LDL-C values during the on-treatment period and after treatment discontinuation, defined as after the day of last injection + 21 days. For missing values occurring during the on-treatment period it was assumed that patients would continue to show benefit. Missing LDL-C values during this period were considered MAR and imputed based on other on-treatment measurements. For patients that stopped their study treatment it was assumed they would no longer benefit from study drug, and their LDL-C values would return to baseline. For these patients the imputed LDL-C values were centered on the patient’s baseline value. Patients not treated or with missing data before taking study medication also had their LDL-C values imputed based on their baseline value."
>
> — FDA Statistical Review, pp. 41-42 (https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2015/125559Orig1s000StatR.pdf)

> "Subgroup analysis on the primary efficacy endpoints was performed using a MMRM in the ITT population with treatment, visit, baseline LDL-C and treatment by visit interaction as covariates in the model. The analysis was performed within the individual level that defined the subgroup. Formal tests for interaction were not performed."
>
> — FDA Statistical Review, p. 71 (https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2015/125559Orig1s000StatR.pdf)

##### Model 2: Percent change in LDL-C at Week 24, on-treatment estimand (mITT population); listed in fixed-sequence hierarchy (key secondary (hierarchy) / supportive)

> "Comments on estimating the on-treatment estimand: The on-treatment estimand used data only during the on-treatment period. Thus, if a subject had a measurement after stopping study drug early, that value was not used in the analysis. In such a case the LDL-C value is not missing, although the MMRM assumes it is. Due to the MAR assumption made by the MMRM, statistical behavior of the missing data in the analysis is the same as the observed data. Because the model uses only on-treatment observations, the model is estimating the treatment effect assuming all subjects included in the mITT population adhered to randomized therapy, contrary to the fact some could not. The analysis therefore attempts to estimate a treatment effect under conditions that were not observed in the clinical trial. It is my opinion the on-treatment estimand lacks clinical relevance due to the underlying implausibility of achieving perfect treatment adherence."
>
> — FDA Statistical Review, p. 43 (https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2015/125559Orig1s000StatR.pdf)

Model specification otherwise same as Model 1 (FDA Statistical Review, p. 40).


##### Model 3: Percent change in ApoB, non-HDL-C, total-C, HDL-C, ApoA1 at Weeks 12/24 (key secondary)

> "Analysis of key secondary efficacy endpoints: Different statistical models were used for continuous secondary endpoints anticipated to have a normal and non-normal distribution. The two endpoints anticipated to have a non-normal distribution were TG and Lp(a). Continuous endpoints assumed to be normally distributed were analyzed using the same MMRM that was used for the primary efficacy endpoint. Continuous endpoints assumed to have a non-normal distribution was analyzed using robust regression (M-estimation). The model included treatment, randomization strata and baseline value as predictor variables. Subjects missing the endpoint had a response imputed. The imputation model included treatment, baseline value, randomization strata, baseline characteristics and post-baseline values. The imputation did not follow the PMM approach. A total of 100 imputed datasets were created. Results from the 100 complete datasets were combined using Rubin’s method. Binary endpoints were analyzed using logistic regression. The model included treatment and baseline value as covariates and randomization strata as a stratification factor. Missing responses were imputed using the approach described above for non-normally distributed continuous endpoints."
>
> — FDA Statistical Review, p. 42 (https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2015/125559Orig1s000StatR.pdf)

PMM restricted to the primary endpoint: see the "Statistical approaches for the analysis of primary and key secondary efficacy endpoints" quote under Model 1 (p. 30).

### Patiromer (Veltassa) — NDA 205739

Therapeutic area: Cardiovascular / Metabolic. Sponsor: Relypsa, Inc.. Approval year: 2015.

#### Model 1: Change in serum potassium (central lab) from Part A baseline to Part A Week 4 (primary (Part A; SPA criterion decrease >=0.7 mEq/L with p<0.05))

- **Trial:** OPAL-HK (RLY5016-301), NCT01810939, Part A (single-arm, open-label, 4 weeks)
- **Endpoint/timepoint:** Change in serum potassium (central lab) from Part A baseline to Part A Week 4
- **Role:** primary (Part A; SPA criterion decrease >=0.7 mEq/L with p<0.05)
- **Model family:** MMRM (single-arm longitudinal repeated-measures model; no treatment term)
- **Response:** Change from Part A baseline in serum K+ (mEq/L)
- **Fixed effects:** time (weekly Part A visits, categorical), T2DM at baseline (yes/no), heart failure at baseline (yes/no), Part A baseline central serum K+ (continuous) [StatR p.15 Table 3.5 footnote verbatim: 'a longitudinal model with an unstructured covariance structure and three categorical covariates: a) time as defined by weekly Part A visits, b) presence of type 2 diabetes mellitus at Part A Baseline and c) presence of heart failure at Part A Baseline; and Part A Baseline central serum potassium as a continuous covariate.']
- **Random effects:** none stated
- **Covariance structure:** Unstructured [StatR p.15]
- **Covariance fallback:** Not stated
- **Denominator df:** Not stated
- **Estimation:** Not stated
- **Time coding:** categorical (weekly visits Weeks 1-4)
- **Estimand / contrast:** Model-based mean change at Week 4 tested against zero (no comparator)

#### Verbatim specification excerpts

##### Model 1: Change in serum potassium (central lab) from Part A baseline to Part A Week 4 (primary (Part A; SPA criterion decrease >=0.7 mEq/L with p<0.05))

> "In Part A, as the primary efficacy analysis, the mean change will be estimated using a longitudinal repeated measures model that includes two binary covariates for the presence of heart failure (HF) at baseline (yes/no) and T2DM at baseline (yes/no) and a continuous covariate containing the Baseline Part A level of serum K+. As agreed by FDA, for the primary efficacy results from Part A of the study to be considered pivotal, the decrease in serum potassium from Part A Baseline to Part A Week 4 must have been ≥ 0.7 mEq/L with p < 0.05."
>
> — FDA Statistical Review, p. 10 (https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2015/205739Orig1s000StatR.pdf)

> "In Study 301, there are more local laboratory results available than those from central laboratory at each visit. Two methods for estimating missing central laboratory data were used. If no central laboratory serum potassium value is available for a visit but a local laboratory value is available, missing central laboratory serum potassium results were estimated from local laboratory results using a linear regression. Multiple imputation procedures were used in the event where the local laboratory result was also missing at a given visit."
>
> — FDA Statistical Review, p. 10 (https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2015/205739Orig1s000StatR.pdf)

> "The primary efficacy outcome for Part A was the change in serum potassium from Part A Baseline to the Part A Week 4 visit; mean change was estimated using a longitudinal repeated measures model. Twenty-four (24) subjects (10%) had neither a central nor a local laboratory serum potassium value at Week 4. Six (6) of the 243 subjects in the Part A ITT Analysis Population did not have at least one post-baseline serum potassium because of early withdrawal from Part A. These 6 subjects were, therefore, not included in the longitudinal Part A primary efficacy analysis."
>
> — FDA Statistical Review, p. 16 (https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2015/205739Orig1s000StatR.pdf)

> "The estimates for Part A Week 1 through Part A Week 4 come from a longitudinal model with an unstructured covariance structure and three categorical covariates: a) time as defined by weekly Part A visits, b) presence of type 2 diabetes mellitus at Part A Baseline and c) presence of heart failure at Part A Baseline; and Part A Baseline central serum potassium as a continuous covariate."
>
> — FDA Statistical Review (Table 3.5 footnote), p. 16 (https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2015/205739Orig1s000StatR.pdf)

> "The reviewer confirmed the efficacy results for both Part A and Part B of the study using the analysis data that were provided by the sponsor. The reviewer also used other nonparametric test statistical methods such as Wilcoxon test to verify the primary efficacy results in Part B. The missing data in these two parts of the study seem to be minor and do not lead to a different conclusion of the primary efficacy results."
>
> — FDA Statistical Review, p. 17 (https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2015/205739Orig1s000StatR.pdf)

### Lixisenatide (Adlyxin) — BLA 208471

Therapeutic area: Cardiovascular / Metabolic. Sponsor: Sanofi-Aventis U.S. LLC. Approval year: 2016.

#### Model 1: Change in HbA1c from baseline at Week 24 (12 for EFC6018, 26 for EFC12626) (supportive (post-hoc, requested in place of LOCF; FDA-preferred for labeling))

- **Trial:** GetGoal Phase 3 program (13 studies incl. EFC6018, EFC10743, EFC6014 GetGoal-M NCT00712673, EFC6019, EFC12626, EFC10780, EFC12261 ...)
- **Endpoint/timepoint:** Change in HbA1c from baseline at Week 24 (12 for EFC6018, 26 for EFC12626)
- **Role:** supportive (post-hoc, requested in place of LOCF; FDA-preferred for labeling)
- **Model family:** MMRM
- **Response:** Change from baseline in HbA1c (%)
- **Fixed effects:** all ANCOVA factors (treatment; randomization strata e.g. HbA1c stratum, metformin use; country, pooled China vs other) + visit + treatment-by-visit + baseline-by-visit, baseline HbA1c covariate [StatR p.11 verbatim (EFC12626): 'The MMRM model included all factors in the ANCOVA model as well as visit (Week 12, 20, 26 for HbA1c and Week 2, 6, 12, 20, 26 for body weight), treatment-by-visit interaction, and baseline-by-visit interaction.']
- **Random effects:** none stated
- **Covariance structure:** Not stated
- **Covariance fallback:** Not stated
- **Denominator df:** Not stated
- **Estimation:** Not stated
- **Time coding:** categorical visits
- **Estimand / contrast:** LS-mean difference at primary timepoint using all available post-baseline observations regardless of treatment discontinuation or rescue (treatment-policy-like)
- **Missing data / intercurrent events:** MAR [StatR p.5: 'MMRM assumes data are missing at random (MAR). The conclusions from the MMRM analysis may be subject to bias due to violation of the MAR assumption.']
- **MNAR sensitivity:** FDA-requested MI under the null: placebo-controlled studies - placebo-arm MAR imputation, lixisenatide arm imputed from placebo model (reference-based); active-controlled - control imputed as baseline+error, lixisenatide as baseline+0.4%+error; 100 imputations, ANCOVA, combined [StatR p.20]. EFC12626 vs glulisine TID: 0.28% (95% CI 0.157, 0.408) - NI (0.4%) no longer shown.
- **Software:** SAS PROC MIXED [StatR p.18 footnote: 'In SAS Proc Mixed procedure, the sponsor set singular=1e-11, otherwise the likelihood was infinite and there was no output.']
- **Results:** EFC12626 (Table 8/SumR Table 2): lixi n=284 -0.63, glulisine QD n=290 -0.57, TID n=291 -0.84; lixi vs QD -0.06 (-0.176, 0.061) p=0.341; lixi vs TID +0.21 (0.094, 0.331) p=0.0005. EFC6019 vs exenatide +0.18 (0.046, 0.307). EFC6014 AM -0.41 (-0.580,-0.234); EFC6015 -0.69 (-0.811,-0.56); EFC10780 vs sitagliptin 0.04 (-0.198, 0.288).
- **FDA comments:** Pre-specified primary was ANCOVA with LOCF; 'Since the Division no longer recommends LOCF ... the sponsor also performed post-hoc MMRM analysis using all available post-baseline observations ... Currently we think this analysis is more appropriate for labeling.' [StatR p.5]. Division Director: MMRM estimates 'reasonably reflective' and used in label, but MI result 'calling into question the persuasiveness of the reported results based on the sponsor's MMRM analysis' for EFC12626 [SumR p.9].
- **Spec source:** StatR verbatim

#### Verbatim specification excerpts

##### Model 1: Change in HbA1c from baseline at Week 24 (12 for EFC6018, 26 for EFC12626) (supportive (post-hoc, requested in place of LOCF; FDA-preferred for labeling))

> "The pre-specified primary analysis is an analysis of covariance (ANCOVA) model using the last observation carried forward method (LOCF) for missing observations. Since the Division no longer recommends LOCF as the approach for dealing with missing data, the sponsor also performed post-hoc MMRM analysis using all available post-baseline observations regardless of treatment discontinuation or initiation of rescue therapy. Currently we think this analysis is more appropriate for labeling."
>
> — FDA Statistical Review, p. 58 (https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2016/208471Orig1s000StatR.pdf)

> "The LOCF approach for handling missing data is no longer recommended by the Division. The sponsor also performed post-hoc supportive analyses for all Phase 3 efficacy studies in this resubmission, including mixed-effect model with repeated measures (MMRM) using on-treatment data which excluded data after treatment discontinuation or initiation of rescue therapy and MMRM using all postbaseline observations regardless of adherence to assigned treatment. MMRM assumes missing data are MAR. Upon our request, the sponsor performed post-hoc sensitivity analyses to examine the impact of violation of the MAR assumption in the Phase 3 studies."
>
> — FDA Statistical Review, p. 63 (https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2016/208471Orig1s000StatR.pdf)

> "The primary analysis was an ANCOVA model with treatment (lixisenatide, insulin glulisine QD, and insulin glulisine TID), stratum of HbA1c at Visit 7 (Week -1) (<8%, ≥8%), randomization stratum of metformin use (yes, no), and country as fixed effects and using the corresponding baseline value as a covariate. [...] As a post-hoc supportive analysis, a MMRM was performed for HbA1c and body weight respectively using all available post-baseline observations. The MMRM model included all factors in the ANCOVA model as well as visit (Week 12, 20, 26 for HbA1c and Week 2, 6, 12, 20, 26 for body weight), treatment-by-visit interaction, and baseline-by-visit interaction. The same MMRM was also performed using on-treatment data."
>
> — FDA Statistical Review (Study EFC12626), p. 64 (https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2016/208471Orig1s000StatR.pdf)

> "As a supportive analysis, a MMRM was performed using all available post-baseline observations. The MMRM model included all factors in the ANCOVA model as well as visit (Week 8, 12, 16, 24), treatment-by-visit interaction, and baseline-by-visit interaction. The same MMRM was also performed using on-treatment data."
>
> — FDA Statistical Review (Study EFC12261), p. 68 (https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2016/208471Orig1s000StatR.pdf)

> "1. In SAS Proc Mixed procedure, the sponsor set singular=1e-11, otherwise the likelihood was infinite and there there was no output. 2. In the MMRM model, country was pooled as China and other countries."
>
> — FDA Statistical Review (Table 8 footnotes), p. 71 (https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2016/208471Orig1s000StatR.pdf)

> "In the study design, the sponsor did not intend to continue measuring HbA1c after treatment discontinuation or initiation of rescue therapy. There was considerable amount (>10%) of missing data in some of the Phase 3 studies. MMRM assumes data are missing at random (MAR). The conclusions from the MMRM analysis may be subject to bias due to violation of the MAR assumption. Upon request, the sponsor performed post-hoc sensitivity analyses to examine the impact of violation of the MAR assumption. The post-hoc sensitivity analyses confirmed most of the conclusions from the MMRM analysis using all available post-baseline observations. They suggest there is a possibility that lixisenatide did not achieve noninferiority versus insulin glargine TID based on a non-inferiority margin of 0.4% (LS mean treatment difference was 0.28%; 95% CI: 0.157, 0.408). However, considering that the imputation approach is very conservative and that the upper bound of the 95% CI for the treatment difference is just a little over 0.4%, this possibility is not very high."
>
> — FDA Statistical Review, p. 59 (https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2016/208471Orig1s000StatR.pdf)

> "MMRM assumes missing data are MAR. Considering that there was considerable amount of missing data and that there was evidence that data were not MAR in some of the Phase 3 studies, we sent information request to the sponsor on 1 January 2016 for additional sensitivity analyses to examine the impact of violation of the MAR assumption. The sponsor performed the analyses for all 13 Phase 3 studies. In these analyses, the imputation was under the null hypothesis and all observed cases of HbA1c change from baseline at the primary efficacy time point were treated as non-missing. [...] For the placebo-controlled studies, missing values at the primary efficacy time point in the placebo arm were imputed based on the MAR assumption. The regression model contained terms for baseline HbA1c values and randomization strata. Missing values in the lixisenatide arm were imputed using the baseline HbA1c values, randomization strata and parameters from the imputation model for the placebo group plus an error.  For the active-controlled studies, the missing values at the primary efficacy time point were imputed as equal to their baseline plus an error in the control group and equal to their baseline plus 0.4% plus an error in the lixisenatide group. The error was normally distributed with mean zero and a standard deviation set equal to the estimated pooled standard deviation. Missing HbA1c values at the primary efficacy time point were imputed 100 times to generate 100 datasets with complete HbA1c values at the primary efficacy time point. Each of the complete dataset was analyzed by the same ANCOVA model as done for the primary analysis."
>
> — FDA Statistical Review, p. 73 (https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2016/208471Orig1s000StatR.pdf)

> "I conducted subgroup analyses on HbA1c using MMRM, similar to the one used for the post-hoc supportive analyses, with additional covariate on the subgroups being analyzed and treatment-by-subgroup and treatment-by-visit-by-subgroup interactions. The estimates for treatment difference within subgroups and the p-value for testing difference in treatment difference between subgroups were presented in Table 11 for Study EFC12626 and Table 12 for Study EFC12261. The sponsor’s forest plots for treatment difference within subgroups were presented in Appendices."
>
> — FDA Statistical Review, p. 76 (https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2016/208471Orig1s000StatR.pdf)

> "The sponsor repeated the analyses using a mixed effect model repeated measure (MMRM model) using all available data (including data obtained post-rescue or retrieved). Dr. He performed a sensitivity analysis for missing data that relied on a method that also used all available data but did make the assumption that data were missing at random (i.e., an ANCOVA model using multiple imputations for missing values). While Dr. He’s analyses changed the estimates of efficacy somewhat; overall conclusions for 10 of the 11 studies were not altered. Missing data handling in this way did however affect the conclusion of study EFC12626, the study comparing lixisenatide to insulin glulisine TID. Using a multiple imputation for missing values model, a conclusion of non-inferiority of lixisenatide to glulisine TID (using a NI margin of 0.4%) could no longer be made (LS mean treatment difference [95% CI]: 0.28 [0.157, 0.408]) calling into question the persuasiveness of the reported results based on the sponsor’s MMRM analysis. Overall the statistical group viewed estimates of efficacy using the MMRM analyses to be reasonably reflective of the effect of Adlyxin and recommended that these be used to reflect Adlyxin efficacy in the final product label. It will be emphasized that Adlyxin was not as effective as insulin glulisine TID in the product label."
>
> — FDA Division Director Summary Review, p. 10 (https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2016/208471Orig1s000SumR.pdf)

### Semaglutide (Ozempic) — NDA 209637 (original approval)

Therapeutic area: Cardiovascular / Metabolic. Sponsor: Novo Nordisk A/S. Approval year: 2017.

#### Model 1: Change in HbA1c (primary) and body weight (key secondary) from baseline to end of treatment (Week 30 or 56) (primary (pre-specified))

- **Trial:** SUSTAIN 1-5 (trials 3623, 3626, 3624, 3625, 3627); also CVOT SUSTAIN 6 (3744) confirmatory secondaries
- **Endpoint/timepoint:** Change in HbA1c (primary) and body weight (key secondary) from baseline to end of treatment (Week 30 or 56)
- **Role:** primary (pre-specified)
- **Model family:** MMRM
- **Response:** Change from baseline
- **Fixed effects:** treatment, country, stratification factor (if applicable) as fixed factors and baseline value as covariate, 'all nested within visit' [StatR (Ref 4138507) p.8 verbatim: 'The model included treatment, country, stratification (if applicable) as fixed factors and baseline value as covariate, all nested within visit. An unstructured covariance matrix was assumed for measurements within the same subject.']
- **Random effects:** none stated
- **Covariance structure:** Unstructured [StatR p.8]
- **Covariance fallback:** Not stated
- **Denominator df:** Not stated
- **Estimation:** Not stated
- **Time coding:** categorical visits (all terms nested within visit)
- **Estimand / contrast:** LS-mean difference at end of treatment, on-treatment without rescue medication observation period (hypothetical-type)
- **Missing data / intercurrent events:** MAR; data after treatment discontinuation or rescue excluded (agreed at 2010 EOP2)
- **MNAR sensitivity:** Retrieved-dropout MI within arm followed by ANCOVA (FDA-preferred); additional: retrieved-dropout imputation with early/late (<12 wk) discontinuation factor; placebo-based MI for SUSTAIN 1 [StatR p.8, p.13, Table 14]
- **Software:** Not stated
- **Results:** Shown graphically (Figure 1); FDA: 'It appears that the on-treatment MMRM analysis overestimated the treatment effect of semaglutide.' [p.13]
- **FDA comments:** 'MMRM rarely estimates a relevant causal effect in the presence of missing data.' [Exec Summary]; 'some off-treatment measurements at scheduled visits were replaced with on-treatment measurements taken at premature treatment discontinuation visits. Considering these problems, both approaches are not acceptable.' [p.12]
- **Spec source:** StatR verbatim

#### Verbatim specification excerpts

##### Model 1: Change in HbA1c (primary) and body weight (key secondary) from baseline to end of treatment (Week 30 or 56) (primary (pre-specified))

> "The pre-specified primary analysis for continuous endpoints was an MMRM analysis using on-treatment data. It was based on all randomized and exposed patients using the on-treatment without rescue medication observation period. The model included treatment, country, stratification (if applicable) as fixed factors and baseline value as covariate, all nested within visit. An unstructured covariance matrix was assumed for measurements within the same subject. The applicant also performed an in-trial MMRM analysis. It used the same analysis model as the on-treatment MMRM, but included all data collected during trial regardless of treatment adherence or rescue status."
>
> — FDA Statistical Review, p. 105 (https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2017/209637Orig1s000StatR.pdf)

> "Following FDA’s advice at the pre-NDA meeting, the applicant performed retrieved dropout analysis for the HbA1c and body weight endpoints. Retrieved dropouts were defined as subjects who had their HbA1c value at the primary endpoint visit assessed after the on-treatment observation period (> 7 days after last dose). Within each treatment arm, multiple imputation was performed for missing data based on measurements from retrieved dropouts in the same treatment arm. An ANCOVA model was fit to the complete datasets, containing the same covariates as the primary analysis."
>
> — FDA Statistical Review, p. 105 (https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2017/209637Orig1s000StatR.pdf)

> "The pre-specified primary analysis was a mixed model for repeated measurements (MMRM) analysis using on-treatment data. MMRM rarely estimates a relevant causal effect in the presence of missing data. The applicant also performed multiple imputation based on data from retrieved dropouts followed by an analysis of covariance (ANCOVA) model (Section 3.2.2). The statistical reviewer thinks results from this analysis are more appropriate for labeling."
>
> — FDA Statistical Review (Executive Summary), p. 101 (https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2017/209637Orig1s000StatR.pdf)

> "The applicant’s pre-specified primary analysis was on-treatment MMRM. It only used on-treatment data before the onset of rescue therapy and assumed missing data were missing at random (MAR). The in-trial MMRM analysis also assumed missing data were MAR. In both analyses, some off-treatment measurements at scheduled visits were replaced with on-treatment measurements taken at premature treatment discontinuation visits. Considering these problems, both approaches are not acceptable."
>
> — FDA Statistical Review, p. 109 (https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2017/209637Orig1s000StatR.pdf)

> "The amount of missing data was moderate (5-10%) in the 5 key efficacy trials. The pre-specified primary analysis using on-treatment MMRM relies on the MAR assumption which is questionable. Following FDA’s advice at the pre-NDA meeting, the applicant performed retrieved dropout analysis for the HbA1c and body weight endpoints. We consider it a more appropriate way of handling missing data and based our conclusions on this analysis."
>
> — FDA Statistical Review, p. 117 (https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2017/209637Orig1s000StatR.pdf)

##### Model 2: Change in HbA1c / body weight to end of treatment, all in-trial data (sensitivity)

Model statement: see Model 1 first quote ("The applicant also performed an in-trial MMRM analysis. It used the same analysis model as the on-treatment MMRM [...]", p. 105).


> "1. Control arms were pooled in studies 3623, 3626, 3627 in the analyses. An MMRM model was fit to all in-trial observations including treatment, country as fixed factors, and baseline body weight as covariate. For trials 3625 and 3627, the model also included the stratification variable as a fixed factor."
>
> — FDA Statistical Review (Table 13 footnote), p. 119 (https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2017/209637Orig1s000StatR.pdf)

> "‡ Except for Study 3744, estimated using in-trial MMRM analysis including all data collected regardless of treatment discontinuation or initiation of rescue medication. The pre-specified primary analysis is an on-treatment MMRM analysis that is not recommended. The treatment effects from the in-trial MMRM analysis were smaller than those from the on-treatment MMRM analysis in all the key efficacy trials."
>
> — FDA Statistical Review, p. 125 (https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2017/209637Orig1s000StatR.pdf)

##### Model 3: Change in HbA1c, volume-matched control arms (sensitivity (FDA information request, Feb 2017))

> "1. To justify the assumption that the volume of placebo is not impactful, please compare each semaglutide dose to its matching placebo dose using in trial MMRM for the primary endpoint in the placebo-controlled and sitagliptin-controlled studies (3623, 3626, 3627) where the control arms were pooled in analyses."
>
> — FDA Statistical Review (Information Request), p. 127 (https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2017/209637Orig1s000StatR.pdf)

> "1. Volume matched control arms were used in the analyses. An MMRM model was fit to all in-trial observations including treatment, country as fixed factors, and baseline body weight as covariate. For trials 3625 and 3627, the model also included the stratification variable as a fixed factor."
>
> — FDA Statistical Review (Table 15 footnote), p. 120 (https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2017/209637Orig1s000StatR.pdf)

> "In the efficacy analyses, volume matching control groups were pooled for the placebo-controlled trials 3623 and 3627 and the sitagliptin-controlled trial 3626. The applicant later conducted additional analyses using volume matched control arms instead of a pooled control arm. The results were shown in Table 15 of Appendix. In trial 3623, the 1.0 mg placebo group showed a larger reduction of HbA1c from baseline compared to the 0.5 mg placebo group (-0.44 vs - [...] 0.06%). Correspondingly, the estimated treatment difference for each semaglutide dose versus its volume matched placebo group was affected. The relative effect of high and low doses of semaglutide appeared to be reversed. Since conclusions from this trial remained unchanged (both doses of semaglutide achieved superiority to placebo), we do not consider the pooling approach problematic."
>
> — FDA Statistical Review, pp. 110-111 (https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2017/209637Orig1s000StatR.pdf)

- **Role:** primary

- **Fixed effects:** baseline HbA1c and baseline eGFR covariates; P002 adds prior antihyperglycemic therapy status; P006 adds prior-sulfonylurea stratum [StatR p.14 verbatim: 'Covariates in the model, both for the primary and sensitivity analyses, included baseline HbA1c (%) and baseline estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR).']; treatment/time terms not itemized in review
- **Random effects:** none stated

- **Software:** J2R/tipping-point code from www.missingdata.org.uk; otherwise Not stated

- **FDA comments:** Oct 2014 IND advice: 'the missing data assumption for the proposed cLDA model may not allow for a reliable estimate'; 'The cLDA ... method likely does not appropriately address missing data as they both treat the behavior of missing data for those patients who are off-treatment to be the same as that of observed data for those patients who are on-treatment'; labeling: 'The cLDA primary analysis does not adequately address missing data'; RTB analysis recommended for label [StatR p.6-7, p.35]. Table footnote: 'this mixed model repeated measures method constrains baseline value to be equal between treatments.'
