### Pitolisant (Wakix) — NDA 211150

- Therapeutic area: Neurology / Psychiatry
- Sponsor: Bioprojet Pharma (US: Harmony Biosciences)
- Approval year: 2019

Overview: Correction to the README: the HARMONY I and I-bis primary analyses were not MMRM. They were single-timepoint ANCOVA-type linear mixed-effects models (LME) on final ESS with center (I-bis: re-allocated center clusters) as a random intercept, with mean-of-last-2-values imputation. FDA ran a true MMRM (AR(1)) with center random as an alternative analysis. HARMONY I-bis secondaries also used random-center models: Poisson for responders (a GLMM) and a 'linear fixed effect model' with random center for MWT/SART. HARMONY CTP (supportive cataplexy trial) used a non-linear mixed-effects model whose details are only in image-only tables.

#### Model 1: Final ESS total score at Week 8 (ESSF; mean of last 2 available values) (primary)

- **Trial:** HARMONY I (P07-03, NCT01067222)
- **Model family:** linear mixed model (random intercept for center) - ANCOVA form, single timepoint
- **Response:** Final ESS score (not change), LOCF-type imputation (mean of last 2 values) [StatR p.14, Table 11]
- **Fixed effects:** treatment, baseline ESS (ESSBL) [StatR p.14]
- **Random effects:** Center (random intercept) [StatR p.14]
- **Covariance:** N/A (single timepoint; center variance component)
- **Covariance fallback:** N/A
- **Denominator df:** Not stated
- **Estimation:** Not stated
- **Time coding:** N/A (single final value)
- **Estimand / contrast:** LS-mean difference in final ESS pitolisant vs placebo (superiority), then pitolisant vs modafinil NI margin 2; step-down at alpha 0.025
- **Missing data:** 'Estimation for missing values were made by carrying forward the arithmetic mean of the last 2 values. For patients who did not have any post-baseline values, the final value was assimilated with baseline.'
- **MNAR / other sensitivity:** None; PP-population sensitivity and ANCOVA without center supportive [StatR p.15]
- **Software:** Not stated
- **Results:** Placebo N=30 LS mean 15.48 (1.03); pitolisant N=31 12.39 (1.01); diff -3.10 (SE 1.30; 95% CI -5.73, -0.46), p=0.022. NI vs modafinil failed: diff 0.07 (-2.17, 2.32), p=0.95 [StatR Tables 11-12]
- **FDA comments:** FDA ran an alternative MMRM (see next model) to confirm; README describes this primary as 'MMRM' but StatR states 'analysis of covariance with linear mixed effect model' with center random [StatR p.14]
- **Spec source:** StatR verbatim

#### Model 2: Change from baseline in ESS at Week 8 (FDA reviewer alternative analysis (sensitivity))

- **Trial:** HARMONY I (P07-03, NCT01067222)
- **Model family:** MMRM with center random effect (hybrid: AR(1) R-matrix + random center intercept)
- **Response:** Change from baseline at each weekly visit, observed values (not LOCF) [StatR p.30]
- **Fixed effects:** baseline, treatment, visit, treatment-by-visit [StatR p.30]
- **Random effects:** Center [StatR p.30]
- **Covariance:** AR(1) [StatR p.30]
- **Covariance fallback:** Not stated
- **Denominator df:** Not stated
- **Estimation:** Not stated
- **Time coding:** Categorical weekly visits
- **Estimand / contrast:** LS-mean difference at Week 8 vs placebo and vs modafinil
- **Missing data:** Observed data, MAR (no LOCF) [StatR p.30]
- **MNAR / other sensitivity:** Hodges-Lehmann/permutation re-analysis (non-model)
- **Software:** Not stated
- **Results:** Week 8 N=25/26/28 (placebo/pitolisant/modafinil); LS mean -2.73 / -6.41 / -7.09; pitolisant - placebo -3.68 (SE 1.16; 95% CI -5.96, -1.39) p=0.002; modafinil - placebo -4.36 (-6.59, -2.12) p=0.0002; pitolisant - modafinil 0.68 (-1.56, 2.92) p=0.55 [StatR Table 14; MedR Table 12]
- **FDA comments:** 'as an alternative analysis this reviewer conducted a mixed model repeated measures (MMRM; with AR (1) variance covariance structure) to confirm if Applicant's primary efficacy analysis is consistent' [StatR p.30]
- **Spec source:** StatR verbatim

#### Model 3: Final ESS total score at Week 8 (primary)

- **Trial:** HARMONY I-bis (P09-15, NCT01638403)
- **Model family:** linear mixed model (random intercept for re-allocated center) - ANCOVA form, single timepoint
- **Response:** Final ESS (mean of last 2 available post-baseline values)
- **Fixed effects:** treatment, baseline ESS [StatR p.15-16]
- **Random effects:** Re-allocated center (small centers randomly re-allocated into clusters) as random intercept: 'thus hypothesis of center variability of the model intercept' [StatR Table 28 footnote]
- **Covariance:** N/A (single timepoint)
- **Covariance fallback:** N/A
- **Denominator df:** Not stated
- **Estimation:** Not stated
- **Time coding:** N/A
- **Estimand / contrast:** LS-mean difference vs placebo; NI vs modafinil margin 2
- **Missing data:** Mean of last 2 values carried forward
- **MNAR / other sensitivity:** None; PP and ANCOVA-without-center supportive
- **Software:** Not stated
- **Results:** Placebo N=32 LS mean 15.49 (1.32); pitolisant N=66 13.30 (1.19); diff -2.19 (SE 0.99; 95% CI -4.17, -0.22), p=0.03. Modafinil N=65 10.59 vs pitolisant 13.34: diff -2.75 (-4.48, -1.02) favoring modafinil; NI not achieved [StatR Tables 28-29]. Without center re-allocation: -1.94 (95% CI -4.05, 0.07), p=0.065 [MedR p.57]
- **FDA comments:** FDA verified the center re-allocation appendix was in the SAP issued Feb 13, 2013, a month before database lock, countering EMA's statement that pooling was not pre-planned; result not significant without re-allocation [MedR p.57]. Table footnote mislabels 'LME = mixed model repeated measures'
- **Spec source:** StatR verbatim (table footnote)

#### Model 4: ESS responder rate (ESSF <=10 or ESSF-ESSBL >=3) (secondary)

- **Missing data:** Mean of last 2 values carried forward
- **MNAR / other sensitivity:** None
- **Software:** Not stated
- **Results:** Responders 65.2% vs 34.4%; RR 2.14 (95% CI 1.35, 3.39), p=0.001; vs modafinil RR 0.87 (0.74, 1.02), p=0.086 [StatR p.44-45, Table 30]
- **FDA comments:** No multiplicity control for secondary endpoints; logistic regression consistent [StatR p.45]

The final visit scores were imputed using last observation carried forward (LOCF). The difference in ESS final scores between pitolisant and modafinil was assessed if there was a statistically significant difference between pitolisant and placebo groups."

> "Statistical Methodology for the Primary Efficacy Analysis: In the primary efficacy analysis, the Applicant used a linear mixed effect model to compare the differences between the final Epworth Sleepiness Scale results in the treatment groups. Statistical significance was defined as p < 0.05."
>
> — FDA Clinical (Medical) Review (HARMONY 1), p. 42 (https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2019/211150Orig1s000MedR.pdf)

The hypothesis testing involved a superiority (vs. placebo) and non-inferiority (vs. modafinil) test of pitolisant. The non-inferiority test was based on the non-inferiority margin of -2."

>

##### Model 7: Drug Liking VAS Emax and other PD endpoints (supportive (abuse-potential, non-efficacy))

> "Pharmacodynamic endpoints will be analyzed using a mixed-effect model for a crossover study. The model will include treatment, period, treatment sequence and first-order carryover effect as fixed effects, and subject nested within treatment sequence as a random effect. If the carryover effect is found to be non-significant at the alpha=0.25 level of significance, then the term will be dropped from the analysis model. The residuals from the mixed-effect model will be investigated for normality using the Shapiro-Wilk W-test. Parameters will be analyzed as having a normal distribution if the probability value of the test is ≥0.05 and paired t-tests will be used for comparisons. A 2.5% Type-I error with a P value less than 0.025 will be considered as statistically significant for all individual hypothesis tests. All statistical tests will be performed using one-tailed significance criteria. Multiple comparison adjustments will not be made."
>
> — FDA Statistical Review, CSS abuse-potential section (Study P16-02 SAP excerpt), p. 80 (https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2019/211150Orig1s000StatR.pdf)

> "Since the normality tests of the residuals from the mixed-effect model did not support normal distributions for above comparisons based on the Shapiro-Wilk W-test, this reviewer carried out pairwise t-tests for comparisons at a level of 0.025 (one-sided). A pairwise t-test is considered appropriate if the distribution is not too skewed."
>
> — FDA Statistical Review, CSS abuse-potential section, p. 88 (https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2019/211150Orig1s000StatR.pdf)

### Istradefylline (Nourianz) — NDA 022075

- Therapeutic area: Neurology / Psychiatry
- Sponsor: Kyowa Kirin, Inc.
- Approval year: 2019

Overview: Primary analysis was ANCOVA with LOCF and Williams' test. MMRM with compound symmetry was a pre-specified sensitivity analysis in both Japanese trials. The FDA reviewer added an unstructured-covariance MMRM. Results were similar.

#### Model 1: Change from baseline in daily OFF time at Week 12 (sensitivity (pre-specified))

- **Trial:** Study 6002-009 (NCT00955526)
- **Model family:** MMRM
- **Response:** Change from baseline in daily OFF time (hours) at each week [StatR Sec 3.2.1.2]
- **Fixed effects:** treatment group, pooled study site, week, treatment-by-week interaction; baseline as covariate [StatR Sec 3.2.1.2]
- **Random effects:** None (R-matrix only)
- **Covariance:** Compound symmetry (SAP-specified) [StatR Sec 3.2.1.2]; FDA additionally fitted unstructured

##### Model 1: Change from baseline in daily OFF time at Week 12 (sensitivity (pre-specified))

### Lumateperone (Caplyta) — NDA 209500

- Therapeutic area: Neurology / Psychiatry
- Sponsor: Intra-Cellular Therapies, Inc.
- Approval year: 2019

Overview: All three placebo-controlled trials (005, 301, 302) used MMRM with unstructured covariance on PANSS change. FDA's advice moved Study 005's primary analysis from ANCOVA-LOCF to MMRM. The MMRM/MAR primary model became contested in failed Study 302. In Study 302, CGI-S (key secondary) was presumably analyzed by MMRM, but the specification was not extracted.

#### Model 1: PANSS total change from baseline to Day 28 (primary)

- **Trial:** ITI-007-301 (NCT02282761)
- **Model family:** MMRM
- **Response:** PANSS change from baseline at each visit [MDR p.177]
- **Fixed effects:** study visit, baseline PANSS, baseline PANSS-by-visit, treatment (28 mg, 42 mg, placebo), treatment-by-visit [MDR p.177]
- **Random effects:** None (R-matrix only)
- **Covariance:** Unstructured
- **Covariance fallback:** Not stated
- **Denominator df:** Not stated
- **Estimation:** Not stated
- **Time coding:** Categorical study visit
- **Estimand / contrast:** LS-mean placebo-subtracted difference at Day 28; mixture-based gatekeeping (Dmitrienko et al. 2016) across 2 doses x 2 endpoints
- **Missing data:** MAR (MMRM) [MDR]
- **MNAR / other sensitivity:** Pre-specified pattern-mixture model with placebo-based multiple imputation (MNAR; dropouts on lumateperone follow placebo trajectory) [MDR p.177, SAP p.27]: 42 mg -3.9 (95% CI -7.4, -0.4) vs MMRM -4.2
- **Software:** Not stated
- **Results:** N=150 per arm; LS mean change 28 mg -12.9 (1.3), 42 mg -14.5 (1.3), placebo -10.3 (1.3); 42 mg diff -4.2 (95% CI -7.8, -0.6), nominal p=0.014, adjusted p=0.045; 28 mg -2.6 (-6.2, 1.1) NS [MDR Table 66]
- **FDA comments:** No model disagreement; pattern-mixture estimate close to MMRM
- **Spec source:** MDR verbatim (quoting SAP)

#### Model 2: CGI-S change from baseline to Day 28 (key secondary)

- **Trial:** ITI-007-301 (NCT02282761)
- **Model family:** MMRM
- **Response:** CGI-S change from baseline
- **Fixed effects:** Not separately stated (analyzed 'via MMRM')
- **Random effects:** None (R-matrix only)
- **Covariance:** Unstructured
- **Covariance fallback:** Not stated
- **Denominator df:** Not stated
- **Estimation:** Not stated
- **Time coding:** Categorical visit
- **Estimand / contrast:** LS-mean difference at Day 28
- **Missing data:** MAR
- **MNAR / other sensitivity:** Not stated
- **Software:** Not stated
- **Results:** 42 mg vs placebo -0.3 (95% CI -0.5, -0.1), unadjusted p=0.003, multiplicity-adjusted p=0.045 [MDR p.189]
- **FDA comments:** 'the CGI-S results were not replicated in other studies in this program' [MDR p.189]
- **Spec source:** MDR verbatim

#### Model 3: PANSS total change from baseline to Day 42 (primary)

- **Trial:** ITI-007-302 (NCT02469155)
- **Model family:** MMRM
- **Response:** Change from baseline at each pre-specified timepoint [MDR p.197]
- **Fixed effects:** study visit, baseline PANSS, baseline-by-visit, treatment (14 mg, 42 mg, risperidone 4 mg, placebo), treatment-by-visit [MDR p.197]
- **Random effects:** None (R-matrix only)
- **Covariance:** Unstructured
- **Covariance fallback:** Not stated
- **Denominator df:** Not stated
- **Estimation:** Not stated
- **Time coding:** Categorical study visit
- **Estimand / contrast:** LS-mean placebo-subtracted difference at Day 42; fixed-sequence 42 mg PANSS -> 42 mg CGI-S -> 14 mg PANSS -> 14 mg CGI-S
- **Missing data:** MAR (MMRM); discontinuation 37% risperidone vs 21% placebo vs 25% 42 mg
- **MNAR / other sensitivity:** Pre-specified placebo-based pattern-mixture MI; post hoc applicant MNAR analyses (non-responder imputation, MI with added shift akin to tipping point); FDA Wilcoxon rank-sum with worst-observed-value imputation (risperidone vs placebo p=0.4) [MDR p.207-209]
- **Software:** Not stated
- **Results:** N=174 per arm; LS mean change 14 mg -15.0, 42 mg -14.6, risperidone -20.5, placebo -15.1; diffs 14 mg 0.1 (-3.4, 3.5), 42 mg 0.5 (-2.9, 3.8) p=0.789, risperidone -5.4 (-8.9, -1.9) nominal p=0.003 [MDR Table 74]
- **FDA comments:** Applicant argued 'the primary efficacy analysis (i.e., MMRM with Missing at Random assumption) was not well-suited to account properly for the higher discontinuation rate in the risperidone arm'; FDA's Wilcoxon worst-value analysis 'aligns with the Applicant's assertion' that 302 was failed rather than negative [MDR p.208-209]

- **Response:** PANSS change from baseline

- **Random effects:** None (R-matrix only)

- **Spec source:** MDR verbatim

#### Verbatim specification excerpts

##### Model 1: PANSS total change from baseline to Day 28 (primary)

> "The treatment effect on the primary efficacy endpoint, change from baseline to Day 28 in PANSS total score, was evaluated using a MMRM model. The model includes the PANSS change from baseline as response variable and study visit, baseline PANSS total score, baseline PANSS total score-by-study visit interaction, treatment (lumateperone 28 mg, lumateperone 42 mg, placebo), and treatment-by-study visit interaction. An unstructured covariance matrix was used to model the correlation among repeated measures within subject."
>
> — FDA Multi-Disciplinary Review (Study 301), p. 178 (https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2019/209500Orig1s000MultidisciplineR.pdf)

> "A pattern-mixture model using a placebo-based multiple imputation method was pre-specified in the SAP to explore the impact of a different assumption regarding missing data. The primary analysis (MMRM) assumes Missing At Random (MAR). The placebo-based multiple imputation sensitivity analysis considered a Missing Not At Random (MNAR) mechanism for the missing data, where it was assumed that outcomes of subjects who discontinued early from the lumateperone arms would follow a trajectory similar to the placebo arm, taking into account observed values prior to discontinuation (Study 301 SAP page 27)."
>
> — FDA Multi-Disciplinary Review (Study 301), p. 178 (https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2019/209500Orig1s000MultidisciplineR.pdf)

> "A mixture-based gatekeeping procedure was pre-specified to adjust for multiplicity due to testing two doses and two efficacy endpoints. This method proposed by Dmitrienko et al is a valid approach for controlling the familywise error rate (Dmitrienko, Kordzakhia et al. 2016)."
>
> — FDA Multi-Disciplinary Review (Study 301), p. 178 (https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2019/209500Orig1s000MultidisciplineR.pdf)

> "The point estimate of the treatment difference and 95% confidence interval obtained from the pattern-mixture model (PPM) for the 42-mg lumateperone dose versus placebo are close to the estimates obtained from the MMRM primary analysis (PPM: -3.9 (-7.4, -0.4) versus MMRM: -4.2 (-7.8, -0.6)). The primary endpoint efficacy results appear robust to possible deviations from the Missing at Random assumption used for the primary analysis."
>
> — FDA Multi-Disciplinary Review (Study 301), p. 187 (https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2019/209500Orig1s000MultidisciplineR.pdf)

##### Model 2: CGI-S change from baseline to Day 28 (key secondary)

> "The point estimate of the difference in change from baseline in the CGI-S score at Day 28 (analyzed via MMRM) for the 42 mg lumateperone dose versus placebo is -0.3 (95% CI: -0.5, -0.1) with an unadjusted p-value of 0.003 (multiplicity adjusted p-value=0.045). Note, that the CGI-S results were not replicated in other studies in this program."
>
> — FDA Multi-Disciplinary Review (Study 301), p. 190 (https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2019/209500Orig1s000MultidisciplineR.pdf)

No further CGI-S model specification text found in: 209500Orig1s000MultidisciplineR.pdf.

##### Model 3: PANSS total change from baseline to Day 42 (primary)

> "The treatment effect on the primary efficacy endpoint, change from baseline to Day 42 in PANSS total score, was evaluated using an MMRM model. The model included the change from baseline at each pre-specified timepoint as the response variable and study visit, baseline PANSS total score, baseline PANSS total score-by-study visit interaction, treatment (lumateperone 14 mg, lumateperone 42 mg, risperidone 4 mg, and placebo) and treatment-by-study visit interaction. An unstructured covariance matrix was used to model the correlation among repeated measurements within subject."
>
> — FDA Multi-Disciplinary Review (Study 302), p. 198 (https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2019/209500Orig1s000MultidisciplineR.pdf)

> "A placebo-based multiple imputation sensitivity analysis assuming a Missing Not At Random (MNAR) missingness mechanism was pre-specified to evaluate the impact of deviations of the Missing At Random assumption in the primary analysis."
>
> — FDA Multi-Disciplinary Review (Study 302), p. 198 (https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2019/209500Orig1s000MultidisciplineR.pdf)

> "In response to the Division’s concerns about the primary efficacy results of Study 302 (i.e., lumateperone 42 mg arm did not separate from placebo, whereas the risperidone 4 mg arm did), the Applicant conducted numerous post-hoc sensitivity analyses. The Applicant made the case that the primary efficacy analysis (i.e., MMRM with Missing at Random assumption) was not well-suited to account properly for the higher discontinuation rate in the risperidone arm (37%) compared to the placebo arm (21%) or the 42 mg lumateperone arm (25%). The Applicant’s post-hoc sensitivity analyses were conducted under varying Missing Not At Random assumptions (e.g., a responder analysis treating all patients without a Day 42 assessment as non-responders and several variants of multiple imputation with a shift added (akin to tipping point analysis))."
>
> — FDA Multi-Disciplinary Review (Study 302), p. 209 (https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2019/209500Orig1s000MultidisciplineR.pdf)

> "This hypothesis could not be rejected (two-sided p-value=0.4). In other words, under the assumption that assigning the worst observed PANSS change score to the missing PANSS change scores at Day 42 is reasonable, one would not be able to reject the hypothesis that the PANSS change scores for the placebo and risperidone subjects are originating from the same distribution. This analysis aligns with the Applicant’s assertion about viewing Study 302 as “failed” study."
>
> — FDA Multi-Disciplinary Review (Study 302; FDA Wilcoxon sensitivity analysis), p. 209 (https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2019/209500Orig1s000MultidisciplineR.pdf)

##### Model 4: PANSS total change from baseline to Day 28 (primary (supportive trial))

> "The Applicant did incorporate advice provided by the agency into those documents (e.g., change of primary analysis from Analysis of Covariance using last observation carried forward (LOCF) to a mixed-effect model repeated measures (MMRM) approach). It would have been prudent to submit the SAP and IAP for agency review prior database lock, data analysis, and reporting of results."
>
> — FDA Multi-Disciplinary Review (Study 005), p. 157 (https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2019/209500Orig1s000MultidisciplineR.pdf)

> "The change from baseline to Day 28 in PANSS total score was pre-specified as a MMRM with terms for treatment, baseline score, time point (treated as categorical variable), as well as [...] interaction between treatment and time point. An unstructured covariance matrix was used to model the correlation among the repeated measures."
>
> — FDA Multi-Disciplinary Review (Study 005), pp. 157–158 (https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2019/209500Orig1s000MultidisciplineR.pdf)

> "The pre-specified sensitivity analyses (i.e., analysis of covariance with last observation carried forward on intent-to-treat (ITT) set and per-protocol set) to investigate the impact of the method of choice for handling missing data in the primary analysis are not informative because they rely on the stricter assumption of missing completely at random data, whereas the primary analysis method (MMRM) uses the less strict assumption of missing at random (MAR) data. Note that missing primary efficacy data was not an issue in Study 005."
>
> — FDA Multi-Disciplinary Review (Study 005), p. 159 (https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2019/209500Orig1s000MultidisciplineR.pdf)

> "The Applicant updated the primary analysis to the proposed repeated measures model but did not submit the SAP or the Interim Statistical Analysis Plan (ISAP) until the Clinical Study Report was submitted. Although both the SAP and ISAP were finalized prior to database lock, FDA had no opportunity to review them. The primary efficacy analysis did not account for the increase in sample size from 268 to 328 after the unblinded interim analysis."
>
> — FDA Multi-Disciplinary Review (Study 005 concerns), p. 259 (https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2019/209500Orig1s000MultidisciplineR.pdf)

### Lemborexant (Dayvigo) — NDA 212028

- Therapeutic area: Neurology / Psychiatry
- Sponsor: Eisai Inc.
- Approval year: 2019

Overview: Unusual design: MMRM is fitted to each of 30 datasets after MNAR pattern-mixture multiple imputation under complete-case missing values (CCMV), then combined with Rubin's rules. The MNAR imputation is part of the primary analysis. The SUNRISE-1 sample PROC MIXED code uses `type=UN group=treatment` (arm-specific unstructured covariance) and `ddfm=kr`. Discrepancy with the README: SUNRISE-1's fallback is UN -> AR(1); only SUNRISE-2 has UN -> Toeplitz -> AR(1). The sample MODEL statements omit the baseline covariate that the SAP text includes. The driving study (Study 106) used repeated-measures ANOVA with UN covariance.

#### Model 1: Change from baseline in log(LPS) at Days 29/30 (PSG) (primary)

- **Trial:** SUNRISE-1 / E2006-G000-304 (NCT02783729)
- **Model family:** MMRM (after MNAR pattern-mixture MI)
- **Response:** Change from baseline in log-transformed LPS [SAP1 p.22]
- **Fixed effects:** age group (55-64, >=65), region (North America, Europe), treatment, visit, treatment-by-visit; baseline log(LPS) covariate [SAP1 p.22] (note: sample MODEL statement omits the baseline term)
- **Random effects:** None (R-matrix only)
- **Covariance:** Unstructured [SAP1 p.22]; sample code: 'REPEAT visit/sub=subject type=UN group=treatment' (UN heterogeneous by treatment arm) [SAP1 p.38-39]
- **Covariance fallback:** AR(1) on non-convergence [SAP1 p.22] (no Toeplitz step in SUNRISE-1)
- **Denominator df:** Kenward-Roger (ddfm=kr in sample PROC MIXED code) [SAP1 p.38-39]
- **Estimation:** Not stated
- **Time coding:** Categorical visit (Days 1/2, Days 29/30)
- **Estimand / contrast:** Ratio of LS geometric means (active/placebo) at Days 29/30; sequential gatekeeping LEM10 -> LEM5 -> key secondaries
- **Missing data:** 'Before the implementation of the MMRM model, the missing values will be imputed using pattern-mixture model multiple imputation (MI) assuming... MNAR utilizing the complete case missing value pattern (CCMV)'; post-discontinuation retrieved data used [SAP1 p.22]
- **MNAR / other sensitivity:** MMRM assuming MAR without imputation; MI with CCMV-4; tipping-point MI with shifts; FDA: MMRM without imputation and J2R (jump-to-placebo) pattern-mixture [SAP1 p.23-24; MDR]
- **Software:** SAS 9.4 or later; PROC MI (MCMC monotone + MNAR modelobs=CCMV, 30 imputations, seed 2359), PROC MIXED, PROC MIANALYZE [SAP1 p.22, p.38-39, Section 8]
- **Results:** LSGM ratio to baseline: placebo 0.70 (0.62, 0.78); zolpidem 0.85; LEM5 0.54, ratio to placebo 0.77 (0.67, 0.89) p<0.001; LEM10 0.51, ratio 0.72 (0.63, 0.83) p<0.001 [MDR Table 50]
- **FDA comments:** FDA objected pre-NDA (June 14, 2018) to CCMV-based primary imputation and to TPA interpretability; FDA sensitivity analyses reproduced conclusions [MDR p.136-137]
- **Spec source:** SAP verbatim

#### Model 2: Change from baseline in SE, WASO (vs placebo) and WASO2H (vs zolpidem) at Days 29/30 (key secondary)

- **Trial:** SUNRISE-1 / E2006-G000-304 (NCT02783729)
- **Model family:** MMRM (after MNAR pattern-mixture MI)
- **Response:** Change from baseline (untransformed SE %, WASO min, WASO2H min per MDR tables)
- **Fixed effects:** age group, region, treatment, visit, treatment-by-visit; corresponding baseline as covariate [SAP1 p.24-25]
- **Random effects:** None (R-matrix only)
- **Covariance:** Unstructured [SAP1 p.22]; sample code: 'REPEAT visit/sub=subject type=UN group=treatment' (UN heterogeneous by treatment arm) [SAP1 p.38-39]
- **Covariance fallback:** AR(1) on non-convergence [SAP1 p.22] (no Toeplitz step in SUNRISE-1)
- **Denominator df:** Kenward-Roger (ddfm=kr in sample PROC MIXED code) [SAP1 p.38-39]
- **Estimation:** Not stated
- **Time coding:** Categorical visit (Days 1/2, Days 29/30)
- **Estimand / contrast:** LS-mean difference at Days 29/30 vs placebo (SE, WASO) or vs zolpidem (WASO2H)
- **Missing data:** MNAR pattern-mixture MI (CCMV) before MMRM
- **MNAR / other sensitivity:** MAR MMRM, CCMV-4, tipping point
- **Software:** SAS 9.4 or later; PROC MI (MCMC monotone + MNAR modelobs=CCMV, 30 imputations, seed 2359), PROC MIXED, PROC MIANALYZE [SAP1 p.22, p.38-39, Section 8]
- **Results:** SE: LEM5 7.1 (5.6, 8.5), LEM10 8.0 (6.6, 9.5) vs placebo; WASO: LEM5 -24.0 (-30.0, -18.0), LEM10 -25.3 (-31.4, -19.3); WASO2H vs zolpidem: LEM5 -6.6 (-11.2, -2.1) p=0.004, LEM10 -8.0 (-12.5, -3.5) p<0.001. ITT N placebo 208, zolpidem 263, LEM5 266, LEM10 269 [MDR Tables 51-53]
- **FDA comments:** All significant after MCP [MDR]
- **Spec source:** SAP verbatim + MDR tables

#### Model 3: Change from Study Baseline in log(sSOL) at Month 6 (sleep diary) (primary)

- **Trial:** SUNRISE-2 / E2006-G000-303 (NCT02952820)
- **Model family:** MMRM (after MNAR pattern-mixture MI)
- **Response:** Change from baseline in log-transformed sSOL [SAP2 p.25]
- **Fixed effects:** Study Baseline value, region (North America, Europe and New Zealand, Asia), age group (<65, >=65), treatment, time, treatment-by-time [SAP2 p.25]
- **Random effects:** None (R-matrix only)
- **Covariance:** Unstructured; sample code 'type=UN' (not grouped) [SAP2 p.25, Section 7]
- **Covariance fallback:** Toeplitz, then AR(1) [SAP2 p.25]
- **Denominator df:** Kenward-Roger (ddfm=kr in sample code) [SAP2 Section 7]
- **Estimation:** Not stated
- **Time coding:** Categorical (1st 7 nights, Months 1-6)
- **Estimand / contrast:** Ratio of LS geometric means active/placebo at Month 6
- **Missing data:** MNAR pattern-mixture MI using CCMV before MMRM; includes retrieved post-discontinuation data [SAP2 p.25]
- **MNAR / other sensitivity:** CCMV-7 MI; tipping point; MAR MMRM; FDA: MMRM without imputation and J2R [SAP2; MDR p.150]
- **Software:** SAS 9.4 or later; PROC MI (CCMV, 30 imputations, seed 2006), PROC MIXED, PROC MIANALYZE [SAP2]
- **Results:** ITT placebo 318, LEM5 316, LEM10 315; LSGM ratio to baseline 0.62 / 0.45 / 0.43; ratio to placebo LEM5 0.73 (0.64, 0.84), LEM10 0.70 (0.61, 0.81), both p<0.001 [MDR Table 37]. FDA MAR MMRM: 0.73 (0.63, 0.85), 0.70 (0.61, 0.82); FDA J2R: 0.76 (0.66, 0.87), 0.74 (0.64, 0.86) [MDR Tables 38-39]
- **FDA comments:** 'At the pre-NDA meeting held on June 14, 2018, the Agency raised concerns about the proposed primary analysis method which was based on missing data imputation using a complete case missing value (CCMC) assumption... concerns on the interpretability of Eisai's proposed tipping point analysis' [MDR p.136-137]
- **Spec source:** SAP verbatim

#### Model 4: Change from baseline in sSE and sWASO at Month 6 (key secondary)

- **Trial:** SUNRISE-2 / E2006-G000-303 (NCT02952820)
- **Model family:** MMRM (after MNAR pattern-mixture MI)
- **Response:** Change from baseline (untransformed per MDR tables)
- **Fixed effects:** baseline, region, age group, treatment, time, treatment-by-time [SAP2 p.28-29]
- **Random effects:** None (R-matrix only)
- **Covariance:** Unstructured; sample code 'type=UN' (not grouped) [SAP2 p.25, Section 7]
- **Covariance fallback:** Toeplitz, then AR(1) [SAP2 p.25]
- **Denominator df:** Kenward-Roger (ddfm=kr in sample code) [SAP2 Section 7]
- **Estimation:** Not stated
- **Time coding:** Categorical (1st 7 nights, Months 1-6)
- **Estimand / contrast:** LS-mean difference at Month 6
- **Missing data:** MNAR CCMV MI before MMRM
- **MNAR / other sensitivity:** CCMV-7, tipping point, MAR MMRM; FDA J2R
- **Software:** SAS 9.4 or later; PROC MI (CCMV, 30 imputations, seed 2006), PROC MIXED, PROC MIANALYZE [SAP2]
- **Results:** sSE: LEM5 4.5 (2.2, 6.9), LEM10 4.7 (2.4, 7.0), p<0.001; sWASO: LEM5 -17.5 (-27.3, -7.6) p<0.001, LEM10 -12.7 (-22.4, -3.0) p=0.011 [MDR Tables 40-41]; FDA J2R: sSE 4.2/3.8, sWASO -15.3/-11.7 min, all p<0.02 [MDR Sec 8.1.1.8]
- **FDA comments:** FDA J2R sensitivity yields same conclusions
- **Spec source:** SAP verbatim + MDR tables

#### Model 5: SDLP (standard deviation of lateral position) (supportive (safety/PD, non-efficacy))

- **Trial:** Study 106 (driving performance, incomplete-block crossover)
- **Model family:** repeated-measures ANOVA (MMRM-type, crossover)
- **Response:** SDLP
- **Fixed effects:** treatment, time, period, sequence, age group, treatment-by-time [MDR CSS review of Study 106]
- **Random effects:** None (R-matrix only)
- **Covariance:** Unstructured (repeated effect for time with subject within period) [MDR]
- **Covariance fallback:** Not stated
- **Denominator df:** Not stated
- **Estimation:** Not stated
- **Time coding:** Categorical time
- **Estimand / contrast:** LS-mean difference each lemborexant dose vs placebo
- **Missing data:** Not stated
- **MNAR / other sensitivity:** None
- **Software:** Not stated
- **Results:** 95% CIs of SDLP change below 2.4 cm for 2.5/5/10 mg; 2/32 subjects >4.4 cm at 10 mg [MDR p.112]
- **FDA comments:** 'Reporting p-value from the primary analysis is misleading' (symmetry/non-inferiority framing) [MDR CSS review]
- **Spec source:** MDR verbatim

#### Verbatim specification excerpts

##### Model 1: Change from baseline in log(LPS) at Days 29/30 (PSG) (primary)

> "The change from baseline of LPS on Days 1/2 and Days 29/30, will be analyzed using the mixed effect model repeated measurement analysis (MMRM) with factors of age group (55 to 64, and ≥ 65 years old), region (North America and Europe), treatment, visit (Days 1/2 and Days 29/30), and treatment-by-visit interaction as fixed effect, and baseline LPS as a covariate based on FAS. Since LPS is known to be non-normally distributed, a log-transformation will be used in the analysis. The unstructured covariance matrix (UN) will be used in the analysis. In the case of non-convergence of UN, the autoregressive [AR(1)] covariance matrix will be used in the model. Before the implementation of the MMRM model, the missing values will be imputed using pattern-mixture model multiple imputation (MI) assuming the missing values are missing not at random (MNAR) utilizing the complete case missing value pattern (CCMV - subjects who completed primary efficacy assessments without missing values). The missing values for a given visit will be imputed using all available values including the retrieved measurement from the post-discontinuation data."
>
> — SUNRISE-1 (E2006-G000-304) SAP Final V3.0 §3.4.1, p. 22 (https://cdn.clinicaltrials.gov/large-docs/29/NCT02783729/SAP_001.pdf)

> "Step 1 (imputing missing data): Thirty multiple imputed complete datasets were to be constructed using the imputation regression model of age, sex, race (white, black, and other), and region (North America, and Europe), baseline BMI, baseline log(LPS), baseline ISI, baseline sSOL, and individual log(LPS) assessments on Days 1, 2 , 29, and 30, with a predefined arbitrary seed number (seed=2359). SAS PROC MI will be used to implement the imputation procedure using all available values. The dataset will be converted into monotone missing pattern by imputing arbitrary missing data as the first step. The monotone data will then be imputed with monotone regression method and MNAR. The sample SAS statement can be found in Section 7."
>
> — SUNRISE-1 SAP V3.0 §3.4.1 (Multiple Imputation), p. 23 (https://cdn.clinicaltrials.gov/large-docs/29/NCT02783729/SAP_001.pdf)

> "Step 2 (performing MMRM using each imputed dataset): The MMRM model with factors of age group (55 to 64, and ≥ 65 years old), region (North America, and Europe), treatment, visit (Days 1/2, and Days 29/30), and treatment-by-visit interaction as fixed effect, and the baseline log(LPS) as a covariate will be applied to each imputed dataset. SAS PROC MIXED will be used for the MMRM analysis. The sample SAS statement can be found in Section 7."
>
> — SUNRISE-1 SAP V3.0 §3.4.1, p. 23 (https://cdn.clinicaltrials.gov/large-docs/29/NCT02783729/SAP_001.pdf)

> "Step 3 (combine results): Resulting treatment effect parameter estimators and standard errors from each of 30 multiple imputed datasets from Step 2 will be combined using SAS PROC MIANALYZE to obtain the pooled treatment effect and variance parameter estimators according to Rubin’s rules (Rubin DB, 1987)."
>
> — SUNRISE-1 SAP V3.0 §3.4.1, p. 23 (https://cdn.clinicaltrials.gov/large-docs/29/NCT02783729/SAP_001.pdf)

> "MMRM analysis assuming MAR: The same primary endpoint analysis described above will be analyzed using MMRM assuming the missing values are missing at random (MAR; MMRM analysis without missing value imputation). [...] MI Imputation assuming MNAR utilizing CCMV-4: The same MMRM method used in the primary analysis will be applied utilizing CCMV-4 (ie, up to 4 monotone missing patterns will be used for missing value imputation as follows): [...] Tipping point analysis: A range of shifts will be used in the multiple imputation of missing data assuming MNAR to identify the specific shift and treatment effect that will tip the results from statistically significant to non-significant."
>
> — SUNRISE-1 SAP V3.0 §3.4.1 (sensitivity analyses), p. 24 (https://cdn.clinicaltrials.gov/large-docs/29/NCT02783729/SAP_001.pdf)

```sas
PROC MI data=<dataset> nimpute=30 seed=2359 out=<dataset1>;
 VAR age BMI baseline… visit1-visit4;
 MCMC chain=multiple nbiter=500 niter=300 impute=monotone;
 BY treatment;
RUN;

IMPUTE MISSING VALUES:

PROC MI data=<dataset1> nimpute=1 seed=2359 out=<dataset2>;
 CLASS treatment sex race region;
 MONOTONE regression ( /details);
 MNAR model (visit1-visit4/ modelobs=CCMV);
 VAR treatment age sex race region BMI baseline….;
 BY _imputation_;
RUN;

PERFORMING MMRM:

PROC MIXED data=<dataset2>;
 CLASS subject treatment agegrp visit;
 MODEL value=treatment agegrp region visit visit*treatment / ddfm=kr;
 REPEAT visit/sub=subject type=UN group=treatment;
 LSMEANS visit*treatment;
 ESTIMATE ‘5mg – ZOL Days 1_2’ treatment 0 -1 1 0 visit*treatment       0 0 -1 0 1 0 0 0/CL;
 ESTIMATE ‘10mg – ZOL Days 1_2’ treatment 0 -1 0 1 visit*treatment      0 0 -1 0 0 0 1 0/CL;
 ESTIMATE ‘5mg – ZOL Days 29_30’ treatment 0 -1 1 0 visit*treatment     0 0 0 -1 0 1 0 0/CL;
 ESTIMATE ‘10mg – ZOL Days 29_30’ treatment 0 -1 0 1 visit*treatment    0 0 0 -1 0 0 0 1/CL;
 BY _imputation_;
 ODS output estimates=<dataset3>;
RUN;

COMBINE RESULTS:

PROC MIANALYZE data=<dataset3>;
 MODELEFFECTS estimate;
 STDERR stderr;
RUN;
```

— SUNRISE-1 SAP V3.0 §7 (Programming Specifications), pp. 38–39 (https://cdn.clinicaltrials.gov/large-docs/29/NCT02783729/SAP_001.pdf) (page header/footer lines between pp. 38 and 39 omitted; the "IMPUTE MISSING VALUES:", "PERFORMING MMRM:", "COMBINE RESULTS:" captions are SAP text between code blocks)

> "The change from baseline of log(LPS), SE, WASO2H, and WASO on Days 1/2 and Days 29/30 was analyzed using the mixed effect model repeated measurement analysis (MMRM) with factors of age group (55 to 64, and ≥ 65 years old), region (North America and Europe), treatment, visit (Days 1/2 and Days 29/30), and treatment-by-visit interaction as fixed effect, and baseline as a covariate based on FAS. Because the Applicant considered LPS to be non-normally distributed and the Agency had no evidence to counter that assumption, a log-transformation would be used in the primary analysis. The distribution of the LPS would be explored. In the case of log transformation, statistical comparisons were conducted using the least squares geometric means (LSGM). The unstructured covariance matrix (UN) was used in the analysis. In the case of non-convergence of UN, the autoregressive [AR(1)] covariance matrix were used in the model. Before the implementation of the MMRM model, the missing values were imputed using pattern-mixture model multiple imputation assuming the missing values are missing not at random utilizing the complete case missing value pattern (CCMV - subjects who completed primary efficacy assessments without missing values)."

> "The statistical plan was finalized before the data were unblinded. At the pre-NDA meeting held on June 14, 2018, the Agency raised concerns about the proposed primary analysis method which was based on missing data imputation using a complete case missing value (CCMC) assumption. The Agency also raised concerns on the interpretability of Eisai’s proposed tipping point analysis (TPA). The Applicant agreed to amended statistical analysis plan with the details of the revised TPA."
>
> — FDA Multi-Disciplinary Review (Study 303), p. 138 (https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2019/212028Orig1s000MultidisciplineR.pdf)

> "The change from baseline of log(sSOL), SE and sWASO, which were measured at the first 7 nights, Month 1, Month 2, Month 3, Month 4, Month 5 and Month 6, were analyzed using the mixed effect model repeated measurement (MMRM) analysis on the FAS. The model was adjusted for the corresponding Study Baseline value, region (North America, Europe and New Zealand, Asia), age group (<65 years old, ≥65 years old), treatment, time (first 7 nights, Month 1, Month 2, Month 3, Month 4, Month 5 and Month 6) and the interaction of treatment by time. Since the Applicant considered sSOL to be non-normally distributed and the Agency had no evidence to against the assumption, a log-transformation was used in the primary analysis. The distribution of the sSOL was explored. The unstructured covariance matrix (UN) was used in the analysis. In the case of nonconvergence of UN, the Toeplitz covariance matrix (TOEP) would be used. In the case of nonconvergence with TOEP, the autoregressive covariance matrix [AR (1)] would be used in the model."
>
> — FDA Multi-Disciplinary Review (Study 303), p. 138 (https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2019/212028Orig1s000MultidisciplineR.pdf)

> "Before the NDA submission, FDA had concerns about the missing data imputation for the primary analysis. The missing values were imputed using a pattern mixture model utilizing multiple imputation assuming the missing values are missing not at random (MNAR) utilizing the complete case missing value pattern (CCMV - subjects who completed all primary efficacy assessments without missing values). To assess the robustness of the primary analysis results, the FDA statistical reviewer performed two sensitivity analyses: MMRM analysis without missing data imputation and pattern mixture imputation based on jump to placebo. MMRM analysis without missing data imputation assumes that the missing data mechanism is missing at random (MAR). The results from the MMRM analysis without imputation (Table 38) are very similar to the primary analysis results. The other sensitivity analysis that the FDA reviewer performed is pattern mixture imputation based on jump to placebo. This method assumes that the missing data mechanism is missing not at random (MNAR). An imputation model for the missing observations in the treatment group is constructed not from the observed data in the treatment group but rather from the observed data in the placebo group. The results (Table 39) are still very similar to the primary analysis results. The Applicant also performed several sensitivity analyses. The MMRM analysis with multiple imputation assuming CCMV-7 yields very similar results."
>
> — FDA Multi-Disciplinary Review (Study 303), p. 150 (https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2019/212028Orig1s000MultidisciplineR.pdf)

### Eptinezumab-jjmr (Vyepti) — BLA 761119

- Therapeutic area: Neurology / Psychiatry
- Sponsor: Lundbeck Seattle BioPharmaceuticals (originator Alder BioPharmaceuticals)
- Approval year: 2020

Overview: The README frames this entry as single-timepoint ANCOVA. The primary ANCOVA was fitted with SAS PROC MIXED, but it has no random or repeated effect, so it is not a mixed model. The SAPs do contain MMRM-type models: PROMISE-2's key secondary 'reduction in migraine prevalence Weeks 1-4' (UN, Kenward-Roger), PROMISE-2's repeated-measures sensitivity analysis for the primary endpoint, and PROMISE-1's Weeks 1-24 repeated-measures analysis. So this is not a false positive.

#### Model 1: Reduction in daily migraine prevalence from baseline to Week 4 (Weeks 1, 2, 3, 4) (key secondary)

- **Trial:** PROMISE-2 / ALD403-CLIN-011 (NCT02974153), chronic migraine
- **Model family:** MMRM
- **Response:** Subject-level change in migraine rate (daily prevalence) for Weeks 1-4 [SAP2 p.23-24]
- **Fixed effects:** treatment group, week, baseline value of outcome, treatment-by-week [SAP2 p.24]
- **Random effects:** None (R-matrix only)
- **Covariance:** Unstructured [SAP2 p.24]
- **Covariance fallback:** Not stated
- **Denominator df:** Kenward-Roger [SAP2 p.24]
- **Estimation:** Not stated
- **Time coding:** Categorical week (Weeks 1-4)
- **Estimand / contrast:** Difference in change in average daily migraine prevalence over Weeks 1-4; Holm within key-secondary block
- **Missing data:** eDiary normalization/blending rules (Missing Data Rules 1-2) [SAP2]
- **MNAR / other sensitivity:** None
- **Software:** SAS PROC MIXED [SAP]
- **Results:** 300 mg -11.0 (95% CI -14.22, -7.77); 100 mg -8.26 (-11.48, -5.05); both p<0.0001 vs placebo [StatR p.25-26]
- **FDA comments:** Significant per decision rule; no model-specific comment. SAP cites 'repeated-measures approach (Mallinckrodt and Lipkovich, 2016)' [SAP2 p.23]
- **Spec source:** SAP verbatim

#### Model 2: Change from baseline in monthly migraine days, Weeks 1-4, 5-8, 9-12 (and all six 4-week intervals) (sensitivity)

- **Trial:** PROMISE-2 / ALD403-CLIN-011 (NCT02974153)
- **Model family:** MMRM
- **Response:** Change from baseline in migraine days per 4-week interval, without Missing Data Rule 2 (intervals with <21 diary days excluded) [SAP2 p.27, Sec 2.7.3]
- **Fixed effects:** treatment group, timepoint, baseline, treatment-by-timepoint [SAP2 p.27, Sec 2.7.3]
- **Random effects:** None (R-matrix only)
- **Covariance:** Unstructured [SAP2 p.27, Sec 2.7.3]
- **Covariance fallback:** Not stated
- **Denominator df:** Kenward-Roger [SAP2 p.27, Sec 2.7.3]
- **Estimation:** Not stated
- **Time coding:** Categorical 4-week intervals
- **Estimand / contrast:** Overall Weeks 1-12 treatment difference, CI, p-value [SAP2 Sec 3.4.1]
- **Missing data:** Observed intervals only (MAR)
- **MNAR / other sensitivity:** Separate ANCOVA with baseline-substitution for AE/burden/LOE withdrawals
- **Software:** SAS PROC MIXED [SAP]
- **Results:** Not reported in FDA StatR (only ANCOVA-based sensitivity results shown in Table 3-13)
- **FDA comments:** StatR repeats SAP description; reports sensitivity support for 300/100 mg without MMRM numbers [StatR Sec 3.2.2, Table 3-13]
- **Spec source:** SAP verbatim

#### Model 3: Change from baseline in migraine days over six 4-week intervals (Weeks 1-24); also Weeks 1-12 subset (supportive/sensitivity)

- **Trial:** PROMISE-1 / ALD403-CLIN-006 (NCT02559895), episodic migraine
- **Model family:** repeated-measures model (MMRM without treatment-by-time interaction as specified)
- **Response:** Change from baseline in migraine days per 4-week interval [SAP1 p.29]
- **Fixed effects:** treatment group, timepoint (Weeks 1-4, ..., 21-24), baseline migraine days (continuous) [SAP1 p.29]; no treatment-by-timepoint term listed
- **Random effects:** None (R-matrix only)
- **Covariance:** Unstructured; 'If the model fails to converge, an alternative covariance structure will be specified' [SAP1 p.29]
- **Covariance fallback:** Unspecified alternative structure [SAP1 p.29]
- **Denominator df:** Not stated
- **Estimation:** Not stated
- **Time coding:** Categorical [SAP1 p.29]
- **Estimand / contrast:** Treatment difference per timepoint; overall Weeks 1-12 difference for diary-complete subset (Missing Data Rule 1)
- **Missing data:** Missing Data Rule 1 normalization; subset with >=21 diary days
- **MNAR / other sensitivity:** None
- **Software:** SAS PROC MIXED [SAP]
- **Results:** Not reported in FDA StatR
- **FDA comments:** Not stated
- **Spec source:** SAP verbatim

#### Verbatim specification excerpts

##### Model 1: Reduction in daily migraine prevalence from baseline to Week 4 (Weeks 1, 2, 3, 4) (key secondary)

> "The reduction in migraine prevalence from baseline to Week 4 endpoint will be the difference in daily prevalence rates between Week 1 and baseline, Week 2 and baseline, etc. The treatment effect will be tested using a repeated-measures approach (Mallinckrodt and Lipkovich, 2016),5 [...] using the subject level change in migraine rate (see Section 2.2.2) for Weeks 1, 2, 3 and 4 as the outcome variable. The model will specify an unstructured variance/covariance matrix and include the treatment group, week, baseline value of the outcome variable and with treatment group-by-week interaction. The Kenward-Roger approximation will be used to estimate the degrees of freedom."
>
> — PROMISE-2 (ALD403-CLIN-011) SAP v1.0, pp. 24–25 (https://cdn.clinicaltrials.gov/large-docs/53/NCT02974153/SAP_001.pdf)

> "Reduction in Migraine Prevalence from Baseline to Week 4: The treatment effect was tested using a repeated-measures approach using the subject level change in migraine rate for Weeks 1, 2, 3 and 4 as the outcome variable. The model specified an unstructured variance/covariance matrix and included the treatment group, week, baseline value of the outcome variable and with treatment group-by-week interaction."
>
> — FDA Statistical Review (PROMISE-2), p. 19 (https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2020/761119Orig1s000StatR.pdf)

##### Model 2: Change from baseline in monthly migraine days, Weeks 1-4, 5-8, 9-12 (and all six 4-week intervals) (sensitivity)

> "2. The primary endpoint will be analyzed using repeated measures where the individual time periods (Weeks 1-4, 5-8 and 9-12) are included in the model and Missing Date Rule 2 is not used. Hence, subject who do not complete the diary for more than 7 days out of 28 are not included for that 4 week period. The model will specify an unstructured variance/covariance matrix and include the treatment group, timepoint, baseline, and treatment group-by-timepoint interaction. The Kenward-Roger approximation will be used to estimate the degrees of freedom."
>
> — PROMISE-2 SAP v1.0 §2.7.3, p. 28 (https://cdn.clinicaltrials.gov/large-docs/53/NCT02974153/SAP_001.pdf)

> "Finally, a repeated measures model will be run that includes all 6 four week intervals and both missing data rules outlined in Section 2.7.2. This model will be identical in structure to the model specified for the missing data sensitivity analysis outlined above but will look at how the primary analysis, based upon the ANCOVA model, compares to a repeated measures analysis."
>
> — PROMISE-2 SAP v1.0 §2.7.3, p. 28 (https://cdn.clinicaltrials.gov/large-docs/53/NCT02974153/SAP_001.pdf)

> "For the repeated measures the estimated treatment difference, for each time point, and associated confidence interval will be estimated using SAS procedure, Proc Mixed. The overall Week 1-12 estimated treatment difference, associated confidence interval and p-value will be reported."
>
> — PROMISE-2 SAP v1.0 §3.4.1, p. 31 (https://cdn.clinicaltrials.gov/large-docs/53/NCT02974153/SAP_001.pdf)

> "The primary endpoint was analyzed using repeated measures where the individual time periods (Weeks 1-4, 5-8, and 9-12) were included in the model and Missing Date Rule 2 (eDiary completed for fewer than 21 days) was not used; hence, subjects who did not complete the diary for more than 7 days out of 28 were not included for that 4-week period. The model specified an unstructured variance/covariance matrix and included the treatment group, timepoint, baseline, and treatment group-by-timepoint interaction."
>
> — FDA Statistical Review (PROMISE-2 sensitivity analyses), p. 9 (https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2020/761119Orig1s000StatR.pdf)

##### Model 3: Change from baseline in migraine days over six 4-week intervals (Weeks 1-24); also Weeks 1-12 subset (supportive/sensitivity)

> "The change from baseline in migraine days for the six, 4 week intervals from Weeks 1 to 24 will also be analyzed using repeated measures. The model will include treatment group, timepoint (Weeks 1-4, 5-8 9-12, 13-16, 17-20, 21-24), and baseline migraine days as fixed factors. Estimated treatment difference, for each timepoint, and associated confidence interval will be estimated using SAS procedure, Proc Mixed. The unstructured (UN) covariance structure will be specified. If the model fails to converge, an alternative covariance structure will be specified. The timepoint variable will be categorical and baseline migraine days will be continuous. The repeated measures analysis will be repeated for weeks 1-12 using the same subjects and a subset where only subjects/four week intervals where the eDiary was completed a minimum of 21 days and applying Missing Data Rule 1 described in Section 2.2.2. Only the overall week 1-12 estimated treatment difference, associated confidence interval and p-value will be reported for this analysis."

### Opicapone (Ongentys) — NDA 212489

- Therapeutic area: Neurology / Psychiatry
- Sponsor: Neurocrine Biosciences (trials run by BIAL - Portela & Ca, S.A.)
- Approval year: 2020

Overview: Primary analysis was ANCOVA with last-available-value imputation. MMRM on observed cases was the sponsor's main missing-data sensitivity analysis in both BIPARK trials. Covariance structure and df method are not stated in the StatR. No protocol or SAP is posted.

#### Model 1: Change from baseline in absolute OFF-time (min) at end of double-blind period (sensitivity)

- **Trial:** BIPARK-I / Study 301 (NCT01568073)
- **Model family:** MMRM
- **Response:** Change from baseline in absolute OFF-time at each post-baseline visit [StatR p.8]
- **Fixed effects:** Not stated in StatR for Study 301 (primary ANCOVA: treatment, region, baseline OFF-time)
- **Random effects:** Not stated (classic MMRM presumed)
- **Covariance:** Not stated
- **Covariance fallback:** Not stated
- **Denominator df:** Not stated
- **Estimation:** Not stated
- **Time coding:** Categorical visit (LS means by visit) [StatR p.8]
- **Estimand / contrast:** LS-mean difference OPC 50 mg vs placebo at endpoint (superiority only)
- **Missing data:** Observed cases (MAR) vs primary 'last available post-baseline value' imputation [StatR p.8; Sec 3.2.4.1.1]
- **MNAR / other sensitivity:** FDA: arm-swap mean-imputation scenarios A and B (ANCOVA) [StatR Sec 3.2.4.1.1]
- **Software:** Not stated
- **Results:** MMRM FAS observed case -54.9 (95% CI -91.3, -18.5) p=0.003; PPS -52.1 (-89.0, -15.3) p=0.006; vs primary ANCOVA-LOCF -60.8 [StatR Table 6]
- **FDA comments:** Reviewer replicated MMRM; recommends calling LOCF 'last available value'; NI vs entacapone set aside [StatR p.8; Sec 3.2.4.1.1]
- **Spec source:** StatR summary

#### Model 2: Change from baseline in absolute OFF-time (min) at end of double-blind period (sensitivity)

- **Trial:** BIPARK-II / Study 302 (NCT01227655)
- **Model family:** MMRM
- **Response:** Change from baseline in OFF-time, observed cases [StatR p.17-18]
- **Fixed effects:** treatment, time, pooled country, treatment-by-visit; baseline OFF-time covariate [StatR p.17]
- **Random effects:** Not stated (classic MMRM presumed)
- **Covariance:** Not stated
- **Covariance fallback:** Not stated
- **Denominator df:** Not stated
- **Estimation:** Not stated
- **Time coding:** Categorical visit
- **Estimand / contrast:** LS-mean difference OPC 50 mg vs placebo
- **Missing data:** Observed cases, MAR; 50 mg dropout 16.9%, mostly AEs [StatR p.20]
- **MNAR / other sensitivity:** MI-based ANCOVA sensitivity; FDA additional analyses because missingness 'may not occur randomly' [StatR p.20]
- **Software:** Not stated
- **Results:** Sponsor MMRM OC -58.6 (95% CI -97.1, -20.0) p=0.003; FDA -58.5 (-97.2, -19.8) p=0.0031; adjusted to 16-h waking day -58.4 (-95.4, -21.4) p=0.0021 [StatR Table 14]
- **FDA comments:** 'the missing rate in OPC 50mg group is 16.9%... the primary reason for drop-out was adverse event which indicates the missing for each group may not occur randomly. Hence, the reviewer performed further sensitivity analyses' [StatR p.20]
- **Spec source:** StatR verbatim

#### Verbatim specification excerpts

##### Model 1: Change from baseline in absolute OFF-time (min) at end of double-blind period (sensitivity)

> "If the primary variable was missing at endpoint, it was replaced by the last available post-baseline observation until endpoint. Sensitivity analyses were performed on the primary endpoint using a mixed model for repeated measurement (MMRM), modeling the change from baseline in absolute OFF-time at each post-baseline visit was used to estimate and compare the least square (LS) means by visit to account for missing data and early discontinuations in both the FAS and the PP set."
>
> — FDA Statistical Review (Study 301), p. 9 (https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2020/212489Orig1s000StatR.pdf)

> "The reviewer recommends calling the last available value approach throughout the report instead of last observation carried forward (LOCF)."
>
> — FDA Statistical Review (Study 301, Reviewer’s Comments), p. 10 (https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2020/212489Orig1s000StatR.pdf)

> "Sensitivity analysis was performed on the LOCF approach in both FAS and PPS population. In addition, a mixed model repeated measures [MMRM] analysis was provided to check the impact of missing values only for comparison between OPC 50mg and placebo."
>
> — FDA Statistical Review §3.2.4.1.1 (Study 301), p. 15 (https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2020/212489Orig1s000StatR.pdf)

> "The reviewer was able to replicate sensitivity analysis results in Table 6. In addition to the repetition of MMRM analysis, the reviewer performed further sensitivity analyses with two different scenarios of missing pattern (see Table 7). These sensitivity analyses only focused on comparisons between OPC 50mg vs. placebo. Scenario A is to replace a missing endpoint in placebo group with the mean endpoint value of OPC 50mg group, and to replace a missing endpoint in OPC 50mg group with the mean endpoint of placebo group. Scenario B is to replace a missing change at the endpoint from baseline in the placebo group with the mean change of OPC 50mg group at the endpoint, and a missing change in OPC 50mg group with the mean change of placebo group at the endpoint. Results are summarized in Table 7. Table 6 and Table 7 show the minor impact of missing values in this study. In the superiority test, MMRM and two different scenarios yielded similar treatment effects to the primary efficacy results and maintained a statistical significance in both FAS and PPS population."
>
> — FDA Statistical Review §3.2.4.1.1 (Study 301), p. 15 (https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2020/212489Orig1s000StatR.pdf)

No covariance-structure or fixed-effects text for the Study 301 MMRM found in: 212489Orig1s000StatR.pdf.

##### Model 2: Change from baseline in absolute OFF-time (min) at end of double-blind period (sensitivity)

> "Three different sensitivity analyses were performed on the primary efficacy variable to account for missing data and the impact of early discontinuations. The first sensitivity analysis used MMRM with treatment, time, pooled country and treatment by visit interaction as fixed effects and baseline OFF-time as a covariate. The second was to test the robustness of the results under the assumption of missing at random (MAR) that is made by the MMRM analysis. The last one was a repeat of the primary analysis but included awake time at the last post-baseline visit as a covariate."
>
> — FDA Statistical Review (Study 302), p. 18 (https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2020/212489Orig1s000StatR.pdf)

> "The overall observed missing/drop-out rate was 11.9%. Besides, the missing rate in OPC 50mg group is 16.9% which is much higher than other two groups, and the primary reason for drop-out was adverse event which indicates the missing for each group may not occur randomly. Hence, the reviewer performed further sensitivity analyses in addition to ones that the sponsor provided and results are presented in Table 12."
>
> — FDA Statistical Review (Study 302, Reviewer’s Comment), p. 20 (https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2020/212489Orig1s000StatR.pdf)

> "Results in Table 12 show the minor impact of missing values in this study. In both FAS and PPS population, ANCOVA with LOCF approach and MMRM using observed cases yielded similar results and both were statistically significant. Sensitivity analyses using multiple imputation approach showed small differences from what the sponsor provided, and these differences are in acceptable ranges when considering randomness from imputation procedure."
>
> — FDA Statistical Review (Study 302, Reviewer’s Report), p. 23 (https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2020/212489Orig1s000StatR.pdf)

### Satralizumab-mwge (Enspryng) — BLA 761149

- Therapeutic area: Neurology / Psychiatry
- Sponsor: Genentech (Roche); trials run by Chugai
- Approval year: 2020

Overview: MMRM is used only for secondary continuous endpoints, as sensitivity/exploratory analyses of the VAS-pain and FACIT-Fatigue key secondaries and for other secondaries. The key-secondary primary analysis is ANCOVA with BOCF. The SAPs pre-specify switching to 'GEE or Generalized Linear Mixed-effect model' if normality fails, a decision made before unblinding. FDA reported only ANCOVA (BOCF/observed-case) results and criticized BOCF.

#### Model 1: Change from baseline in VAS pain and FACIT-Fatigue every 24 weeks (Week 24 key secondary) (sensitivity/supportive for key secondary (primary key-secondary analysis = ANCOVA with BOCF))

- **Trial:** SAkuraSky / BN40898 (NCT02028884)
- **Model family:** MMRM
- **Response:** Change from baseline at each 24-week visit in double-blind period [SAP1 p.23-24]
- **Fixed effects:** treatment group, protocol-specified visit, treatment-by-visit; baseline measurement and stratification factors (baseline ARR, geographic region) as covariates [SAP1 p.16, p.24]
- **Random effects:** None (visit as repeated measure; R-matrix only)
- **Covariance:** Unstructured [SAP1 p.24]
- **Covariance fallback:** 'other covariance structure will be used' (unspecified) [SAP1 p.24]
- **Denominator df:** Not stated
- **Estimation:** Not stated
- **Time coding:** Categorical protocol-specified visits
- **Estimand / contrast:** LS-mean difference at each visit; 'If treatment-by-visit interaction is not statistically significant, the full model will be kept'
- **Missing data:** MMRM 'incorporating all data in double blind period' (MAR) [SAP1 p.16]
- **MNAR / other sensitivity:** Primary ANCOVA uses BOCF; random hot-deck MI sensitivity. Non-normality fallback: 'GEE or Generalized Linear Mixed-effect model analysis will be used' (decided before unblinding) [SAP1 p.24]
- **Software:** SAS 9.2 or later [SAP]
- **Results:** Not reported in FDA StatR (FDA shows ANCOVA-BOCF and observed-case results: VAS diff 6.38 (-0.28, 13.03) p=0.0602; FACIT -2.09 (-4.75, 0.57) p=0.1224; both NS) [StatR Table 5]
- **FDA comments:** 'The imputation of BOCF is likely to be biased, particularly for patients who had missing assessment due to reaching the primary endpoint' - trial not designed to capture Week 24 change [StatR p.16]
- **Spec source:** SAP verbatim

#### Model 2: Change from baseline in VAS pain and FACIT-Fatigue every 24 weeks (exploratory/sensitivity for key secondary)

- **Trial:** SAkuraStar / BN40900 (NCT02073279)
- **Model family:** MMRM

- **Estimation:** Not stated
- **Time coding:** Categorical visits
- **Estimand / contrast:** LS-mean difference by visit
- **Missing data:** All double-blind data (MAR)
- **MNAR / other sensitivity:** Hot-deck MI, OLE-baseline/withdrawal-visit imputation (ANCOVA); GEE/GLMM if non-normal
- **Software:** SAS 9.2 or later [SAP]
- **Results:** Not reported in FDA StatR (ANCOVA-BOCF VAS diff 3.21 (-5.09, 11.52) p=0.4436; NS)

#### Verbatim specification excerpts

##### Model 1: Change from baseline in VAS pain and FACIT-Fatigue every 24 weeks (Week 24 key secondary) (sensitivity/supportive for key secondary (primary key-secondary analysis = ANCOVA with BOCF))

> "In addition, a Mixed-effect model repeated measures (MMRM) for secondary endpoints will be adjusted for Baseline ARR and Geographical region (stratification factors)."
>
> — SAkuraSky (SA-307JG) SAP v9.0 §5.10.1.2, p. 18 (https://cdn.clinicaltrials.gov/large-docs/84/NCT02028884/SAP_001.pdf)

> "For secondary continuous endpoints, a Mixed-effects model repeated measures (MMRM) analysis incorporating all data in double blind period will be used to utilize all the data collected over time with consideration of the variance-covariance matrix of the repeated measures. This method allows a general unstructured variance-covariance matrix and will include data from subjects with incomplete data from some scheduled time points."
>
> — SAkuraSky SAP v9.0 §5.10.1.3 (Handling of Missing Data), p. 18 (https://cdn.clinicaltrials.gov/large-docs/84/NCT02028884/SAP_001.pdf)

> "The MMRM will include treatment group, protocol-specified visit, treatment-by-visit interaction as fixed effects; the baseline measurements and stratification factors as a covariate; and visit as a repeated measure. The unstructured covariance matrix will be assumed in the model. If the unstructured covariance matrix does not converge, other covariance structure will be used. If treatment-by-visit interaction is not statistically significant, the full model will be kept. If the normality assumption for the key secondary variable does not hold, GEE or Generalized Linear Mixed-effect model analysis will be used. The assessment will be performed prior to unblinding."
>
> — SAkuraSky SAP v9.0 §5.10.3.1, p. 26 (https://cdn.clinicaltrials.gov/large-docs/84/NCT02028884/SAP_001.pdf)

```sas
Mixed effect Model Repeat Measurement (MMRM)

proc mixed data=VAS method=REML;

    class REGION TREATMENT VISIT USUBJIDARR;

    model CHG = BASE TREATMENT REGION VISIT ARR
    TREATMENT*VISIT/ddfm=KR;

    repeated VISIT / type=un subject = USUBJID;

    lsmeans TREATMENT*VISIT / pdiff cl;

  ods output lsmeans = lsm; * contains the adjusted means;

  ods output diffs = dif; * contains treatment differences;

run;
```

— SAkuraSky SAP v9.0 Appendix 7.7 (SAS Codes), pp. 58–59 (https://cdn.clinicaltrials.gov/large-docs/84/NCT02028884/SAP_001.pdf) (page header/footer lines omitted; "USUBJIDARR" as in the text layer. This code gives REML estimation and Kenward-Roger df, which results_05.md lists as "Not stated")

> "A large number of patients did not have assessments at Week 24, either due to reaching primary endpoint or discontinuation. The primary analysis was to use baseline observation carry-forward (BOCF) to impute the missing values. Note that patients exited the double-blind period when they experienced their first PDR. Thus, the study was not designed to be able to fully capture the change from baseline to Week 24 in either of the secondary endpoints. The imputation of BOCF is likely to be biased, particularly for patients who had missing assessment due to reaching the primary endpoint. Analysis results with BOCF and without imputation are presented in Table 5. Neither methods yielded statistically significant treatment difference in VAS or FACIT."
>
> — FDA Statistical Review (SAkuraSky), p. 17 (https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2020/761149Orig1s000StatR.pdf)
