### Serdexmethylphenidate/dexmethylphenidate (Azstarys) — NDA 212994

- Therapeutic area: Neurology / Psychiatry
- Sponsor: Corium, Inc. (KemPharm KP415 program)
- Approval year: 2021

Overview: The primary analysis is a hybrid 'MMRM' with both a subject random effect and a Toeplitz R-matrix. FDA documented that the covariance structure was switched from UN (which the Agency had requested) to Toeplitz in a late SAP amendment embedded in a meeting package, without the Agency noticing. FDA re-analysis under UN gave the same conclusions. The FDA abuse-potential reviews (CSS) use crossover mixed models.

#### Model 1: Average of mean changes from baseline in SKAMP-C across all post-dose time points on classroom Day 28 (primary)

- **Trial:** KP415.E01 (NCT03292952), laboratory classroom study
- **Model family:** MMRM with subject random effect (hybrid: Toeplitz + random subject intercept)
- **Response:** Change from baseline (Day 21 predose) in SKAMP-C at each post-dose time point (0.5-13 h) [MDR p.71-72]
- **Fixed effects:** time, treatment, time-by-treatment, site; baseline SKAMP-C (Day 21 predose) covariate [MDR p.71]
- **Random effects:** 'Subject was the random effect' [MDR p.72]
- **Covariance:** Toeplitz (final SAP amendment, eCTD 49), changed from unstructured [MDR p.72]
- **Covariance fallback:** Not stated
- **Denominator df:** Not stated
- **Estimation:** Not stated
- **Time coding:** Categorical post-dose time points
- **Estimand / contrast:** LS-mean of average change across time points, SDX/d-MPH minus placebo
- **Missing data:** Not stated
- **MNAR / other sensitivity:** None; residual diagnostics (Shapiro-Wilk W=0.98) [MDR p.115]
- **Software:** Not stated
- **Results:** Day-21 baseline: LS mean -4.87 vs 0.54; diff -5.4 (95% CI -7.1, -3.7), p<0.001. Rejected post-hoc Day-28 baseline: diff -7.3 (-9.0, -5.5) [MDR Table 26]. Randomized 74 KP415 / 76 placebo
- **FDA comments:** 'In eCTD 11 the Agency asked the Applicant to use the unstructured covariance matrix. In eCTD 37 the Applicant pre-specified un. However, the Applicant changed from un to Toeplitz in eCTD 49. The Agency was not aware that it was changed to Toeplitz in this last SAP amendment embedded in a meeting package.' FDA re-ran with UN: 'results mirror the results using the Toeplitz with only minor deviations (plus/minus 0.1 in the LS means)'. Post-hoc baseline change rejected as 'inconsistent with good scientific principles' [MDR p.70-72]
- **Spec source:** MDR verbatim

#### Model 2: SKAMP-C change from baseline at each post-dose time point (onset and duration of effect) (secondary (not key; unadjusted p-values))

- **Trial:** KP415.E01 (NCT03292952), laboratory classroom study
- **Model family:** MMRM with subject random effect (same model as primary)
- **Response:** Change from Day 21 predose baseline at each time point
- **Fixed effects:** Same as primary
- **Random effects:** Subject
- **Covariance:** Toeplitz (FDA also UN)
- **Covariance fallback:** Not stated
- **Denominator df:** Not stated
- **Estimation:** Not stated
- **Time coding:** Categorical
- **Estimand / contrast:** LS-mean difference at each time point; onset = earliest significant time point; duration = interval with significance [MDR p.72]
- **Missing data:** Not stated
- **MNAR / other sensitivity:** None
- **Software:** Not stated
- **Results:** Differences (pre-specified baseline): 0.5 h -2.3; 1 h -7.4; 2 h -10.1; 4 h -9.7; 8 h -7.1; 10 h -3.9; 12 h -1.0; 13 h -1.6 [MDR Table 27]
- **FDA comments:** Onset/duration not pre-specified as key secondary; no multiplicity control [MDR p.72]
- **Spec source:** MDR verbatim

#### Model 3: SKAMP-C primary endpoint re-analysis with unstructured covariance (FDA reviewer sensitivity)

- **Trial:** KP415.E01 (NCT03292952), laboratory classroom study
- **Model family:** MMRM (UN) with subject random effect
- **Response:** As primary
- **Fixed effects:** As primary
- **Random effects:** Subject (as primary)
- **Covariance:** Unstructured
- **Covariance fallback:** N/A
- **Denominator df:** Not stated
- **Estimation:** Not stated
- **Time coding:** Categorical
- **Estimand / contrast:** As primary
- **Missing data:** Not stated
- **MNAR / other sensitivity:** None
- **Software:** Not stated
- **Results:** 'mirror the results using the Toeplitz with only minor deviations (plus/minus 0.1 in the LS means) and no change in conclusions' [MDR p.72]
- **FDA comments:** Conducted because covariance change to Toeplitz was not noticed by the Agency
- **Spec source:** MDR verbatim

#### Model 4: Drug Liking Emax and other PD endpoints (supportive (abuse-potential, non-efficacy))

- **Trial:** Human abuse potential crossover studies (KP415/SDX vs d-MPH/phentermine vs placebo)
- **Model family:** linear mixed model (random intercept) for crossover
- **Response:** Emax (predose response as covariate in some)
- **Fixed effects:** sequence, period, treatment, first-order carryover; predose covariate [MDR CSS reviews]
- **Random effects:** Subject (or subject nested within sequence) [MDR CSS]
- **Covariance:** Not stated
- **Covariance fallback:** Not stated
- **Denominator df:** Not stated
- **Estimation:** Not stated
- **Time coding:** N/A
- **Estimand / contrast:** Pairwise LS-mean differences
- **Missing data:** Not stated
- **MNAR / other sensitivity:** None
- **Software:** SAS PROC MIXED (sponsor SAP quoted in MDR) [MDR]
- **Results:** Not extracted
- **FDA comments:** Carryover significant (p=0.0030); reviewer kept carryover term since first-period analysis not pre-specified [MDR CSS]
- **Spec source:** MDR verbatim (CSS section)

#### Verbatim specification excerpts

##### Model 1: Average of mean changes from baseline in SKAMP-C across all post-dose time points on classroom Day 28 (primary)

> "The estimate of the difference between KP415 and placebo on the primary endpoint was based on a repeated measures analysis using a mixed-effect model repeated measure (MMRM) model where: [...] Time, treatment, the interaction of time and treatment, and site were fixed effects; [...] Baseline SKAMP-C score (predose Visit 5 (Day 21)) was included as covariate; [...] Subject was the random effect. The Toeplitz covariance structure was specified. To check if the assumptions of the MMRM model are met, residuals were examined through histograms, normal plots, Shapiro-Wilk’s test, and plots of the residuals versus fitted values."
>
> — FDA Multi-Disciplinary Review (Study KP415.E01, Statistical Analysis Plan), pp. 90–91 (https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2021/212994Orig1s000MultidisciplineR.pdf)

> "Statistical reviewer’s note: In eCTD 11 the Agency asked the Applicant to use the unstructured covariance matrix. In eCTD 37 the Applicant pre-specified un. However, the Applicant changed from un to Toeplitz in eCTD 49. The Agency was not aware that it was changed to Toeplitz in this last SAP amendment embedded in a meeting package. The objective of the meeting was not to review the SAP, but to discuss the acceptability of the proposed post-hoc analysis (i.e., change of baseline from Day 21 to Day 28 in primary efficacy endpoint model). This reviewer conducted the analysis (primary efficacy and comparison at time points) using the un structure. The results mirror the results using the Toeplitz with only minor deviations (plus/minus 0.1 in the LS means) and no change in conclusions."
>
> — FDA Multi-Disciplinary Review (Study KP415.E01), p. 91 (https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2021/212994Orig1s000MultidisciplineR.pdf)

> "I consider the use of the post-hoc analysis that was proposed after study completion and data unblinding to be inconsistent with good scientific principles and unacceptable despite the Applicant’s explanations."
>
> — FDA Multi-Disciplinary Review (Study KP415.E01), p. 90 (https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2021/212994Orig1s000MultidisciplineR.pdf)

> "The normality assumption appears to hold (Shapiro-Wilk’s W = 0.98 for studentized residuals over all post-dose time points for change from baseline in SKAMP-C score). The MMRM model appears suitable for analysis of the primary efficacy endpoint."
>
> — FDA Multi-Disciplinary Review (Model Assumptions Check), p. 134 (https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2021/212994Orig1s000MultidisciplineR.pdf)

##### Model 2: SKAMP-C change from baseline at each post-dose time point (onset and duration of effect) (secondary (not key; unadjusted p-values))

> "If the primary endpoint was statistically significant, then general secondary endpoint analyses were performed. The same MMRM model used for the primary endpoint was used to estimate the least square means and corresponding 95% confidence intervals at each time point and treatment on Day 28. Differences in least square means between the treatment groups and unadjusted p-values were reported for each time point. The onset of effect was defined as the earliest post-dose time point at which a statistically significant difference (p-value <0.05) between KP415 and placebo in the mean change in the SKAMP-C scores was shown. The duration of effect was defined in the study protocol as the length of the time interval such that statistically significant differences between KP415 and placebo were reached at each time point during the interval. Onset and duration of effect were not prespecified as key secondary endpoints in either the study protocol or the statistical analysis plan."
>
> — FDA Multi-Disciplinary Review (Study KP415.E01), p. 91 (https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2021/212994Orig1s000MultidisciplineR.pdf)

##### Model 3: SKAMP-C primary endpoint re-analysis with unstructured covariance (FDA reviewer sensitivity)

Same quote as Model 1 (the p. 91 "Statistical reviewer’s note" describes the FDA re-analysis with the unstructured covariance). No further specification text found in: 212994Orig1s000MultidisciplineR.pdf.

##### Model 4: Drug Liking Emax and other PD endpoints (supportive (abuse-potential, non-efficacy))

> "The SAS mixed effects linear model procedure (PROC MIXED) will be used to construct an ANOVA model for the primary endpoint, Drug Liking Emax. The model will include terms for [...] treatment, period, sequence and first-order carryover effect (‘priortrt’) as fixed effects, with subject nested within sequence as a random effect. If the carryover effect is found to be non-significant at the 25% level, this term will be dropped from the model. If carryover effect is found to be significant at the 25% level, indicator variables (one for each treatment in the model) for ‘prior treatment’ will be created to maintain the first-order carryover effect variable without confounding the effects of the treatment, period and sequence variables."
>
> — FDA Multi-Disciplinary Review, CSS statistical review of oral abuse-potential study (sponsor SAP excerpt), pp. 167–168 (https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2021/212994Orig1s000MultidisciplineR.pdf)

> "Reviewer’s comments: Even though the sponsor set priortrt for carryover effects in the dataset, the results of the primary analysis was not from a model included priortrt. In fact, the carryover effect was significant in the primary analysis."
>
> — FDA Multi-Disciplinary Review, CSS statistical review, p. 168 (https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2021/212994Orig1s000MultidisciplineR.pdf)

> "The statistical model used in the reviewer’s primary analysis was a mixed-effects model which included sequence, period, treatment and the first-order-carryover as fixed effects, and subject as a random effect. For the primary endpoint Drug Liking Emax, Levene’s test for homogeneity of variances was not significant (p=0.1817). The first-order-carryover effect was significant (p=0.0030 <0.05). Because the sponsor did not prespecify the first period analysis if the p-value of the first-order-carryover effect was significant at 0.05 level, the reviewer kept the first-order-carryover effect in the model."
>
> — FDA Multi-Disciplinary Review, CSS statistical review, p. 172 (https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2021/212994Orig1s000MultidisciplineR.pdf)

> "A mixed-effects analysis of covariance (ANCOVA) model for a crossover study was used to compare PD endpoints (e.g., Emax, Emin, AUEs) between treatments. The model included treatment, period and treatment sequence as fixed effects, and baseline (pre-dose) measurement as a covariate where applicable, and subject nested within sequence as a random effect. A first-order direct carryover effect from the treatment of previous period was included in the model if it was found to be significant at the 25% level."
>
> — FDA Multi-Disciplinary Review, CSS review of a second abuse-potential study, p. 201 (https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2021/212994Orig1s000MultidisciplineR.pdf)

Sources consulted:

- ✔ https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2021/212994Orig1s000MultidisciplineR.pdf
- No SAP posted

### Viloxazine (Qelbree) — NDA 211964

Therapeutic area: Neurology / Psychiatry. Sponsor: Supernus Pharmaceuticals, Inc.. Approval year: 2021.

Entry notes: Key secondary endpoints (CGI-I, Conners 3-Parent Composite T-score, WFIRS-P) were analyzed by single-timepoint ANCOVA (treatment + baseline), NOT by MMRM [IR Tables 10-12, 22-24]; only the primary endpoint used a mixed model.

#### Model 1: Change from baseline in ADHD-RS-5 total score at end of study (Week 6 for 301/302; Week 8 for 303; Week 7 for 304) (primary)


- **Trial:** Studies 812P301 (NCT03247530), 812P302 (NCT03247543), 812P303 (NCT03247556), 812P304
- **Endpoint/timepoint:** Change from baseline in ADHD-RS-5 total score at end of study (Week 6 for 301/302; Week 8 for 303; Week 7 for 304)
- **Role:** primary
- **Model family:** MMRM
- **Response:** Change from baseline in ADHD-RS-5 total score [IR p.32-33]
- **Fixed effects:** Baseline ADHD-RS-5 total score, age group category, treatment, visit (in weeks), treatment-by-visit interaction [IR p.32-33 verbatim: 'comprises the baseline ADHD-RS-5 total score, age group category, treatment, visit (in weeks), and treatment-by-visit interaction as fixed independent variables']
- **Random effects:** None stated (covariance modeled via R-matrix only)
- **Covariance:** Unstructured [IR p.33]
- **Covariance fallback:** Not stated
- **Denominator df:** Kenward-Roger [IR p.33]
- **Estimation:** REML [IR p.33 verbatim: 'estimated using the restricted maximum-likelihood method, with unstructured variance-covariance matrix and Kenward-Roger approximation to estimate denominator degrees of freedom']
- **Time coding:** Categorical visit (implied by treatment-by-visit interaction and LS means by visit) [IR]
- **Estimand / contrast:** LS-mean difference vs placebo in change from baseline at end of study (EOS) per dose, ITT population; fixed-sequence high-to-low dose testing
- **Missing data:** MAR [IR p.33: 'MMRM assumes a missing at random missing data mechanism']
- **MNAR / sensitivity:** Prespecified multiple imputation under MNAR; 'Consistent results' in 301 and 'same conclusions' in 304 [IR p.40, p.53]; details of MNAR mechanism not stated
- **Software:** Not stated
- **Results:** 301 (N=155 PBO/147 100mg/158 200mg): LSMD -5.8 (SE 1.61; 95% CI -8.9,-2.6; p=0.0004) and -6.9 (1.58; -10.0,-3.8; p<0.0001). 302 (N=104/94/103; 200/400 mg): -4.5 (1.98; -8.4,-0.6; p=0.0232) and -5.1 (1.93; -8.9,-1.3; p=0.0091). 303 (N=97/107/97; 200/400 mg): -6.0 (2.05; -10.0,-1.9; nominal p=0.0038, adj 0.0063) and -5.8 (2.11; -9.9,-1.7; p=0.0063). 304 (N=96/99/97; 400/600 mg): -5.1 (1.93; -8.9,-1.3; nominal p=0.0082, adjusted 0.071) and -3.5 (1.93; -7.3,0.3; p=0.071) [IR Tables 9, 13, 17, 21]. Units: ADHD-RS-5 points.
- **FDA comments:** Reviewer confirmed applicant's MMRM results; reviewer also used the primary MMRM for post hoc subgroup analyses by race, sex, age (IR §16.1). No disagreement with the model; Study 304 failed only via the fixed-sequence hierarchy.
- **Specification source:** StatR/IR verbatim (FDA Integrated Review p.32-33)

#### Verbatim specification excerpts

##### Model 1: Change from baseline in ADHD-RS-5 total score at end of study (Week 6 for 301/302; Week 8 for 303; Week 7 for 304) (primary)

> "Analysis method: The prespecified primary efficacy analysis model, mixed model repeated measures (MMRM), was used to evaluate the treatment effect in the studies. The model, which assesses the change from baseline in ADHD-RS-5, comprises the baseline ADHD-RS-5 total score, age group category, treatment, visit (in weeks), and treatment-by-visit interaction as fixed independent variables. MMRM assumes a missing at random missing data mechanism. The model parameters were to be estimated using the restricted maximum-likelihood method, with unstructured variance-covariance matrix and Kenward-Roger approximation to estimate denominator degrees of freedom."
>
> — FDA Integrated Review, (doc pp. 32-33), PDF pp. 44-45 (https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2021/211964Orig1s000IntegratedR.pdf)

>
> — FDA Integrated Review, Table 9 footnote, PDF p. 50 (https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2021/211964Orig1s000IntegratedR.pdf)

> "Consistent results were seen for the sensitivity analyses of the primary endpoint based on multiple imputation with the missing not at random (MNAR) missing data mechanism."
>
> — FDA Integrated Review, (Study 301), PDF p. 52 (https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2021/211964Orig1s000IntegratedR.pdf)

> "This reviewer conducted an exploratory subgroup analysis by race, gender, and age. The primary efficacy analysis model, mixed model repeated measures (MMRM), was used to investigate the treatment effect. The subgroup analyses were post hoc and any findings could be due to chance."
>
> — FDA Integrated Review, §16.1, PDF p. 239 (https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2021/211964Orig1s000IntegratedR.pdf)

> "The missing data pattern plots (Figure 43, Figure 44, Figure 45, Figure 46) suggest that the missing at random assumption might be reasonable because the dropouts, within each treatment group, may not depend on unobserved ADHD-RS-5 total scores."
>
> — FDA Integrated Review, §16.3, PDF p. 244 (https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2021/211964Orig1s000IntegratedR.pdf)

### Olanzapine/samidorphan (Lybalvi) — NDA 213378

Therapeutic area: Neurology / Psychiatry. Sponsor: Alkermes, Inc.. Approval year: 2021.

Entry notes: ENLIGHTEN-2 (A303) co-primary weight endpoints were NOT analyzed by a mixed model: primary = ANCOVA (percent weight change) and logistic regression (>=10% gain) after 500-fold MI (MCMC + sequential regression), combined across stages with the Cui-Hung-Wang statistic [MDR p.66-67]. MMRM appears only as an A303 sensitivity analysis. FDA also noted the A303 LS-means-by-visit plot was from separate per-visit MI-ANCOVA models, not a single longitudinal model [MDR p.97]. Result tables for A305 are images in the PDF and could not be extracted; results below come from README/MDR text.

#### Model 1: Change from baseline in PANSS total score at Week 4; also key secondary CGI-S change at Week 4 (primary (and key secondary CGI-S))


- **Trial:** ENLIGHTEN-1 (ALK3831-A305), NCT02634346
- **Endpoint/timepoint:** Change from baseline in PANSS total score at Week 4; also key secondary CGI-S change at Week 4
- **Role:** primary (and key secondary CGI-S)
- **Model family:** MMRM
- **Response:** Change from baseline in PANSS total (CGI-S for key secondary)
- **Fixed effects:** Region (U.S. vs non-U.S.), visit, treatment, visit-by-treatment interaction (categorical); baseline PANSS total as covariate [MDR p.47 verbatim: 'The model included region (U.S. vs. non-U.S.), visit, treatment, and interaction term of visit and treatment as categorical variables, and baseline PANSS total score as a covariate']
- **Random effects:** None stated
- **Covariance:** Unstructured [MDR p.47: 'a mixed model with repeated measurements (MMRM) with an unstructured variance-covariance matrix']
- **Covariance fallback:** Not stated
- **Denominator df:** Not stated
- **Estimation:** Not stated
- **Time coding:** Categorical visit
- **Estimand / contrast:** LS-mean difference ALKS 3831 vs placebo (and olanzapine vs placebo, no multiplicity adjustment for olanzapine as active control) at Week 4, FAS; 'All observed measures ... included. Missing data will not be imputed.'
- **Missing data:** MAR implied (no imputation; all observed data)
- **MNAR / sensitivity:** Delta-adjusted pattern-mixture model: ALKS 3831 dropouts worsened by delta vs ALKS 3831 continuers, placebo dropouts follow placebo continuers; sequential regression MI (20 imputations; imputation model region + previous timepoints + baseline), ANCOVA (region, treatment, baseline PANSS) on Week-4 CFB, Rubin's rules; deltas = 10-50% of observed treatment difference [MDR p.47-48]
- **Software:** Not stated
- **Results:** ALKS 3831 vs placebo LSMD -6.4 (SE 1.8; 95% CI -10.0,-2.8; p<0.001); olanzapine vs placebo -5.3 (SE 1.8; 95% CI -8.9,-1.7; p=0.004) [README / MDR p.13]. Randomized 135 PBO / 134 ALKS 3831 / 134 OLZ [MDR p.48]; per-arm FAS N not extracted (table image).
- **FDA comments:** No disagreement with the model reported in text; FDA noted trial designed to show each active arm beats placebo rather than formal NI.
- **Specification source:** MDR verbatim (p.47)

#### Model 2: Percent change from baseline in body weight at Week 24 (sensitivity)


- **Trial:** ENLIGHTEN-2 (ALK3831-A303), NCT02694328
- **Endpoint/timepoint:** Percent change from baseline in body weight at Week 24
- **Role:** sensitivity
- **Model family:** MMRM
- **Response:** Percent change from baseline in body weight
- **Fixed effects:** Treatment, visit, treatment-by-visit, race, age (categorical fixed effects); baseline weight as covariate [MDR p.67 verbatim: 'The MMRM model will include treatment, visit, treatment-by-visit interaction term, race and age as categorical fixed effects, and baseline weight as a covariate']
- **Random effects:** None stated
- **Covariance:** Unstructured [MDR p.67]
- **Covariance fallback:** Not stated
- **Denominator df:** Not stated
- **Estimation:** Not stated
- **Time coding:** Categorical visit
- **Estimand / contrast:** Treatment difference ALKS 3831 vs olanzapine at Week 24 using 'all observed post-randomization on-treatment weight measurements without imputation of missing data' (on-treatment/hypothetical-type)
- **Missing data:** MAR (no imputation); on-treatment data only
- **MNAR / sensitivity:** Separate delta-adjusted PMM (olanzapine dropouts' unobserved gain decreased by delta) [MDR p.66-67]
- **Software:** Not stated
- **Results:** Not stated (sensitivity results not extracted; primary MI-ANCOVA/CHW: -2.38%, 95% CI -3.88,-0.88, p=0.003)
- **FDA comments:** Amendment 5 (Sept 2018) replaced LOCF with MI and MMRM without imputation [MDR p.68]. No FDA comment specific to the MMRM.
- **Specification source:** MDR verbatim (p.67)

#### Model 3: Change in PANSS total score from randomization to end of Part A (equivalence vs olanzapine, margin 10 points); exploratory weight endpoints analyzed analogously (primary (of a Phase 2 study FDA deemed exploratory/supportive))


- **Trial:** Study ALK3831-302 (Phase 2 dose-ranging, olanzapine lead-in)
- **Endpoint/timepoint:** Change in PANSS total score from randomization to end of Part A (equivalence vs olanzapine, margin 10 points); exploratory weight endpoints analyzed analogously
- **Role:** primary (of a Phase 2 study FDA deemed exploratory/supportive)
- **Model family:** MMRM
- **Response:** Change from baseline in PANSS total
- **Fixed effects:** Weight-change strata in the olanzapine lead-in period, treatment group, visit, treatment-by-visit (categorical); baseline value covariate [MDR p.81]
- **Random effects:** None stated
- **Covariance:** AR(1) [MDR p.81 verbatim: 'The covariance structure will AR(1). Missing data will not be imputed.']
- **Covariance fallback:** Not stated

- **Estimand / contrast:** Pooled ALKS 3831 (3 doses) vs olanzapine, equivalence margin 10 points; FAS 1
- **Missing data:** MAR (no imputation)
- **MNAR / sensitivity:** Not stated

- **Results:** Not stated

#### Verbatim specification excerpts

##### Model 1: Change from baseline in PANSS total score at Week 4; also key secondary CGI-S change at Week 4 (primary (and key secondary CGI-S))

> "The primary analysis for both the primary and the secondary endpoint was based on a mixed model with repeated measurements (MMRM) with an unstructured variance-covariance matrix. The model included region (U.S. vs. non-U.S.), visit, treatment, and interaction term of visit and treatment as categorical variables, and baseline PANSS total score as a covariate. All observed measures on the primary analysis set will be included. Missing data will not be imputed."
>
> — FDA Multi-Discipline Review, Study A305 Primary Analysis, PDF p. 88 (https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2021/213378Orig1Orig2s000MultidisciplineR.pdf)

> "To assess the robustness of the primary analysis with respect to missing data, the Applicant pre- specified a sensitivity analysis using a Delta-adjusted Pattern Mixture Model. It incorporates the clinical assumption that ALKS 3831 subjects who discontinue at a given time point would have, on average, their unobserved PANSS worsened by some amount δ compared with the observed PANSS of subjects on the same treatment arm who continue to the next timepoint. Subjects who discontinue from the placebo arm would have the same PANSS trajectory as the placebo subjects who stay on the study. A sequential regression-based multiple imputation (MI) procedure will be used to incorporate the assumption and to allow uncertainty in the imputations to be reflected appropriately in the analysis. The imputation model will include the measurement at the current timepoint as the response variable, and region (U.S. vs. non-U.S.) as factor, the measurements at the previous timepoints and the baseline as covariates. Twenty imputations will be carried out. For each of the 20 imputed data sets, the ANCOVA model with region (U.S, vs. non-U.S.) and treatment group as factors and baseline PANSS as covariate will be fitted to the change from baseline at Week 4 to obtain the treatment effect estimate and standard error. Rubin’s rule will be used to combine the treatment effect estimates and standard errors across imputations. The shift parameters to be used in the sensitivity analysis will account for 10%, 20%, 30%, 40%, and 50% of the observed treatment difference between ALKS 3831 and placebo."
>
> — FDA Multi-Discipline Review, Study A305 Sensitivity Analysis for Missing Data, PDF pp. 88-89 (https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2021/213378Orig1Orig2s000MultidisciplineR.pdf)

##### Model 2: Percent change from baseline in body weight at Week 24 (sensitivity)

> "Analysis based on mixed model with repeated measurements (MMRM) model. The MMRM model will include treatment, visit, treatment-by-visit interaction term, race and age as categorical fixed effects, and baseline weight as a covariate. An unstructured covariance structure will be applied. The analysis will be performed on all observed post-randomization on-treatment weight measurements without imputation of missing data."
>
> — FDA Multi-Discipline Review, Study A303 Sensitivity Analyses for Missing Data, PDF p. 108 (https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2021/213378Orig1Orig2s000MultidisciplineR.pdf)

> "The delta-adjusted Pattern Mixture Model. This approach is to assess the potential impact of missing data due to missing not at random (MNAR). It incorporates the clinical assumption that olanzapine subjects who discontinue at a given time point would have, on average, their unobserved weight gain decreased by some amount δ compared with the observed weight gain of subjects in the olanzapine arm who continue to the next time point, while ALKS 3831 subjects who discontinue would have the same weight gain trajectory as the ALKS 3831 subjects that stay on the study."
>
> — FDA Multi-Discipline Review, Study A303 Sensitivity Analyses for Missing Data, PDF p. 108 (https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2021/213378Orig1Orig2s000MultidisciplineR.pdf)

> "Multiple imputation and MMRM without imputation would be utilized, instead of last observation carried forward."
>
> — FDA Multi-Discipline Review, Study A303 Protocol Amendment 5, PDF p. 109 (https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2021/213378Orig1Orig2s000MultidisciplineR.pdf)

> "Note: The MI ANCOVA model (Primary Analysis Model) was applied on Applicant's MI data (observed and imputed data) at each visit. LS Means are based on an individual ANCOVA model for each visit, not including data from all visits in one model."
>
> — FDA Multi-Discipline Review, Figure 16 note (Study A303), PDF p. 138 (https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2021/213378Orig1Orig2s000MultidisciplineR.pdf)

##### Model 3: Change in PANSS total score from randomization to end of Part A (equivalence vs olanzapine, margin 10 points); exploratory weight endpoints analyzed analogously (primary (of a Phase 2 study FDA deemed exploratory/supportive))

> "The primary analysis was to assess whether the effect of pooled ALKS 3831 (when all three doses were pooled) were equivalent to that of olanzapine based on a pre-specified equivalence margin of 10 points. If this analysis shows equivalence, similar analyses on individual dose levels will be performed."
>
> — FDA Multi-Discipline Review, Study 302 Primary analysis, PDF p. 122 (https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2021/213378Orig1Orig2s000MultidisciplineR.pdf)

> "The primary analysis model was based on mixed-model for repeated measures MMRM model. The model will include variables for weight change strata in the olanzapine lead-in period, treatment group, visit, and treatment group-by-visit interaction term as categorical fixed effect; baseline value will be included as a covariate. The covariance structure will AR(1). Missing data will not be imputed."
>
> — FDA Multi-Discipline Review, Study 302 Primary analysis, PDF p. 122 (https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2021/213378Orig1Orig2s000MultidisciplineR.pdf)

> "The analysis method was analogous to that for the primary efficacy endpoint. For binary outcomes, a Cochran-Mantel-Haenszel (CMH) option was used to make adjustments for the olanzapine lead-in period weight change strata. FDA Comment: This was an exploratory phase 2 study. We consider all analyses purely exploratory. There has not been an established equivalence margin to demonstrate the equivalence of one drug to another for a psychiatric disorder."
>
> — FDA Multi-Discipline Review, Study 302, PDF p. 123 (https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2021/213378Orig1Orig2s000MultidisciplineR.pdf)

### Aducanumab-avwa (Aduhelm) — BLA 761178

Therapeutic area: Neurology / Psychiatry. Sponsor: Biogen, Inc. (with Eisai). Approval year: 2021.

Entry notes: Primary results Tables 6-7 are images; numbers below are from reviewer text. Secondary clinical endpoints (MMSE, ADAS-Cog13, ADCS-ADL-MCI) model specification not found in extracted text (Not stated). Statistical reviewer Massie argued the primary MMRM 'may not be correct' given significant treatment*visit*age-group and treatment*visit*country interactions, ~45-50% missing Week-78 data, and doubtful MAR.

#### Model 1: Change from baseline in CDR-SB at Week 78 (primary)


- **Trial:** ENGAGE (221AD301, NCT02477800) and EMERGE (221AD302, NCT02484547)
- **Endpoint/timepoint:** Change from baseline in CDR-SB at Week 78
- **Role:** primary
- **Model family:** MMRM
- **Response:** Change from baseline in CDR-SB
- **Fixed effects:** Treatment group, time (categorical), treatment-by-time, baseline CDR-SB, baseline CDR-SB-by-time, baseline MMSE, AD symptomatic medication use at baseline (yes/no), region, laboratory ApoE e4 status [StatR p.18-19 verbatim]
- **Random effects:** None stated
- **Covariance:** Unstructured [StatR p.19: 'An unstructured covariance matrix was to be used to model the within-patient variance-covariance errors']
- **Covariance fallback:** Heterogeneous Toeplitz, then heterogeneous AR(1) [StatR p.19-20 verbatim]
- **Denominator df:** Kenward-Roger [StatR p.20]
- **Estimation:** Not stated
- **Time coding:** Categorical
- **Estimand / contrast:** Mean difference in CDR-SB change at Week 78 vs placebo, ITT; all observed data including after intercurrent events (treatment discontinuation, change in AD symptomatic meds) - treatment-policy [StatR p.18 verbatim, citing ICH E9(R1)]
- **Missing data:** MAR [StatR p.20: 'missing data are assumed to be missing at random']
- **MNAR / sensitivity:** FDA reviewer two-parameter tipping-point (separate shifts for high dose and placebo dropouts) for Study 302: significance lost if alpha(high) slightly >0.3 with alpha(placebo)=0, or line alpha(high)=0.3+0.7*alpha(placebo) [StatR p.50]
- **Software:** Not stated
- **Results:** Final BLA data, high dose vs placebo at Week 78: 302 -0.390 (SE 0.155; 95% CI -0.694,-0.086; p~0.01); 301 +0.032 (SE 0.150; 95% CI -0.262,0.326; p~0.83). Placebo LS means 1.56 (301) / 1.74 (302); high-dose LS means 1.59 / 1.35 [StatR p.28]. 302 Opportunity-to-Complete subset (N=953): -0.36 (95% CI -0.70,-0.02; p=0.0368). 302 censoring after post-baseline AD med start: -0.410 (SE 0.158; p=0.0098) / -0.431 (SE 0.161; p=0.0074) [StatR Table 9]. Low-dose numbers not extracted.
- **FDA comments:** Massie: 'MMRM implicitly imputes missing data from completers but there may not be enough overlap in model covariates between dropouts and completers ... especially with 70% missing'; significant treatment*visit*Agegroup and treatment*visit*Country interactions 'suggest that the primary MMRM model may not be correct' [StatR p.89, 104]. Robust regression (LTS/M-estimation) of 301 Week-78 data showed no high-dose effect (0.0265, SE 0.1247, p=0.83) [StatR p.33]. Reviewer did not recommend approval.
- **Specification source:** StatR verbatim (p.18-20)

#### Verbatim specification excerpts

##### Model 1: Change from baseline in CDR-SB at Week 78 (primary)

> "The estimand of the primary analysis is the mean difference of the change from baseline CDR- SB scores at Week 78 between treatment groups in the ITT population [ICH E9 (R1) Addendum 2014, 2017]. All observed data was to be included in the primary analysis, including data collected after intercurrent events [ICH E9 (R1) Addendum 2017], i.e., treatment discontinuation or a change in concomitant use of AD symptomatic medication. The change from baseline CDR- SB scores was to be summarized by treatment group at each post-baseline visit. A mixed model repeated measures (MMRM) model was to be used as the primary analysis to analyze change from baseline CDR-SB using fixed effects of treatment group, time (categorical), treatment group-by-time interaction, baseline CDR-SB, baseline CDR-SB by time interaction, baseline MMSE, AD symptomatic medication use at baseline(yes/no), region, and laboratory ApoE ε4 status (carrier/non-carrier). An unstructured covariance matrix was to be used to model the within-patient variance-covariance errors. If the unstructured covariance structure matrix resulted in a lack of convergence, the heterogeneous Toeplitz covariance structure followed by the heterogeneous first-order autoregressive covariance structure was to be used. The Kenward- Roger approximation was to be used to estimate the denominator degrees of freedom. In the primary analysis, missing data are assumed to be missing at random [Rubin 1976]."
>
> — FDA Statistical Review, Primary analysis (Studies 301/302), PDF pp. 19-20 (https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2021/761178Orig1s000StatR.pdf)

> "There is a lot of missing data in study 302 (and 301) at Week 78 (>40%) caused by early stopping due to futility. Week 78 is the only Visit with apparent efficacy for CDRSB in study 302. Unblinding due to ARIA and high dose titration limitations vary significantly by APOE+ vs. APOE- (as do, to some extent, CDRSB changes) and the maximum dose for the high dose APOE+ changed after protocol amendment 4. Therefore, Missing at Random may not be a reasonable assumption for missing data without stratifying by APOE."
>
> — FDA Statistical Review, reviewer discussion of missing data, PDF p. 29 (https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2021/761178Orig1s000StatR.pdf)

> "Figure 15 shows a tipping point analysis of Study 302, investigating combinations of degrees of informative missingness that could alter the significance (above the shaded grid region) on the primary outcome at Week 78. Alpha (“high”) and Alpha (placebo) allow for adjustments to the mean response for dropouts independently for high dose and placebo, i.e., the graph shows the treatment difference when the mean in dropouts is assumed to be the mean in completers for the given group plus an additional amount: + alpha(“high”) if the given group is high dose or +alpha(placebo) if it is placebo. The figure investigates the potential impact of such possible informative missing data in dropouts. Combinations of the two alpha’s above the yellow shaded grid would suggest a loss of significance, e.g., if α(high) is a little greater than 0.3 and α(placebo) = 0 or if α(high)=0 and α(placebo)=-0.43 or any combination of α(high) and α(placebo) above the line α(high) =0.3 +0.7*α(placebo). The same would be true for any combination of α(“high”) and of α(placebo) in the orange region at the upper left of the figure. Considering the overall outcome of Study 301 it is not unrealistic that high dose dropouts could be worse than placebo."
>
> — FDA Statistical Review, Study 302 tipping point, PDF p. 51 (https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2021/761178Orig1s000StatR.pdf)

> "The sponsor makes an argument about outliers being influential more in study 301 than 302. However, a robust regression, which is by design less affected by outliers (least trimmed squares /M estimation), of study 301 Week 78 data shows no effect of the high dose on CDRSB ( Placebo-High = 0.0265, S.E. = 0.1247, p=0.8315). The low dose is also still numerically better than the high dose in the robust analysis of study 301 (-0.0628, S.E. = 0.1249, p=0.6153)."
>
> — FDA Statistical Review, robust regression, Study 301, PDF p. 34 (https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2021/761178Orig1s000StatR.pdf)

> "Missing data was very high proportion in the ITT dataset. Missing data may not be MAR due to changes in enrollment characteristics later in the study. MMRM implicitly imputes missing data from completers but there may not be enough overlap in model covariates between dropouts and completers due to changes in enrollment, especially with 70% missing. The implicit imputation may be slightly off due to omission of time dependence of model effects that nonetheless appear significant. Randomization helps but such a high amount missing may overwhelm this protection. We have 3 issues: very high missing, some differences in characteristics between completers and dropouts in model effects impacting outcome, and potential model bias due to not incorporating the time dependence of these effects which the data suggests is important, This is a recipe for trouble and we are on thinner ice with differences between dropouts and completers in country for example which the data suggests is an effect modifier. We agree that the results are reasonably consistent between the ITT and OTC but the OTC is more reliable due to a more reasonable amount of missing data and it has a slightly higher p-value, i.e, farther from the level considered for an isolated single study approval."
>
> — FDA Statistical Review, reviewer conclusions, PDF pp. 89-90 (https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2021/761178Orig1s000StatR.pdf)

> "Note that 302 has significant interactions with treatment*visit*Agegroup and treatment*visit*Country, as well as visit*agegroup and visit*country. Study 301 also has a significant country*visit interaction. These, among other interactions such as baseline disease stage group found by the reviewer, suggest that the primary MMRM model may not be correct. Since demographic and disease characteristics changed somewhat after PV4, those missing Week 78 have different characteristics and if the model is not correct the model may be biased given the large amount of missing data for the ITT population. Different demographics of those without the opportunity to complete such as more from the Asian region and DEU (Germany), more mild baseline disease stage, more symptomatic AD medications at baseline, and increased age may cause the model to not be valid under MAR since the model does not account for interactions with these variables and Visit, but the data suggests they are significant (should be included)."
>
> — FDA Statistical Review, reviewer conclusions, PDF p. 105 (https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2021/761178Orig1s000StatR.pdf)

##### Model 2: Change from baseline in amyloid PET SUVR (composite and regional ROIs, cerebellum reference) at Weeks 26 and 78 (secondary (biomarker; basis of accelerated approval surrogate))

> "For the 18F-florbetapir amyloid PET analysis population, an MMRM model was to be used to analyze change from baseline SUVR for each target ROI with cerebellum as the reference region. Fixed effects of the model were to include treatment groups (placebo, low dose and high dose), visit (Week 26 and Week 78), treatment group-by-visit interaction, baseline SUVR (continuous), baseline SUVR by visit interaction, baseline MMSE (continuous), laboratory ApoE ε4 status (carrier and non- carrier), and baseline age (continuous). Visit and treatment group were to be treated as categorical variables in the model along with their interactions. An unstructured covariance matrix was to be used to model the within-patient variance-covariance errors. If the unstructured covariance structure matrix resulted in a lack of convergence in any of the parameters, the heterogeneous Toeplitz covariance structure followed by the heterogeneous first-order autoregressive covariance structure was to be used for all the parameters. The Kenward-Roger approximation was to be used to estimate the denominator degrees of freedom. Adjusted means for each treatment group, pairwise adjusted differences with placebo, 95% confidence intervals for the differences and associated p-values were to be presented at week 26 and week 78. The same MMRM model was also to be used to analyze the change from baseline SUVR for the composite ROI with each of the reference regions. No multiple comparison adjustment was to be used for amyloid PET analysis."
>
> — FDA Statistical Review, By Visit summary and MMRM model (amyloid PET), PDF p. 23 (https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2021/761178Orig1s000StatR.pdf)

##### Model 3: Change from baseline in CDR-SB at Week 54 (exploratory) (sensitivity (sponsor) / FDA-preferred reanalysis)

> "A sensitivity analysis was to be conducted using the per protocol analysis population. MMRM was also to be performed as a sensitivity analysis. Additional sensitivity analysis was to include treating visit as a continuous variable in the model."
>
> — FDA Statistical Review, Study 103 (PRIME) planned analyses, PDF p. 77 (https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2021/761178Orig1s000StatR.pdf)

> "In the final study report the sponsor presents the analysis of Week 54 from an ANCOVA of Week 54 data only instead of the more appropriate MMRM (given the presence of dropouts 11% placebo [10% concurrent placebo] and 18% in 10 mg/kg). The MMRM was resigned to a sensitivity analysis by the sponsor. There were 20 randomized patients excluded from the ANCOVA. The sponsor’s ANCOVA result for 10 mg vs. pooled placebo was 1.26 [S.E.=0.556], p=0.0246. The more appropriate MMRM has a less favorable p-value for 10 mg vs. pooled placebo: 1.08 [S.E.=0.537], p=0.0462. Regardless, the comparisons with pooled placebo are nonrandomized comparisons. The pooled placebo LSMean at Week 54 was 1.90 [S.E.=0.34] worse than either study 301 or 302 in a shorter study and the Week 54 CDRSB variance was 4.57. The MMRM estimate of the titration group vs. pooled placebo comparison is not significant.: 0.73 [S.E.=0.57], p=0.2044 as compared to the ANCOVA 1.19 [S.E.=0.58], p=0.0432. Dropouts were 5/44 for placebo overall and 1/22 for the titration group. The one BIIB037 titration group dropout had a 6.5 point increase from baseline to Week 26 and then dropped out. The by visit ANCOVA seems to be biased by informative censoring of this Week 26 CDRSB value: the week 54 LSMean for the titration group based on ANCOVA is 0.70 as compared to 1.14 for MMRM."
>
> — FDA Statistical Review, Study 103 (PRIME) results, PDF pp. 82-83 (https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2021/761178Orig1s000StatR.pdf)

#### Verbatim specification excerpts

##### Model 1: Change from baseline in mean monthly migraine days across 12-week treatment period; same model for continuous secondaries (monthly headache days, acute medication use days, MSQ v2.1 RFR, AIM-D PDA and PI) (primary (and key secondary continuous endpoints))

> "The primary endpoint was analyzed using MMRM. The statistical model included treatment group, visit, prior exposure (yes/no) to a migraine preventive medication, and treatment group- by-visit interaction as categorical fixed effects. It also included the baseline score and baseline- by-visit interaction as covariates. An unstructured covariance matrix was used to model the covariance of within-participant repeated measurements. The Kenward-Roger approximation was used to estimate the denominator degrees of freedom. Sensitivity analyses for missing data handling were planned, including: (1) analysis of covariance model based on 3-month average of the monthly migraine days, (2) MMRM based on primary measures collected during the double-blind and follow-up periods, (3) analysis of covariance with multiple imputations within group, and (4) a pattern-mixture model approach based on the reference-based copy reference method. Sensitivity analysis using multiple imputations in conjunction with robust regression were conducted to assess the robustness of the primary MMRM analysis to the possible violation of the normality assumption. The 50% or greater responder endpoint, where responders were defined as a participant with at least 50% reduction in 3-month average of monthly migraine days, was analyzed using a logistic regression model. The other secondary efficacy endpoints were analyzed in the same manner as that was used to analyze the primary endpoint."
>
> — FDA Integrated Review, Study 3101-301-002 (ADVANCE) Analysis Methods, PDF p. 44 (https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2021/215206Orig1s000IntegratedR.pdf)

> "Prespecified sensitivity analyses using various methods for handling missing data assuming missing at random and missing not at random yielded similar results as the primary analysis (results not shown). An additional mixed-effects model for repeated measures was conducted based on primary measures collected during the double-blind and follow-up periods. The result was consistent with the primary analysis (Table 124)."
>
> — FDA Integrated Review, §16.2, PDF p. 195 (https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2021/215206Orig1s000IntegratedR.pdf)

##### Model 2: Change from baseline in mean monthly migraine days across 12 weeks; same MMRM for continuous secondaries (primary (supportive trial))

> "The primary endpoint was analyzed using mixed-effects model for repeated measures (MMRM). The response variable was the change from baseline to each postbaseline month in monthly migraine days. The model included baseline monthly migraine days as a covariate, treatment group and visit (month) as fixed factors, and treatment group-by-visit and baseline-by-visit as interaction terms. The restricted maximum likelihood method was used. The within-patient correlation was modeled using the unstructured covariance matrix (compound symmetry covariance matrix if convergence failed). The Kenward-Roger approximation was used to estimate denominator degrees of freedom. Contrasts were constructed to obtain the average treatment effects across the 12-week (Months 1 to 3) treatment period to compare each atogepant treatment group versus the placebo group."
>
> — FDA Integrated Review, Study CGP-MD-01 Analysis Methods, PDF p. 36 (https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2021/215206Orig1s000IntegratedR.pdf)

> "Two sensitivity analyses were planned on the primary analysis. The first used a pattern-mixture model approach based on the reference-based copy reference method for missing value imputation. This analysis used a missing-not-at-random mechanism for missing data to assess the impact of potential deviation from a missing at random assumption in the primary analysis. The second sensitivity analysis used multiple imputations in conjunction with robust regression to assess the robustness of the primary MMRM analysis with respect to the possibility of a violation of the normality assumption. The normality assumption of MMRM analysis is usually not a concern for trials of this size; therefore, the statistical review mainly focused on the sensitivity analysis for missing data. For secondary endpoints, pairwise comparisons were analyzed using MMRM for continuous variables, and generalized linear mixed model for repeated measures of the binary response of at least 50% reduction."
>
> — FDA Integrated Review, Study CGP-MD-01 Analysis Methods, PDF p. 37 (https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2021/215206Orig1s000IntegratedR.pdf)

> "A pattern-mixture model based on nonignorable missing (i.e., missing not at random) was conducted to assess the robustness of the primary mixed-effects model for repeated measures analysis to the possible violation of the missing at random assumption. In the pattern-mixture model, the placebo group was used as reference to impute missing values. Each imputed dataset is analyzed using analysis of covariance with treatment group as a factor and baseline value as a covariate and the estimates and p-values were obtained from combining all the results from each individual analysis. The result of the pattern-mixture model is consistent with the primary analysis (Table 121). As shown in Figure 35, the change in the number of migraine days after the first month has similar trends in the placebo and atogepant groups. Therefore, imputing missing data for the atogepant groups based on the pattern of the placebo group yielded a similar result as the mixed-effects model for repeated measures analysis under missing at random assumption."
>
> — FDA Integrated Review, §16.1, PDF p. 193 (https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2021/215206Orig1s000IntegratedR.pdf)

> "In study CGP-MD-01, it was required that a minimum of 12 days’ diary data during each postbaseline 4-week treatment period be evaluable for that particular period. However, the requirement was updated to “14 days” in study 3101-301-002 as requested by FDA during the End of Phase 2 meeting. Therefore, the statistical reviewer conducted an additional analysis using the “14 days” requirement for study CGP-MD-01. The estimated treatment effects were similar to the primary analysis, although the p-value after adjusting for multiplicity is slightly larger than 0.05 for the atogepant 60 mg QD group, and the atogepant 30 mg QD group (Table 123). The analysis using the evaluable requirement of “12 days” is considered as the primary analysis as that was consistently specified in all versions of the Statistical Analysis Plan."
>
> — FDA Integrated Review, §16.1, PDF p. 194 (https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2021/215206Orig1s000IntegratedR.pdf)

#### Verbatim specification excerpts

##### Model 1: Change from baseline in WASO and LPS (PSG) at Month 1 and Month 3 (primary); sTST and IDSIQ sleepiness domain (secondary) (primary (and secondary))

> "The main analysis was performed using the full analysis set. A longitudinal data analysis method (i.e., linear mixed effects model) was used for the analysis of change from baseline in WASO, LPS, sTST, and IDSIQ scores, separately. All available data, regardless of occurrence of intercurrent events (e.g., study treatment discontinuation, the use of prohibited medication), was included in the model. The analysis model adjusted for the baseline value of the relevant response variable (either WASO, LPS, sTST or IDSIQ sleepiness domain score), age group (<65; ≥65 years), treatment (higher dose; lower dose; placebo), time point (Month 1; Month 3), and the interaction of treatment by time point and baseline by time point. To evaluate the efficacy hypotheses, appropriate contrasts were used to test the treatment differences of interest (i.e., the difference in least squares mean change from baseline between higher dose daridorexant versus placebo and lower dose daridorexant versus placebo at Month 1 and Month 3). An unstructured covariance matrix was used to model the correlation among repeated measurements. This approach relies on the missing at random (MAR) assumption. The Applicant conducted two sensitivity analyses to explore violations of the MAR assumptions: Jump-to-reference: a multiple imputation sensitivity analysis in which patients who discontinue study treatment are assumed to have the same mean trajectory as patients who complete the study in the placebo arm. Tipping point analysis: multiple imputation analyses are conducted in which patients who drop out are assumed to follow a trajectory similar to the completers but with a fixed shift in the mean trajectory (μcompleters+Δ). The Applicant explored shift parameters from 0 to 60 minutes."
>
> — FDA Integrated Review, Trials ID-078A301/302 statistical methods (doc pp. 32-33), PDF pp. 51-52 (https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2022/214985Orig1s000IntegratedR.pdf)

> "Statistical Reviewer Comments: Regarding the Applicant’s treatment policy estimand and mixed model for repeated measures (MMRM) estimation model, estimates from the MMRM model will answer the clinical question under the treatment policy estimand if the intercurrent event does not lead to study discontinuation. In the case that an intercurrent events leads to study discontinuation and therefore missing data, MMRM estimates will estimate the treatment policy when it is reasonable to assume that treatment discontinuation does not change the expected symptoms. After discussion with the clinical team, this assumption is unlikely to be met (patients suffer mean worsening of PSG measures of insomnia that exceed in magnitude the mean treatment effects (see Section 7.7.4.1.3); therefore, MMRM estimates may not estimate the treatment policy estimand when many patients discontinue treatment. The proposed sensitivity analyses were reasonable to explore deviations from MAR because patients are expected to worsen after treatment discontinuation. The Applicant’s proposed MMRM analysis assumes that LPS, ΔLPS, WASO, and ΔWASO are normally distributed. There is a priori evidence that WASO, LPS, and ΔLPS distributions are not normally distributed (Ratti et al. 2013; Murphy et al. 2017). Because LPS and WASO can only take on positive values, they are unlikely to be normally distributed. In this situation, the treatment effect standard errors may be inflated, yielding a decrease in statistical power. In some situations, this could cause a type II error. In addition, most statistical tests using the estimates resulting from an MMRM model with a mis-specified error distribution may be conservative (i.e., the observed type I error may be smaller than its nominal level [e.g., 3% instead of 5%])."
>
> — FDA Integrated Review, Statistical Reviewer Comments (doc p. 34), PDF p. 53 (https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2022/214985Orig1s000IntegratedR.pdf)

> "For the WASO endpoint, the results of the sensitivity analyses (tipping point analysis and jump to reference) indicated that the primary analysis is unlikely to be impacted by violation of the MAR assumptions. For the LPS endpoint, conclusions about the 50-mg dose were unlikely to be impacted by violations of MAR. However, for the 25-mg dose, the p-value crossed the testing threshold for 30 minutes at Month 3 and 60 minutes at Month 1. These tipping points indicate that the LPS results are robust up to worsening greater than a return to baseline, see Table 12."
>
> — FDA Integrated Review, Trial ID-078A301 results, PDF p. 64 (https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2022/214985Orig1s000IntegratedR.pdf)

##### Model 2: LPS change from baseline, log-transformed (sensitivity (sponsor post hoc/planned normality sensitivity; FDA recreated))

> "Statistical Reviewer Comment: For the LPS endpoint, the Applicant prespecified an MMRM analysis using the untransformed data with planned sensitivity analysis to assess the impact of non-normality on the p-value for the primary analysis. This sensitivity analysis consisted of conducting an MMRM analysis to the primary MMRM analysis but with the log transformed LPS data. The change from assuming a normal LPS distribution to a log-normal distribution changes the population level summary compared from differences in means to ratios of geometric means. Therefore, this sensitivity may be better considered as a supplementary analysis estimating a supplementary estimand with the new population level summary. The Applicant reported that the p-values of the 25-mg dose at Month 1 and Month 3 decreased to 0.0004 and 0.0021. This Statistical Reviewer recreated this sensitivity analysis, see Section 16.2. Although this sensitivity analysis suggested a lack of robustness to model assumptions, the prespecified analysis must be used for decision making because it is the only analysis with the type I error rate controlled. Because the sensitivity analysis is conducted after seeing the data, its type I error rate is not controlled."
>
> — FDA Integrated Review, Trial ID-078A302 Statistical Reviewer Comment (doc pp. 45-46), PDF pp. 64-65 (https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2022/214985Orig1s000IntegratedR.pdf)

> "The primary endpoints (LPS and WASO) were observed to have a skewed distribution, see Figure 41, Figure 42, Figure 43, and Figure 44. The prespecified mixed model for repeated measures (MMRM) model assumed a normal error distribution. When the assumption of normal error distribution is violated, the model standard errors may be overestimated. While overestimation of the standard error does not inflate the type I error, the statistical power may be impacted. FDA is less concerned about type II errors; however, in this case, the clinical team was concerned about insufficient evidence to support the LPS endpoint. To explore if there is evidence for violation of the normality assumption, quantile-quantile plots (Q-Q plot) for each MMRM model’s residuals were visually inspected. In a normal Q-Q plot, normally distributed residuals will fall on a 45-degree line. Deviations from this diagonal line indicate lack of normality in the residuals. In Figure 45, the residuals for the prespecified MMRM analysis (Trial ID-078A302, LPS endpoint) deviate from the 45-degree line. For points with a theoretical residual with a predicted quantile greater than 1, the observed residuals are greater than the theoretical residual. This pattern suggests that a log transformation or similar data transformation may provide a better model fit. In Figure 46, a Q-Q plot for the residuals from a MMRM analysis with log-transformed LPS in Trial ID-078A302 indicates a better model fit because the residuals fall on a 45-degree line. Similar results are seen for the Trial ID- 078A301 LPS endpoint and both WASO endpoints. While the model fit is improved by log transforming the outcome data, all statistical inference should be made on the originally specified normal outcome distribution in order to protect the type I error because the log transformation is made after seeing the data."
>
> — FDA Integrated Review, §16.2 Statistical Model Assumptions Assessment, PDF p. 278 (https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2022/214985Orig1s000IntegratedR.pdf)

##### Model 3: Change in SDLP (standard deviation of lateral position) on Days 2 and 5 (supportive (safety/clin-pharm))

> "The assay sensitivity and the primary driving endpoint were analyzed based on an MMRM with treatment, study day, period, sex, age group (50 to 64 and 65 to 80 years), and the interaction of treatment by study day as fixed effects, and subject as a random effect. An unstructured covariance matrix was used to account for the correlation between repeated measurements from the same subject. The model effects were estimated from the least square mean differences for each of the hypotheses (i.e., for H0, the difference in the least square means between daridorexant [50 and 100 mg] and placebo on Days 2 and 5, based on the same MMRM). The least squares mean, difference in least square means of each daridorexant dose compared to placebo, 95% confidence intervals, and p-values were calculated. Statistical Reviewer Comment: The Applicant used an equivalence test to compare daridorexant to placebo. An equivalence test places the hypothesis of no difference in the alternative hypothesis. In this construction, rejection of the null hypothesis implies no difference between drug and placebo."
>
> — FDA Integrated Review, Study ID-078-108 (driving study), PDF p. 301 (https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2022/214985Orig1s000IntegratedR.pdf)

##### Model 4: Drug Liking VAS Emax and other PD endpoints (supportive (safety/clin-pharm))

> "Analysis of primary and secondary endpoints were performed using a mixed-effect ANOVA model. The model was to include treatment, period, and treatment sequence as fixed effects, and baseline (pre-dose) measurement as a covariate where applicable, and subject nested within sequence as a random effect. A first-order direct carry-over effect from the treatment of the previous period was included in the model if it was found significant at 25% level. For the first treatment period, treatment ‘A’ was used for all subjects and all PD endpoints. From each model, least squares means and CIs were provided for each treatment; and difference in least squares mean, CIs of the difference, and p-values were provided for each treatment comparison. The assumption of normal distribution of the data required for the ANOVA model was examined using a Shapiro-Wilk W normality test on the residuals from the mixed-effect model. Parameters were analyzed under the assumption of a normal distribution if the p-value of the test was ≥ 0.05."
>
> — FDA Integrated Review, human abuse potential study, PDF p. 359 (https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2022/214985Orig1s000IntegratedR.pdf)

#### Verbatim specification excerpts

##### Model 1: Rate of decline (slope) of ALSFRS-R total score over 24 weeks; same model for all continuous secondary/exploratory endpoints (ATLIS, SVC, pNF-H, etc.) (primary (and secondary))

> "The primary efficacy endpoint is the rate of decline (slope) in the ALSFRS-R over time. The placebo and AMX0035 arms were compared by a shared-baseline, linear mixed effects analysis. FDA has traditionally had concerns with the use of a slope analysis because of questions regarding the assumptions of linearity of the ALSFRS-R over time. With such an approach, sensitivity analyses allowing for non-linearity are important. The Applicant reported that historical analyses have shown ALS to be a disease with linear progression over time. However, the Applicant also noted that linearity could not be assumed at this point for the study given the unknown effect of the treatment, and therefore, to confirm linearity, the primary analysis model would be modified to include quadratic terms for time. If the quadratic terms for time were not significant (p-value > 0.10) then linearity would be assumed, and the linear primary model would be used for the primary analysis. If any one of the interaction terms is significant (p-value < 0.10), then the quadratic version of the model would be used."
>
> — FDA Summary Review, Statistical Analysis, PDF p. 13 (https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2022/216660Orig1s000SumR.pdf)

> "FDA typically recommends the use of a combined analysis of function and survival, such as the joint rank analysis of the ALSFRS-R, as the primary analysis in ALS. FDA has long indicated that deaths may cause bias if ignored in the primary analysis since some deaths are expected in the double-blind period. Missing data as a result of death are not missing at random, and therefore not appropriate to impute data after death. The advice to use a combined analysis of function and survival, such as a joint rank analysis, was provided to the Applicant at the pre-IND meeting and in an advice email after review of the SAP in March 2019. A joint rank analysis was later conducted by the Applicant as a post hoc analysis."
>
> — FDA Summary Review, Statistical Analysis, PDF p. 13 (https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2022/216660Orig1s000SumR.pdf)

> "As described in Dr. Massie’s review, all continuous primary, secondary, and exploratory efficacy measures were to use the same statistical model and were to be presented in hierarchical order. Covariates of age, rate of disease progression prior to entering the trial (del- FS) and change of the efficacy outcome being measured (if other than ALSFRS-R) interacting with time were to be included in the analysis. The analyses of the secondary endpoints have the same concerns as the primary analysis of not incorporating deaths. The use of a joint rank analysis would be applicable to these endpoints as well."
>
> — FDA Summary Review, Statistical Analysis, PDF p. 13 (https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2022/216660Orig1s000SumR.pdf)

> "The Applicant met its prespecified primary endpoint, demonstrating a statistically significant (p = 0.034) slowing of disease progression as measured by the ALSFRS-R total score compared to placebo, at the end of the 24-week, randomized, controlled phase of the study. The estimated least squares (LS) mean ALSFRS-R total score was 2.32 points higher at Week 24 compared to placebo. The primary prespecified model was a shared baseline, linear, mixed effects model, as noted in Table 2."
>
> — FDA Summary Review, Primary Endpoint, PDF p. 16 (https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2022/216660Orig1s000SumR.pdf)

> "Dr. Massie also used the primary analysis to check for the impact of individual sites, and found more influential sites, some of which affected the significance of the treatment difference. In other words, the removal of a single site from the study renders the primary analysis treatment effect no longer statistically significant [e.g., without site 701 (n = 13): slope difference = -0.079; SE=0.049; p=0.1027 with a corresponding Week 24 mean difference of 1.90]. This particular site had a within site estimated treatment difference more than twice as large as the overall estimate (5.75 vs 2.32). Dr. Massie also notes that this same site had a substantive quantitative difference for time to death in the OLE phase, with a within- site hazard ratio (0.23, drug over placebo) more than two times smaller than the overall hazard ratio (0.64)."
>
> — FDA Summary Review, Primary Endpoint, PDF p. 18 (https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2022/216660Orig1s000SumR.pdf)

##### Model 2: Change from baseline in ALSFRS-R at Week 24 (sensitivity (FDA reviewer reanalysis))

> "In a sensitivity analysis, Dr. Massie used a more common model frequently used in FDA review work, a Mean-By-Visit MMRM model of change from baseline which does not rely on a linearity assumption. This model also does not incorporate deaths in the analysis. This analysis did not show a nominally significant treatment difference in ALSFRS-R at Week 24 in the mITT population, with an estimated difference of 1.86 (SE 1.04), p = 0.0749."
>
> — FDA Summary Review, Primary Endpoint, PDF p. 18 (https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2022/216660Orig1s000SumR.pdf)

### Lecanemab-irmb (Leqembi) — BLA 761269

Therapeutic area: Neurology / Psychiatry. Sponsor: Eisai Inc.. Approval year: 2023.

Entry notes: Study 301 sponsor Table 5 (CDR-SB) is an image; FDA's own reproduced FAS analysis is in text. Study 201's primary analysis was Bayesian (NDLM dose-response with longitudinal imputation); MMRM was the 'conventional' analysis.

#### Model 1: Change from baseline in CDR-SB at 18 months (Week 79) (primary)


- **Trial:** CLARITY-AD (Study 301), NCT03887455
- **Endpoint/timepoint:** Change from baseline in CDR-SB at 18 months (Week 79)
- **Role:** primary
- **Model family:** MMRM
- **Response:** Change from baseline CDR-SB
- **Fixed effects:** Baseline CDR-SB (covariate), treatment group, visit, stratification variables (clinical subgroup, AD symptomatic medication at baseline, APOE4 carrier status, geographical region), baseline CDR-SB-by-visit, treatment-by-visit [s001 StatR §3.2.1.2 verbatim]; actual (not IxRS) stratification data
- **Random effects:** None stated
- **Covariance:** Unstructured
- **Covariance fallback:** Heterogeneous Toeplitz -> heterogeneous compound symmetry -> Toeplitz -> compound symmetry; if a structured matrix is used, sandwich estimator for treatment-effect variance [verbatim: 'If a structured covariance is used, then the sandwich estimator was to be used to estimate variance of the treatment effect estimator']
- **Denominator df:** Not stated
- **Estimation:** Not stated
- **Time coding:** Categorical visit
- **Estimand / contrast:** LS-mean difference at 18 months, FAS; all observed post-baseline data without imputation
- **Missing data:** MAR
- **MNAR / sensitivity:** Rank ANCOVA after MI (1000 imputations, seed=2401, MAR); tipping point with treatment-specific shifts (delta_c, delta_t) added to MI values, rank ANCOVA, Rubin's rules; also IxRS-strata version, FAS+/PP, APOE4 carriers, censoring at discontinuation/AD-med change
- **Software:** Not stated
- **Results:** Applicant (FAS+): adjusted mean difference -0.451, 27.1% less decline, p=0.00005. FDA FAS (COVID site exclusions), Week 78 n=719 PBO/693 LEC: adjusted means 1.603 (SE 0.081) vs 1.208 (0.082); difference -0.394 (95% CI -0.613,-0.176), p=0.00040, -24.6%. ApoE4 homozygotes: +0.25 (SE 0.28; 95% CI -0.30,0.80), interaction p=0.017.
- **FDA comments:** Massie: tipping point 1.5 (sponsor, half-point grid), ~1.1 with finer grid; 0.5 when data after ARIA-E and/or AD-med changes censored (39.5% vs 28.2% missing). Deaths ignored but few. Study 301 'appears to confirm the clinical benefit'.
- **Specification source:** StatR verbatim (s001 Statistical Review §3.2.1.2)
