#### Verbatim specification excerpts

##### Model 1: Change from baseline in CDR-SB at 18 months (Week 79) (primary)

> "The estimand (International Council for Harmonisation of Technical Requirements of Pharmaceuticals of Human Use [ICH] E9 [R1], 2019) of the primary analysis is the mean difference of the change from baseline in CDR-SB at 18 months between treatment groups on FAS. All observed data were to be included in the primary analysis, including data collected after intercurrent events (ICH E9 [R1], 2019), i.e., initiation of new AD concomitant treatment or change of AD concomitant treatment or treatment discontinuation. The primary analysis of the change from baseline in CDR-SB at 18 months was to be performed to compare BAN2401 versus placebo using an MMRM on the FAS. The MMRM was to include baseline CDR-SB as a covariate, with treatment group, visit, stratification variables (i.e., clinical subgroup, use of AD symptomatic medication at baseline [yes, no], APOE4 carrier status [carriers, noncarriers], and geographical region [North America, Europe, and Asia Pacific]), baseline CDR-SB-by-visit, and treatment group-by-visit interaction as fixed effects. For stratification variables, actual data (laboratory data for APOE4 carrier status, CRF data for clinical subgroup and use of AD symptomatic medication at baseline, and IxRS data for geographical region) were to be used. An unstructured covariance matrix was to be employed to model the covariance of within-subject effect; if MMRM fails to converge then a covariance structure with fewer parameters from the following list was to be employed according to the prespecified order in the list until the MMRM converges. The list of covariance structure was to include Heterogeneous Toeplitz, Heterogeneous Compound Symmetry, Toeplitz, and Compound Symmetry. If a structured covariance is used, then the sandwich estimator was to be used to estimate variance of the treatment effect estimator. This primary analysis was to include all observed postbaseline data of the change from baseline CDR-SB without imputation of missing values. The treatment effect for BAN2401 versus placebo was to be compared at 18 months based on the MMRM. The least squares (LS) means (adjusted means) and difference in LS means (adjusted mean difference) between BAN2401 treatment and placebo, and corresponding 95% confidence interval (CI) were to be presented."
>
> — FDA s001 review package (Statistical Review, Study 301), Statistical Review (Massie) §3.2.1.2, Primary Estimand, PDF pp. 379-380 (https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2024/761269Orig1s001.pdf)

> "The following sensitivity analyses were to be conducted to assess the robustness of the primary analysis to missing data: • The sensitivity analysis using rank analysis of covariance (ANCOVA) after multiple imputations (MIs) at 18 months was to be performed. The imputation model was to be a regression model including the following variables: baseline and post baseline observed values, treatment group, and stratification variables (ie, clinical subgroup, use of AD symptomatic medication at baseline, APOE4 carrier status, and geographical region). Missing data was to be imputed via the imputation model using the standard MI method assuming missing at random (MAR) (Rubin 1987). After 1000 imputations with prespecified random seed (seed=2401), rank ANCOVA was to be performed using imputed datasets. The rank ANCOVA model was to include baseline CDR-SB as a covariate, with treatment group and stratification variables (ie, clinical subgroup, use of AD symptomatic medication at baseline, APOE4 carrier status, and geographical region) as factors. Analysis results from the imputed datasets were to then be combined based on Rubin’s rules (Rubin, 1987). The Hodges- Lehmann estimate of median difference and its 95% CI were also to be calculated using imputed datasets and combined based on Rubin’s rules (Rubin, 1987). • Tipping point analysis using shift parameter (delta) separately for each treatment group based on MIs was to be performed. The missing data are first imputed by the imputation model specified from the rank ANCOVA after MIs approach (assuming missing at random) with prespecified random seed (seed=2401). To reflect the worse performance after early withdrawal, pre-specified shift parameters δ_c and δ_t are added to the imputed values for subjects on placebo and BAN2401 treatment, respectively. The adjusted multiple imputed datasets were then to be analyzed by a rank ANCOVA model and the results were to be combined using the Rubin’s rule for inference. The p-value was to be provided for each pair of shift parameters (δ_c, δ_t). The robustness of the primary analysis outcomes was to be evaluated based on the scientific plausibility of the tipping point. • The analysis using the same model as the primary analysis with just one change which is using randomization stratification variables based on IxRS classification (instead of actual data) was to be conducted."
>
> — FDA s001 review package (Statistical Review, Study 301), Statistical Review (Massie) §3.2.1.2, Sensitivity Analyses, PDF pp. 380-381 (https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2024/761269Orig1s001.pdf)

> "The following supplementary analyses were to be conducted to assess the robustness of the primary analysis: • It is postulated that BAN2401 treatment will demonstrate a clinically meaningful effect on the clinical outcome measures assessed for the overall population. However, a greater magnitude of effect is expected for the APOE4 carrier population based on the BAN2401 mechanism of action and the fact that increased levels of toxic soluble Aβ aggregate species have been noted in human APOE4 carrier pathological specimens compared to noncarriers (Hashimoto et. al., 2012, Tai et al., 2013). Further support is provided from Study 201 data. Therefore, the analysis using the same model as the primary analysis was to also be performed for the change from baseline in the CDR-SB at 18 months in APOE4 carriers on the FAS. • The analysis using the same model as the primary analysis was to be performed on the FAS+ and the Per Protocol Analysis Set. • The analysis using the same model as the primary analysis was to be performed on the FAS where subjects were to be censored at the time of treatment discontinuation or initiation of new AChEIs or memantine treatment regimens if they were not on AChEIs or memantine at randomization, and were to be censored at the time of dose adjustment of AChEIs or memantine if they were already on stable treatment with AChEIs or memantine at randomization."
>
> — FDA s001 review package (Statistical Review, Study 301), Statistical Review (Massie) §3.2.1.2, supplementary analyses, PDF p. 381 (https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2024/761269Orig1s001.pdf)

> "For the MMRM analysis, missing data were assumed to be missing at random. Different assumptions for missing data were explored as part of sensitivity analyses."
>
> — FDA s001 review package (Statistical Review, Study 301), clinical/integrated section, Missing Data, PDF p. 137 (https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2024/761269Orig1s001.pdf)

> "In the FAS analysis set for FDA with prespecified exclusions of sites due to COVID pandemic the results were as follows. At week 78 sample sizes non-missing were 719 and 693 Adjusted mean (SE) were 1.603 (0.081) and 1.208 (0.082) Adjusted mean difference: Lecanemab - Placebo -0.394 95% Confidence interval for differences: -0.613, -0.176 P-value: 0.00040 % Difference vs. Placebo: -24.6%"
>
> — FDA s001 review package (Statistical Review, Study 301), Statistical Review (Massie) FDA FAS results, PDF p. 388 (https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2024/761269Orig1s001.pdf)

> "Twenty two (2.5%) placebo and 39 (4.3%) lecanemab had no post-baseline efficacy assessments and were therefore not in the FAS+ (or FAS agreed with FDA population on which the primary analysis was based). There were 8 placebo and 7 lecanemab deaths in the ITT population by Week 79, of which 5 and 7, respectively, were in the FAS+ population. Ignoring these bad outcomes in the primary analysis could potentially cause bias in the primary analysis, but the proportion of deaths is low enough for any corresponding bias to be small. Tipping point sensitivity analyses for missing data based on multiple imputations using shift parameters (delta) for informative missingness, separately for each treatment group for generating outcomes for missing data were performed. The robustness of the primary analysis outcomes was evaluated based on the scientific plausibility of the tipping point. The applicant reported a tipping point of 1.5 for the FAS+ population, meaning missing outcomes would have to have a 1.5 point worse shift on CDR-SB for lecanemab than the shift for placebo missing outcomes in order for the primary analysis to lose significance, assuming no informative missingness for placebo. The sponsor used half point increments for the shift parameter. If smaller shifts are considered the tipping point is closer to 1 than 1.5, being about 1.1. The tipping point is lower if data after both ARIA-E and/or changes in concomitant AD medications are censored. In the overall population, 5.7% of subjects were on an AD symptomatic medication but did not remain on a stable dose during the study with similar rates seen for PBO (6.2%) and LEC10-BW (5.2%). In the overall population, 7.3% of subjects started a new AD symptomatic medication regardless of use at Baseline, which was similar in PBO (7.5%) and LEC10-BW (7.1%). If data after both ARIA-E and/or changes in concomitant AD medications are censored there is 39.5% missing at Week 79 for lecanemab and 28.2% for placebo and the tipping point for the primary analysis of CDR-SB is 0.5 meaning under the assumption that missing or censored lecanemab Week 79 outcomes would be 0.5 worse on CDR- SB than observed data in the lecanemab group for patients who had no ARIA or changes in concomitant AD medications with the same covariates as the affected subject."
>
> — FDA s001 review package (Statistical Review, Study 301), Statistical Review (Massie) §3.2.1.4.2 Reviewer’s Results, PDF pp. 390-391 (https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2024/761269Orig1s001.pdf)

##### Model 3: Change from baseline in ADCOMS at 12 months (conventional analysis); key secondaries at 18 months (secondary (conventional analysis supporting Bayesian primary))

> "Statistical methods for the final conventional analyses were to use a mixed effects model with repeated measures on the change from baseline in the derived ADCOMS at 12 months. The model was to include baseline ADCOMS as covariate, with treatment group, visit, randomization stratification variables (i.e., clinical subgroup [MCI due to AD, Mild Alzheimer’s Disease Dementia], the presence or absence of ongoing AD treatment [ AChEIs or memantine or both], APOE4 status [positive, negative]), region, treatment group-by-visit interaction as fixed effects. An unstructured covariance matrix was to be employed to model the covariance of within subject effects. These analyses were to be performed on the full analysis set as well as the per protocol set. The analysis was only to be performed at early success or at the end of 12 months assessment using all randomized subjects in the Full Analysis Set. There was to be no conventional analysis at each interim analysis before early success is claimed and as such the applicant felt that there was to be no multiplicity adjustment needed to account for the interim analyses."
>
> — FDA Statistical Review (s000, Study 201), Conventional Analyses, PDF p. 15 (https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2023/761269Orig1s000StatR.pdf)

> "Conventional analysis was to be performed using all available data at the time of success (if applicable), and at 18 months of treatment, regardless of success. Conventional analysis was to be based on the MMRM model including baseline as covariate, with treatment group, visit, randomization stratification variables (i.e., clinical subgroup [MCI due to AD, Mild Alzheimer’s Disease Dementia], the presence or absence of ongoing AD treatment [AChEIs or memantine or both], APOE4 status [positive, negative]), region, treatment group-by-visit interaction as fixed effects. If there is an imbalance across treatment groups based on randomization stratification variables, an additional MMRM model was to be run without the randomization stratification variables. In addition, an ANCOVA model was also to be used with treatment as a factor and baseline value as a covariate. These statistical models were to be used to compare the combined 10 mg dose group (including bi-weekly and monthly regimens) with placebo for the key secondary endpoints. The rationale for combining the two 10 mg dose regimens was to account for the loss of subjects positive for APOE4 in the 10 mg/kg biweekly dose group and the inability to randomize APOE4 carriers to the 10 mg/kg biweekly group following a regulatory request by European Health Authorities in July 2014."
>
> — FDA Statistical Review (s000, Study 201), Key Secondary Endpoint Analyses, PDF p. 17 (https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2023/761269Orig1s000StatR.pdf)

> "The conventional MMRM analyses (censored at the time of initiation or change of AChEIs or memantine treatment regimens) in the Full Analysis Set are as follows. In the individual treatment group analysis the LS mean changes from Baseline in ADCOMS at 18 months were 0.193 for placebo, and 0.173, 0.192, 0.199, 0.166, and 0.136 for BAN2401 2.5 mg/kg biweekly, 5 mg/kg monthly, 5 mg/kg biweekly, 10 mg/kg monthly, and 10 mg/kg biweekly groups, respectively. The respective LS mean differences from placebo for the individual BAN2401 treatment groups were -0.020, -0.001, 0.006, -0.028, and -0.057 for the 2.5 mg/kg biweekly, 5 mg/kg monthly, 5 mg/kg biweekly, 10 mg/kg monthly, and 10 mg/kg biweekly groups, respectively. The LS mean difference of -0.057 (P=0.034; 90% CI: -0.102, -0.013) for 10 mg/kg biweekly showed 30% less decline than placebo."

> — FDA Statistical Review (s000, Study 201), Conventional Analyses on ADCOMS at 18 Months, PDF p. 29 (https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2023/761269Orig1s000StatR.pdf)

##### Model 4: Change from baseline in amyloid PET SUVr (whole cerebellum reference) at 18 months (secondary (accelerated-approval surrogate evidence))

> "PD Analysis Set 2 is the group of subjects who had sufficient amyloid PET data to derive at least 1 amyloid PET parameter. The change from Baseline and percentage change from Baseline in brain amyloid level parameters were analyzed using the MMRM with treatment group/combined treatment groups, visit, disease stage (MCI due to AD, Mild AD), the presence or absence of concomitant AD treatment (AChEIs and/or memantine) at Baseline, ApoE4 status (positive, negative), region, treatment group by- visit interaction as factors, and Baseline brain amyloid levels as covariate. The mixed-effects model within each randomization stratum (subgroup) was similar and was reduced by removing corresponding stratification factor from the model in overall population. SUVr of global cortical average with respect to reference region. Only PET data using florbetapir tracer was included. AChEIs = acetylcholinesterase inhibitor, AD = Alzheimer’s disease, ApoE4 = apolipoprotein є4 variant, LS = least square, MCI = mild cognitive impairment, MMRM = mixed-effects model with repeated measures, PD = pharmacodynamics, PET = positron emission tomography, SUVr = standard uptake value ratio. a: P-values for comparing each combined BAN2401 group versus the placebo group. b: adjusted P-values based on Dunnett-Hsu method (see Section 9.7.1.6.2)."

### Trofinetide (Daybue) — NDA 217026

Therapeutic area: Neurology / Psychiatry. Sponsor: Acadia Pharmaceuticals. Approval year: 2023.

Entry notes: CGI-I (a 7-point ordinal score, not a change score) was analyzed by MMRM with baseline CGI-S as covariate. FDA reproduced analyses in R with Satterthwaite-type df, giving RSBQ LSMD -3.2, p=0.0157 vs applicant (SAS, Kenward-Roger) -3.1, p=0.0175. FDA reviewer noted including both baseline RSBQ and RSBQ severity stratum 'may be redundant'.

#### Model 1: Change from baseline to Week 12 in RSBQ total score (primary (co-primary))


- **Trial:** LAVENDER (ACP-2566-003), NCT04181723
- **Endpoint/timepoint:** Change from baseline to Week 12 in RSBQ total score
- **Role:** primary (co-primary)
- **Model family:** MMRM
- **Response:** Change from baseline RSBQ total
- **Fixed effects:** Treatment, baseline RSBQ severity stratum (<35/>=35), visit, baseline value, age group (5-10, 11-15, 16-20), treatment-by-visit, baseline-by-visit [StatR §3.2.2 verbatim]
- **Random effects:** None stated
- **Covariance:** Unstructured [StatR Table 6 footnote: 'An unstructured matrix was used to model within-subject errors']
- **Covariance fallback:** Not stated
- **Denominator df:** Kenward-Roger (sponsor); FDA used R with approximate Satterthwaite [Table 6 footnote]
- **Estimation:** Not stated
- **Time coding:** Categorical visit
- **Estimand / contrast:** LS-mean difference at Week 12, FAS; both co-primaries p<0.05 required
- **Missing data:** MAR
- **MNAR / sensitivity:** J2R/PMM-MNAR: trofinetide missing values imputed from placebo-completer model, 50 imputations, ANCOVA, Rubin's rules: -2.7 (SE 1.29), p=0.0338; COVID-19 MAR PMM variant -2.7, p=0.0406. Tipping-point analysis removed in SAP Amendment 2.

- **Results:** N=93 PBO/91 TROF (FAS). LS mean CFB -1.7 (SE 0.90) vs -4.9 (0.94); LSMD -3.2 (SE 1.30; 95% CI -5.7,-0.6), p=0.0157 (FDA) / -3.1, p=0.0175 (applicant); Cohen's d 0.37 [StatR Table 6, 9]
- **FDA comments:** Differential dropout 24.7% vs 9.6%; J2R p-values larger but <0.05; RSBQ not validated as endpoint so magnitude hard to interpret.
- **Specification source:** StatR verbatim (§3.2.2, Table 6 footnote)

#### Verbatim specification excerpts

##### Model 1: Change from baseline to Week 12 in RSBQ total score (primary (co-primary))

> "The primary endpoints were analyzed using a mixed effects model for repeated measured (MMRM) with fixed effects of treatment group, baseline RSBQ severity (<35 total score vs ≥ 35 total score), visit, baseline value (RSBQ for RSBQ endpoint and CGI-S for the CGI-I endpoint), age group (5-10 years old, 11-15 years old, and 16-20 years old), treatment by visit interaction terms, and baseline value by visit interaction terms with an unstructured covariance matrix. Treatment effects and standards errors are estimated with least square means (LS mean). The Applicant controlled for multiple comparisons by requiring both co-primary endpoints to have a p-value < 0.05 to declare success in the study. Also, the key secondary endpoint was only tested if both co-primary endpoints were significant at alpha = 0.05. The Applicant explored the impact of violations of the missing at random assumption for the missing data using a reference-based imputation model where missing data from the trofinetide arm was imputed using an imputation model built from the placebo completer data. Reviewer’s Note: The design and statistical analysis plan of Study 003 is adequate to assess the efficacy of trofinetide. The Applicant included both RSBQ score at baseline and RSBQ severity strata at baseline in the model analysis model because of the randomization plan. Having both terms in the model may be redundant"
>
> — FDA Statistical Review, §3.2.2 (Study 003), PDF p. 13 (https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2023/217026Orig1s000StatR.pdf)

> "In amendment 2 to the SAP, the Applicant removed the tipping point sensitivity analyses. In addition, a sensitivity analysis exploring the impact of COVID-19 was added."
>
> — FDA Statistical Review, §3.2.2.1 Protocol Amendments, PDF p. 13 (https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2023/217026Orig1s000StatR.pdf)

> "The MMRM included age group, baseline RSBQ severity, planned treatment, study visit, treatment-by-visit interaction, Baseline-by- visit interaction, and Baseline total score as fixed effects. An unstructured matrix was used to model within-subject errors. Sponsor used Kenward-Roger method for calculating the denominator degrees of freedom for tests of fixed effects. The statistics are slightly off by using R with approximate Satterwaite method for estimating the degrees of freedom."
>
> — FDA Statistical Review, Table 6 footnote, PDF p. 17 (https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2023/217026Orig1s000StatR.pdf)

> "The Applicant conducted jump to reference (J2R) sensitivity analyses for both primary endpoints (CFB RSBQ and CGI-I). Their J2R analysis imputed missing observations in trofinetide subjects by creating an imputation model from the placebo subjects who completed the study. With this imputation model, the applicant imputed 50 datasets which were then analyzed using an ANCOVA model that adjusted for the same baseline factors as the primary analysis. The results of these 50 analyses were combined using Rubin’s Rules, see Appendix for details. Table 9 presented the results of multiple sensitivity analyses. The J2R sensitivity analyses are contained in the row labeled PMM-MNAR. For both the CFB12 in RSBQ and CGI-I at Week 12, both p-values are larger than the MMRM analysis (first row in Table 9). However, this increased p-value is still below 0.05. Therefore, the small numbers missing data (effective rate of about 10%) may not impact overall efficacy conclusions."
>
> — FDA Statistical Review, Sensitivity Analyses, Missing Data, PDF p. 21 (https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2023/217026Orig1s000StatR.pdf)

> "Reviewer’s Note: The Applicant’s J2R sensitivity is useful to explore the impact of missing data under the assumption that the trofinetide dropouts look similar to the placebo completers. However, if the trofinetide dropouts do worse than the placebo completers, the J2R sensitivity may not fully explore the potential impact of the missing data. For Study 003, the small percentage of dropouts limits the impact of missing data."
>
> — FDA Statistical Review, Sensitivity Analyses, Reviewer’s Note, PDF p. 23 (https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2023/217026Orig1s000StatR.pdf)

> "The sensitivity analysis is implemented for Full Analysis Set using multiple imputations that are based on the distribution of placebo group responses over time to account for the intercurrent event of treatment discontinuations and missing assessments. The underlying assumption is that subjects with missing data due to early withdrawal evolve in the same way as placebo subjects that remain in the study. The following steps are involved, and the imputed values will be constrained to be within the limits of 0 - 90 for RSBQ total score and 1 - 7 for CGI-I score: • Non-monotone (intermediate) missing data at Baseline (not applicable for CGI-I score), Week 2, Week 6, and Week 12 will be multiply imputed using the Markov chain Monte Carlo (MCMC) method to create 50 monotone datasets. The imputation models for post baseline RSBQ total score and CGI-I score will include effects as follows: Post baseline RSBQ total score: age group (5-10 years old, 11-15 years old, and 16-20 years old), Baseline RSBQ severity (<35 total score and ≥35 total score), Baseline RSBQ total score, and treatment group CGI-I score: age group (5-10 years old, 11-15 years old, and 16-20 years old), Baseline RSBQ severity (<35 total score and ≥35 total score), Baseline CGI-S score, and treatment group. • The monotone missing data will be imputed using a parametric, sequential linear regression method in which the missing data are imputed only on data from the placebo arm. A single imputation will be performed sequentially at each visit for each of the 50 imputed datasets. The predictors and their order in the PROC MI VAR statement for each visit are summarized in Table 5. The following SAS codes are to impute missing observations using the control-based pattern imputation method."
>
> — FDA Statistical Review, Appendix 1, PMM-MNAR, PDF p. 35 (https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2023/217026Orig1s000StatR.pdf)

```sas
proc mi data=xxxx seed=2566003 nimpute=1 out=outname;
 by _Imputation_;
 class Trt Baseline_RSBQ_severity Age_group;
 monotone reg (/details);
 mnar model( W2_RSBQ W6_RSBQ W12_RSBQ / modelobs= (Trt='Placebo')); var
Age_group Baseline_RSBQ_severity Baseline_RSBQ W2_RSBQ W6_RSBQ
W12_RSBQ;
run;
```

— FDA Statistical Review, Appendix 1, PMM-MNAR SAS code (RSBQ), PDF pp. 35-36 (https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2023/217026Orig1s000StatR.pdf)

> "The change from Baseline to each post baseline visit values will then be calculated and analyzed for each of the 50 fully imputed datasets using the analysis of co-variance (ANCOVA) model. The ANCOVA model for RSBQ total score will have treatment group, Baseline RSBQ severity, and age group as fixed factors and Baseline RSBQ total score as a covariate; the ANCOVA model for CGI-I score will have treatment group, age group, and Baseline RSBQ severity as fixed factors and Baseline CGI-S score as a covariate. • The results will be summarized by post baseline visit using the SAS MIANALYZE procedure to yield a combined estimate for treatment effect with its associated 95% confidence interval (CI) and p-value."
>
> — FDA Statistical Review, Appendix 1, PMM-MNAR, PDF p. 36 (https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2023/217026Orig1s000StatR.pdf)

> "Coprimary and key secondary efficacy endpoints were analyzed using the MMRM method assuming data missing at random. The MMRM included randomization strata of age group and baseline RSBQ severity score, baseline RSBQ (for RSBQ analysis), baseline CGI-S (for CGI-I scale analysis) and baseline CSBS-DP-IT Social Composite score (for the key secondary endpoint), treatment, visit, treatment-by-visit interaction and baseline-by-visit interaction as fixed effects and participant as a random effect; an unstructured covariance matrix modeled within-participant errors. The Kenward–Roger method was used for calculating denominator degrees of freedom for tests of fixed effects. Each coprimary endpoint was considered positive if P ≤ 0.05, and both must be positive for the study to be positive. If both coprimary endpoints were positive, the key secondary endpoint was also considered positive if P ≤ 0.05 and was statistically controlled for type 1 error at 5% through a hierarchical sequential gatekeeper procedure. Effect size was determined with Cohen’s d 23 . Sensitivity analyses of the coprimary endpoints included multiple imputations based on pattern-mixture models assuming missing not at random using the analysis of covariance method, the use of actual derived baseline values for randomization strata (MMRM) and visits impacted by COVID-19 (analysis of covariance); a supportive analysis (MMRM) used the per-protocol analysis set."
>
> — Neul et al. 2023, Nat Med (Europe PMC full text), Methods, Statistical analysis, PDF p. 1 (https://www.ebi.ac.uk/europepmc/webservices/rest/PMC10287558/fullTextXML)

> "Statistical analyses were performed using version 9.4 of SAS."
>
> — Neul et al. 2023, Nat Med (Europe PMC full text), Methods, Statistical analysis, PDF p. 1 (https://www.ebi.ac.uk/europepmc/webservices/rest/PMC10287558/fullTextXML)

### Rozanolixizumab-noli (Rystiggo) — BLA 761286

Therapeutic area: Neurology / Psychiatry. Sponsor: UCB Inc.. Approval year: 2023.

Entry notes: Unusual specification: the MMRM included 'study subject as a random effect' AND an unstructured covariance for repeated measures (random intercept on top of UN R-matrix), fitted stagewise and combined via Lehmacher-Wassmer inverse-normal p-values with repeated CIs.

#### Model 1: Change from baseline in MG-ADL to Day 43 (primary)


- **Trial:** MycarinG (MG0003), NCT03971422
- **Endpoint/timepoint:** Change from baseline in MG-ADL to Day 43
- **Role:** primary
- **Model family:** MMRM (stagewise, combined across 2 adaptive stages)
- **Response:** Change from baseline MG-ADL
- **Fixed effects:** Treatment group, baseline MG-ADL, region, stratification factors AChR(+/-) and MuSK(+/-), treatment-by-day [IR §6.2.2.3 verbatim]
- **Random effects:** Study subject [IR verbatim: 'as fixed factors and study subject as a random effect']
- **Covariance:** Unstructured for repeated measures (Days 8, 15, 22, 29, 36, 43)
- **Covariance fallback:** Not stated
- **Denominator df:** Not stated
- **Estimation:** Not stated
- **Time coding:** Categorical day
- **Estimand / contrast:** LS-mean difference at Day 43; hypothetical + treatment-policy strategies for ICEs; stagewise inverse-normal combination (Lehmacher-Wassmer) of independent stagewise p-values; multiplicity-adjusted repeated 95% CIs; parallel gatekeeping with truncated Hochberg
- **Missing data:** MAR
- **MNAR / sensitivity:** Jump-to-reference imputation (randomized set); composite strategy with trimmed-mean imputation (supplementary); FAS, all-6-doses subgroup, COVID-excluded subgroup - all consistent

#### Verbatim specification excerpts

##### Model 1: Change from baseline in MG-ADL to Day 43 (primary)

> "The primary efficacy analysis of the primary endpoint was conducted with a stagewise mixed model repeated measures (MMRM) using an inverse-normal method of combining independent stagewise p-values. The model included treatment group, baseline MG-ADL score, region, stratification factors including AChR(+/-) and MuSK(+/-), and treatment group by day (interaction term) as fixed factors and study subject as a random effect. The MMRM included days 8, 15, 22, 29, 36 and 43. An unstructured covariance matrix was used for the repeated measures. Missing data were handled under a missing at random assumption using a hypothetical and treatment policy strategy to handle intercurrent events (ICEs). The combined p-value (2-sided) for the two stages was based on the stagewise inverse-normal combination of independent stagewise p-values using the Lehmacher and Wassmer method. The multiplicity adjusted 95% Cis were provided for the differences in least squares (LS) mean change from baseline in MG-ADL score to day 43 (visit 10) between rozanolixizumab groups and placebo. The lower bound of the 2-sided 95% repeated confidence interval for a given treatment group was found as the smallest value for which the multiplicity-adjusted combination test yields nonrejection at a two-sided alpha =5%. The upper bound of the confidence interval was found analogously."
>
> — FDA Integrated Review, Study MG0003 statistical methods, PDF p. 61 (https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2023/761286Orig1s000IntegratedR.pdf)

> "All results in Table 18 below were from the combined MMRM, except Cis and p-values, which were based on the stagewise inverse-normal combination using the Lehmacher and Wassmer method."
>
> — FDA Integrated Review, §6.2.2.4, Table 18 and text, PDF p. 68 (https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2023/761286Orig1s000IntegratedR.pdf)

> "The following sensitivity analyses were repeated for the primary endpoint: • Sensitivity Analysis #1: the full analysis set (FAS) using the hypothetical and treatment policy strategy to handle intercurrent events (ICEs) • Sensitivity Analysis #2: the randomized set using a jump-to-reference approach for imputation of missing data and using the hypothetical and treatment policy strategy to handle ICEs • Sensitivity Analysis #3: the subgroup of the randomized set who received all 6 subcutaneous doses using hypothetical and treatment policy strategy to handle ICEs • Sensitivity Analysis #4: the subgroup of the FAS excluding confirmed COVID-19 cases, using treatment policy strategy to handle ICEs. The following supplementary analyses were repeated for the primary endpoint: • Supplementary Analysis #1: the randomized set using the composite strategy to handle the occurrence of an intercurrent event as treatment failures and using a trimmed mean approach to impute missing data • Supplementary Analysis #2: the randomized set using the treatment policy strategy to handle ICEs. Results of sensitivity analyses and supplementary analyses are in Table 19. The results of the prespecified sensitivity analyses and supplementary analyses were consistent with the primary analysis results."
>
> — FDA Integrated Review, §6.2.2.4 sensitivity/supplementary analyses, PDF p. 68 (https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2023/761286Orig1s000IntegratedR.pdf)

> "Analyses were conducted to assess the treatment effect for subgroups defined by various demographics and clinical characteristics. The subgroup analyses of age, sex, region and weight to evaluate the efficacy of primary endpoint in Table 24 were generated by the FDA reviewer. To be consistent with the methodologies applied in the primary efficacy analyses of the primary endpoint and the key secondary endpoints, the output’s results on subgroups of age, sex and region were from the combined mixed model repeated measures (MMRM) model using an unstructured covariance matrix except for the 95% Cis, which were based on the same method used to produce the multiplicity adjusted 95% Cis for the primary endpoint and key secondary endpoints. The output’s results of subgroup analysis of weight including 97.5% CI were from the MMRM model using a covariance matrix of first order autoregressive structure. Of note, the sample size of the subgroup of weight less than 50 kg was small, thus limiting the ability to produce the multiplicity adjusted 95% Cis with the method used for the primary endpoint and limiting the ability to use an MMRM model with an unstructured covariance matrix."
>
> — FDA Integrated Review, §6.2.2.4.3 Subgroup Analyses, PDF pp. 73-74 (https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2023/761286Orig1s000IntegratedR.pdf)

##### Model 2: Change from baseline in MG-C and QMG to Day 43 (key secondary)

> "The key secondary endpoints of change from baseline to day 43 in MG-C score, change from baseline to day 43 in QMG score, and changes from baseline to day 43 in MGSPRO domains muscle weakness fatigability score, physical fatigue score and bulbar symptoms score were analyzed using the same approach as that of the primary analysis of the primary endpoint."
>
> — FDA Integrated Review, Study MG0003 statistical methods, PDF p. 61 (https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2023/761286Orig1s000IntegratedR.pdf)

### Zuranolone (Zurzuvae) — NDA 217369

Therapeutic area: Neurology / Psychiatry. Sponsor: Sage Therapeutics / Biogen. Approval year: 2023.

Entry notes: Most detailed covariance fallback of the batch: UN with Newton-Raphson -> Fisher scoring -> FA0(T) -> Toeplitz -> AR(1); sandwich (EMPIRICAL) SE if not UN; OM option for LSMEANS. MDD-program efficacy sections redacted (B4 CCI), so MDD-trial MMRMs not extractable.

#### Model 1: Change from baseline in HAMD-17 total at Day 15 (primary); Days 3, 28, 45 (key secondary, fixed sequence) (primary (and key secondary))


- **Trial:** SKYLARK (PPD-301), NCT04442503

#### Verbatim specification excerpts

##### Model 1: Change from baseline in HAMD-17 total at Day 15 (primary); Days 3, 28, 45 (key secondary, fixed sequence) (primary (and key secondary))

> "Certain medications including, but not limited to, new antidepressants or benzodiazepines are prohibited in the protocol until Day 45 follow-up; however, the treatment policy strategy requires that data following initiation of such prohibited medications are included in analysis. The protocol does not specify any rescue process, hence there is no rescue medication."
>
> — FDA Integrated Review, §6.2.2.1.3 (Study PPD-301) estimand, PDF p. 62 (https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2023/217369Orig2s000IntegratedR.pdf)

> "Change from baseline HAMD-17 total score was analyzed using a mixed effects model for repeated measures (MMRM) that included treatment (zuranolone or placebo), baseline HAMD- 17 total score, antidepressant use at baseline (yes or no), assessment time point, and time point- by-treatment interaction as explanatory variables. All explanatory variables were treated as fixed effects. All postbaseline time points were included in the model. The main comparison was between zuranolone and placebo at Day 15. An unstructured (UN) covariance structure with the default Newton-Raphson algorithm used by SAS PROC MIXED will be used to model the within-subject errors. If there is a convergence issue with the unstructured covariance model, the Fisher Scoring algorithm (via the SCORING option of the PROC MIXED statement), the no- diagonal factor analytic structure (via the TYPE=FA0(T) option of the REPEATED statement, where T is the total number of time points), Toeplitz, Autoregressive (1) [AR (1)] covariance structure will be used, following this sequence until convergence is achieved. If the model still does not converge with AR (1) structure, no results will be reported. When the covariance structure is not UN, the sandwich estimator for the variance-covariance matrix will be derived, using the EMPIRICAL option in the PROC MIXED statement in SAS. Observed Margins (OM) option will be used in SAS with LSMEAN statement. Model-based point estimates (i.e., treatment difference in LS mean, 95% confidence intervals [CIs], and p-values) were reported. The p-value was interpreted at 2-sided 5% level of significance. If the comparison of zuranolone versus placebo was significant at the 0.05 level, the hypothesis testing for the key secondary endpoints followed with a multiplicity adjustment by a fixed sequence approach in the order as listed (CFB to Days 3, 28, and 45 on the HAMD-17, and the CFB to Day 15 on the CGI-S)."
>
> — FDA Integrated Review, §6.2.2.1.3 (Study PPD-301), PDF p. 62 (https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2023/217369Orig2s000IntegratedR.pdf)

> "Source: Statistical analyst’s analysis of adsl.xpt, adqshamd.xpt; same as Applicant’s results in tables 14.2.1.1.1 and 14.2.1.1.2. The HAMD-17 total score was calculated as the sum of the 17 individual item scores. A negative change indicates improvement. Model used is the Mixed Model for Repeated Measures (MMRM) with treatment, baseline HAMD-17 total score, antidepressant use at baseline (Yes or No), assessment time point, and time point-by treatment interaction as fixed effects with an unstructured covariance structure."
>
> — FDA Integrated Review, Table 23 footnote, PDF p. 66 (https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2023/217369Orig2s000IntegratedR.pdf)

##### Model 2: Change from baseline in CGI-S at Day 15 (key secondary)

> "Model used is the Mixed Model for Repeated Measures (MMRM) with treatment (SAGE-217 or placebo), baseline CGI-S score, antidepressant use at baseline (Yes or No), assessment time point, and time point-by-treatment interaction as fixed effects with an unstructured covariance structure."
>
> — FDA Integrated Review, Table 24 footnote, PDF p. 68 (https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2023/217369Orig2s000IntegratedR.pdf)

See also Model 1, second quote (fixed-sequence testing including "the CFB to Day 15 on the CGI-S").

##### Model 3: HAMD-17 response (>=50% reduction), HAMD-17 remission (<=7), CGI-I response at Day 15 (secondary)

> "Similar to those methods described above for the primary endpoint, an MMRM will be used for the analysis of the CFB in other time points in HAMD-17 total score, MADRS total score, HAM-A total score, EPDS total score, PHQ-9 score, and selected individual items and/or subscale scores in HAMD-17. Generalized estimating equation (GEE) methods will be used for the analysis of HAMD-17 response (defined as ≥50% reduction from baseline in HAMD-17 total score) and HAMD-17 remission (defined as HAMD-17 total score of ≤7.0). GEE models will include terms for treatment, baseline score, stratification factor, assessment time point, and time point-by- treatment as explanatory variables. The comparison of interest will be the difference between SAGE-217 and matching placebo at Day 15. Model-based point estimates (i.e., odds ratios), 95% confidence intervals, and p-values will be reported. A GEE method will also be used for the analysis of CGI-I response (defined as “much improved” or “very much improved”) including terms for treatment, baseline CGI-S score, stratification factor, assessment time point, and time point-by-treatment as explanatory variables."
>
> — FDA Integrated Review, §15.2.1 (Study PPD-301 protocol/SAP excerpt), PDF p. 241 (https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2023/217369Orig2s000IntegratedR.pdf)

##### Model 4: Change from baseline in HAMD-17 at Day 15 (supportive (Phase 2))

> "For the primary endpoint, the CFB to Day 15 in HAMD-17 total score, the difference between treatment groups was evaluated by a mixed model for repeated measures (MMRM), with treatment, baseline HAMD-17 total score, baseline antidepressant use, assessment time point, and time-point-by-treatment interaction as fixed effects. Observed values and change/percent CFB in HAMD-17 total score and individual item scores are summarized by treatment group. In comparing the visit value to baseline within each treatment group, least-squares (LS) mean CFB is presented along with the associated 95% confidence interval (CI). In comparing treatments (zuranolone minus placebo), LS-mean differences in CFB are presented along with associated 95% CI and pairwise treatment p-value. An unstructured (UN) covariance structure was used to model the within-subject errors. The Kenward-Roger approximation was used to estimate denominator degrees of freedom. If there was a convergence issue with the UN covariance model, Toeplitz, compound symmetry, or Autoregressive (order 1) (AR[1]) covariance structure was used, following this sequence until convergence was achieved. When the covariance structure was not UN, the sandwich estimator for the variance-covariance matrix was derived, using the EMPIRICAL option in the PROC MIXED statement in SAS. There was no secondary endpoint included in the multiplicity adjustment for the overall Type I error control."
>
> — FDA Integrated Review, §6.2.2.2.3 (Study PPD-201B), PDF p. 70 (https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2023/217369Orig2s000IntegratedR.pdf)

> "Source: Statistical analyst’s analysis of adsl.xpt and adeff.xpt datasets; same as applicant’s study report. The HAMD-17 total score was calculated as the sum of the 17 individual item scores. A negative change indicates improvement. Model used is the Mixed Model for Repeated Measures (MMRM) with treatment, baseline HAMD-17 total score, antidepressant use at baseline (Yes or No), assessment time point, and time point-by treatment interaction as fixed effects with unstructured covariance structure."
>
> — FDA Integrated Review, Table 27 footnote, PDF p. 73 (https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2023/217369Orig2s000IntegratedR.pdf)

##### Model 5: SDLP on Day 2 and Day 6/8 (supportive (safety/clin-pharm))

> "For both Study 113 and Study 117, SDLP data were analyzed using a mixed model with fixed effects for sequence, period, and treatment, with repeated periods for subjects. Separate analysis models were conducted for Day 2 and Day 8 results. In addition to treatment effect, p-values for significance testing of period and sequence effects were provided. Pairwise comparisons of differences in means and 2-sided 95% confidence intervals (CIs) on differences were provided for all active treatments versus placebo."
>
> — FDA Integrated Review, §15.3.3 Analysis Methodology, PDF p. 254 (https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2023/217369Orig2s000IntegratedR.pdf)

> "Mixed effects model with fixed effects for sequence, period and treatment, with repeated observations for subjects for each of the driving timepoints, an unstructured covariance structure and Kenward-Roger degrees of freedom. Estimated differences are first treatment label listed minus second treatment label. SAGE-217 30 mg versus placebo difference in LS means on day 2 is estimated as the average of 2 SAGE-217 treatment groups versus placebo."
>
> — FDA Integrated Review, Table 90 footnote (Study 113), PDF p. 117 (https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2023/217369Orig2s000IntegratedR.pdf)

### Gepirone (Exxua) — NDA 021164

Therapeutic area: Neurology / Psychiatry. Sponsor: Fabre-Kramer Pharmaceuticals. Approval year: 2023.

Entry notes: Prespecified primary analyses were ANOVA (treatment + center) on LOCF data; mixed models appear only as FDA reviewer sensitivity analyses and as an FDA random-study-effect pooled analysis (meta-analysis alternative). Label Table 4 does not name the model. The posted StatR is the 2007 review (with an older review appended).

#### Model 1: Change from baseline in HAMD-17 total at Week 8 (sensitivity (FDA reviewer))


- **Trial:** Study FKGBE007 (label Study 2; N=122 PBO / 116 gepirone ER)
- **Endpoint/timepoint:** Change from baseline in HAMD-17 total at Week 8
- **Role:** sensitivity (FDA reviewer)
- **Model family:** MMRM
- **Response:** Change from baseline HAMD-17
- **Fixed effects:** Treatment, center, visit, treatment-by-visit (factors); baseline HAMD-17 covariate [StatR Table 3.4 footnote d verbatim]
- **Random effects:** None stated
- **Covariance:** Unstructured [footnote d: 'The MMRM model uses unstructured variance-covariance structure']
- **Covariance fallback:** Not stated
- **Denominator df:** Not stated
- **Estimation:** Not stated
- **Time coding:** Categorical visit
- **Estimand / contrast:** LS-mean difference at endpoint (Week 8), ITT
- **Missing data:** MAR ('if the patient dropouts were non-informative')
- **MNAR / sensitivity:** Not stated
- **Software:** Not stated
- **Results:** LS mean CFB -8.0 (0.77) PBO vs -10.4 (0.78); difference -2.3 (95% CI -4.5,-0.2), p=0.033; vs primary ANOVA-LOCF -2.4 (-4.4,-0.3), p=0.023 [StatR Table 3.4, reviewer]
- **FDA comments:** Reviewer: high dropout makes LOCF unreliable since HAMD-17 declines over time; 'the MMRM method may give more reliable efficacy results if the patient dropouts were non-informative ... This seems to be a reasonable assumption in this study' [StatR p.9]. SAP was internally approved after study start and not submitted to FDA until 2006.
- **Specification source:** StatR verbatim (Table 3.4 footnote)

#### Verbatim specification excerpts

##### Model 1: Change from baseline in HAMD-17 total at Week 8 (sensitivity (FDA reviewer))

> "Given the high percentages of patient dropout as indicated in Table 3.3, the reliability and interpretability of the efficacy results using LOCF data set could be an issue. In general, LOCF procedure is reliable only when the mean outcome measure is stable over the whole study period. This does not seem to be the case as the mean HAMD-17 total score decreased 9 points on average from a mean baseline score of 24 to the time they left the study. Alternatively, the MMRM method may give more reliable efficacy results if the patient dropouts were non-informative, with dropouts only depending on the observed outcome values, not on the unobserved values. This seems to be a reasonable assumption in this study."
>
> — FDA Statistical Review, Study FKGBE007, PDF pp. 10-11 (https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2023/021164Orig1s000StatR.pdf)

> "d: Test for no difference between treatments at the endpoint using MMRM model with treatment, center, visit and the interaction between treatment and visit as factors and baseline total HAMD-17 score as covariate. The MMRM model uses unstructured variance-covariance structure."
>
> — FDA Statistical Review, Table 3.4 footnote d, PDF p. 11 (https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2023/021164Orig1s000StatR.pdf)

##### Model 2: Change from baseline in HAMD-17 at last endpoint (LOCF) (supportive (FDA reviewer pooled reanalysis, alternative to sponsor meta-analysis))

> "Using the data provided by the sponsor, this reviewer confirmed their efficacy results. At the same time, since the data for all the subjects are available in all studies, in particular the HAMD-17 total score at the last endpoint was available for all the subjects (with LOCF for the dropouts), the reviewer used the mixed effects model with PROC MIXED in SAS to explore the same combinations of the studies. By introducing a random effect to catch the differences among different studies, this approach makes use of all the subjects available and may give as reliable efficacy results as the sponsor's meta-analysis. This approach gives the following results. The combination of the two positive and five so called “supportive studies” gives an estimated treatment effect of -1.21 in favor of gepirone ER on the adjusted change in HAMD-17 total score (p=0.002). The combination of the five so called “supportive studies” gives a p- value of 0.20 for the treatment efficacy, see Table 3.11. The combination of all 12 studies gives a p-value of 0.05. A forest plot together with the meta-analysis results are given in Figure 3.1."
>
> — FDA Statistical Review, pooled analysis of 12 short-term studies, PDF p. 19 (https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2023/021164Orig1s000StatR.pdf)

##### Model 3: Change from baseline in HAMD-17 total (sensitivity (FDA reviewers' robustness analysis, earlier review appended to StatR))

> "Robustness analyses using a mixed-effects model with repeated measures on change from baseline in HAMD-17 Total Scores. SAS PROC MIXED was used in these analyses. The results are not presented separately because they were similar to the OC analyses."
>
> — FDA Statistical Review, earlier review (Kelly/Mahjoob) appended, §2.5.2.1, PDF p. 76 (https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2023/021164Orig1s000StatR.pdf)

> "As the studies suffer from large numbers of dropouts, imputation of the missing values becomes a crucial issue. LOCF assumes non-informative censoring which does not hold for these studies. Mixed-effects models with repeated measures also assume non-informative censoring, but there is no need for the imputation of the missing values in the estimation of the treatment effects. The results of the mixed-effects models are not presented in the tables, but the reviewers will comment on which of the classical approaches they followed closest."
>
> — FDA Statistical Review, earlier review (Kelly/Mahjoob) appended, PDF p. 77 (https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2023/021164Orig1s000StatR.pdf)

> "All studies suffered from fairly large numbers of dropouts. As many of the subjects dropped out due to adverse events or lack of efficacy, the censoring was informative and therefore results from the statistical analyses may be biased (for or against efficacy). Statistical methodology cannot offset this problem, but different approaches may reduce the effects. Both the sponsor's use of LOCF in the ANOVA analyses and the reviewers' mixed-effects models for repeated measures assume random non-informative censoring, which does not hold for these studies. The mixed-effects model uses more information in the estimation of the treatment effect. The results of the mixed-effects models were not presented because the reviewers found that both approaches gave consistent results in the absence of a significant Treatment-by-Center interaction and the overall conclusions did not depend on the methodology used in those cases."
>
> — FDA Statistical Review, earlier review (Kelly/Mahjoob) appended, PDF p. 94 (https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2023/021164Orig1s000StatR.pdf)

### Zilucoplan (Zilbrysq) — NDA 216834

Therapeutic area: Neurology / Psychiatry. Sponsor: UCB Inc.. Approval year: 2023.

Entry notes: Like rozanolixizumab (same sponsor), the MMRM included subjects as random effects in addition to an unstructured matrix. Deaths/rescue/MG crisis handled as treatment failure via WOCF imputation fed into the MMRM (composite-like strategy). Responder (Family 2) model not stated.

#### Model 1: Change from baseline in MG-ADL at Week 12 (primary)


- **Trial:** RAISE (MG0010), NCT04115293
- **Endpoint/timepoint:** Change from baseline in MG-ADL at Week 12
- **Role:** primary
- **Model family:** MMRM
- **Response:** Change from baseline MG-ADL (with WOCF-imputed values for treatment failures)
- **Fixed effects:** Treatment group, baseline MG-ADL, baseline QMG, region (North America, Europe, East Asia), treatment-by-visit, baseline MG-ADL-by-visit [IR p.26 verbatim]
- **Random effects:** Subject [IR p.26 verbatim: 'using an unstructured correlation matrix; subjects were added as random effects in the model']
- **Covariance:** Unstructured
- **Covariance fallback:** Not stated
- **Denominator df:** Not stated
- **Estimation:** Not stated
- **Time coding:** Categorical visit (Weeks 1, 2, 4, 8, 12)
- **Estimand / contrast:** LS-mean difference at Week 12, mITT; rescue therapy, MG crisis, or death = treatment failure, imputed by WOCF (worse of baseline or last value)
- **Missing data:** WOCF for ICE-related missing data; otherwise MAR within MMRM
- **MNAR / sensitivity:** Placebo-based J2R imputation then same MMRM: -2.03 (95% CI -3.16,-0.89), p<0.001; per-protocol -2.35; COVID-free set -2.24 [IR Table 16]
- **Software:** Not stated
- **Results:** N=86 ZIL / 88 PBO. LSM CFB -4.39 (95% CI -5.28,-3.50) vs -2.30 (-3.17,-1.43); difference -2.09 (95% CI -3.24,-0.95), p<0.001 [IR Table 13]. Excluding 12 AChEI-timing deviators: -1.97, p=0.0012; removing affected Day-84 assessments: -2.14, p=0.0003.
- **FDA comments:** Reviewer verified sponsor results; reran same MMRM (with WOCF) on subgroups descriptively, since final SAP versions dropped subgroup testing. 'No major statistical issues were identified.'
- **Specification source:** IR verbatim (p.26, p.30)

#### Model 2: Change from baseline at Week 12 in QMG, MGC, MG-QOL15r (Family 1, fixed sequence) (key secondary)


- **Trial:** RAISE (MG0010), NCT04115293
- **Endpoint/timepoint:** Change from baseline at Week 12 in QMG, MGC, MG-QOL15r (Family 1, fixed sequence)
- **Role:** key secondary
- **Model family:** MMRM
- **Response:** Change from baseline per scale

#### Verbatim specification excerpts

##### Model 1: Change from baseline in MG-ADL at Week 12 (primary)

> "The primary endpoint was analyzed using a mixed effect repeated measures (MMRM) model that included treatment group, baseline MG-ADL score, baseline QMG score, region (North America, Europe, and East Asia) and interactions terms treatment-by-visit and baseline MG- ADL score-by-visit as fixed effects, using an unstructured correlation matrix; subjects were added as random effects in the model; weeks 1, 2, 4, 8, and 12 were included in the model. Efficacy analyses were based on the modified intent-to-treat (mITT) population defined as all randomized subjects who received at least one dose of study drug grouped by randomized treatment group (for reporting efficacy data). Subjects were grouped based on the assigned treatment. Any rescue therapy or MG crisis or death were considered as treatment failure, and any missing data due to these reasons were imputed using baseline or last value available, whichever was worse, i.e., worst observation carry forward (WOCF)."
>
> — FDA Integrated Review, Study MG0010 (RAISE) statistical methods, PDF p. 39 (https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2023/216834Orig1s000IntegratedR.pdf)

> "The mixed model repeated measures (MMRM) model included treatment group (drug or placebo), region (North America, Europe, and East Asia), MG-ADL total score at baseline, QMG score at baseline, visit (week 1, 2, 4, 8 and 12), treatment by visit and baseline MG-ADL score by visit interactions. An unstructured covariance structure was used. P-values were for the comparison of treatment groups in change from baseline to week 12."
>
> — FDA Integrated Review, §6.2.2.4 primary results, PDF p. 43 (https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2023/216834Orig1s000IntegratedR.pdf)

> "Any rescue therapy, MG crisis, or death were considered as treatment failure, and any related missing data were imputed using baseline or last value available, whichever was worse, i.e., WOCF."
>
> — FDA Integrated Review, §6.2.2.4 primary results, PDF p. 43 (https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2023/216834Orig1s000IntegratedR.pdf)

> "In the sensitivity analyses performed by the Applicant, missing data were analyzed by imputing the placebo-based distribution with a J2R (jump-to-reference) approach. The primary endpoint was analyzed using the same MMRM model after the imputations. Per-protocol analysis was also performed. The results of the sensitivity analyses were consistent with those of the primary analysis."
>
> — FDA Integrated Review, §6.2.2.4 sensitivity analyses, PDF p. 47 (https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2023/216834Orig1s000IntegratedR.pdf)

> "Therefore, the same MMRM model used in the primary endpoint analysis including the WOCF (worst observation carried forward) approach, was rerun on the subsets, and the estimates were reported descriptively without p-values, as can be seen in the above table."
>
> — FDA Integrated Review, §6.2.2.4.5 subgroups, PDF p. 51 (https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2023/216834Orig1s000IntegratedR.pdf)

> "No major statistical issues were identified. There was only one single Phase 3 study to review, and it provided statistical evidence that zilucoplan 0.3 mg/kg is effective in treating patients with gMG."
>
> — FDA Integrated Review, Statistical Issues and Conclusions, PDF p. 52 (https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2023/216834Orig1s000IntegratedR.pdf)

### Donanemab-azbt (Kisunla) — BLA 761248

- Therapeutic area: Neurology / Psychiatry
- Sponsor: Eli Lilly and Company
- Approval year: 2024

README discrepancy: the README Keywords say NCS2 was 'an unusual primary-analysis choice the Division had not agreed to in advance'. The StatR (p.6) says the Division had not agreed to *iADRS as endpoint*, but on the *model*: "After Sponsor responded to the Division's concerns about bias and Type I error inflation, the Division agreed to the NCS2 model as the primary analysis model." The SAP posted on ClinicalTrials.gov (README says none posted) is SAP v3 and matches the StatR text.

#### Model 1: iADRS change from baseline at Week 76 (intermediate-tau and overall populations) (primary)

> "For the NCS2 model, 3 knots over the observation time were placed: 2 at the boundaries (minimum and maximum observation time) and 1 internal knot at the median observation time. The baseline estimates were restricted to be the same for treatment and placebo groups. The model was estimated using restricted maximum likelihood method." [StatR p.14; same text SAP §4.3.2]

- **trial:** TRAILBLAZER-ALZ 2 (AACI), NCT04437511
- **model_family:** other — natural cubic spline longitudinal model with 2 df (NCS2); GLS/MMRM-type model with time continuous and baseline constrained equal across arms (cLDA-like)
- **response:** iADRS score at baseline and each scheduled post-baseline visit as dependent variable (raw score; baseline included in response vector) [StatR p.14]
- **fixed_effects:** NCS basis expansion terms (2), basis-by-treatment interaction (2), baseline age, concomitant AChEI and/or memantine use at baseline (yes/no), pooled investigator (sites <2 subjects pooled by country); baseline tau category added for overall population [StatR p.14]
- **random_effects:** none stated (within-subject covariance via R-matrix)
- **covariance:** unstructured [StatR p.14; SAP]
- **covariance_fallback:** heterogeneous Toeplitz → heterogeneous AR(1) → heterogeneous CS → CS [StatR p.14; SAP]. FDA note: in R the UN NCS2 did not converge; heterogeneous Toeplitz unavailable in R; R converged with ARH(1) — 'considered a minor concern' [StatR p.13]
- **df_method:** Kenward-Roger [StatR; SAP]
- **estimation:** REML
- **time_coding:** continuous (weeks from baseline to actual exam date) via spline basis
- **estimand_contrast:** adjusted mean difference in change from baseline at Week 76; percent slowing = difference / placebo change
- **missing_data:** MAR; measurements after death treated as missing (FDA had advised accounting for death; sponsor did not) [StatR p.15]
- **mnar_sensitivity:** pre-specified: death imputed as worst score (iADRS=0) then NCS2 → 3.2 (1.3,5.0) intermediate tau, 2.9 (1.1,4.6) overall; censoring after ARIA-E/IRR; FDA-requested rank ANCOVA with MAR MI; FDA-requested delta-pair tipping point (imputation + rank ANCOVA, Rubin's rule): tipping near (0,-4) intermediate tau and (0,-2) overall [StatR pp.16-18, 34-36]
- **software:** SAS (FDA analyst verified with independent SAS coding and sponsor SAS programs); FDA also attempted R (convergence issue noted) [StatR p.13]
- **result:** Intermediate tau: placebo -9.3 (0.5) N=594 vs donanemab -6.0 (0.5) N=588; difference 3.3 (95% CI 1.9, 4.6), p<0.001. Overall: -13.1 vs -10.2; difference 2.9 (1.5, 4.3), p<0.001 [StatR Table 4]
- **fda_comments:** Reviewer: NCS2 is GLS with time continuous vs MMRM categorical; sponsor chose NCS2 for power; MMRM demoted to sensitivity. NCS2 QQ-plot residuals not normal for iADRS/ADCS-iADL (FDA suggests per-visit QQ plots). Treatment difference ~3 points 'small in magnitude' [StatR]
- **spec_source:** StatR verbatim + SAP verbatim
- **sources:** https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2024/761248Orig1s000StatR.pdf; https://cdn.clinicaltrials.gov/large-docs/11/NCT04437511/SAP_001.pdf

Visit was treated as a categorical variable. An unstructured covariance matrix was used... The Kenward-Roger approximation was to estimate the denominator degrees of freedom." [StatR p.15]

#### Verbatim specification excerpts

##### Model 1: iADRS change from baseline at Week 76 (intermediate-tau and overall populations) (primary)

> "Additionally, there were multiple exchanges between Sponsor and the Division on the choice of primary statistical analysis model for study AACI. MMRM had typically been used in AD studies, including study AACG, as the primary analysis model. However, for study AACI, Sponsor proposed natural cubic splines with 2 degrees of freedom (NCS2) based on analyses that showed NCS2 attaining higher statistical power compared to MMRM. After Sponsor responded to the Division’s concerns about bias and Type I error inflation 2, the Division agreed to the NCS2 model as the primary analysis model."
>
> — FDA Statistical Review §2, PDF p. 36 (printed p. 7) (https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2024/761248Orig1s000StatR.pdf)

> "A natural cubic spline analysis (see Appendix 6.1 Natural Cubic Spline) with 2 degrees of freedom (NCS2) was pre-specified to assess the difference between treatment groups in iADRS change from baseline at Week 76. For the NCS2 model, 3 knots over the observation time were placed: 2 at the boundaries (minimum and maximum observation time) and 1 internal knot at the median observation time. The baseline estimates were restricted to be the same for treatment and placebo groups. The model was estimated using restricted maximum likelihood method. The iADRS score at baseline and at each of the scheduled post-baseline visits were included in model as a dependent variable. Study visit was assumed continuous with values equal to weeks between baseline and post-baseline exam dates. NCS basis functions were constructed using visits in weeks. The model included the fixed effects: NCS basis expansion terms (two terms), NCS basis expansion term-by-treatment interaction (two terms), baseline age, concomitant acetylcholinesterase inhibitor (AchEI) and/or memantine use at baseline (yes/no), and pooled investigator 6. Baseline tau category was included as a covariate in the model for the overall population. An unstructured variance-covariance structure matrix was assumed for the within-subject variance-covariance errors. If the unstructured variance-covariance structure matrix resulted in a lack of convergence, the following structures were used in sequence: heterogeneous Toeplitz covariance structure, heterogeneous autoregressive order 1 covariance structure, heterogeneous compound symmetry covariance structure, and compound symmetry covariance structure. The Kenward-Roger approximation was used to estimate the denominator degrees of freedom. The treatment group contrast in mean change from baseline at Week 76 with 95% CI was estimated using NCS2. NCS2 assumed missing data were missing at random. Measurements after death were treated as missing."
>
> — FDA Statistical Review §3.2.2.1, PDF p. 43 (printed p. 14) (https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2024/761248Orig1s000StatR.pdf)

> "Reviewer Comment: • NCS2 is a generalized least squares model of longitudinal data that treated time as a continuous variable in the mean response. NCS2 modeled the temporal mean trend with polynomials, specifically with cubic polynomials, that were spliced together at knot locations. In contrast, mixed model with repeated measures (MMRM) treated time as a categorical variable and did not assume a trend over time. The MMRM had typically been the primary analysis model of longitudinal data in AD studies. However, Sponsor proposed NCS2 as the primary analysis model on the basis that NCS2 attained higher statistical power compared to MMRM (see Section 2 INTRODUCTION for the regulatory [...] background). MMRM analysis of iADRS became a sensitivity analysis (Section 3.2.2.3 Sensitivity Analyses). • Ignoring deaths, a negative outcome, could bias the results. Although the Division had advised Sponsor to account for death in the primary efficacy analysis 7 prior to the BLA submission, Sponsor instead assumed death was not informative and measurements after death were treated as missing. Sponsor instead pre-specified a sensitivity analysis imputing death as the worst outcome in the NCS2 analysis of iADRS (Section 3.2.2.3 Sensitivity Analyses)."
>
> — FDA Statistical Review §3.2.2.1, PDF pp. 43–44 (printed pp. 14–15) (https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2024/761248Orig1s000StatR.pdf)

> "When using R software, the NCS2 model of iADRS did not converge with an unstructured variance-covariance structure matrix. As stated in the protocol, if the unstructured covariance matrix did not converge, a heterogenous Toeplitz covariance structure would be fitted, but heterogenous Toeplitz was not an option in R software. NCS2 did converge with heterogeneous autoregressive order 1 covariance structure in R software, however, an unstructured covariance was preferred because it had less assumptions. The NCS2 fit with a different covariance structure using R versus SAS software was considered a minor concern."
>
> — FDA Statistical Review §3.1, PDF p. 38 (printed p. 9) (https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2024/761248Orig1s000StatR.pdf)

> "where x is the treatment variable, and the indicator 1i ( x) is 1 if subject i is in the treatment group and 0 otherwise. The residual vector ε ij of each subject follows a multivariate normal distribution with mean zero and an assumed covariance structure. [...] Interior knots are typically spaced according to quantiles of 𝑡𝑡. For a natural cubic spline with 2 degrees of freedom (e.g., 2 knots at the boundaries, 1 knot at the median observation time), there are m = 2 basis functions. For a natural cubic spline with 3 degrees of freedom (e.g., 2 boundary knots, 2 internal knots over the time course, usually at 33rd and 67th percentiles), there are m = 3 basis functions. Note that the estimation of the covariance matrix used categorical time."
>
> — FDA Statistical Review Appendix 6.1 (equation omitted; garbled in text layer), PDF p. 70 (printed p. 41) (https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2024/761248Orig1s000StatR.pdf)

> "Residuals appeared approximately normal for most analyses, except for NCS2 analysis of iADRS and ADCS-iADL. However, these plots contained residuals from all time points, which were correlated. The sample sizes of the analyses (iADRS:1599, iADL:1606) were large and the residuals were expected (according to the Central Limit Theorem) to be normal as the sample size increased. Note that plotting the quantile-quantile plot for each scheduled visit, instead of combining all visits, would provide for a more useful diagnostic check."
>
> — FDA Statistical Review Appendix 6.4, PDF p. 77 (printed p. 48) (https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2024/761248Orig1s000StatR.pdf)

> "Death Imputed As Worst Score The pre-specified sensitivity analysis imputed the worst possible iADRS score 0 for measurements after death until Week 76 for death cases. NCS2 was then fitted to the data."
>
> — FDA Statistical Review §3.2.2.3, PDF p. 46 (printed p. 17) (https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2024/761248Orig1s000StatR.pdf)

> "During the BLA review, we requested Sponsor to conduct a tipping point analysis to explore the plausibility of missing data assumptions under which the conclusions change, i.e., under which there is no longer a statistically significant effect shown for the endpoints of iADRS and CDR-SB change from baseline at Week 76 in the intermediate tau and overall population. Data were imputed using the fitted model as was done for the rank ANCOVA (see Appendix Section 6.3 Rank ANCOVA). Decreases on the iADRS scale represented worsening, so a range of delta values from 0 to -5 was explored for donanemab participants in increments of 1. For participants on placebo, delta ranged from 0 to -2 in increments of 1. [...] Then the rank ANCOVA was conducted on the modified data and Cochran-Mantel-Haenszel test statistics were combined using Rubin’s rule."
>
> — FDA Statistical Review §3.2.2.3, PDF p. 47 (printed p. 18) (https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2024/761248Orig1s000StatR.pdf)

> "A NCS analysis (Donahue et al. 2023) with 2 degrees of freedom (NCS2) will be used to assess the difference between treatment groups in iADRS score at Week 76. For this NCS2 model applied to primary analysis, 3 knots over the observation time will be placed: 2 at the boundaries (minimum and maximum observation time), and 1 internal knot at the median observation time. The baseline estimates are restricted to be the same for treatment and placebo groups. The model will be estimated using restricted maximum likelihood method. The iADRS score at baseline and at each of the scheduled post-baseline visits (according to Schedule of Activities [SoA]) will be included in model as a dependent variable. Study visit will be treated as a continuous variable with values equal to weeks between baseline and post-baseline exam dates, and the NCS basis function will be derived using these visits in weeks. The model will include these fixed effects: NCS basis expansion terms (two terms), NCS basis expansion term-by-treatment interaction (two terms), baseline age, concomitant AchEI and/or memantine use at baseline (yes/no), and pooled investigator. Baseline tau category will also be included as a covariate to the model applied to overall population. An unstructured variance-covariance structure matrix will be used to within-subject variance-covariance errors. If the unstructured variance-covariance structure matrix results in a lack of convergence, the following structures will be used in sequence: Heterogeneous Toeplitz covariance structure Heterogeneous autoregressive order 1 covariance structure Heterogeneous compound symmetry covariance structure, and Compound symmetry covariance structure Mean change from baseline values, and the comparisons between change from baseline values by treatment arms will be estimated through the proper contrast set up. The primary time point for treatment comparison will be at Week 76. The Kenward-Roger approximation will be used to estimate the denominator degrees of freedom."
>
> — SAP v3 §4.3.2, PDF p. 17 (printed p. 16) (https://cdn.clinicaltrials.gov/large-docs/11/NCT04437511/SAP_001.pdf)

> "At Week 76, the donanemab arm compared to the placebo arm had statistically significantly less decline as measured by iADRS. The NCS2 difference in adjusted mean change from baseline of iADRS in the intermediate tau population (3.3; 95% CI 1.9, 4.6; p < 0.001) and the overall population (2.9; 95% CI 1.5, 4.3; p < 0.001) are shown in Table 4 and Figure 6."
>
> — FDA Statistical Review §3.2.4.1, PDF p. 55 (printed p. 26) (https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2024/761248Orig1s000StatR.pdf)

##### Model 2: CDR-SB change from baseline at Week 76 (key secondary (gated in graphical procedure; inherits alpha from iADRS))

> "Mixed model with repeated measures (MMRM) was fitted to CDR-SB. The change from baseline score in CDR-SB at each scheduled post-baseline visit during the treatment period was the dependent variable. The model included fixed effects terms: treatment, visit, treatment-by-visit interaction, baseline CDR-SB score, baseline score-by-visit interaction, age at baseline, concomitant AChEI and/or memantine use at baseline (yes/no), and pooled investigator. Baseline tau category was included as a fixed effect in the model for the overall population. Visit was treated as a categorical variable. An unstructured covariance matrix was used to model the within-subject variance-covariance errors 8. The Kenward-Roger approximation was to estimate the denominator degrees of freedom. For MMRM, the primary time point for treatment comparison was Week 76. The treatment group contrast in mean change from baseline with 95% CI was calculated using the MMRM model. MMRM assumed missing data were missing at random. Measurements after death were treated as missing."
>
> — FDA Statistical Review §3.2.2.2, PDF p. 44 (printed p. 15) (https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2024/761248Orig1s000StatR.pdf)

> "If the unstructured variance-covariance structure matrix resulted in a lack of convergence, the following structures would be used in sequence: heterogeneous Toeplitz covariance structure, heterogeneous autoregressive order 1 covariance structure, heterogeneous compound symmetry covariance structure, and compound symmetry covariance structure."
>
> — FDA Statistical Review footnote 8, PDF p. 44 (printed p. 15) (https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2024/761248Orig1s000StatR.pdf)

> "MMRM analysis will be applied as the main analytical approach for CDR-SB, with similar model details as described in Section 4.3.3.1. Other than CDR-SB, NCS2 analysis will be applied to the rest of endpoint measurements as the main analytical approach on both the overall [...] population and the intermediate baseline tau subpopulation separately."
>
> — SAP v3 §4.4.1.2, PDF pp. 20–21 (printed pp. 19–20) (https://cdn.clinicaltrials.gov/large-docs/11/NCT04437511/SAP_001.pdf)

> "Although Sponsor pre-specified CDR-SB subgroup analysis using NCS2, we conducted instead subgroup analysis of CDR-SB using its primary analysis model MMRM (Section 3.2.2.2 Analysis of Select Clinical Endpoints) to allow comparison between the results of the overall population and subgroups."
>
> — FDA Statistical Review §3.2.2.6, PDF p. 49 (printed p. 20) (https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2024/761248Orig1s000StatR.pdf)

> "A major statistical issue is the sensitivity of the primary analysis of CDR-SB change from baseline at Week 76 to missing data assumptions. Study discontinuation was high with the donanemab arm having a higher rate compared to the placebo arm (27% vs. 20%). During the BLA review, the Sponsor conducted a sensitivity analysis of CDR-SB to varying missing data assumptions using tipping point analysis (Sections 3.2.2.3 Sensitivity Analyses, Section 3.2.4.3.4 Tipping Point Analyses). The primary analysis of CDR-SB change from baseline at Week 76 became non-significant near the delta pair (0, 0.5) where the treatment difference between imputed subjects might still favor donanemab. Also, the tipping point occurred with the minimum within-subject scale increment of 0.5."
>
> — FDA Statistical Review §5.1, PDF p. 68 (printed p. 39) (https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2024/761248Orig1s000StatR.pdf)

> "At Week 76, the donanemab arm compared to the placebo arm had statistically significantly less decline as measured by CDR-SB. The difference in adjusted mean change from baseline of CDR-SB in the intermediate tau population was -0.7 (95% CI -1.0, -0.4; p < 0.001) and the overall population was -0.7 (95% CI -1.0, -0.5; p < 0.001) (Figure 7, Appendix Table 7)."
>
> — FDA Statistical Review §3.2.4.2, PDF p. 56 (printed p. 27) (https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2024/761248Orig1s000StatR.pdf)

Also: SAP §4.3.3.1 MMRM text (see Model 4).

> "For ADAS-Cog13 change from baseline at Week 76, the estimates with death imputed as the worst score in the intermediate tau population (-1.0; 95% CI -2.2, 0.1; p = 0.07) and the overall population (-1.0; 95% CI -2.0, 0.0; p =0.04) were not statistically significant compared to the alpha allocation of 0.04 and 0.01, respectively. ##### Model 4: iADRS change from baseline at Week 76 (sensitivity)

> "MMRM The MMRM analysis of iADRS was similar to the MMRM analysis specified for CDR-SB. See Section 3.2.2.2 Analysis of Select Clinical Endpoints."

> "For MMRM analysis, the change from baseline score on the iADRS at each scheduled postbaseline visit (according to the SoA) during the treatment period will be included as the dependent variable. Baseline tau category will also be included as a fixed effect to the model applied to overall population. Visit will be considered a categorical variable. An unstructured covariance matrix will be used to model the within-subject variance-covariance errors. If the unstructured covariance structure matrix results in a lack of convergence, the following tests will be used in sequence: heterogeneous Toeplitz covariance structure heterogeneous autoregressive covariance structure heterogeneous compound symmetry covariance structure compound symmetry covariance structure The Kenward-Roger approximation will be used to estimate the denominator degrees of freedom. For MMRM, the primary time point for treatment comparison will be at Week 76. The treatment group contrast in least-squares mean progression and its associated p-value and 95% CI will be calculated for the treatment comparison of donanemab versus placebo using the MMRM model specified above."

NCS2 estimates of iADRS mean change from baseline at Week 76 were smaller than the observed mean change at Week 76, a pattern that was also seen in the MMRM analysis (Appendix Figure 13)."
