### Eplontersen (Wainua) — NDA 217388

- Therapeutic area: Rare Disease / Genetic / Metabolic-genetic
- Sponsor: Ionis Pharmaceuticals (applicant of record; AstraZeneca is the partner)
- Approval year: 2023 (December 21, 2023)
- Trial: NEURO-TTRansform (ION-682884-CS3), NCT04136184. Open-label, 6:1 eplontersen vs inotersen reference arm. The comparator is the external placebo cohort of NEURO-TTR (ISIS-420915-CS2, NCT01737398).
- Note: the mNIS+7 and Norfolk QOL-DN Week 35 primary/secondary analyses are propensity-score-weighted ANCOVA with MI (one post-baseline visit). They are not mixed models and are excluded below.

#### Model 1: Percent change from baseline in serum TTR at Week 35 (primary; sponsor's first-ranked co-primary)

- Role: primary at the Week 35 interim, which became the final confirmatory analysis. FDA downgraded TTR to an "additional"/PD endpoint [IR §6.2.1.4.4].
- model_family: MMRM, propensity-score weighted (ATT weights).
- Response: percent change from baseline in serum TTR (g/L). External-placebo TTR values were converted to the current assay first with y=0.0057x^2+0.5843x-0.3819 [SAP §4.10.2.1].
- Fixed effects [SAP verbatim]: "The MMRM model will also include the effects of treatment (ION-682884 or NEURO-TTR placebo), time (categorical), disease stage (Stage 1/Stage 2), V30M mutation (Yes/No), and previous treatment with Vyndaqel® or Diflunisal (Yes/No), treatment-by-time interaction, baseline value of the endpoint, and the baseline-by-time interaction."
- Weighting [SAP verbatim]: "The ATT (average treatment effect for treated) approach will be used with weight: =1 for subjects in the 682884-CS3 treated group; pred/(1-pred) for subjects in the NEURO-TTR placebo control group". The PS comes from a logistic regression on stage, V30M and prior treatment.
- Random effects: none (covariance modeled via R-matrix only).
- Covariance [SAP verbatim]: "An unstructured variance-covariance matrix will be used to model the within-patient errors, and the degrees of freedom will be determined using Kenward-Roger method".
- Fallback [SAP verbatim, in sequence]:
  1. SCORING=4 (Fisher scoring for the first 4 iterations).
  2. TYPE=FA0(t).
  3. CSH with a robust "sandwich" estimator (PROC MIXED EMPIRICAL).
  4. ARH(1) plus sandwich.
  5. CS plus sandwich.
  6. AR(1) plus sandwich.
- df: Kenward-Roger (DDFM=kr).
- Estimation: Not stated. REML is the PROC MIXED default, but the SAP does not state it.
- Time: categorical. There are 5 post-baseline visits. FDA notes that CS3 visits (weeks 5, 9, 13, 25, 35) and CS2 visits (weeks 5, 8, 13, 23, 35) "were aligned to be the same five visit numbers" [IR p.46].
- SAS code [SAP verbatim]: `MODEL endpoint=trtp distac pretrtc v30ttrc baseline visit visit*baseline visit*trtp / DDFM=kr; REPEATED visit / SUBJECT=usubjid TYPE=un; LSMEANS visit*trtp / CL DIFF; Weight wt;`
- Estimand/contrast: LS-mean difference (eplontersen minus external placebo) at Week 35. Uses FAS on-treatment data up to Week 35.
- Missing data: no imputation. The SAP assumes MAR: "the missing data follows a missing at random mechanism". If the Shapiro-Wilk test on residuals is significant at α=0.01, "a stratified Wilcoxon rank sum test will be provided and the result will be considered as Primary Analysis for TTR."
- MNAR sensitivity [SAP §4.10.3.2]: MI under MAR, CIR and J2R (Carpenter et al. 2013).
  - The imputation model is a Bayesian "repeated measures Gaussian model" with the same covariates as the primary MMRM.
  - It produces ≥500 imputations, each analysed by PS-weighted ANCOVA and combined with Rubin's rules. Seed 2855.
  - It uses on-study data in the Safety Set.
  - Other sensitivity analyses: PPS (Sens. 5), PS with 6 covariates adding gender, mBMI and region (Sens. 7), and PS-quartile-stratified Wilcoxon/Hodges-Lehmann (Sens. 1).
- Software: SAS PROC MIXED (sample code in the SAP). The publication says "SAS version 9.3 or later" [Pub].
- Results [IR Table 16, p.45]:
  - FAS N=140 eplontersen and 59 external placebo.
  - LSM -81.20 (95% CI -84.55, -77.84) vs -14.76 (-18.73, -10.80).
  - Difference -66.43 (95% CI -71.39, -61.47), p<0.0001.
- FDA comments: "With no imputation for missing data in the MMRM model, we were able to get the exact same numbers not only for the descriptive ... but also the estimate for effect size and p-value as in Applicant's report" [IR pp.45-46]. FDA refused TTR as a primary endpoint at pre-IND.

#### Model 2: TTR at Week 65; mNIS+7 and Norfolk QOL-DN at Week 66 (primary per the SAP Week 66 final analysis; reported in the publication)

- Role: Week 66 co-primary analyses in the SAP. All three endpoints were significant at Week 35, so the Week 66 tests "will not be conducted" in the hierarchy. However, the JAMA publication reports Week 65/66 MMRM results as its primary efficacy endpoints. This conflicts with the README statement that the Week 66 analyses were "never conducted": the hierarchical tests were not run, but the analyses were.
- model_family: MMRM, PS-weighted.
- Fixed effects [SAP verbatim]: "Similar to the interim analysis for TTR, the MMRM model will include the effects of treatment ..., time (categorical), disease stage ..., V30M mutation ..., and previous treatment ..., treatment-by-time interaction, baseline value of the endpoint, and the baseline-by-time interaction."
- The publication [Pub] says: "The MMRM contains fixed effects of treatment, time (categorical), disease stage, V30M variant, previous treatment with a transthyretin stabilizer, baseline value of the end point, treatment × time interaction, and the baseline × time interaction."
- Random effects: none (R-matrix).
- Covariance: UN, by reference to the interim TTR model. The SAP's Westfall-Young resampling code fits paired `PROC MIXED ... REPEATED visit / SUBJECT=subject_id TYPE=un; ... DDFM=kr` for the Week 35 and Week 66 data. The fallback sequence is as in Model 1.
- df: Kenward-Roger. Estimation: Not stated. Time: categorical.
- Missing data: no imputation, MAR. The publication says "Missing data were not imputed for MMRM analyses." MNAR sensitivity is MI with MAR/CIR/J2R, as in Model 1, applied to all three endpoints at Week 66.
- Software: SAS 9.3 or later [Pub].
- Results [Pub abstract]:
  - TTR at Week 65: -81.7% vs -11.2%, difference -70.4% (95% CI -75.2 to -65.7), P<.001.
  - mNIS+7 at Week 66: 0.3 vs 25.1, difference -24.8 (95% CI -31.0 to -18.6), P<.001.
  - Norfolk QoL-DN at Week 66: -5.5 vs 14.2, difference -19.7 (95% CI -25.6 to -13.8), P<.001.
  - Per the PMC page, N was 144/60 for TTR and 141/59 for mNIS+7 and Norfolk.
- FDA comments: Not stated. The IR evaluated Week 35 only.

#### Model 3: TTR (and Week 66 endpoints) by subgroup (supportive)

- model_family: PS-weighted MMRM with subgroup interactions [SAP §4.10.4].
- Fixed effects [verbatim]: "fixed categorical effects for treatment, time, disease stage, V30M mutation, and previous treatment, treatment-by-time interaction, treatment-by-subgroup interaction, and treatment-by-time-by-subgroup interaction. The baseline value of the endpoint and the baseline-by-time interaction will be included as covariates". The interaction is tested at 0.10.
- Covariance, df and estimation: Not stated for this model (the primary model uses UN/KR).
- Results: a forest plot of Week 35 TTR LSM differences is reproduced in IR Figure 28. Numeric values were not extracted.
- FDA comments: none specific to the model.

#### Model 4: Secondary, PD and exploratory endpoints (secondary/exploratory)

- Endpoints:
  - NSC change at Week 35 and Week 66.
  - SF-36 PCS, PND and mBMI at Week 65.
  - PD endpoints.
  - Exploratory ECHO parameters (wall thickness >15 mm subset).
- Specification: "Treatment group differences will be evaluated using the same method as the primary efficacy analysis (MMRM described in Section 4.10.2)." It is applied to FAS and PPS, with "No sensitivity analyses". The ECHO MMRM has treatment, stage, V30M, prior treatment and baseline as fixed effects [SAP §4.10.5-4.10.7].
- Covariance and df: by reference to the primary model (UN, KR).
- Results: Not stated in the sources consulted. FDA comments: Not stated.

#### Verbatim specification excerpts

##### Model 1: Percent change from baseline in serum TTR at Week 35 (primary; sponsor's first-ranked co-primary)

> "The percent change in serum TTR from Baseline to Week 35 will be analyzed using the MMRM model adjusted by propensity score weights. The MMRM model will also include the effects of treatment (ION-682884 or NEURO-TTR placebo), time (categorical), disease stage (Stage 1/Stage 2), V30M mutation (Yes/No), and previous treatment with Vyndaqel® or Diflunisal (Yes/No), treatment-by-time interaction, baseline value of the endpoint, and the baseline-by-time interaction. The propensity score will be calculated for each NEURO-TTR placebo or ION-682884 patient using a logistic regression model with covariates including disease stage (Stage 1/Stage 2), V30M mutation (Yes/No), and previous treatment with Vyndaqel® or Diflunisal (Yes/No)."
>
> — Protocol Amendment 5 + SAP v2.1, §4.10.2.1, p. 160 (https://cdn.clinicaltrials.gov/large-docs/84/NCT04136184/Prot_SAP_000.pdf)

```sas
PROC LOGISTIC data=xxx;
CLASS trtp distac pretrtc v30ttrc ;
MODEL trtp (event="ION-682884")=distac pretrtc v30ttrc ;
OUTPUT out=Propensity_Scores pred=pred;
run;

PROC MIXED data=xxx;
CLASS trtp visit usubjid distac pretrtc v30ttrc;
MODEL endpoint=trtp distac pretrtc v30ttrc baseline visit visit*baseline visit*trtp /
DDFM=kr;
REPEATED visit / SUBJECT=usubjid TYPE=un;
LSMEANS visit*trtp / CL DIFF;
Weight wt;
RUN;
```

— Protocol Amendment 5 + SAP v2.1, §4.10.2.1 example SAS code, p. 160 (https://cdn.clinicaltrials.gov/large-docs/84/NCT04136184/Prot_SAP_000.pdf)

> "The ATT (average treatment effect for treated) approach will be used with weight: =1 for subjects in the 682884-CS3 treated group; pred/(1-pred) for subjects in the NEURO-TTR placebo control group In this model, missing data are not explicitly imputed. Instead, all available post-baseline assessments up to the Week 35 endpoint during the treatment period (which fall in the visit windows) for subjects in the FAS are utilized, and via modelling of the within-subject correlation structure, the endpoint treatment differences (which are adjusted to take account of missing data) are derived. The estimation of treatment differences is based upon the assumption that the missing [...] data follows a missing at random mechanism (i.e., the missingness of the observations may be dependent on the observed outcomes or covariates, but not on unobserved outcomes). An unstructured variance-covariance matrix will be used to model the within-patient errors, and the degrees of freedom will be determined using Kenward-Roger method (Kenward, M. G. and Roger, J. H. (1997)). If there are convergence issues with the model, the six methods below will be conducted in the following sequence to solve the convergency issues."
>
> — Protocol Amendment 5 + SAP v2.1, §4.10.2.1, pp. 160-161 (https://cdn.clinicaltrials.gov/large-docs/84/NCT04136184/Prot_SAP_000.pdf)

> "1) SCORING=4 option could be used in the PROC MIXED statement in SAS. This will direct SAS to use the Fisher scoring with the first 4 iterations. 2) TYPE = FA0(t) option will be used where t is the dimension of covariance matrix."
>
> — Protocol Amendment 5 + SAP v2.1, §4.10.2.1 convergence fallbacks, p. 161 (https://cdn.clinicaltrials.gov/large-docs/84/NCT04136184/Prot_SAP_000.pdf)

```sas
PROC MIXED data=xxx;
CLASS trtp visit usubjid distac pretrtc v30ttrc;
MODEL endpoint=trtp distac pretrtc v30ttrc baseline visit visit*baseline
visit*trtp / DDFM=kr;
REPEATED visit / SUBJECT=usubjid TYPE= FA0(t); *where t is the dimension
of covariance matrix;
LSMEANS visit*trtp / CL DIFF;
Weight wt;
RUN;
```

##### Model 2: TTR at Week 65; mNIS+7 and Norfolk QOL-DN at Week 66 (primary per the SAP Week 66 final analysis; reported in the publication)

> "For percent change from Baseline of TTR at Week 65, change from Baseline of mNIS+7 at Week 66, and change from Baseline of Norfolk QOL-DN at Week 66, a MMRM model adjusted by propensity score weights will be used. Similar to the interim analysis for TTR, the MMRM model will include the effects of treatment (ION-682884 or NEURO-TTR placebo), time (categorical), disease stage (Stage 1/Stage 2), V30M mutation (Yes/No), and previous treatment with Vyndaqel® or Diflunisal (Yes/No), treatment-by-time interaction, baseline value of the endpoint, and the baseline-by-time interaction. The propensity score will be calculated using the same logistic regression model in the primary analysis (Section 4.10.2.1). In this model, missing data are not explicitly imputed. Instead, all available post-baseline assessments up to the Week 65 (or Week 66) endpoints during the treatment period (which fall in the visit windows) for subjects in the FAS are utilized and via modeling of the within subject correlation structure, the endpoint treatment differences (which are adjusted to take account of missing data) are derived."

### Givinostat (Duvyzat) — NDA 217865

- Therapeutic area: Rare Disease / Genetic / Metabolic-genetic
- Sponsor: Italfarmaco S.p.A.
- Approval year: 2024 (March 21, 2024)
- Trial: EPIDYS (Study 48), NCT02851797. 2:1 randomization; the Target Population is VL MFF >5% and ≤30%.
- Note on the primary analysis: it is a single-timepoint ANCOVA on log-transformed 4SC change at Month 18, fit in SAS PROC MIXED with Kenward-Roger df after single-value Class 1/Class 2 imputation [SAP §4.4.4.2, p.32]. It is not a repeated-measures model, so it is not counted below. The sponsor's tipping-point Approach 2 "inclus[ed] 4SC repeated measures for the Class 1 imputation" [IR p.61], but no model specification is given.
- All mixed models below except Model 4 are FDA reviewer re-analyses.

#### Model 1: 4SC change from baseline at Month 18, Target Population (sensitivity; FDA reviewer)

- model_family: MMRM.
- Response: change in 4SC time (seconds), untransformed.
- Fixed effects, random effects, covariance, df, estimation and time coding: Not stated. The reviewer describes it only as "MMRM of all observed data".
- Missing data [IR p.59 verbatim]: "A missing data handling method requiring less stringent assumptions (relative to single value imputation for missing data) in order to be valid is MMRM of all observed data (note: here the single value imputation for the Class 2 missing data is also included since otherwise it would be informatively missing)".
- Results [IR p.59]:
  - Reviewer MMRM: "estimated difference of -1.64 (SE = 0.94), p = 0.083 (N = 119...)".
  - Applicant ANCOVA: -1.78 s, p=0.037 (untransformed); GLS mean ratio 0.86 (95% CI 0.745-0.989), p=0.035 (log scale).
  - Reviewer analysis excluding Class 1 imputations: -1.77 (SE 0.947), p=0.065, N=108.
- MNAR/tipping point: the Applicant's prespecified tipping-point MI used 10 imputations, Rubin's rules, PROC MIANALYZE, and a shift applied to the givinostat arm only. At zero shift it gave p=0.117 (Approach 1) and 0.064 (Approach 2).
- FDA comments:
  - The single mean imputation's "standard deviation of the imputed values is less than the standard deviation for observed data ... can increase the type I error".
  - The zero-shift tipping point being non-significant "illustrates the inadequacy of the Applicant's primary missing data handling method".
  - Unequal group variances with 2:1 allocation inflate type I error (Hayes 2000).
  - The reviewer suggested MMRM as the more appropriate primary approach.
- Software: Not stated.

#### Model 2: Rank-based 4SC at Month 18 (sensitivity; FDA reviewer)

- model_family: MMRM on ranks ("rank MMRM ANCOVA").
- Specification fields: Not stated.
- Rationale [IR p.59]: "Due to possible excessive influence of Class 2 missing data which involves a somewhat arbitrary imputed value (twice the maximum observed 4SC time across all subjects and visits) ... a MMRM analysis based on ranks of 4SC time may have better statistical properties".
- Result: difference in mean ranks at Month 18 of -6.1 (SE 4.2), p=0.147.
- Software: Not stated.

#### Model 3: VL MFF (MRS) change at Month 18 (sensitivity; FDA reviewer re-analysis of the key secondary/PD endpoint)

- model_family: MMRM. Specification fields: Not stated.
- Results [IR p.65]: "The Month 18 difference based on MMRM, which uses all observed post-baseline data without imputation and which is valid under a weaker assumption regarding the missing data, i.e., missing at random, is -2.54 (SE = 1.40), p = 0.073 (N = 114)."
- Comparisons:
  - Applicant: -2.92, nominal p=0.0354.
  - Reviewer re-imputation based on mean change: -2.43 (95% CI -5.06, 0.21), p=0.071.
  - Completers: -2.17, p=0.122.
- FDA comments: the Applicant's imputation ignored baseline and was optimistic for a high-baseline dropout. The VL MFF result "would not be nominally significant at Month 18 based on a method that makes missing data assumptions more in line with regulatory guidances".

#### Model 4: 4SC change at each visit, with and without time-varying VL MFF terms (supportive/supplementary; sponsor SAP, conditional)

- Trigger: a significant VL MFF key secondary effect plus trends over time [SAP §4.4.7.2].
- model_family: MMRM.
- Specification [SAP p.39 verbatim]: "A mixed effects model with repeated measures (MMRM) will be fitted to the change from baseline in the primary endpoint to each post-baseline visit at which the endpoint is assessed. The model will include baseline values for: 4SC, time to rise from floor, time to run/walk 10 metres, distance walked in 6 minutes and re-derived age at first dose (in years and months) as covariates, concomitant steroid use (according to the 4 possible strata), treatment and visit as fixed effects and the treatment by visit interaction. F-tests from PROC MIXED will be based on Kenward-Roger's adjusted degrees of freedom. An unstructured variance/covariance matrix will be used for the repeated visits within a subject."
- Second model: adds VL MFF at each visit, VL MFF×visit, VL MFF×treatment and VL MFF×treatment×visit. This is a mediation-style comparison of LS-mean differences.
- Random effects: none (R-matrix). Fallback: Not stated. Estimation: Not stated. Time: categorical.
- Software: SAS PROC MIXED; "SAS version 9.2 or higher" [SAP p.7].
- Results: Not stated. The sources do not show whether it was run. VL MFF was not formally significant after Hochberg.
- FDA comments: Not stated.

#### Verbatim specification excerpts

##### Model 1: 4SC change from baseline at Month 18, Target Population (sensitivity; FDA reviewer)

> "A possible approach for handling a subject unable to perform the test would be a single value imputation for that patient only, together with a more appropriate approach for subjects with missing data not related to the inability to perform the test, e.g., MMRM of all observed post-baseline 4SC data."
>
> — FDA Integrated Review, p. 51 (https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2024/217865Orig1s000IntegratedR.pdf)

> "The review team identified one problem with this imputation method: the standard deviation of the imputed values is less than the standard deviation for observed data, although the former is truly more uncertain. Underestimating the true variability like this can increase the type I error/ false positive rate."
>
> — FDA Integrated Review, p. 59 (https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2024/217865Orig1s000IntegratedR.pdf)

> "A missing data handling method requiring less stringent assumptions (relative to single value imputation for missing data) in order to be valid is MMRM of all observed data (note: here the single value imputation for the Class 2 missing data is also included since otherwise it would be informatively missing) which includes dropouts in the analysis by means of analyzing all post-baseline assessments, i.e., including earlier available assessments while still acknowledging their Month 18 assessment is missing. This approach gives an estimated difference of -1.64 (SE = 0.94), p = 0.083 (N = 119: note that 1 subject with a class 1 imputation in the Applicant’s analysis had no post-baseline 4SC assessment after Week 4)."
>
> — FDA Integrated Review, p. 60 (https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2024/217865Orig1s000IntegratedR.pdf)

> "The fact that the zero-shift part of the tipping point analysis is not significant also illustrates the inadequacy of the Applicant’s primary missing data handling method."
>
> — FDA Integrated Review, p. 63 (https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2024/217865Orig1s000IntegratedR.pdf)

##### Model 2: Rank-based 4SC at Month 18 (sensitivity; FDA reviewer)

> "Due to possible excessive influence of Class 2 missing data which involves a somewhat arbitrary imputed value (twice the maximum observed 4SC time across all subjects and visits) on the distribution of 4SC for a subject unable to perform the 4SC test, a MMRM analysis based on ranks of 4SC time may have better statistical properties for the analysis of 4SC times. A rank MMRM ANCOVA for 4SC time in the Target population yields a difference in mean ranks at Month 18 of -6.1 (SE = 4.2), p = 0.147."
>
> — FDA Integrated Review, p. 60 (https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2024/217865Orig1s000IntegratedR.pdf)

##### Model 3: VL MFF (MRS) change at Month 18 (sensitivity; FDA reviewer re-analysis of the key secondary/PD endpoint)

> "In fact, if the imputation was based on the mean change at Month 18 in completers from the same treatment group and concomitant steroid therapy stratum, the VL MFF analysis at Month 18 is no longer nominally significant (-2.43 [95% C.I.: -5.06 ,0.21], p = 0.071). The analysis results based on completers only is an estimated difference of -2.17 (SE = 1.39), p = 0.122 (N = 112). The Month 18 difference based on MMRM, which uses all observed post-baseline data without imputation and which is valid under a weaker assumption regarding the missing data, i.e., missing at random, is -2.54 (SE = 1.40), p = 0.073 (N = 114)."
>
> — FDA Integrated Review, p. 66 (https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2024/217865Orig1s000IntegratedR.pdf)

##### Model 4: 4SC change at each visit, with and without time-varying VL MFF terms (supportive/supplementary; sponsor SAP, conditional)

> "A mixed effects model with repeated measures (MMRM) will be fitted to the change from baseline in the primary endpoint to each post-baseline visit at which the endpoint is assessed. The model will include baseline values for: 4SC, time to rise from floor, time to run/walk 10 metres, distance walked in 6 minutes and re-derived age at first dose (in years and months) as covariates, concomitant steroid use (according to the 4 possible strata), treatment and visit as fixed effects and the treatment by visit interaction. F-tests from PROC MIXED will be based on Kenward-Roger’s adjusted degrees of freedom. An unstructured variance/covariance matrix will be used for the repeated visits within a subject. The above model will then be repeated with the addition of the following terms: MRS VL MFF value at each visit, MRS VL MFF by visit interaction, MRS VL MFF by treatment interaction, MRS VL MFF by treatment by visit interaction. For each of the two models, the following will be presented and used to assess whether the treatment effect is reduced by the addition of MRS VL MFF to the model: for each visit included in the model, adjusted least squares means and associated 2-sided CIs will be estimated and presented for givinostat and placebo."
>
> — SAP v6.0, §4.4.7.2, p. 40 (https://cdn.clinicaltrials.gov/large-docs/97/NCT02851797/SAP_001.pdf)

> "The analysis and statistical reporting will be conducted at Veristat using SAS version 9.2 or higher."
>
> — SAP v6.0, general considerations, p. 8 (https://cdn.clinicaltrials.gov/large-docs/97/NCT02851797/SAP_001.pdf)

### Mavorixafor (Xolremdi) — NDA 218709

- Therapeutic area: Rare Disease / Genetic / Metabolic-genetic (WHIM syndrome)
- Sponsor: X4 Pharmaceuticals, Inc.
- Approval year: 2024 (April 26, 2024)
- Trial: X4P-001-103 ("4WHIM"), NCT03995108; N=31 randomized (17 placebo, 14 mavorixafor), ITT

#### Model 1: TATANC (hours ANC ≥500 cells/µL over 24 h), overall across Weeks 13/26/39/52 (primary)

- Model family: MMRM
- Response: raw TATANC (hours) at each post-baseline visit (not change from baseline); baseline TAT as covariate [IntegratedR p.35-36]
- Fixed effects: treatment, visit (Weeks 13, 26, 39, 52), treatment×visit, Ig use (randomization stratum), baseline TAT [IntegratedR p.36]
- Random effects: verbatim "participant as the repeated random effect" [IntegratedR p.36]; effectively the SAS REPEATED subject (R-matrix), no G-side random effects described
- Covariance: unstructured [IntegratedR p.36; Table 14 footnote p.43]
- Covariance fallback: verbatim "If the unstructured matrix failed to converge, other covariance structures were employed in the following order: compound symmetry, autoregressive, and Toeplitz." [IntegratedR p.36]
- df method: Kenward-Roger [IntegratedR p.36]
- Estimation: Not stated in the Integrated Review (README states REML [README], not verified in source)
- Time coding: categorical visit
- Estimand / contrast: verbatim "An overall adjusted mean estimate (least-squares means) that estimated the treatment effect over visits was calculated ... The inferential p-value was based on overall evaluation." [IntegratedR p.36] — i.e., LS-mean difference averaged across 4 visits, not at a single landmark; by-visit contrasts also reported. Negative LS means / CI bounds truncated ("mapped") to 0.
- Missing data: no imputation of fully missing visits; MAR under MMRM; within-profile missing time points handled by linear interpolation; missing 24-h value imputed by time-0 value [IntegratedR p.39]
- MNAR sensitivity: jump-to-reference MI (reference = placebo) and tipping-point analysis (shift of −20.34 h needed to lose significance, judged implausible since TAT is bounded 0-24) [IntegratedR p.50-51]; sensitivity treating a visit as missing if ≥50% consecutive time points missing; post hoc analysis excluding Week 52 data for 3 placebo subjects mistakenly dosed with open-label mavorixafor and 1 mavorixafor subject who missed dosing (Week 52 nominal p 0.026 vs 0.10 originally) [IntegratedR p.49-50]
- Software: Not stated for the MMRM (SAS PROC MI mentioned only for wart-score imputation) [IntegratedR]; README asserts SAS PROC MIXED [README]
- Results (ITT; placebo N=17, mavorixafor N=14; Week 52 n=17/10): overall LS mean 2.75 h (95% CI 0.00, 5.89) placebo vs 15.04 h (11.16, 18.93) mavorixafor; difference 12.30 h (7.16, 17.43), p<0.0001. By visit: Wk13 15.83 (10.23, 21.43); Wk26 12.58 (6.53, 18.64); Wk39 13.39 (7.92, 18.86); Wk52 7.38 (−1.58, 16.34) [IntegratedR Table 14, p.42-43]
- FDA comments: results confirmed by FDA statistical team; FDA raised sustainability concern because Week 52 CIs overlap; flagged imbalanced dropout (3/14 vs 0/17) as possible bias; concluded sensitivity analyses demonstrated robustness [IntegratedR p.49-51]. Separate concern: TATANC is a PD endpoint, not a validated surrogate.
- Spec source: Integrated Review verbatim (SAP summarized by FDA)

#### Model 2: TATALC (hours ALC ≥1000 cells/µL), overall across Weeks 13-52 (key secondary #1)

- Model family: MMRM
- Response: raw TATALC (hours)
- Fixed effects: treatment, visit (Weeks 13, 26, 39, 52), treatment×visit, Ig use, baseline TAT [IntegratedR p.37]
- Random effects: "participant as the repeated random effect" (R-side)
- Covariance: UN [Table 16 footnote, p.45]; fallback presumably same as primary ("similar MMRM") — Not explicitly stated
- df method: Kenward-Roger [Table 16 footnote]
- Estimation: Not stated
- Time coding: categorical visit
- Estimand / contrast: overall LS-mean difference across visits
- Missing data: same as primary (no imputation, MAR)
- MNAR sensitivity: jump-to-reference and tipping-point analyses also run; consistent [IntegratedR p.51]; post hoc Week-52 dosing-error exclusion analysis (CIs no longer overlapping at Week 52)
- Software: Not stated
- Results: LS mean 4.55 h (2.18, 6.93) placebo vs 15.80 h (12.95, 18.65) mavorixafor; difference 11.25 h (7.53, 14.96), p<0.0001; Wk52 difference 8.90 (2.34, 15.46) [IntegratedR Table 16, p.45]
- FDA comments: confirmed by FDA; same PD-endpoint caveat
- Spec source: Integrated Review verbatim

#### Model 3: Total wart change score at Week 52 (key secondary #3; tested descriptively after hierarchy broke)

- Model family: MMRM (applied to multiply-imputed data)
- Response: total wart change score (sum of regional CGI-C scores, −2 to +1 per region, 3 target regions)
- Fixed effects: treatment, visit (Weeks 26 and 52), treatment×visit, Ig use, baseline CGI-S (sum of 3 target areas), age, sex [IntegratedR p.38; Table 18 footnote p.48]
- Random effects: "participant as the repeated random effect"
- Covariance: UN [Table 18 footnote]
- Covariance fallback: Not stated
- df method: Kenward-Roger [Table 18 footnote]
- Estimation: Not stated
- Time coding: categorical visit (2 visits)
- Estimand / contrast: LS-mean difference at Week 52
- Missing data: missing total wart change score imputed via MI under MAR (SAS PROC MI) before MMRM [IntegratedR p.39]
- MNAR sensitivity: Not stated
- Software: SAS PROC MI for imputation; MMRM procedure Not stated
- Results: placebo N=17 (Wk52 n=17), mavorixafor N=14 (n=11); LS mean −1.15 (−2.21, −0.08) placebo vs −1.08 (−2.45, 0.29) mavorixafor; difference 0.07 (−1.69, 1.82), nominal p=0.94 [IntegratedR Table 18, p.48]
- FDA comments: no wart benefit; reported descriptively because composite endpoint failed
- Spec source: Integrated Review verbatim

Note: composite clinical efficacy endpoint (O'Brien rank-sum ANCOVA) and total infection score (ANCOVA) are not mixed models; FDA win-ratio reanalysis is also not a mixed model. Exploratory MMRMs for change from baseline in ANC (597 vs 23 cells/µL) and ALC (956 vs 71) are mentioned but not specified further [IntegratedR p.42, 44].

#### Verbatim specification excerpts

##### Model 1: TATANC (hours ANC ≥500 cells/µL over 24 h), overall across Weeks 13/26/39/52 (primary)

> "The primary endpoint analysis compared the difference between mavorixafor and placebo with respect to the mean time above ANC threshold using mixed-effects model for repeated measures [...] (MMRM) analysis. The model used TATANC as a dependent variable; treatment, visit (Weeks 13, 26, 39 and 52), treatment*visit, Ig use (randomization strata), and baseline TAT as covariates; and participant as the repeated random effect. The unstructured covariance matrix was used to estimate model within-subject errors. A Kenward-Roger approximation for the degrees of freedom was used. An overall adjusted mean estimate (least-squares means) that estimated the treatment effect over visits was calculated. Two-sided p-values and 95% Cis associated with the least squares (LS) mean difference between groups were presented overall and by visit. The inferential p-value was based on overall evaluation. The estimates for each treatment group and the 95% Cis were also presented. If the unstructured matrix failed to converge, other covariance structures were employed in the following order: compound symmetry, autoregressive, and Toeplitz."
>
> — FDA Integrated Review, SAP summary, pp. 48-49 (https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2024/218709Orig1s000IntegratedR.pdf)

> "No imputation of missing ANC/ALC assessments (i.e., a full visit missing) was performed for the primary endpoint or the first key secondary endpoint analyses. The primary analysis method (i.e., MMRM) treated missing data under the missing at random assumption."
>
> — FDA Integrated Review, Handling of Missing Data, p. 52 (https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2024/218709Orig1s000IntegratedR.pdf)

> "The analysis results (LS mean, LS mean difference, 95% CI, P-value) are based on an MMRM analysis with time above threshold (TAT) as a dependent variable; treatment, visit (Weeks 13, 26, 39 and 52), treatment*visit, Ig use (randomization strata), and baseline TAT as covariates; and participant as the repeated random effect. The Kenward-Roger approximation for degrees of freedom is used. The UN covariance structure is employed. Negative values of LS mean or lower bound of 95% CI produced from the model for the actual values are mapped to 0."
>
> — FDA Integrated Review, Table 14 footnote, p. 56 (https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2024/218709Orig1s000IntegratedR.pdf)

> "Jump to reference method: A reference-based multiple imputation approach. Imputation of values in the placebo arm will assume missing-at-random. For imputation of values in the mavorixafor arm, it will be assumed that participants who discontinue the study early immediately adopt a distribution with predicted mean values at future visits similar to participants in the reference arm (placebo arm). This approach assumes that any effect of mavorixafor before discontinuation immediately disappears after discontinuation."
>
> — FDA Integrated Review, sensitivity analyses, p. 64 (https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2024/218709Orig1s000IntegratedR.pdf)

> "Tipping point analysis: a negative value of 20.34 needed to be added to all imputed missing values in the mavorixafor group to make the treatment difference not significant, which is implausible since the TAT value over a 24-hour period should be between 0 and 24."
>
> — FDA Integrated Review, sensitivity analyses, p. 64 (https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2024/218709Orig1s000IntegratedR.pdf)

##### Model 2: TATALC (hours ALC ≥1000 cells/µL), overall across Weeks 13-52 (key secondary #1)

> "The TATALC was compared between treatment groups using a similar MMRM model as used for the primary endpoint, with TAT of ALC used with factors of treatment, visit (Weeks 13, 26, 39 and 52), treatment*visit, Ig use (randomization strata), and baseline TAT as covariates, and participant as the repeated random effect."
>
> — FDA Integrated Review, SAP summary, p. 50 (https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2024/218709Orig1s000IntegratedR.pdf)

Table 16 footnote: identical wording to the Table 14 footnote quoted under Model 1 (UN covariance, Kenward-Roger df).

> "Same sensitivity analyses (i.e., jump to reference analysis, tipping point analysis) were also conducted for the first key secondary endpoint TATALC. The results are consistent with the primary analysis results."
>
> — FDA Integrated Review, sensitivity analyses, p. 64 (https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2024/218709Orig1s000IntegratedR.pdf)

##### Model 3: Total wart change score at Week 52 (key secondary #3; tested descriptively after hierarchy broke)

> "The total wart change score was analyzed using an MMRM model with factors of treatment, visit, treatment*visit, Ig use (randomization strata), baseline CGI-S (sum in the 3 target areas), age, and gender as covariates."
>
> — FDA Integrated Review, SAP summary, p. 51 (https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2024/218709Orig1s000IntegratedR.pdf)

> "The missing total wart change score was imputed with the multiple imputation method (under missing at random assumption) using the SAS PROC MI procedure."

> "The analysis results (LS mean, LS mean difference, 95% CI, P-value) are based on an MMRM analysis with total wart change score as a dependent variable; treatment, visit (Weeks 26 and 52), treatment*visit, Ig use (randomization strata), baseline CGI-S (sum in the 3 target areas), age, and sex as covariates; and participant as the repeated random effect. The Kenward-Roger approximation for degrees of freedom is used. The UN covariance structure is employed."

### Arimoclomol (Miplyffa) — NDA 214927

- Therapeutic area: Rare Disease / Genetic / Metabolic-genetic (Niemann-Pick disease type C)
- Sponsor: Zevra Denmark A/S (originally Orphazyme A/S)
- Approval year: 2024 (September 20, 2024; after 2021 CRL)
- Trial: CT-ORZY-NPC-002, NCT02612129; N=50 (34 arimoclomol, 16 placebo), 2:1

#### Model 1: 5DNPCCSS change from baseline to Month 12 (primary, original NDA; sponsor's prespecified analysis)

- Model family: MMRM
- Response: change from baseline in 5-domain NPCCSS (0-25)
- Fixed effects: treatment, visit (visits 3-6 = months 3, 6, 9, 12), treatment×visit, miglustat use (yes/no), baseline 5DNPCCSS [IntegratedR p.~40 and resubmission StatR p.17]. SAP (decoded, README): "fitted with treatment, miglustat level and visit as fixed effects along with a treatment by visit interaction term" [SAP via README]
- Random effects: SAP notation includes subject term s_ij and residual e_ijk ("sij and eijk are assumed to be independent ... multivariate normal") [SAP via README] — FDA describes as standard MMRM with UN within-patient covariance
- Covariance: unstructured — verbatim "An unstructured covariance matrix was used to capture correlations among repeated measures within the same patient." [IntegratedR p.~40]
- Covariance fallback: Not stated
- df method: not specified in SAP; verbatim reviewer note: "The SAP did not specify a method for the degree of freedom in MMRM ... In this review, the default degree of freedom method in SAS Proc Mixed procedure is used, which is the between-subject degrees of freedom. The reviewer observes that the primary efficacy results are not sensitive to the degree of freedom method." [IntegratedR, resubmission StatR p.17]
- Estimation: Not stated in SAP; FDA appendix notes REML variant of its EM re-implementation [IntegratedR p.~226-227]
- Time coding: categorical visit
- Estimand / contrast: treatment effect from treatment×visit term at Month 12; sponsor characterized as a "hypothetical" estimand (all patients adhere to blinded treatment); data after early-escape (open-label arimoclomol) excluded ("censored"); unscheduled-visit data excluded (including a death patient's worst score of 25)
- Missing data: no imputation; MAR [SAP]; Type B meeting (Jan 2018): "MMRM analysis is acceptable for the NPCSS, provided that the sponsor demonstrates that the Missing At Random (MAR) assumption is met."
- MNAR sensitivity: SAP-specified MI under MAR (SAS PROC MI / MIANALYZE, regression imputation), tipping-point analysis (successive worsening imputed in arimoclomol arm, placebo median in placebo arm), nonparametric test [IntegratedR p.48-49]
- Software: SAS (SAP states analysis in SAS; FDA used SAS PROC MIXED and its own EM-algorithm implementation) [IntegratedR]
- Results: arimoclomol N=34 (12-month n=28), placebo N=16 (n=15); LS-mean change 0.72 (SE 0.40) vs 2.12 (0.55); difference −1.40 (95% CI −2.76, −0.03), p=0.0456 [IntegratedR resubmission Table 8]
- FDA comments (major disagreement): FDA rejected the hypothetical estimand and MAR assumption. FDA derived the MMRM's "implicitly imputed values of missing data" (conditional means via EM algorithm, Jennrich-Schluchter 1986) and showed implausible results — e.g., an early-escape patient observed at 16 points at Month 12 was implicitly imputed at 10.8; a patient who died at the worst score (25) was excluded and imputed as improving [IntegratedR p.74-75, Figure 14, Appendix p.226]. FDA's alternatives (while-on-treatment and treatment-policy estimands) used ANCOVA, not MMRM: while-on-treatment −1.17 (−2.65, 0.31), p=0.12; treatment-policy methods 1-4 p=0.16-0.32. This reanalysis was one of three CRL deficiencies.
- Spec source: IntegratedR verbatim + SAP (cipher-decoded, via README)

#### Model 2: NPCCSS natural progression rate (supportive / exploratory, OLE vs natural history)

- Model family: linear mixed model with random intercept and random slope (random-coefficients)
- Response: 5DNPCCSS score over time
- Fixed effects: time (continuous); applied separately to pooled untreated patients (NPC-001 natural-history + NPC-002 placebo) and to arimoclomol-treated patients (2-year data)
- Random effects: random intercept and random slope on time — verbatim "A mixed effect model including time (as a continuous variable), random intercept, and random slope was used for the estimation." [IntegratedR p.~50]
- Covariance: Not stated; df method: Not stated; Estimation: Not stated
- Time coding: continuous
- Estimand / contrast: annual progression slope
- Missing data / MNAR: Not stated
- Software: Not stated
- Results: Applicant: untreated slope 1.7 points/year. FDA re-fit same model: untreated 1.7 (95% CI 0.7, 2.6) vs arimoclomol-treated 1.6 (0.6, 2.5) points/year [IntegratedR p.~50]
- FDA comments: FDA rejected Applicant's comparison of observed 24-month change (2.4) to the natural-history slope as inappropriate (different measures; relies on linearity); its own slopes showed no difference
- Spec source: IntegratedR verbatim

Note: R4DNPCCSS (resubmission primary) and the label's miglustat-subgroup analysis used ANCOVA under while-on-treatment/treatment-policy estimands, not MMRM. Whether secondary endpoints in the SAP used MMRM could not be verified (SAP text layer is cipher-encoded, numerals lost).

#### Verbatim specification excerpts

##### Model 1: 5DNPCCSS change from baseline to Month 12 (primary, original NDA; sponsor's prespecified analysis)

> "Per the SAP, the primary analysis method for the change from baseline to 12 months in the 5DNPCCSS score was based on a mixed model for repeated measures (MMRM). The MMRM included treatment, visit, treatment-by-visit interaction, miglustat use (yes/no), and baseline 5DNPCCSS score. The visits included in the MMRM model were visits 3, 4, 5, and 6 (months 3, 6, 9, and 12). An unstructured covariance matrix was used to capture correlations among repeated measures within the same patient. The hypothetical treatment effect was estimated from the treatment-by-visit interaction term at month 12."
>
> — FDA Integrated Review (original NDA review), §6.2.1.4, p. 156 (https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2024/214927Orig1s000IntegratedR.pdf)

> "According to the SAP, the primary analysis excluded data after initiation of early escape medication (open-label arimoclomol treatment). Thus, for the two patients who met early escape (both randomized to arimoclomol), the 5DNPCCSS scores observed at the following timepoints were excluded from the Applicant’s primary analysis:"
>
> — FDA Integrated Review (original NDA review), p. 156 (https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2024/214927Orig1s000IntegratedR.pdf)

> "The prespecified primary analysis method for the 5DNPCCSS endpoint in the SAP is a mixed model for repeated measures (MMRM). The MMRM included treatment, visit, treatment-by-visit interaction, miglustat use (yes/no), and baseline 5DNPCCSS score. The visits included in the MMRM model are visits 3, 4, 5, and 6 (months 3, 6, 9, and 12). An unstructured covariance matrix is used to capture correlations among repeated measures within the same patient. The treatment effect was estimated from the treatment-by-visit interaction term at month 12. Reviewer Note: The SAP did not specify a method for the degree of freedom in MMRM. However, the SAP states that the MMRM analysis is performed in the SAS. In this review, the default degree of freedom method in SAS Proc Mixed procedure is used, which is the between-subject degrees of freedom. The reviewer observes that the primary efficacy results are not sensitive to the degree of freedom method. Results are similar with different degree of freedom methods available in the SAS Proc Mixed procedure."
>
> — FDA Integrated Review (resubmission statistical review), p. 566 (https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2024/214927Orig1s000IntegratedR.pdf)

> "Regarding patients with early escape, Section 6.1 (Full Analysis Set) of the SAP states the following: “Patients who use the escape route will be censored at the point where they start rescue medication (open label arimoclomol)”."
>
> — FDA Integrated Review (resubmission statistical review), p. 566 (https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2024/214927Orig1s000IntegratedR.pdf)

> "The Agency agreed that a Mixed Model Repeated Measures (MMRM) analysis is acceptable for the NPCSS, provided that the sponsor demonstrates that the Missing At Random (MAR) assumption is met."
>
> — FDA Integrated Review (resubmission review, quoting Type B meeting minutes, Jan 17, 2018), p. 558 (https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2024/214927Orig1s000IntegratedR.pdf)

> "For the continuous primary endpoint, you propose to use MMRM as the primary analysis and the multiple imputation as a sensitivity analysis for dealing with missing data. Note that both analyses require data missing at random (MAR) assumption, which cannot be formally tested. Since data can be missing not at random (MNAR), in addition to proposing some methods for justifying the MAR, you should propose several sensitivity analyses for MNAR (e.g., pattern mixture models or selection models) to further assess the impact of the missing data."
>
> — FDA Integrated Review (resubmission review, quoting FDA advice letter, July 9, 2018), p. 558 (https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2024/214927Orig1s000IntegratedR.pdf)

> "In the SAP Version 4, three “sensitivity” analyses were specified: multiple imputation with the MAR assumption, tipping point analysis, and nonparametric test (see Appendix B of this review for details). Neither pattern mixture models nor selection models assuming MNAR were specified."
>
> — FDA Integrated Review (resubmission review), p. 558 (https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2024/214927Orig1s000IntegratedR.pdf)

> "In the pre-NDA meeting briefing package, the Applicant explained that their prespecified MMRM analysis estimated a treatment effect (hypothetical estimand) under the hypothetical scenario that all randomized patients in the study adhered to their blinded treatments through month 12. [...] However, we did not agree with the Applicant’s hypothetical estimand at the pre-NDA meeting because the hypothetical 5DNPCCSS scores after early escape route or premature study discontinuation due to adverse events are not clinically plausible"
>
> — FDA Integrated Review (original NDA review), p. 190 (https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2024/214927Orig1s000IntegratedR.pdf)

> "In the Applicant’s MMRM analysis, the hypothetical 5DNPCCSS scores at the visits after early escape route or premature study discontinuation were treated as missing data. The Applicant’s MMRM analysis relied on the missing at random (MAR) assumption and did not explicitly impute the missing data. The underlying MAR assumption of the MMRM analysis implies that the conditional distribution (i.e., mean and SD) of a missing hypothetical score given observed data can be reasonably estimated. However, based on our evaluation of the Applicant’s MMRM analysis, we question the appropriateness of the MAR assumption. Specifically, we derived the estimated means of the missing hypothetical scores conditional on the observed trajectories using the Applicant’s MMRM model (for details see Appendix 16)."
>
> — FDA Integrated Review (original NDA review), p. 190 (https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2024/214927Orig1s000IntegratedR.pdf)

> "This subsection provides details of the Statistical Team’s approach to understand how the missing values of the primary endpoint were handled in the SAP-defined mixed model for repeated measures (MMRM) analysis."
>
> — FDA Integrated Review (original NDA review), Appendix, p. 340 (https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2024/214927Orig1s000IntegratedR.pdf)

> "Recall that several algorithms are available in the literature to implement the MMRM model. By default, the SAS PROC MIXED procedure uses a Newton-Raphson algorithm which is different from the EM algorithm described above. In the review team’s evaluation, the results from the SAS PROC MIXED procedure using the Newton-Raphson algorithm were almost identical to those from the EM algorithm with only negligible numerical difference."
>
> — FDA Integrated Review (original NDA review), Appendix, p. 342 (https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2024/214927Orig1s000IntegratedR.pdf)

##### Model 2: NPCCSS natural progression rate (supportive / exploratory, OLE vs natural history)

> "This progression rate was estimated based on a combined dataset from Study NPC-001 (a natural history study) and the placebo arm in Study NPC-002. A mixed effect model including time (as a continuous variable), random intercept, and random slope was used for the estimation. We considered this comparison inappropriate as progression measures are different between the Arim/Arim arm and untreated patients; change from baseline to 24 months versus progression rate (slope) assuming a linearity of progression in time. To illustrate the issue, we estimated progression rate (slope in time) for both arimoclomol-treated patients (based on 2-year data) and untreated patients (based on the pooled data described above) using the same mixed effect model. The estimated progression rate (slope) was 1.7 points/year (95% CI: 0.7, 2.6) for untreated patients and 1.6 points/year (95% CI: 0.6, 2.5) for arimoclomol-treated patients."
>
> — FDA Integrated Review (original NDA review), p. 166 (https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2024/214927Orig1s000IntegratedR.pdf)

### Levacetylleucine (Aqneursa) — NDA 219132

- Therapeutic area: Rare Disease / Genetic / Metabolic-genetic (Niemann-Pick disease type C)
- Sponsor: IntraBio Ltd.
- Approval year: 2024 (September 24, 2024)
- Trial: IB1001-301, NCT05163288; 2-period, 2-sequence crossover (12 wk each, no washout), N=60 (30 per sequence)

#### Model 1: fSARA total score at end of each treatment period (primary evidence per FDA; Applicant's primary was mSARA)

- Model family: MMRM (applied to a 2×2 crossover; repeated measures = the two period-end visits, Visit 4 and Visit 6)
- Response: fSARA total score at end of period (FDA presents both total score and change from baseline, giving identical difference); baseline = Visit 2
- Fixed effects: treatment, period, sequence, baseline value (Visit 2), baseline×period — verbatim "The MMRM included treatment, period, sequence, baseline mSARA value at Visit 2, and baseline-by-period interaction as fixed effects." [IntegratedR §6.2.2.3 p.44]
- Random effects: none described (within-subject UN covariance)
- Covariance: unstructured [IntegratedR p.44]
- Covariance fallback: Not stated
- df method: Not stated
- Estimation: Not stated
- Time coding: categorical period
- Estimand / contrast: LS-mean treatment difference (levacetylleucine − placebo); treatment-policy strategy for intercurrent events (AE discontinuation, rescue/prohibited meds)
- Missing data: per-period LOCF (2 subjects; one died after withdrawal)
- MNAR sensitivity: exclusion of ineligible/deceased subject (−0.45; −0.71, −0.20; p<0.001); alternative imputation with best score 0 (−0.42; −0.70, −0.14; p=0.004); completers n=58 (−0.48; −0.73, −0.22; p<0.001); nonparametric sign test (−0.5; −0.68, −0.31); Period-1-only t-test adjusting for baseline (−0.35; −0.90, 0.19; p=0.202); sequence (carryover) effect p=0.6027 [IntegratedR p.52-53]
- Software: Not stated
- Results: 60 subjects (both sequences N=30); LS mean 5.12 (SE 0.14) levacetylleucine vs 5.57 (0.14) placebo; difference −0.45 (95% CI −0.70, −0.19), p=0.0009 [IntegratedR Table 19, p.51-52; FDA statistical team analysis]
- FDA comments: FDA required its own rescored 4-domain fSARA instead of Applicant's mSARA; FDA assessed sequence effect within the MMRM as carryover check; noted LOCF for one subject biased toward placebo
- Spec source: IntegratedR verbatim (SAP summarized)

#### Model 2: mSARA total score (Applicant's prespecified primary)

- Model family: MMRM; same specification as Model 1 [IntegratedR p.44]
- Results: LS mean difference −0.96 (SE 0.25; 95% CI −1.45, −0.46), p=0.0003 [IntegratedR endpoint summary table following Table 21]
- Other fields: as Model 1
- Spec source: IntegratedR verbatim

#### Model 3: SARA total score (key secondary for US)

- Model family: MMRM, same fixed effects ("period, sequence, treatment, baseline value, and baseline-period interaction"), LOCF for 2 subjects [IntegratedR Table 21 footnote, p.55]
- Results: LS mean 13.87 (0.31) vs 15.15 (0.32); difference −1.28 (−1.91, −0.65), p=0.0001; Period-1-only −1.39 (−2.62, −0.16), p=0.03
- Spec source: IntegratedR verbatim

#### Model 4: Exploratory endpoints — 5DNPCCSS change from baseline, SCAFI, mDRS (exploratory)

- Model family: MMRM "used in the primary analysis" (same fixed effects); for 5DNPCCSS, LOCF not used [IntegratedR Table 86, p.198-199]
- Results: 5DNPCCSS −0.30 (−0.74, 0.15); SCAFI 0.07 (0.0, 0.15); mDRS −0.02 (−0.04, −0.00) [IntegratedR p.197-198]
- Spec source: IntegratedR verbatim

#### Verbatim specification excerpts

##### Model 1: fSARA total score at end of each treatment period (primary evidence per FDA; Applicant's primary was mSARA)

> "The primary efficacy endpoint, mSARA at Visit 4 or Visit 6, was analyzed using a mixed model for repeated measures (MMRM) with an unstructured covariance structure. The MMRM included treatment, period, sequence, baseline mSARA value at Visit 2, and baseline-by-period interaction as fixed effects."
>
> — FDA Integrated Review, §6.2.2.3, p. 58 (https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2024/219132Orig1s000IntegratedR.pdf)

> "Per the SAP, a treatment policy strategy was considered for the primary analysis for the following intercurrent events 1) treatment discontinuation due to AEs, 2) taking the rescue/prohibited medications sulfasalazine or rosuvastatin, or 3) taking of prohibited medications N-acetyl-DL-leucine (Tanganil, racemate of D and L enantiomers) or levacetylleucine as a chemical grade substance or supplied outside of Trial IB1001-301. Therefore, all data collected was used regardless of whether the intercurrent events occurred or not. No subjects had the second and third types of intercurrent events. For missing data, a LOCF on a per-period basis was applied."
>
> — FDA Integrated Review, §6.2.2.3, p. 58 (https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2024/219132Orig1s000IntegratedR.pdf)

> "MMRM adjusting for period, sequence, treatment, baseline value, and baseline-period interaction. Last observation carried forward"
>

### Vanzacaftor/tezacaftor/deutivacaftor (Alyftrek) — NDA 218730

- Therapeutic area: Rare Disease / Genetic / Metabolic-genetic (cystic fibrosis)
- Sponsor: Vertex Pharmaceuticals Incorporated
- Approval year: 2024 (December 20, 2024)
- Trials: SKYLINE 102 (NCT05033080; FAS 398: 202 ELX/TEZ/IVA, 196 VNZ/TEZ/D-IVA) and SKYLINE 103 (NCT05076149; FAS 573: 289 vs 284); active-controlled non-inferiority (margin −3.0 pp)

#### Model 1: ppFEV1 absolute change from baseline through Week 24 (primary, NI; both trials)

- Model family: MMRM
- Response: absolute change from baseline (post-run-in Day 1) in ppFEV1 at Day 15, Week 4, 8, 16, 24
- Fixed effects: verbatim "For Trial 102, the model included fixed categorical effects for treatment, visit, age at screening (<18 versus ≥18 years of age), and treatment-by-visit interaction, with baseline ppFEV1 and baseline SwCl as continuous covariates." Trial 103 adds genotype group (F/F, F/G, F/RF, TCR/non-F) [IntegratedR §16 SAP summary p.346]
- Random effects: none (covariance via R-matrix)
- Covariance: unstructured — "An unstructured covariance structure was used to model the within-subject errors." [p.346]
- Covariance fallback: "If the model estimation did not converge, an alternative covariance structure like compound symmetry would have been used." Trial 103: first collapse genotype to 2 levels (F/F vs non-F/F) or remove it, then CS [p.346]
- df method: Kenward-Roger ("Denominator degrees of freedom for the F-test for fixed effects were estimated using the Kenward-Roger approximation") [p.346]
- Estimation: REML [p.346]
- Time coding: categorical visit
- Estimand / contrast: treatment-policy for off-protocol CFTR modulator use >3 days and treatment discontinuation; contrast = LS-mean difference "through Week 24 (estimated by averaging Weeks 16 and 24)"; NI if lower 95% CI bound ≥ −3.0; supplementary hypothetical-strategy estimand (post-ICE data set to missing) with same MMRM [p.346-347]
- Missing data: MAR conditional on observed data and covariates
- MNAR sensitivity: tipping-point analysis (Figure 101; tipping points "rarely occurred in the clinically plausible missing data assumptions") [p.365]
- Software: Applicant's Not stated; FDA statistical analyst re-analysis "Software: R" [Tables 18, 26]
- Results: Trial 102 (n=193/187): LS mean 0.3 (SE 0.3) ELX/TEZ/IVA vs 0.5 (0.3); difference 0.2 (95% CI −0.7, 1.1), 1-sided NI p<0.00001. Trial 103 (n=276/268): 0.0 (0.2) vs 0.2 (0.3); difference 0.2 (−0.5, 0.9), NI p<0.00001 [IntegratedR Tables 18, 26, p.45, 53]
- FDA comments: Division had recommended a Week-24 landmark analysis to capture durability; Applicant kept "through Week 24" averaging, so FDA ran a post hoc landmark MMRM (Model 2)
- Spec source: IntegratedR verbatim (SAP summary appendix)

#### Model 2: ppFEV1 change from baseline at Week 24, landmark (FDA post hoc sensitivity)

- Model family: MMRM (FDA reviewer/analyst), presumably same model with Week-24 contrast
- Fixed/random/covariance/df: Not stated separately (described only as "an MMRM analysis for change from baseline in ppFEV1 at Week 24")
- Software: R (FDA analyst) — inferred from table source notes; not explicitly stated for this analysis → Not stated
- Results: Trial 102 LS mean difference 0.3% (95% CI −1.3%, 0.8%) as printed (CI does not contain the point estimate; likely a typo in the review); Trial 103 0.2% (−0.6%, 1.0%) [IntegratedR p.~47, 54]
- FDA comments: "For future development programs, the Division continues to recommend landmark analyses for ppFEV1 endpoints."
- Spec source: IntegratedR verbatim

#### Model 3: Sweat chloride absolute change from baseline through Week 24 (key secondary #1)

- Model family: MMRM "similar to the primary analysis" with SwCl at Day 15, Week 4, 16, 24; contrast = average of Weeks 16 and 24 [p.347]
- Results: Trial 102 (n=194/184) LS mean 0.9 (0.8) vs −7.5 (0.8); difference −8.4 mmol/L (−10.5, −6.3), p<0.0001. Trial 103 (n=276/270) −2.3 vs −5.1; −2.8 (−4.7, −0.9), p=0.0034 [Tables 19, 27]
- FDA comments: SwCl is a PD marker; clinical meaning of difference unclear
- Other fields as Model 1

#### Model 4: Proportion with SwCl <60 and <30 mmol/L through Week 24, pooled Trials 102+103 (key secondary #2, #3)

- Model family: GEE (marginal, not mixed-effects)
- Response: binary SwCl below threshold at each visit
- Fixed effects: treatment, age at screening, genotype group (F/MF, F/F, F/G, F/RF, TCR/non-F), visit, treatment×visit, baseline ppFEV1, baseline SwCl [p.347-348]
- Random effects: none (GEE)
- Covariance: logit link, unstructured working correlation; fallback: collapse genotype to 3 levels or remove, then compound symmetry [p.348]
- Estimand / contrast: odds ratio through Week 24 (average of Weeks 16 and 24)
- Results: pooled OR <60: 2.21 (p<0.0001); <30: 2.87 (p<0.0001). Per-trial: Trial 102 OR 4.28 (2.57, 7.11) and 7.19 (3.54, 14.59); Trial 103 1.10 (0.65, 1.87) and 2.06 (1.33, 3.18) [Table 194, p.364-365]
- FDA comments: Division disagreed with pooling across the two trials' different populations and with the clinical meaningfulness of the diagnostic thresholds as response criteria [p.68-69]

#### Model 5: CFQ-R RD change through Week 24; ppFEV1 and SwCl through Week 52 (other secondary)

- Model family: MMRM "similar to the primary analysis"; CFQ-R RD at Weeks 8, 16, 24; Week-52 analyses add Weeks 36 and 52 and average Weeks 16/24/36/52 [p.348-349]
- Results: CFQ-R RD Trial 102 2.3 (−0.6, 5.2), Trial 103 −0.1 (−2.3, 2.1); ppFEV1 W52 0.1 (−0.8, 1.0) and 0.3 (−0.4, 1.0); SwCl W52 −8.0 (−9.9, −6.1) and −2.8 (−4.6, −1.0) [Table 194]
- FDA comments: not multiplicity-controlled; FDA had advised adding a clinically meaningful non-SwCl endpoint to the hierarchy

Note: pulmonary exacerbations used a negative binomial model (no random effects). The review also contains population PK/PD nonlinear mixed-effects models (ppFEV1 and SwCl exposure-response) — not counted here as efficacy analyses.

#### Verbatim specification excerpts

##### Model 1: ppFEV1 absolute change from baseline through Week 24 (primary, NI; both trials)

> "The primary analysis of the primary estimand was performed using a mixed-effects model for repeated measures (MMRM) with change from baseline at Day 15, Week 4, Week 8, Week 16, and Week 24 as the dependent variable. For Trial 102, the model included fixed categorical effects for treatment, visit, age at screening (<18 versus ≥18 years of age), and treatment-by-visit interaction, with baseline ppFEV1 and baseline SwCl as continuous covariates. The model estimated using restricted maximum likelihood. Denominator degrees of freedom for the F-test for fixed effects were estimated using the Kenward-Roger approximation. An unstructured covariance structure was used to model the within-subject errors. If the model estimation did not converge, an alternative covariance structure like compound symmetry would have been used. For Trial 103, the model included an additional fixed categorical effect for genotype group (F/F, F/G, F/RF, TCR/non-F). If the model estimation did not converge, genotype group was considered with two levels (F/F and non-F/F) or removed from the model, and if non-convergence persisted, an alternative covariance structure like compound symmetry would have used. Conditional on the observed data and covariates, missing data was assumed to be missing at random. The primary result obtained from the model was the estimated treatment difference through Week 24 (estimated by averaging Weeks 16 and 24)."
>
> — FDA Integrated Review, §16 SAP summary, p. 370 (https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2025/218730Orig1s000IntegratedR.pdf)

> "The treatment policy strategy will be used to handle treatment discontinuation prior to Week 24, which means that observed ppFEV1 values will be used, if available, after treatment discontinuation."
>
> — FDA Integrated Review, §16 estimand, p. 370 (https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2025/218730Orig1s000IntegratedR.pdf)

> "An alternative estimand was defined similarly to the primary estimand with the exception that intercurrent events were addressed using the hypothetical strategy. In the hypothetical strategy, observed values after intercurrent events were set to missing to provide a conservative and robust test of noninferiority for the primary endpoint. Supplementary analysis of this alternative estimand was performed similarly to the primary analysis."
>
> — FDA Integrated Review, §16 supplementary analysis, p. 371 (https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2025/218730Orig1s000IntegratedR.pdf)

> "The MMRM used for the primary analysis of the primary estimand was used for the subgroup analyses, where the similar model was applied to each category of the subgroup."
>
> — FDA Integrated Review, §16 subgroup analysis, p. 371 (https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2025/218730Orig1s000IntegratedR.pdf)

> "Intercurrent events of premature treatment discontinuation and use of non-trial medications that affect CFTR processing or function for >3 days were handled with a treatment policy strategy. Conditional on the observed data and covariates, missing data was assumed to be missing at random, and its impact was assessed by tipping point analyses."
>
> — FDA Integrated Review, §6.2.2.3, p. 66 (https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2025/218730Orig1s000IntegratedR.pdf)

> "The robustness of the primary analysis, the change from baseline in ppFEV1 through 24 weeks, to missing data was supported by tipping point sensitivity analyses. The tipping points of losing significance are denoted as red cells and, as shown in in Figure 101, rarely occurred in the clinically plausible missing data assumptions in both trials."
>
> — FDA Integrated Review, p. 389 (https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2025/218730Orig1s000IntegratedR.pdf)

##### Model 2: ppFEV1 change from baseline at Week 24, landmark (FDA post hoc sensitivity)

> "The Applicant specified that the primary endpoint would be analyzed through Week 24, defined as the average of the values from Weeks 16 and 24. During the development of VNZ/TEZ/D-IVA, the Division recommended the use of a landmark analysis at Week 24 to better capture durability of treatment effect. The Applicant maintained the through 24-week analysis; therefore, the statistical reviewer and analyst performed an additional landmark analysis using an MMRM analysis for change from baseline in ppFEV1 at Week 24. The landmark analysis at Week 24 resulted in an LS mean difference (95% CI) of 0.3% (-1.3%, 0.8%), which supported the noninferiority of VNZ/TEZ/D-IVA to ELX/TEZ/IVA, as well. In addition, the robustness of the analysis results regarding missing data was supported by the tipping point sensitivity analysis. See Section 16.2 for details. Although the landmark analysis was post hoc and exploratory, the results were supportive of the treatment effect of VNZ/TEZ/D-IVA. For future development programs, the Division continues to recommend landmark analyses for ppFEV1 endpoints."
>
> — FDA Integrated Review, Trial 102, p. 70 (https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2025/218730Orig1s000IntegratedR.pdf)

> "Similar to Trial 102, the Applicant specified that the primary endpoint would be analyzed through Week 24, defined as the average of the values from Week 16 and 24. The statistical reviewer and analyst preformed a landmark analysis at Week 24 that resulted in an LS mean difference (95% CI) of 0.2% (-0.6%, 1.0%)."
>
> — FDA Integrated Review, Trial 103, p. 78 (https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2025/218730Orig1s000IntegratedR.pdf)

### Atrasentan (Vanrafia) — NDA 219208

Therapeutic area: Rare Disease / Genetic / Metabolic-genetic. Sponsor: Novartis (Chinook). Approval year: 2025.

Notes: WebFetch of the IntegratedR failed (>10 MB); PDF downloaded with curl and read via pdftotext. SAP not public; the review's SAP summary is the spec source. Copy-reference MI uses SAS PROC MI MNAR statement (per review text).

#### Model 1: log ratio-to-baseline 24-h UPCR at Week 36 (interim analysis, main stratum IA ITT set) (primary)

- **Trial:** ALIGN (CHK01-01), NCT04573478
- **Endpoint:** log ratio-to-baseline 24-h UPCR at Week 36 (interim analysis, main stratum IA ITT set)
- **Model family:** MMRM
- **Response:** natural-log ratio of post-baseline UPCR to baseline (log change from baseline)
- **Fixed effects:** baseline log UPCR, baseline eGFR, treatment, visit, treatment-by-visit, randomization stratum region (Asia vs other)
- **Random effects:** none stated (within-subject errors via covariance matrix)
- **Covariance:** unstructured [IntegratedR p.33]
- **Covariance fallback:** ARH(1) then AR(1) if non-convergence [IntegratedR p.33]
- **Denominator df:** Kenward-Roger (per SAS code in SAP) [IntegratedR p.33]
- **Estimation:** Not stated
- **Time coding:** categorical visit
- **Estimand / contrast:** ratio of adjusted geometric mean ratios (back-transformed LSM difference) at Week 36, reported as relative % reduction
- **Missing data:** MAR; data after transplant/chronic dialysis and after restricted-medication use (steroids, immunosuppressants, SGLT2i, other IgAN drugs) censored/excluded and treated as MAR
- **MNAR / sensitivity:** all-data-regardless-of-censoring MMRM; MAR MI; copy-reference MI (MCMC for intermittent, Jeffreys prior, by arm x region x screening UPCR; monotone imputed from control model via SAS MNAR statement); FDA tipping-point (Torres et al. 2025 method)
- **Software:** SAS (per SAP program code cited in IntegratedR; version not stated)
- **Result:** N=135 vs 135; GMR Wk36 adj LSM 0.6 (SE 0.05) vs 1.0 (0.05); ratio 0.64 (95% CI 0.55, 0.74); -36% (-45%, -26%); p<0.0001. Sensitivity range 34%-37% reduction (Table 112). SGLT2i stratum N=15/14: ratio 0.71 (0.44, 1.14), p=0.15
- **FDA comments:** Division disagreed with sponsor's data exclusions/ICE assumptions; required all-data-regardless-of-rescue analysis for FDA efficacy review (all-data MMRM ratio 0.63, 95% CI 0.55, 0.73). Subgroup MMRMs add subgroup, trt x subgroup, subgroup x visit, 3-way interaction; FDA added Bayesian hierarchical shrinkage for subgroups
- **Spec source:** StatR-equivalent verbatim (IntegratedR summarizing SAP)

#### Verbatim specification excerpts

##### Model 1: log ratio-to-baseline 24-h UPCR at Week 36 (interim analysis, main stratum IA ITT set) (primary)

> "The primary statistical analysis model is based on the mixed model repeated measures (MMRM) model. The logarithm ratio to baseline in UPCR postbaseline assessments are analyzed using the MMRM adjusting for baseline log UPCR, baseline eGFR, treatment, visit, and treatment-by-visit interaction, and the randomization stratification factor region (Asia versus other regions). An unstructured variance covariance matrix was used to model the within-subject errors. In case of convergence issues, a heterogenous autoregressive (1) (TYPE = ARH(1)) structure will be used, followed by an autoregressive (1) (TYPE = AR(1)) structure if the heterogenous autoregressive (1) does not converge. Per the statistical analysis system (SAS) program code in the SAP, the method of Kenward-Roger approximation was used to estimate the denominator degrees of freedoms. The adjusted least-squares mean (LSM) at each week of analysis for each arm, and the difference in adjusted LSM at each week of analysis comparing atrasentan and placebo, respective 95% confidence interval, and p-values will be reported. The adjusted LSMs and difference in adjusted LSM will be back-transformed and reported as percent change from baseline."
>
> — FDA Integrated Review, p. 51 (https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2025/219208Orig1s000IntegratedR.pdf)

> "For subjects in the main stratum, UPCR (24-hour), UACR (24-hour), total protein (24-hour), and eGFR values based on samples collected after a subject has undergone kidney transplantation, or chronic dialysis (≥30 days cumulatively over one or more periods of time) will be excluded from all primary efficacy analyses of the laboratory parameters."
>
> — FDA Integrated Review, p. 51 (https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2025/219208Orig1s000IntegratedR.pdf)

> "Censoring of the data will occur onward from the start date of the earliest censoring event determined for each laboratory parameter. If a subject uses a systemic steroid for ≥7 days but less than 21 days in the 30 days prior to the Week-36 endpoint assessment, the Week-36 24-hour urine assessments (UPCR, UACR, and total protein) will be censored in the analyses, but the Week 36 and successive eGFR values will not be censored for this event. If a lab assessment is collected on the same date of the start date of the censoring event, the lab assessment will be assumed to have been collected prior to the event and will not be censored. Data that are to be excluded for the primary efficacy analysis are considered missing at random (MAR) according to the MMRM model. To address the potential impact of exclusion of these data and the robustness of the primary efficacy analysis findings to the MAR assumption, the Applicant included several sensitivity analyses. The following relevant analyses of interest are included here with limited detail: MMRM model including all UPCR data collected regardless of censoring: all data collected will be included in the analysis model for the primary statistical analysis model. Copy Reference Multiple Imputation Method Analysis: First, intermittent missing values will be imputed using the Markov Chain Monte Carlo methodology, which assumes a multivariate normal distribution over all variables included in the imputation model, using Jeffrey’s prior. This imputation will be done separately for the group combination of treatment group, randomization stratification factors region, and categories of screening UPCR. The model will include baseline values and postbaseline values through Week 36. After this, the monotone missing values will be multiply imputed using the imputation model built from the control group, i.e., assuming the missing data in the treatment group will have a profile that equals the profile of the control group for all time points (using the MNAR option under the MODEL statement). The model includes baseline UPCR, baseline eGFR, and region."
>
> — FDA Integrated Review, p. 52 (https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2025/219208Orig1s000IntegratedR.pdf)

> "Of note, the Division did not agree with these data exclusions and the assumptions made for the intercurrent events specified for the primary analysis and conveyed this to the Sponsor during discussions of the development program. The Division also indicated that an analysis including all data regardless of rescue would be critical for the efficacy evaluation. For the FDA efficacy review, analysis of the UPCR and eGFR include all data collected regardless of rescue."
>
> — FDA Integrated Review, pp. 52–53 (https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2025/219208Orig1s000IntegratedR.pdf)
>
> *(Matched to the source text only in part: the passage spans a page break or table in the PDF.)*

> "MMRM model fit to the log-transformed ratio with baseline, including log baseline, baseline eGFR, treatment, visit, treatment by visit interaction, and stratification factor region."
>
> — FDA Integrated Review (table footnote), p. 58 (https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2025/219208Orig1s000IntegratedR.pdf)

> "Several sensitivity analyses were performed to assess the robustness of the primary analysis to deviations of the missing data assumption using different imputation methods (e.g., copy-reference and tipping point analysis). Because no subjects could be used as retrieved dropouts in the atrasentan arm, missing data from atrasentan subjects (including any subjects whose data were excluded due to use of restricted medications) were imputed based on the placebo arm using copy-reference (Table 15). The results of sensitivity analyses were consistent with the primary analysis (range: 34% to 37%, with significant one-sided p-value<0.0001) (Table 115). In a tipping point sensitivity analysis, the results were generally robust to deviations of missing data assumptions (Table 115). Analyses of the primary endpoint were conducted by prespecified subgroups (Figure 2). In general, the sample estimates of treatment effect (based on MMRM with missing-at-random multiple imputation) on proteinuria reduction were consistent across all subgroups. Findings for the SGLT2i cohort for the primary efficacy endpoint was consistent with findings in the main stratum IA ITT Set (Table 111)."
>
> — FDA Integrated Review, p. 60 (https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2025/219208Orig1s000IntegratedR.pdf)

##### Model 3: change from baseline in eGFR (interim assessment; Week 136 key secondary at final) (key secondary (interim descriptive assessment))

> "The change from baseline in eGFR will be evaluated using the MMRM model and adjusted for baseline eGFR, baseline natural log of UPCR, treatment, visit, and treatment-by-visit interaction, and the randomization stratification factor region (Asia versus other regions). An unstructured variance covariance matrix will be used to model the within-subject errors. In case of convergence issues, a heterogenous autoregressive (1) (TYPE = ARH(1)) structure will be used, followed by an autoregressive (1) (TYPE = AR(1)) structure if the heterogenous autoregressive (1) does not converge. Per the SAS program code in the SAP, the method of Kenward-Roger approximation will be used to estimate the denominator degrees of freedoms."
>
> — FDA Integrated Review, p. 53 (https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2025/219208Orig1s000IntegratedR.pdf)

##### Model 4: eGFR chronic slope (piecewise linear spline, knots at Weeks 2, 4, 6, 12) (sensitivity (demoted from secondary by protocol Amendment 4))

> "In addition, the following analyses are planned for evaluating the chronic slope and total slope. For the chronic slope analysis, i.e., the rate of change in eGFR after a specified time point (Week X), a piece-wise linear spline mixed-effects model will be used with a knot at Week X to characterize the transition between the acute slope (i.e., based on eGFR data prior to Week X), and change/chronic slope (i.e., based on eGFR data after Week X). The model will be fit to all eGFR data, with intercept, acute slope to characterize the acute effect, the change slope after Week X to characterize the chronic effect, and interaction of treatment with acute slope, and interaction of treatment with change slope after Week X, baseline natural log UPCR, and region stratified category. The between-patient random intercept, random acute slope, and random change slope are assumed. The analysis is repeated for knots set at Weeks 2, 4, 6, and 12. By arm adjusted least-squares means, standard errors, difference in chronic slope between arms and respective 95% CI will be reported. In addition, a separate chronic slope analysis assuming only a linear rate of decline is included using a linear mixed-effects model, allowing for a random slope and random intercept. For this analysis, only data collected after Week X is included in the model."
>
> — FDA Integrated Review, pp. 53–54 (https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2025/219208Orig1s000IntegratedR.pdf)

> "Chronic slope and total slope analyses were removed as secondary endpoints and instead, added as sensitivity analyses."
>
> — FDA Integrated Review (protocol amendment table, Amendment 4), p. 193 (https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2025/219208Orig1s000IntegratedR.pdf)

#### Model 1: change from baseline in blood Phe, mean of Weeks 5-6 (Part 2), PAP (>=30% Part-1 responders) (primary)

- **Trial:** APHENITY (PKU-003), NCT05099640

- **Model family:** MMRM
