##### Model 1: change from baseline in blood Phe, mean of Weeks 5-6 (Part 2), PAP (>=30% Part-1 responders) (primary)

> "The primary endpoint was planned to be analyzed using a mixed model for repeated measures (MMRM) that included effects for treatment, baseline blood Phe, baseline Phe level (<600 μmol/L or ≥600 μmol/L), visit (biweekly from baseline up to Weeks 5-6), and visit-by-treatment interaction. An unstructured covariance matrix was planned for the repeated visits within a participant. The least squares (LS) mean estimate, confidence interval, and 2-sided p-value were presented. The mean and percent change of blood Phe levels at each dose level from baseline was also calculated using a Mixed Model for Repeated Measures (MRMM) similar to the primary analysis. The MMRM model (as fit by the Applicant) implicitly imputes missing data under the assumption of missing at random (MAR). Two additional types of imputation would be performed that do not assume MAR: Control-based imputation: for patients in the PTC923 group who discontinued early, their response distribution after discontinuation was assumed to follow the distribution in the control group Tipping-point analysis to assess how severe departures from MAR must be in order to overturn the conclusion of the primary analysis"
>
> — FDA Integrated Review, p. 52 (https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2025/219666Orig1s000IntegratedR.pdf)

> "LS means, SEs, CIs, and p values are based on the MMRM model on change from baseline in blood Phe with treatment, baseline Phe stratum (<600 or ≥600 μmol/L), visit, and treatment-by-visit interaction; baseline blood Phe as fixed effects; and a random participant effect with an unstructured covariance matrix."

> — FDA Integrated Review (PKU-003 primary results table footnote), p. 62 (https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2025/219666Orig1s000IntegratedR.pdf)

> "Efficacy was to be assessed by the change in Phe concentration from period-specific baseline and compared among the three treatment groups: sepiapterin 20 mg/kg QD, sepiapterin 60 mg/kg QD, and sapropterin 20 mg/kg QD. The mean blood Phe concentrations for Day 3, Day 5 and Day 7 (i.e., “weekly mean analysis”) of each treatment period versus Day 1 pre-dose concentrations were used to calculate change from baseline. The change from baseline in Phe levels was modelled using an MMRM, including fixed effects for overall trial baseline Phe, treatment group, sequence, period, and a random participant effect within each sequence, with a first order autoregressive AR (1) covariance structure. Pairwise comparisons in changes from baseline in Phe were planned between each sepiapterin treatment and the sapropterin treatment by calculating the least squares means with Dunnet’s method of adjustment for multiple comparisons."

#### Verbatim specification excerpts

##### Model 1: 6MWT distance at end of each 12-week period (primary (co-primary))

> "A mixed effect model was used to explore the treatment effect on 6MWT distance at the end of each treatment period. For the mixed effect model, the actual 6MWT values were considered as a dependent variable. The analysis model included terms for treatment, period, and sequence as fixed effects, and subject as random effects. For BTHS-SA score, a similar mixed effect model was used. The model will use the compound symmetry or unstructured, (whichever has a better fit by Akaike’s Information Criterion [corrected] value) within-subject variance-covariance matrix. The estimated least squares (LS) means and their standard errors as well as the estimated treatment effect (differences between treatments) was summarized by treatment group at the end of treatment period. The carryover effect was tested from the sequence term using alpha =0.1. If the sequence term was significant, data only in Treatment Period 1 will also be analyzed, using an analysis of covariance model with baseline as a covariate."
>
> — FDA Integrated Review, p. 103 (https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2025/215244Orig1s000IntegratedR.pdf)

> "p-value and 95% CI of the difference were based on the mixed model where actual 6MWT at end of treatment is the dependent variable. p-value and 95% CI of the difference were based on the mixed model where change from predose 6MWT at end of treatment is the dependent variable."
>
> — FDA Integrated Review (6MWT results table footnotes), p. 107 (https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2025/215244Orig1s000IntegratedR.pdf)

##### Model 2: BTHS-SA total fatigue score at end of period (primary (co-primary))

Same as Model 1 (the BTHS-SA covariance sentence is in the same paragraph).

> "p-value and 95% CI of the difference were based on the mixed model which included treatment, period, sequence, visit, and treatment-by-visit interaction as fixed effects and subject as a random effect. p-value and 95% CI of the difference were based on the mixed model where change from predose at end of treatment is dependent variable."
>
> — FDA Integrated Review (BTHS-SA results table footnotes), p. 109 (https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2025/215244Orig1s000IntegratedR.pdf)

##### Model 3: knee-extensor muscle strength by HHD at Week 12 (secondary (later accelerated-approval intermediate endpoint))

> "A similar mixed effect model from the primary analyses was used for the secondary and exploratory efficacy variables."
>
> — FDA Integrated Review, p. 103 (https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2025/215244Orig1s000IntegratedR.pdf)

> "During Part 1, both co-primary endpoints failed to show any benefit with elamipretide compared to placebo. As shown in Table 4, exploratory results using the Applicant’s pre-specified analysis for muscle strength (unadjusted for baseline) measured by HHD resulted in a least squares mean (LSM) difference (95% CI) between elamipretide versus placebo of 6.7 N (-24.8, 38.2), p=0.65. These results do not support a treatment effect of 12-weeks of elamipretide on muscle strength in patients with BTHS."
>
> — FDA Integrated Review (CDTL/clinical-statistical summary), p. 21 (https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2025/215244Orig1s000IntegratedR.pdf)

> "Reviewer Analysis adjusting for baseline, LSM Diff (95% CI): -3.0 (-32.5, 26.6), p=0.83"
>
> — FDA Integrated Review (Table 4 footnote), p. 21 (https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2025/215244Orig1s000IntegratedR.pdf)

> "In SPIBA-201, the Applicant explored 5 secondary endpoints. Of these endpoints, the changes in muscle strength measured by HHD during Part 2 trended most favorably with a consistent trend toward improvement over a period of 3 years. While we acknowledge there were multiple assessments of muscle strength that trended favorably, and may suggest a treatment effect, post-hoc selection of results based on the observed data makes it more likely that the findings will include some random high bias. The number of endpoints that were assessed in both Part 1 and Part 2 of SPIBA-201 that were inconclusive for benefit, strongly suggests that HHD improvements reflect random variation, including random high bias."
>
> — FDA Integrated Review, p. 21 (https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2025/215244Orig1s000IntegratedR.pdf)

##### Model 4: echocardiographic parameters (LVEDV, LVESV, LVEF etc.) at Week 12 (secondary/exploratory)

Same as Model 3 ("A similar mixed effect model from the primary analyses was used for the secondary and exploratory efficacy variables.").

> "Least Squares Mean Difference was elamipretide 40 mg minus placebo at the end of treatment period. P-value and 95% CI of the difference was based on the mixed model which included treatment, period, and sequence as fixed effects and subject as a random effect"
>
> — FDA Integrated Review (echocardiography table footnote), p. 144 (https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2025/215244Orig1s000IntegratedR.pdf)

##### Model 5: change from baseline in LV stroke volume indexed to BSA (supportive (externally controlled))

> "All 12 subjects participating in the SPIBA-201 study and 12 subjects in the SPIBA-001 NH set had at least two serial echocardiogram assessments. Linear trends in stroke volume between treated and NH subjects were compared using two approaches. In each case, to account for differences due to age, stroke volume measurements were indexed to (divided by) body surface area, estimated on the date the echocardiogram was conducted. For the first approach, the slopes of stroke volume (from baseline through all available time points) for each subject in the treated set were estimated and compared to slopes for all subjects in the NH set. All available time points for subjects in the NH were used. Due to limited data availability for the NH set, three-dimensional (3D)-echocardiogram results were used at each time point, unless they were unavailable, in which case a two-dimensional (2D)-echo result was used, if available. For the treated set, 3D results (routinely available) were used. Slopes for each subject were estimated using ordinary least squares (estimated for any subject with at least two time points) and compared between the treated and NH set using a one-way analysis of variance. Slope estimates for each subject were presented in listings. Results for Wilcoxon Rank Sum and Kolmogorov-Smirnov tests were also provided. For the second approach, a Mixed Model Repeated Measures analysis was performed for change from baseline, where baseline for the NH set was the first available time point. The model considered change from baseline as the dependent variable, treatment as a fixed effect, baseline value and time from baseline (in days) as covariates, repeated for subjects. The treatment differences were estimated with restricted maximum likelihood method and assumed compound symmetry variance-covariance matrix was estimated using a sandwich estimator."
>
> — FDA Integrated Review, pp. 125–126 (https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2025/215244Orig1s000IntegratedR.pdf)

> "At baseline, mean LVSV indexed by BSA was comparable between the TRTS and the Echo NH cohort (28.0 and 26.1 mL/m2, respectively). Postbaseline changes in LVSV were collected over a period of 314 days for the TRTS and 854 days for the Echo NH cohort. The LS mean change in LV stroke volume for the TRTS and the Echo NH cohort was 1.9 and -4.8 mL/m2, respectively, with an LS mean difference between treatment groups of 6.7 mL/m2 (95% CI 2.8, 10.7). See Table 33."
>
> — FDA Integrated Review, p. 148 (https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2025/215244Orig1s000IntegratedR.pdf)

> "Analysis of the 6MWT was based on a propensity score-weighted (using stabilized weights) linear regression model to compare treatment cohorts. Change from baseline for total distance walked at the timepoint of interest was the dependent variable. The model included treatment cohort, and fixed effects for baseline covariates age and height. The unstructured covariance structure was used. The least-squares means estimates, standard errors, and 95% CI from the model were summarized for each cohort. Additionally, their differences in least-squared means, corresponding 95% confidence interval, and p-values were displayed. There were no adjustments for multiple comparisons."
>
> — FDA Integrated Review (6MWT external-control analysis; ambiguous 'unstructured covariance' wording, not counted as a mixed model), p. 125 (https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2025/215244Orig1s000IntegratedR.pdf)

#### Verbatim specification excerpts

##### Model 1: change from baseline in log 24-h UPCR at Month 12 (supportive (phase 2))

> "GM RR was calculated as (1-exponentiated least-squares mean)*100%. The SE of GM RR was calculated as the exponentiated (LSM)*(SE of LSM)*100%. LSM, SE, and 95% CI were estimated from MMRM with natural log scale of uPCR. GM RRD was calculated as (1-exponentiated LSMD)*100% and the corresponding SE was calculated as the exponentiated (LSMD)*(SE of LSMD)*100%. The response variable of the MMRM was the change from baseline in uPCR on the natural log scale. The model included fixed effects of treatment, categorical visit, strata and treatment-by-visit interaction, with a fixed effect covariate of baseline uPCR on natural log scale."
>
> — FDA Integrated Review (Table 7 footnote, VIS649-201), p. 42 (https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2025/761434Orig1s000IntegratedR.pdf)

> "The mean (± standard error) percent change from baseline in 24-hour uPCR over time, evaluation of overall treatment effect using an MMRM, is presented in Figure 17. Sibeprenlimab demonstrated dose dependent reductions in 24-hour uPCR from baseline at Month 12: 47.2% (2 mg/kg), 58.8% (4 mg/kg), and 62.0% (8 mg/kg), all nominally statistically significant versus placebo (p=0.048, 0.001, and 0.0004, respectively). Similar trends were observed for spot uPCR measurements. Month 12 uPCR reductions were maintained through Month 16 in the 4 and 8 mg/kg groups, while the 2 mg/kg group began returning toward baseline by Month 16."
>
> — FDA Integrated Review, p. 120 (https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2025/761434Orig1s000IntegratedR.pdf)

##### Model 2: annualized eGFR slope over ~12 months (Week 48) (exploratory (no formal testing))

> "The annualized slope of eGFR estimated over approximately 12 months (Week 48) will be compared between sibeprenlimab and placebo using a linear mixed-effects model with random effects without formal statistical testing. The model will be fitted with fixed effects of treatment group, time (as a continuous variable), treatment-by-time interaction, stratification factors of uPCR-24h and SGLT2i at randomization, baseline eGFR, and random effects of intercept and time. The stratification factor of eGFR will not be included in the linear mixed-effects model to avoid the collinearity between the stratification factor of eGFR at randomization and the covariate of baseline eGFR. The within-subject correlation will be modeled using an unstructured covariance matrix. If the model does not converge, then the Toeplitz covariance structure will be used."
>
> — FDA Integrated Review, pp. 56–57 (https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2025/761434Orig1s000IntegratedR.pdf)

> "Missing Data and Intercurrent Event Handling The missing data and intercurrent events for the exploratory endpoints were handled in the same manner as for the primary analysis. Sensitivity Analyses The same sensitivity analyses will be performed for annualized slope of eGFR estimated over 12 months as for the primary analysis."
>
> — FDA Integrated Review, p. 57 (https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2025/761434Orig1s000IntegratedR.pdf)

> "Intercurrent Events and Missing Data Handling Intercurrent events (ICEs) of early treatment discontinuation (ICE #1) will be handled using the treatment policy strategy. Use of confounding medications/therapies (ICE #2) will be handled by the hypothetical strategy, where the subject’s uPCR-24h9months will be set as missing after this ICE regardless of whether it was collected or missing. Terminal events related to the kidney during the trial (ICE #3), including kidney transplant, chronic dialysis, or death due to kidney disease prior to the 9-month assessment of uPCR-24h, will be handled by the composite strategy. Under this strategy, first the uPCR-24h9months for a subject will be set as missing after ICE #3 regardless of whether it was collected or missing. Next, the log(uPCR-24h9months) will be imputed with the worst possible values of log(uPCR-24h9months) (observed among nonmissing data across the 2 treatment groups) plus a random error term following a normal distribution with mean of 0 and SD of s. The s is the SD of nonmissing log(uPCR 24hBaseline). All missing data for the primary endpoint will be imputed using a multiple imputation procedure under the missing at random assumption. A fully conditional specification multiple imputation method will be used. The following covariates will be included in the imputation model: Baseline variables will include uPCR-24h, spot uPCR, eGFR, sex at birth, age, region, body mass index, and randomization stratification factors of SGLT2i. Postbaseline measurements of spot uPCR and eGFR collected up to 9 months will also be included in the multiple imputation. Of note, during the IND phase, the Agency expressed interest in a treatment policy strategy to handle ICE #2 and indicated that if the Applicant used a different estimand, then the Applicant should also include supplementary analyses based on all observed data (i.e., a treatment policy approach). On June 17, 2025, the Division asked the Applicant to perform the primary analysis using a treatment policy strategy to address intercurrent events related to treatment discontinuation and the use of rescue therapy, with any missing data following these intercurrent events imputed using a placebo-based multiple imputation approach. On June 24, 2025, the Applicant submitted the requested analysis, and these results were subsequently incorporated into the review."
>
> — FDA Integrated Review (primary-endpoint ICE/missing-data handling, applied to exploratory endpoints), p. 55 (https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2025/761434Orig1s000IntegratedR.pdf)

##### Model 3: change from baseline in eGFR at 12 months (exploratory) / 24 months (key secondary at final analysis) (exploratory (12 mo); key secondary (24 mo, future))

> "The mean change of eGFR from baseline at 12 months (week 48) will be analyzed using a mixed model for repeated measures (MMRM). The model will include treatment group, stratification factors of uPCR-24h and SGLT2i at randomization, visit, treatment by visit interaction, baseline eGFR, and baseline eGFR by visit interaction. No formal testing to compare eGFR change from baseline at 12 months between treatment groups will be performed."
>
> — FDA Integrated Review, p. 57 (https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2025/761434Orig1s000IntegratedR.pdf)

> "The mean change of eGFR from baseline at 24 months was updated as one of the key secondary endpoints and the MMRM model was used for the analysis of change from baseline in eGFR at 24 months. In addition, the mean change of eGFR from baseline at 12 months was updated as one of the exploratory endpoints."
>
> — FDA Integrated Review (SAP Amendment 2 summary), p. 185 (https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2025/761434Orig1s000IntegratedR.pdf)

> "Moved the MMRM analysis to estimate eGFR change from baseline over 24 months and eGFR AUC analysis from supplementary analyses to additional analyses of eGFR in Section 9.2.3 of SAP."
>
> — FDA Integrated Review (SAP Amendment 3 summary), p. 184 (https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2025/761434Orig1s000IntegratedR.pdf)

##### Model 4: eGFR acute/chronic slopes (linear spline, knots Week 8 and Week 12) (sensitivity)

> "Additional sensitivity analysis: a linear spline random mixed-effect model with fixed knots at Week 8 (Month 2) and Week 12 (Month 3) will be used to estimate the acute slopes and chronic slopes before and after Week 8 and Week 12, respectively. The model will be fitted with fixed effects of treatment group, time (as a continuous variable), time2 (time after the fixed knot point, as a continuous variable), treatment-by-time interaction, treatment-by-time2 interaction, stratification factors of uPCR-24h and SGLT2i at randomization, baseline eGFR, and random effects of intercept, time, and time2."

#### Verbatim specification excerpts

##### Model 1: change from baseline in log plasma arginine at Week 24 (primary)

> "The primary efficacy endpoint, change from baseline in log-transformed plasma arginine levels at Week 24, was analyzed using a mixed model for repeated measures (MMRM) with an unstructured covariance structure. The Kenward-Roger approximation was used to estimate denominator degrees of freedom. The MMRM included treatment, visit, baseline arginine level (log-transformed), and treatment-by-visit interaction as fixed effects. The visits included in the MMRM model were Weeks 6, 12, 18, and 24, and did not include the arginine data collected at Week 1."
>
> — FDA Integrated Review, p. 106 (https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2026/761211Orig1s000IntegratedR.pdf)

> "In addition to the Applicant’s primary analysis using change in log-transformed values (i.e., targeting the ratio of geometric means), the Agency conducted additional analyses using absolute and percent change in raw plasma arginine values. Results of these supplemental analyses were consistent with the Applicant’s primary analysis. Since the visits for the MMRM model were not prespecified in the SAP, the review team conducted sensitivity analysis including data from Week 1. Results of this sensitivity analysis were consistent with the Applicant’s primary analysis. Among the 32 randomized subjects, only one pegzilarginase subject did not have the primary endpoint measured at Week 24. This subject discontinued treatment (due to personal reasons, per the Applicant) and ultimately withdrew from the trial at Week 6. For this subject, the change from baseline at Week 24 was imputed using this subject’s Week 6 arginine value in the Applicant’s primary analysis. For this subject, the plasma arginine level was 398µM at baseline and 376µM at 6 weeks. The review team conducted an additional analysis using the baseline value to impute the missing data at Week 24. Results of this sensitivity analysis were similar to the Applicant’s primary analysis."
>
> — FDA Integrated Review, p. 106 (https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2026/761211Orig1s000IntegratedR.pdf)

##### Model 2: absolute change from baseline in plasma arginine (raw scale) at Week 24 (sensitivity (FDA supplemental))

Same as Model 1 (first bullet of the Notes: the Agency's absolute and percent change analyses in raw plasma arginine values).

> "LS mean change from baseline to Week 24 is estimated by mixed model for repeated measures (MMRM) including treatment, visit, treatment-by-visit interaction, and baseline arginine value."
>
> — FDA Integrated Review (Table 158 footnote), p. 392 (https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2026/761211Orig1s000IntegratedR.pdf)

> "The trial achieved its primary endpoint, with pegzilarginase demonstrating a significant reduction in plasma arginine level at Week 24. The estimated mean absolute change in plasma arginine level (without transformation) at Week 24 was −294µM in the pegzilarginase group and 18µM in the placebo group, resulting in a treatment difference of −311µM (95% CI: −380, −242; p<0.0001) (Table 158). The estimated mean percentage change in plasma arginine level at Week 24 was −74.7% in the pegzilarginase group and 0.1% in the placebo group, resulting in a treatment difference of −74.7% (95% CI: −91.4, −58.0) (Figure 10). At Week 24, 90% of"
>
> — FDA Integrated Review, p. 116 (https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2026/761211Orig1s000IntegratedR.pdf)

##### Model 3: 2MWT change from baseline at Week 24 (key secondary)

> "The two key secondary endpoints (change from baseline at Week 24 in GMFM-E and 2MWT) were analyzed using MMRM with an unstructured covariance structure that included treatment, visit, corresponding baseline value, and treatment-by-visit interaction as fixed effects. To control the overall type 1 error rate, these two key secondary endpoints were tested using the Hochberg procedure at a one-sided significance level of 0.025. For each endpoint, the null hypothesis was defined as the two treatment groups had the same mean value."
>
> — FDA Integrated Review, p. 107 (https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2026/761211Orig1s000IntegratedR.pdf)

> "The Applicant’s SAP stated that no imputation would be performed for missing data for the key secondary endpoints and that treatment effect would be estimated based on the MMRM relying on the missing at random assumption. There were 3 subjects out of 32 (9.4%) that had missing values for the 2MWT endpoint and 1 subject (3.1%) that had missing values for the GMFM-E and GMFM-D endpoints. Specifically, one pegzilarginase-receiving subject withdrew at Week 6 and could not be assessed for both the 2MWT and GMFM-E/D at Weeks 12 and 24, one placebo subject developed an adverse event and could not complete assessments for the 2MWT at Weeks 12 and 24, and one pegzilarginase subject was deemed too young (2 years of age) to perform the 2MWT at baseline, and therefore change from baseline in 2MWT at Weeks 12 and 24 could not be calculated. To further evaluate the impact of missing data on the 2MWT walk endpoint, the review team conducted additional sensitivity analyses (Table 155 and Figure 84). In addition to the Applicant’s MMRM approach for the secondary endpoints, the review team conducted a Wilcoxon rank-sum test to test the null hypothesis (Equation 1)."
>
> — FDA Integrated Review, p. 107 (https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2026/761211Orig1s000IntegratedR.pdf)

> "LS mean change from baseline to Week 24 is estimated by MMRM with treatment, visit, treatment-by-visit interaction, and baseline value. b p-value obtained from fitting MMRM"
>
> — FDA Integrated Review (Table 17 footnotes), p. 119 (https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2026/761211Orig1s000IntegratedR.pdf)

##### Model 4: GMFM-88 Part E change from baseline at Week 24 (key secondary)

Same as Model 3 (key secondary MMRM specification and missing-data note).

> "The review team conducted additional sensitivity analyses with a rescored GMFM-88 collapsing response options 1 “initiates” and 2 “partially completes” to one to reduce the likelihood of rater scoring variability across the two levels. Rater variability refers to score changes that are due to differences in the raters instead of differences in the subjects. Therefore, each item in the Agency’s rescored GMFM-E and GMFM-D dimensions was scored on the following revised scale: 0 = did not attempt, 1 = attempted, 2 = completed. Results of this additional sensitivity analysis suggest that consistent numerical trends favoring pegzilarginase are seen in the Agency’s modified scoring and the original scoring (Table 156)."
>
> — FDA Integrated Review, p. 389 (https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2026/761211Orig1s000IntegratedR.pdf)

> "Least-square mean change from baseline to Week 24 is estimated by MMRM with treatment, visit, treatment-by-visit interaction, and baseline value."

#### Verbatim specification excerpts

##### Model 1: CSF heparan sulfate, log fold change from baseline at Week 24 (and Weeks 49, 104, 153) (key secondary (operative accelerated-approval endpoint; descriptive))

> "The SAP specified mixed model for repeated measures (MMRM) analyses for the change from baseline in the log-transformed data for the PD biomarkers. For the CSF HS endpoint, an MMRM analysis was planned with the model, including fixed categorical effects for visit week, age at tividenofusp alfa initiation (two levels: <4 years old and ≥4 years old), genotype, and natural logarithm of the baseline CSF HS as a continuous variable. The models were designed with an unstructured covariance structure, with a compound symmetry structure to be used as a backup in case of convergence issues. The Satterthwaite approximation was specified to estimate denominator degrees of freedom for tests of fixed effects."
>
> — FDA Integrated Review, p. 52 (https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2026/761485Orig1s000IntegratedR.pdf)

> "The models assumed a missing-at-random mechanism for handling missing data, with missing data to be implicitly imputed by the MMRM model. This means that no missing values were replaced with nonmissing values, but the analysis treated the affected time point as having occurred, but no value recorded. The model uses the information from the available data at all time points to provide estimates at each time point. All analyses were descriptive with no hypothesis testing."
>
> — FDA Integrated Review, p. 52 (https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2026/761485Orig1s000IntegratedR.pdf)

> "Regarding the analysis methods for the PD endpoints, the SAP clarified the following difference from the analysis that was mentioned in the final study protocol: In Section 10.4.2.1 of the protocol, percent change from baseline is defined as 100*(change from baseline/baseline); however, the SAP biomarkers will be analyzed in the log scale rather than in the linear scale, due to the skewed distributions. Percent change from baseline are derived from the geometric mean of fold change with back transformation. The population parameter targeted by the Applicant’s proposed percent change from baseline derived from the geometric mean of fold change with back transformation cannot be interpreted as the mean or median percent change from baseline, and as a result, it is challenging to interpret the Applicant’s analysis results. For easier interpretation, the review team conducted descriptive analyses for the mean change and mean percent change from baseline for all biomarker/PD endpoints using the observed data (without transformation). The review team’s analysis approach is aligned with the analysis mentioned in the final study protocol."
>
> — FDA Integrated Review, p. 52 (https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2026/761485Orig1s000IntegratedR.pdf)

> "Table 92 shows results of the Applicant’s MMRM analysis. The geometric log fold change from baseline was used as a response variable, with fixed effects for visit week, age group at tividenofusp alfa initiation, genotype, and natural logarithm of baseline CSF HS. The estimated geometric log fold change from baseline at each visit week, back-transformed to the exponential scale, is similar to the observed percentage change shown in Section 6.2.1.4 despite the MMRM model not estimating the mean percentage change."
>
> — FDA Integrated Review §16.2.1, p. 233 (https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2026/761485Orig1s000IntegratedR.pdf)

> "Adjusted mean and its 95% CI were calculated with an REML-based MMRM with fixed effects for visit week, age group at tividenofusp alfa initiation, genotype, and natural logarithm of baseline CSF HS. Unstructured covariance matrix was used."
>
> — FDA Integrated Review (Table 92 footnote), p. 233 (https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2026/761485Orig1s000IntegratedR.pdf)

> "The Applicant fit separate MMRM models to various subgroups (age group, ERT exposure, and genotype). Each model included the fixed effects that were used in the MMRM fit to the entire data set, except for the variable that represented the subgroup level. Figure 5 shows that the estimates of percentage change from baseline were similarly large across subgroups."
>
> — FDA Integrated Review §16.2.1, p. 234 (https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2026/761485Orig1s000IntegratedR.pdf)

### Atacicept-vymj (Trutakna) — BLA 761486

Therapeutic area: Rare Disease / Genetic / Metabolic-genetic. Sponsor: Vera Therapeutics. Approval year: 2026.

Notes: MMRM stated with 'subject as a random effect'; covariance structure not stated. Hybrid MI (MAR-intermittent, J2R-monotone) then MMRM + Rubin. eGFR results withheld (b(4)).

#### Model 1: change from baseline in ln 24-h UPCR at Week 36 (IAS) (primary (interim analysis))

- **Trial:** ORIGIN 3 (VT-001-0050), NCT04716231
- **Endpoint:** change from baseline in ln 24-h UPCR at Week 36 (IAS)
- **Model family:** MMRM (with subject random effect) on multiply imputed data
- **Response:** change from baseline in natural-log UPCR
- **Fixed effects:** baseline SGLT2i use, region (Asia/Other), baseline eGFR category (3 levels), baseline ln UPCR, treatment, visit (Weeks 12, 24, 36), treatment-by-visit
- **Random effects:** subject as a random effect
- **Covariance:** Not stated
- **Covariance fallback:** Not stated
- **Denominator df:** Not stated
- **Estimation:** Not stated
- **Time coding:** categorical visit
- **Estimand / contrast:** LSMD on log scale; relative reduction 1-exp(LSMD); treatment-policy for discontinuation and rescue/prohibited therapy; dialysis/transplant/death data excluded then imputed with unfavorable values
- **Missing data:** Step 2 intermittent missing: MCMC monotone (SAS PROC MI) by arm under MAR, 100 imputations; Step 3 monotone missing: jump-to-reference; Step 4 MMRM per imputed dataset, Rubin's rules
- **MNAR / sensitivity:** J2R built into primary; while-on-treatment sensitivity; two-way tipping point

#### Verbatim specification excerpts

##### Model 1: change from baseline in ln 24-h UPCR at Week 36 (IAS) (primary (interim analysis))

> "The primary efficacy endpoint was to be analyzed using a mixed-effects model for repeated measures (MMRM) including UPCR data up to Week 36 for the IAS population, with fixed effects for baseline SGLT2i use (Yes or No), region (Asia or Other), baseline eGFR category (<45 mL/min/1.73 m2, ≥45 to <90 mL/min/1.73 m2, or ≥90 mL/min/1.73 m2), baseline log-transformed UPCR, treatment, visit (Weeks 12, 24, 36), and treatment-by-visit interaction, plus subject as a random effect. Results were to include least-squares mean differences (LSMDs) on the natural-log scale with standard error (SE, 95% confidence interval (CI), and p-values at each visit, as well as the relative reduction in geometric mean ratio (1-exp[LSMD]) with SEs and 95% CIs."
>
> — FDA Integrated Review, p. 45 (https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2026/761486Orig1s000IntegratedR.pdf)

> "The Applicant’s original statistical analysis plan (SAP) for the interim analysis (IA) (database lock cutoff date: May 15, 2025) was finalized on February 11, 2025, and is referred to as version 1.0. The SAP for the IA was amended once. Version 2 was finalized on May 23, 2025, based on FDA feedback provided on April 29, 2025, and May 9, 2025. The changes that were made to the SAP in this amendment do not raise concerns about the interpretability of the trial results."
>
> — FDA Integrated Review, p. 42 (https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2026/761486Orig1s000IntegratedR.pdf)

> "Intercurrent Events and Missing Data Handling Intercurrent Events (ICEs) included: (1) treatment discontinuation, (2) rescue therapy initiation, (3) prohibited therapy initiation, (4) dialysis/transplant/death. Handling Strategy Step 1 - ICE Strategy: Treatment discontinuation and rescue/prohibited therapy use followed the treatment policy strategy. For dialysis/transplant/death, data after (first) occurrence were excluded as uninterpretable. Step 2 - Intermittent Missing Data: Imputed using multiple imputation (Markov Chain Monte Carlo Monotone in SAS PROC MI) by treatment group under missing at random (MAR) assumption with 100 imputations. Step 3 - Monotone Missing Data: Remaining missing data (withdrawals, missed visits) imputed using jump-to-reference approach (hypothetical strategy). For dialysis/transplant/death ICEs, values after (first) occurrence were imputed again (i.e., replaced) with sufficiently unfavorable values (99th percentile of change from baseline in log(UPCR) from all observed data for both arms) plus random error (residual error from Step 1 model), regardless of other ICEs. Step 4 - Analysis: MMRM performed on each imputed dataset; results combined using Rubin's rules. All UPCR data (including baseline and postbaseline) were to natural log transformed prior to multiple imputation and analysis."
>
> — FDA Integrated Review, pp. 45–46 (https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2026/761486Orig1s000IntegratedR.pdf)

> "Sensitivity Analyses To assess the robustness of the primary analysis to the assumptions used for missing data and for handling ICEs, the following sensitivity analyses were prespecified: While-on-treatment policy will be used to handle all ICEs Two-way tipping point analysis"
>
> — FDA Integrated Review, p. 46 (https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2026/761486Orig1s000IntegratedR.pdf)

> "The primary analysis of UPCR at Week 36 was conducted using an MMRM analysis on the IAS, with intercurrent events handled according to strategies prespecified in the SAP (see Section 6.2.1.5 for details). Missing data were imputed using jump to reference for the atacicept arm (n=3) and multiple imputation under the MAR assumption for the placebo arm (n=2). Results are presented in Table 17. At Week 36, subjects randomized to atacicept achieved a 45.7% reduction in UPCR (95% CI: 37.6%, 52.7%) compared with a 6.8% reduction (95% CI: −7.6%, 19.2%) in subjects randomized to placebo. This corresponded to a statistically significant between-group difference of 41.8% (95% CI: 28.9%, 52.3%; p<0.0001) favoring atacicept at the prespecified significance level of 0.01 (2-sided)."
>
> — FDA Integrated Review, p. 51 (https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2026/761486Orig1s000IntegratedR.pdf)

> "Percentage reduction from baseline was obtained from the geometric mean ratios, where the natural log–transformed ratio to baseline in UPCR (based on 24-hour urine collection) was analyzed using an MMRM."
>
> — FDA Integrated Review (Table 17 footnote), p. 51 (https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2026/761486Orig1s000IntegratedR.pdf)

> "FDA also calculated the Least Squares Mean (95% CI) reduction from baseline in proteinuria for Weeks 12 and 24 using the same MMRM model as was used for the primary efficacy analysis (Figure 3). A treatment effect was observed as early as Week 12 (the first postbaseline measurement), with the two treatment groups continuing to diverge over time through Week 36."
>
> — FDA Integrated Review, p. 51 (https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2026/761486Orig1s000IntegratedR.pdf)

> "The same approach for handling intercurrent events and imputing missing data used for the primary endpoint (UPCR) was applied to the UPCR data at Week 52. Missing data due to subjects not reaching the Week 52 visit window were handled implicitly through MMRM, assuming missing at random (MAR)."
>
> — FDA Integrated Review (subgroup table footnote), p. 55 (https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2026/761486Orig1s000IntegratedR.pdf)

##### Model 3: annualized eGFR total slope through Week 52 (IAS) (exploratory (no formal testing))

> "Exploratory Analyses The following two endpoints were analyzed for eGFR including data up to Week 52 based on the IAS population: Annualized rate of change in eGFR through Week 52 Change from baseline in eGFR by visit up to Week 52 Analysis Methods The annualized slope of eGFR estimated over Week 52 was compared between atacicept and placebo using a mixed-effects model with random intercept and random slope (MMRIRS) without formal statistical testing. In the MMRIRS model, eGFR is the dependent variable with random subject effects (intercepts and slopes) and fixed effects for baseline SGLT2i use, region, baseline eGFR category, baseline total urine protein excretion category, treatment, time, and treatment-by-time interaction. Time (years post-first injection) is continuous, with baseline eGFR assigned time =0. Treatment group differences are constructed via linear contrasts of LS Means, where the eGFR slope difference equals the treatment-by-time interaction parameter."
>
> — FDA Integrated Review, p. 47 (https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2026/761486Orig1s000IntegratedR.pdf)

> "Missing Data and Intercurrent Event Handling Definitions for intercurrent events for these exploratory endpoints were consistent with those used for the primary analysis. Missing data were handled implicitly by the statistical model; no multiple imputation was planned."
>
> — FDA Integrated Review, p. 47 (https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2026/761486Orig1s000IntegratedR.pdf)

No formal testing was performed for these exploratory endpoints."

Therapeutic area: Immunology / Rheumatology / Dermatology. Sponsor: Pfizer. Approval year: 2012.

Notes: HAQ-DI model is a random-patient-intercept model (CS). FDA explicitly rejected the covariance-structure sensitivity as not addressing MAR and did ITT BOCF instead.

#### Model 1: HAQ-DI change from baseline at Month 3 (primary (2nd in fixed-sequence; 3rd in 1044))

- **Trial:** A3921032, A3921045 (ORAL Solo), A3921046 (ORAL Sync), A3921064 (ORAL Standard), A3921044 (ORAL Scan)
- **Endpoint:** HAQ-DI change from baseline at Month 3
- **Model family:** linear mixed model (random intercept) / MMRM with compound symmetry
- **Response:** change from baseline HAQ-DI
- **Fixed effects:** treatment, site/region (US, Europe/Canada, Latin America, Asia/Other), baseline value, visit, treatment-by-visit
- **Random effects:** patient random effect
- **Covariance:** compound symmetry
- **Covariance fallback:** robustness check with AR(1) and unstructured
- **Denominator df:** Not stated
- **Estimation:** Not stated
- **Time coding:** categorical visit
- **Estimand / contrast:** LS mean difference vs placebo at Month 3
- **Missing data:** no imputation; MAR; FAS (randomized with post-baseline data)
- **MNAR / sensitivity:** FDA ITT BOCF reanalysis
- **Software:** Not stated
- **Result:** Applicant FAS diffs: 1032 -0.3 (-0.4,-0.1) both doses; 1045 -0.3/-0.4; 1046 -0.3/-0.4; 1064 -0.3/-0.4 (ADA -0.2); all p<=0.0002. FDA ITT BOCF: diffs -0.2 to -0.4, all p<=0.0007
- **FDA comments:** FDA: MAR 'untestable' and not supported since dropouts may be treatment-related; varying covariance structure 'is not an appropriate sensitivity analysis to assess MAR'; FDA used ITT with BOCF; conclusions unchanged
- **Spec source:** StatR verbatim

#### Verbatim specification excerpts

##### Model 1: HAQ-DI change from baseline at Month 3 (primary (2nd in fixed-sequence; 3rd in 1044))

> "• For HAQ-DI at Month 3 or at Month 6, the mixed-effect model with repeated measures including treatment, site (US, Europe/Canada, Latin America, Asia/Other), baseline value, visit, and treatment-by-visit interaction as fixed effects and patient as random effect was pre-specified to compare treatment difference. Compound symmetry was assumed (though the applicant proposed to check the robustness of the results by fitting other structured covariance matrices, e.g., autoregressive 1, and unstructured. as well). It was also pre-specified that no imputation will be applied to missing data. In one of the communications with the Division, the applicant maintained that the assumption of missing at random for missing data in the HAQ-DI analysis is reasonable, and they gave justifications when different reasons for dropout occur."
>
> — FDA Statistical Review, p. 123 (https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2012/203214Orig1s000StatR.pdf)

> "The applicant assumed a missing-at-random (MAR) mechanism for missing data regardless of reason and used a mixed-effect repeated-measures (MMRM) model to analyze continuous endpoints such as HAQ-DI. Re-analysis of the data by applying baseline observation carried forward (BOCF) imputation for missing data gave similar results to the applicant’s primary analysis."
>
> — FDA Statistical Review (Executive Summary), p. 116 (https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2012/203214Orig1s000StatR.pdf)

> "1. Robustness of efficacy data – analysis sets (ITT vs. FAS excluding subjects without baseline or at least one post-baseline measurements), missing data (MMRM based on MAR assumption on HAQ-DI), statistical analysis models (parametric vs nonparametric analysis on mTSS from study 1044)"
>
> — FDA Statistical Review (Major Statistical Issues), p. 119 (https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2012/203214Orig1s000StatR.pdf)

> "As noted earlier, the applicant’s analyses were conducted on the FAS population, not on the ITT population. The applicant’s analyses excluded non-ignorable number of patients as shown in the Table 2. Also in the analysis of HAQ-DI, the applicant assumed untestable MAR mechanism which is not supported because missing data from dropouts may arise from treatment-related reason such as adverse events. Therefore, BOCF imputation was applied in the analysis of HAQ-DI imputing ‘0’ change from baseline to study endpoint or no improvement to patient with missing value at study endpoint and to those patients in ITT, but not in FAS set (Table 7)."
>
> — FDA Statistical Review, p. 130 (https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2012/203214Orig1s000StatR.pdf)

> "As explained in the statistical analysis plan (SAP), to assess robustness of efficacy data with respect to missing data, the applicant conducted sensitivity analysis on HAQ-DI. They varied the covariance structure from compound symmetry to auto-regressive. However, this approach is not an appropriate sensitivity analysis to assess missing at random (MAR) assumption. therefore, a conservative baseline observation carried forward approach (BOCF) was applied to the missing data to assess the robustness of their positive result against missing not at random scenario."
>
> — FDA Statistical Review, p. 145 (https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2012/203214Orig1s000StatR.pdf)

Sources consulted:

#### Verbatim specification excerpts

##### Model 1: change from baseline in FEV1 over 16 weeks (primary)

> "The primary variable was analyzed using a MMRM model with independent variables of treatment, visit, treatment-by-visit interaction, asthma exacerbations within the past 12 months (yes or no), baseline age (12 -17 years or ≥18 years), gender, height, and baseline FEV1. An unstructured covariance matrix was used for the within-patient correlation modeling. In case there was a convergence problem, a first order autoregressive covariance structure would be assumed instead."
>
> — FDA Statistical Review §3.2.1.2, p. 11 (https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2016/761033Orig1s000StatR.pdf)

> "The primary analysis was based on the full analysis dataset (FAS), including all randomized patients who were treated with at least one dose of study drug. The applicant’s analysis excluded some measurements obtained at scheduled visits that were preceded by usage within 7 days of a limited subset of medications that could significantly confound interpretation. I conducted a sensitivity analysis using all measurements without data exclusions. The primary analysis was also repeated using the multiple imputation method to investigate the impact of missing data on the results."
>
> — FDA Statistical Review §3.2.1.2, p. 12 (https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2016/761033Orig1s000StatR.pdf)

> "Overall change from baseline in FEV1 over 16 weeks and change from baseline to each clinic visit would be analyzed using a mixed model for repeated measures (MMRM) in studies 3081, 3082, and 3083."
>
> — FDA Statistical Review (Executive Summary), p. 7 (https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2016/761033Orig1s000StatR.pdf)

> "The primary endpoint was the change from baseline over 16 weeks in FEV1. In study 3081, patients receiving reslizumab had statistically significantly higher increases from baseline compared to placebo (Figure 1 and Table 5). Both dose levels produced significant improvements in FEV1 over the treatment period. The treatment effect ranged from 115 mL to 160 mL with overlapping 95% confidence intervals. The MMRM estimation that included all measurements without exclusions due to confounding medication produced similar results."
>
> — FDA Statistical Review §3.2.1.4, p. 16 (https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2016/761033Orig1s000StatR.pdf)

##### Model 2: secondary: % predicted FEV1, FVC, FEF25-75, ACQ, AQLQ, ASUI, SABA, EOS (secondary)

> "The same MMRM model as described for the primary efficacy variable analyses was used to analyzed the secondary efficacy endpoints including percent predicted FEV1, FVC, FEF25%-75%, ACQ, AQLQ, ASUI, SABA, and EOS. #### Verbatim specification excerpts

##### Model 1: ISGA success at Day 29 (observed data, visits Days 8, 15, 22, 29) (sensitivity)

> "The protocol specified the primary imputation method to be the multiple imputation (MI) approach. For each treatment arm separately, missing data was imputed using the Markov Chain Monte Carlo (MCMC) method. The protocol specified the following two sensitivity analyses for the handling of missing data: Repeated-measures logistic regression model (GEE), with dichotomized ISGA success as the dependent variable and treatment, analysis center, and visit (i.e., Days 8, 15, 22, and 29) as independent factors. In this analysis, data from all post-baseline visits will be included with no imputation for missing data."
>
> — FDA Statistical Review, p. 9 (https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2016/207695Orig1s000StatR.pdf)

> "The primary imputation method was the multiple imputation (MI) approach using the Markov Chain Monte Carlo (MCMC) method to impute the missing data. The protocol specified the following two sensitivity analyses for the handling of missing data: (i) not impute missing data and analyze using a repeated-measures logistic regression (GEE) with treatment, analysis center, and visit (i.e., Days 8, 15, 22, and 29) in the model and (ii) impute missing data using model-based multiple imputation with treatment and analysis center in the imputation model. In the study reports, the applicant conducted an additional sensitivity analysis where missing data was imputed using the last observation carried forward (LOCF). This reviewer conducted an additional sensitivity analysis where missing data is imputed as failures. The results for the sensitivity analyses as well as the primary imputation method are presented in Table 11. For both trials, the results were generally similar across the various methods for handling missing data."
>
> — FDA Statistical Review, p. 12 (https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2016/207695Orig1s000StatR.pdf)

#### Verbatim specification excerpts

##### Model 1: HAQ-DI change from baseline at Week 16 (key secondary)

> "The continuous HAQ-DI change from baseline at Week 16 was analyzed with a mixed model for repeated measures (MMRM). The repeated-measures analysis was based on the restricted maximum likelihood method assuming an unstructured covariance structure to model the within-subject errors. The model, including treatment, region, prior biologic use, visit (all visits from week 2 to week 16), and treatment-by-visit interaction as fixed effects and baseline as a covariate, was used to test the difference between each active treatment group versus placebo in the change from baseline in HAQ-DI at Week 16. The data collected after treatment discontinuation or rescue were set to missing. Therefore, the MMRM analysis assumed a missing-at-random (MAR) mechanism for missing data due to dropout and post-rescue data."
>
> — FDA Statistical Review, p. 21 (https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2017/761037Orig1s000StatR.pdf)

> "As a sensitivity analysis, data collected after treatment discontinuation or rescue were set to missing, then an LOCF procedure from the point of treatment discontinuation or rescue was used to impute any missing HAQ-DI values for all visits post that point. The change from baseline in HAQ-DI at Week 16 was assessed by fitting an ANCOVA model with the baseline covariate and factors for treatment, region and prior biologic use."
>
> — FDA Statistical Review, p. 21 (https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2017/761037Orig1s000StatR.pdf)

> "There were seven amendments to the original protocol (October 19, 2009): Amendment 1 (February 9, 2010), Amendment 2 (June 1, 2010), Amendment 3 (April 4, 2011), Amendment 4 (November 4, 2011), Amendment 5 (August 8, 2012), Amendment 6 (October 29, 2012), and Amendment 7 (October 8, 2013). The applicant claimed that these amendments were made prior to unblinding and analyses of the efficacy data. The changes included the following: • In the primary method of Part B Cohort 2 missing data handling, the data collected after treatment discontinuation or rescue will be set to missing. No imputation of missing post-baseline values will be performed. Responder status will be determined if possible. With these rules patients will automatically become non-responders for all time points beyond the time point they started rescue medication or discontinued study treatment. (They initially proposed LOCF imputation for treatment discontinuation or rescue.) • Change from baseline in HAQ-DI will be analyzed with a mixed model for repeated measures (MMRM). (They initially proposed an analysis of covariance (ANCOVA) model.)"
>
> — FDA Statistical Review (protocol/SAP amendments), pp. 22–23 (https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2017/761037Orig1s000StatR.pdf)

> "Note: All assessments are set to missing from the time a patient receives rescue medication or discontinues study medication early. No imputation is performed. MMRM with PROC MIXED assuming an unstructured covariance structure: model = baseline, treatment, prior biological use, region, visit, and treatment-by-visit interaction."
>
> — FDA Statistical Review (Table 8 note), p. 30 (https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2017/761037Orig1s000StatR.pdf)

##### Model 2: HAQ-DI change from baseline at Week 12; DAS28-CRP and other continuous secondaries (key secondary)

> "Note: All assessments are set to missing from the time a patient receives rescue medication or discontinues study medication early. No imputation is performed. MMRM with PROC MIXED assuming an unstructured covariance structure: model = baseline, treatment, number of previous anti-TNFs, region, visit, and treatment-by-visit interaction."

Multiple imputation is used to handle the missing HAQ-DI measurements MMRM with PROC MIXED assuming an unstructured covariance structure: model = baseline, treatment, number of previous anti-TNFs, region, visit, and treatment-by-visit interaction."

However, the sensitivity analysis appeared to not address the issue in handling escape since it treated the post escape data as missing prior to doing multiple imputation."

MMRM with PROC MIXED assuming an unstructured covariance structure: model = baseline, treatment, prior biological use, region, visit, and treatment-by-visit interaction."

##### Model 4: mTSS radiographic progression rate over 52 weeks (sensitivity / supplementary (FDA-requested post hoc, estimand #2))

> "The pre-specified statistical analysis of the effect of sarilumab on radiographic progression utilized a linear regression model and an approach often termed linear extrapolation to handle missing and post-escape data. The linear extrapolation approach, which has been used in previous RA trials, imputes a single Week 52 value in patients who escape or withdraw from the study prior to Week 52. In the applicant’s analysis, patient data after escape (+14 days) were considered missing. Then, the applicant fit a line through the baseline score and the last observed radiographic score before escape (+14 days) and used that line to assign a Week 52 value to the patient."
>
> — FDA Statistical Review (addendum, Ref ID 4100256), p. 4 (https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2017/761037Orig1s000StatR.pdf)

> "If the interest is in estimand #2, the linear extrapolation approach requires the assumption that placebo patients’ scores on average would, in the absence of escape, continue to change at the same linear rate as was observed through the time of escape. This assumption is strong and unverifiable, and may tend to overstate true progression on placebo. In addition, the linear extrapolation approach is a single-imputation method that does not appropriately take into account the statistical uncertainty in the imputation process. This leads to underestimates of the variability and overestimates of the degree of evidence of a treatment effect. Alternatively, one can interpret the linear extrapolation approach as providing an estimate of the difference between treatment groups in the on-treatment slope. However, this estimand is likely not a meaningful surrogate for long-term benefit in all patients. For example, patients on sarilumab who show no early progression but cannot tolerate or adhere to the therapy will show benefit (no progression) according to the on-treatment slope despite the fact that they may have progressed after treatment discontinuation. An alternative approach includes in the analysis all observed Week 52 x-ray data, including data collected after treatment discontinuation or escape, with patients analyzed according to their randomized treatment group. This analysis reliably targets estimand #1, the treatment policy estimand. This analysis might also be expected to conservatively target estimand #2, given that patients on placebo who meet escape criteria would be expected to have less future progression in the absence of escape to an effective biologic therapy. During the review cycle, some concerns were raised about the analysis based on all observed data because of the inclusion of data after cross-over from placebo to sarilumab. Therefore, we also considered alternative analyses to more reliably evaluate estimand #2 than the pre-specified linear extrapolation approach. In particular, we sent an information request to the applicant requesting an additional analysis comparing slopes of progression between the treatment arms. The analysis utilized a linear mixed effects model and included all radiographic data observed prior to escape (+14 days), including such data collected at any time point during the 52-week double-blind period. Patient data on the placebo arm after escape (+14 days) were considered missing. Observed data on both sarilumab arms after escape were included in the analysis. The model included the following as covariates: time (study day of x-ray / 365.25), treatment, treatment-by-time interaction, region, and prior biologic use. The treatment-by-time interaction coefficients for the two sarilumab dosing regimens represent differences in slopes (differences in mean changes per year) versus placebo and were of primary interest. This analysis still relies on strong and unverifiable assumptions, e.g., that progression is on average roughly linear over time and that missing values after escape in placebo patients who escape are similar to values over time among placebo patients with observed data, conditional on a linear model of the baseline covariates and the time of the x-ray, and the observed value prior to escape. However, the analysis more appropriately handles statistical uncertainty (presuming the assumptions hold) than the single-imputation linear extrapolation approach. We note that there are a number of alternative methodological approaches that could be considered for evaluating estimand #2— additional research regarding the most appropriate analysis is warranted."
>
> — FDA Statistical Review (addendum, Ref ID 4100256), pp. 4–5 (https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2017/761037Orig1s000StatR.pdf)

> "Discussions with clinical colleagues identified an interest in estimand #2, the difference between treatment groups in the absence of biologic escape on placebo. Therefore, we explored alternative methodologies to more reliably evaluate this estimand than the previously implemented linear extrapolation approach. Ultimately, we requested that the applicant carry out a mixed effects model approach to compare slopes of progression, as described above. We believe that either the analysis including all observed data or the analysis comparing slopes of progression based on a mixed effects model would be a more appropriate choice for deriving and presenting results in labeling than the linear extrapolation approach. Our recommendation is"
>
> — FDA Statistical Review (addendum, Recommendations), p. 6 (https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2017/761037Orig1s000StatR.pdf)

> "(3) Use of either of the alternative analyses would be more consistent with the recommendations in the 2010 National Research Council Report report The Prevention and Treatment of Missing Data in Clinical Trials. In particular, our considerations are based on the goals of evaluating the estimand of interest with minimal and plausible missing data assumptions and ensuring that results are convincing even if those assumptions are violated. The observed data analysis reliably targets one estimand of interest and conservatively targets an alternative estimand of interest, with minimal assumptions. The mixed effects model analysis excluding post-escape data on placebo and comparing slopes is also considered reasonable in this setting—it targets a clear estimand of interest, and although underlying assumptions are unverifiable, sensitivity analyses establish that results are convincing under plausible, alternative assumptions."
>
> — FDA Statistical Review (addendum, Recommendations), p. 7 (https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2017/761037Orig1s000StatR.pdf)

#### Model 2: Change from baseline in ACQ-6 and AQLQ(S)+12 at Week 48/56 (secondary (not multiplicity protected))

#### Verbatim specification excerpts

##### Model 1: Change from baseline in pre-bronchodilator FEV1 and total asthma symptom score at Week 48 (SIROCCO) / Week 56 (CALIMA) (key secondary (multiplicity-protected in EHS stratum; FAS/ELS nominal))

> "The continuous secondary efficacy endpoints including change from baseline in pre- bronchodilator FEV1 at Week 48, change from baseline asthma symptom score at Week 48, change from baseline ACQ-6 score, AQLQ(S) + 12, etc., were analyzed for the 2 Benralizumab treatment groups and the placebo group using a mixed-effect model for repeated measures (MMRM) analysis. For each endpoint, the dependent variable was the change from baseline of the parameter at post baseline scheduled visits up to the EOT visit. The model included treatment group as the explanatory variable and region, the use of maintenance oral corticosteroids (yes/no), visit, and treatment*visit interaction as fixed effects and baseline value as a covariate. The variance-covariance matrix was assumed to be unstructured. Upon non convergence in model fitting, a compound symmetric variance-covariance matrix was to be used instead."
>
> — FDA Statistical Review §3.2.1.2.4, p. 20 (https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2017/761070Orig1s000StatR.pdf)

> "The analyses of the primary and secondary efficacy endpoints followed the ITT principle: the analyses included all data captured during the 48-week double-blind treatment period, including data regardless of whether study treatment was prematurely discontinued, or delayed, and/or irrespective of protocol adherence, unless the patient withdrew consent to study participation."
>
> — FDA Statistical Review §3.2.1.2, p. 18 (https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2017/761070Orig1s000StatR.pdf)

> "The applicant’s blinded data review of the phase 3 asthma exacerbation studies encountered model fitting convergence issues for some of the statistical models. While study protocols indicated that country would be among the baseline covariates adjusted for in formal statistical models, prior to unblinding the study data, the applicant made decision to replace the country covariate effect with region in all analyses where this effect was included2."
>
> — FDA Statistical Review §3.2.1.2, p. 18 (https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2017/761070Orig1s000StatR.pdf)

> "In the eosinophil high strata (EHS), the difference in least-squares mean change from baseline was 0.16 L between Benralizumab Q8W and placebo (95% CI [0.07, 0.25]; p=0.001), and was 0.11 L between Benralizumab Q4W and placebo (95% CI [0.02, 0.20]; p=0.022)."
>
> — FDA Statistical Review §3.2.1.4.2, p. 26 (https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2017/761070Orig1s000StatR.pdf)

##### Model 2: Change from baseline in ACQ-6 and AQLQ(S)+12 at Week 48/56 (secondary (not multiplicity protected))

Model specification: same as Model 1 (StatR §3.2.1.2.4, p. 20, which names ACQ-6 and AQLQ(S)+12 in the same MMRM paragraph).

> "In the high-dose ICS population EHS population, Benralizumab Q8W improved ACQ-6 score compared with placebo (LS Mean Difference: -0.29, 95% CI: [-0.48, -0.10], nominal p-value: 0.003). However, the comparison on ACQ6 score was not multiplicity protected so this result could only be used as supportive descriptive information."

### Sarecycline (Seysara) — NDA 209521

Therapeutic area: Immunology / Rheumatology / Dermatology. Sponsor: Allergan (Almirall trials). Approval year: 2018.

#### Model 1: Absolute change from baseline in inflammatory lesion count at Week 12 (co-primary endpoint) (sensitivity (missing-data handling))

- **Trial:** SC1401 (NCT02320149); SC1402 (NCT02322866)
- **Model family:** MMRM
- **Response:** Change from baseline in inflammatory lesion count
- **Fixed effects:** Treatment, pooled site (analysis center), visit, treatment-by-visit; baseline value as covariate [SAP p.19; MDR p.73]
- **Random effects:** none (covariance modeled via R-matrix only)
- **Covariance:** Unstructured [SAP p.19]
- **Covariance fallback:** Toeplitz (TYPE=TOEP in SAS MIXED) if UN does not converge [SAP p.19]
- **DF method:** Not stated
- **Estimation:** Not stated
- **Time coding:** Visit as fixed effect (Weeks 3,6,9,12); categorical implied
- **Estimand / contrast:** Difference vs placebo at Week 12; 'used to explore the sensitivity of data handling ... for subjects who withdraw' [SAP p.19]
- **Missing data:** Primary = MI (20 imputations, by arm, SAS PROC MI FCS) + ANCOVA; MMRM uses observed data (MAR implicit)
- **MNAR sensitivity:** Worst-case imputation for IGA; BOCF/LOCF for lesion counts (no MNAR for MMRM)
- **Software:** SAS PROC MIXED; SAS version 9.3 or newer [SAP pp.19, ~28]
- **Result:** Observed/MMRM row: SC1401 15.6 vs 10.1 p<0.001; SC1402 15.3 vs 11.2 p<0.001 (mean reductions; p from MMRM) [MDR Table 26 p.76]
- **FDA comments:** Reviewer: results generally similar across imputation methods; no MMRM-specific comment [MDR p.76]. Note: primary ANCOVA was fit in SAS PROC MIXED (Littell et al. 2006) but with pooled site as FIXED effect - not a mixed model [SAP p.18].
- **Spec source:** SAP verbatim (OCR) + MDR

**Notes:** Primary ANCOVA was 'performed using SAS PROC MIXED with the methodology of Littell et al. (2006)' but with pooled site as a FIXED effect and NID residual only, so it is a fixed-effects ANCOVA, not a mixed model (not counted as a model line). Posted SAP is a scanned image; OCR'd locally with tesseract. Verbatim SAP (p.19): "Mixed model repeated measures (MMRM) analysis will be used to explore the sensitivity of data handling for CFB in inflammatory lesion counts for subjects who withdraw from the study. The model will include the fixed effects of treatment, pooled site, and visit, the baseline value as a covariate, and the treatment-by-visit interaction term. An unstructured covariance matrix will be used initially ... If this does not converge, then the Toeplitz covariance structure (TYPE=TOEP in SAS MIXED procedure) will be used instead."

#### Verbatim specification excerpts

##### Model 1: Absolute change from baseline in inflammatory lesion count at Week 12 (co-primary endpoint) (sensitivity (missing-data handling))

> "Mixed model repeated measures (MMRM) analysis will be used to explore the sensitivity of data handling for CFB in inflammatory lesion counts for subjects who withdraw from the study. The model will include the fixed effects of treatment, pooled site, and visit, the baseline value as a covariate, and the treatment-by-visit interaction term. An unstructured covariance matrix will be used initially in the model for the correlation pattern among the repeated measures. If this does not converge, then the Toeplitz covariance structure (TYPE=TOEP in SAS MIXED procedure) will be used instead. If the results from the MMRM analyses differ qualitatively with the results from the primary efficacy analysis, further analyses will be performed to investigate the causes of the difference."
