### Setmelanotide (Imcivree) — NDA 213793

Therapeutic area: Endocrine (genetic obesity: POMC/PCSK1/LEPR deficiency). Sponsor: Rhythm Pharmaceuticals. Approval year: 2020.

Note: Discrepancy: posted SAPs specify an unstructured covariance with random subject effect (fallback CS then Toeplitz) and Satterthwaite df; FDA StatR says 'A compound symmetry covariance matrix was employed'. The FDA reviewer reported only its own ANCOVA, so sponsor LMM estimates were not found. README states no SAP posted; both SAPs are posted.

#### Model 1: Mean percent change from baseline in body weight at ~1 year (DUS) (key secondary #1)

- **Trial:** RM-493-012 (NCT02896192) and RM-493-015 (NCT03287960), single-arm
- **Role:** key secondary #1
- **Model family:** linear mixed model (random intercept)
- **Response:** Percent change from baseline in body weight (all visits)
- **Fixed effects:** time, baseline weight [SAP: 'A linear mixed model repeated measures analysis of variance with a fixed term for time and baseline weight and a random effect for subjects']
- **Random effects:** Random subject intercept [SAP; StatR]
- **Covariance:** SAP: unstructured; FDA StatR: 'A compound symmetry covariance matrix was employed'
- **Covariance fallback:** UN -> CS -> Toeplitz [SAP verbatim]
- **DF method:** Satterthwaite [SAP: 'will use Satterthwaite's degrees of freedom estimates']
- **Estimation:** Not stated
- **Time coding:** Not stated (fixed term for time)
- **Estimand / contrast:** Model-derived mean percent change at ~1 year tested vs 0 (one-sided alpha 0.05); no comparator arm
- **Missing data:** Missingness related to treatment imputed as 0 change (BOCF); unrelated missingness linearly extrapolated or imputed by LMM; observed-data LMM as sensitivity [SAP]
- **MNAR sensitivity:** FDA: all-BOCF and BOCF-for-AE + monotone-regression MI (Rubin) for Study 015 [StatR]
- **Software:** SAS 9.2 or higher [SAP 4.2.3]
- **Result:** Sponsor LMM results not reproduced in StatR. FDA ANCOVA: Study 012 DUS (N=9) -25.6% (95% CI -31.0, -20.1); Study 015 DUS (N=7) -12.8% (-20.5, -5.0); one-sided p<=0.0006 [StatR Table 5]
- **FDA comments:** FDA reviewer replaced the LMM with an ANCOVA (final-visit outcome, baseline covariate) on FAS and DUS; noted lack of parallel control
- **Spec source:** SAP verbatim + StatR verbatim

#### Model 2: Mean percent change in weekly average 'most hunger' score at ~1 year (DUS, age >=12) (key secondary #2)

- **Trial:** RM-493-012 (NCT02896192) and RM-493-015 (NCT03287960), single-arm
- **Role:** key secondary #2
- **Model family:** linear mixed model (random intercept)
- **Response:** Percent change from baseline in weekly average most-hunger score
- **Fixed effects:** time, baseline hunger score [SAP; StatR]
- **Random effects:** Random subject intercept [SAP; StatR]
- **Covariance:** SAP: unstructured; FDA StatR: 'A compound symmetry covariance matrix was employed'
- **Covariance fallback:** UN -> CS -> Toeplitz [SAP verbatim]
- **DF method:** Satterthwaite [SAP: 'will use Satterthwaite's degrees of freedom estimates']
- **Estimation:** Not stated
- **Time coding:** Not stated (fixed term for time)
- **Estimand / contrast:** Mean percent change at ~1 year vs 0
- **Missing data:** As for weight [SAP]
- **MNAR sensitivity:** Not stated
- **Software:** SAS 9.2 or higher [SAP 4.2.3]
- **Result:** FDA ANCOVA: Study 012 DUS (N=7) -27.1% (95% CI -46.9, -7.2); Study 015 DUS (N=7) -43.8% (-64.9, -22.8) [StatR Table 6]
- **FDA comments:** No historical control for hunger; COA team could not confirm construct validity [StatR]
- **Spec source:** SAP verbatim + StatR verbatim

#### Verbatim specification excerpts

##### Model 1: Mean percent change from baseline in body weight at ~1 year (DUS) (key secondary #1)

> "A linear mixed model repeated measures analysis of variance with a fixed term for time and baseline weight and a random effect for subjects will be used to assess the primary efficacy endpoint at approximately 1-yeart. All weight measurements obtained during the study will be included in the model and missing data will be handled as described in Section 4.2.9. An unstructured covariance matrix will be used to model the expected different variances among the participants. In the event the mixed model does not converge with an unstructured covariance matrix; a compound-symmetric then Toeplitz covariance matrix will be employed instead. Additionally, a paired t-test will be derived from the model and compared to no change (0% mean percent weight change from baseline) and will use Satterthwaite's degrees of freedom estimates (1-sided, compared to alpha of 0.05 for the primary success of this endpoint; a comparison to an alpha of 0.025 will also be provided)."
>
> — RM-493-015 SAP, §4.6.2 Key Secondary Efficacy Endpoints (body weight), p. 32 (https://cdn.clinicaltrials.gov/large-docs/60/NCT03287960/SAP_001.pdf)

_The RM-493-012 SAP (NCT02896192) contains the same paragraph (split across pp. 33-34 of that PDF)._

> "The primary method for handling missing primary/key secondary endpoint data at approximately 1 year will first examine the reason for missingness. If unrelated to treatment (e.g.: patient moved), the endpoint will either be extrapolated using a linear model (y=a+b*study week) based on existing data points or imputed using the longitudinal mixed model for analysis. If the reason for missingness is directly related to treatment (lack of efficacy or an AE), weight change at approximately 1 year will be conservatively imputed as 0 kg."
>
> — RM-493-012 SAP, §4.2.9 Handling of missing data, p. 29 (https://cdn.clinicaltrials.gov/large-docs/92/NCT02896192/SAP_001.pdf)

> "For non-primary or key secondary endpoint analyses utilizing a longitudinal mixed model, if a visit it missed, an assumption is made that data will be missing at random, consistent with longitudinal analyses. The first key secondary analysis of the DUS population employs a longitudinal mixed model, and all available data will be included. However, because assuming all missing data is missing at random is too liberal, missing 1 year outcome data will be first imputed as described in the first bullet above (the reason for missingness will first be discerned). As a sensitivity analysis, the model will also be run with observed data; no manual or model- based imputation will be performed."
>
> — RM-493-015 SAP, §4.2.9 Handling of missing data, p. 28 (https://cdn.clinicaltrials.gov/large-docs/60/NCT03287960/SAP_001.pdf)

> "All descriptive statistical analyses will be performed using SAS statistical software (Version 9.2 or higher), unless otherwise noted."
>
> — RM-493-012 SAP, §4.2.3 Computing Environment, p. 26 (https://cdn.clinicaltrials.gov/large-docs/92/NCT02896192/SAP_001.pdf)

> "The continuous key secondary endpoints (percent change from baseline in body weight, weekly average “most hunger”) were analyzed in the DUS population, using a linear mixed model with a fixed term for time and baseline measurement of weight or hunger score and a random effect for subjects. A compound symmetry covariance matrix was employed. The statistical reviewer performed additional analyses of the continuous endpoints using the FAS population. In statistical reviewer’s analyses, an ANCOVA model was used which included measurements from the final visit at 1 year as the outcome and baseline as a covariate."
>
> — FDA Statistical Review, §3.2.2 Statistical Methodologies, p. 9 (https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2020/213793Orig1s000StatR.pdf)

> "There was no missing data for Study 012. For Study 015, the applicant imputed missing values related to study drug as 0 change from baseline, namely baseline observation carried forward (BOCF), and imputed missing values unrelated to study drug using linear extrapolation, with time as a linear factor in the imputation model. The statistical reviewer performed additional sensitivity analyses for Study 015: (1) impute all missing data as BOCF, which is considered a conservative approach, since all subjects with missing values were regarded as non-responders (2) impute missing values due to adverse event as BOCF and impute missing values unrelated to study drug using multiple imputation (monotone regression)."
>
> — FDA Statistical Review, §3.2.2 Statistical Methodologies, p. 9 (https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2020/213793Orig1s000StatR.pdf)

> "1. Linear model contains baseline body weight as a covariate. Two subjects in Study 015 with missing body weight at 1 year: one subject with AE (non-DUS) was imputed as 0 change from baseline. The other subject who die from car accident (DUS) was imputed using multiple imputation and analyzed using Rubin’s rule."
>
> — FDA Statistical Review, Table 5 footnote 1, p. 12 (https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2020/213793Orig1s000StatR.pdf)

##### Model 2: Mean percent change in weekly average 'most hunger' score at ~1 year (DUS, age >=12) (key secondary #2)

> "The second key secondary endpoint is the mean percent change from baseline in weekly average hunger (using “most hunger over the last 24 hours” daily response) in the DUS population (for patients 12 years of age and older). This endpoint will be measured as described above and will be analyzed in a similar manner as the key secondary endpoint. Specifically, it will be analyzed using a linear mixed model for repeated measures analysis of covariance with weekly average hunger percent change from baseline as the outcome and fixed terms for time and baseline hunger and a random effect for subject."
>
> — RM-493-015 SAP, §4.6.2 Key Secondary Efficacy Endpoints (hunger), p. 33 (https://cdn.clinicaltrials.gov/large-docs/60/NCT03287960/SAP_001.pdf)

_FDA Statistical Review text for this endpoint is the same paragraph quoted under Model 1 ('... a linear mixed model with a fixed term for time and baseline measurement of weight or hunger score and a random effect for subjects. A compound symmetry covariance matrix was employed.'). Covariance fallback, Satterthwaite df and missing-data rules: same SAP passages as Model 1._

### Teplizumab-mzwv (Tzield) — BLA 761183

Therapeutic area: Endocrine (delay of Stage 3 type 1 diabetes). Sponsor: Provention Bio. Approval year: 2022.

Note: Primary analysis is Cox/log-rank. No patient-level mixed model contributed to approval. The TN-10 SAP specifies a repeated-measures linear model and GEE for longitudinal markers, and FDA used a study-level random-effects meta-analysis. Both are recorded, but neither is a classic MMRM/LMM finding.

#### Model 1: Immunologic and metabolic markers (e.g., C-peptide) over time up to diabetes onset (exploratory/secondary (longitudinal))

- **Trial:** TN-10 (NCT01030861)
- **Role:** exploratory/secondary (longitudinal)
- **Model family:** repeated-measures linear model ('normal errors linear model for repeated measures'); GEE for categorical or non-normal measures
- **Response:** Marker levels over time
- **Fixed effects:** Not stated
- **Random effects:** Not stated
- **Covariance:** Not stated
- **Covariance fallback:** Not stated
- **DF method:** Not stated
- **Estimation:** Not stated
- **Time coding:** Not stated
- **Estimand / contrast:** Not stated
- **Missing data:** Not stated
- **MNAR sensitivity:** Not stated
- **Software:** Not stated
- **Result:** Not stated as model output; FDA treated TN-10 C-peptide analyses as exploratory and 'uninterpretable' due to informative censoring (OGTT stopped at T1D diagnosis)
- **FDA comments:** StatR: 'These design limitations caused informative censoring and rendered analysis results of available C-peptide data uninterpretable.'
- **Spec source:** SAP verbatim (TN-10 SAP item 4) + StatR

#### Model 2: Change from baseline in log(mean C-peptide AUC+1) at 1 and 2 years (supportive/confirmatory evidence (FDA reanalysis))

- **Trial:** Meta-analysis of 5 new-onset (Stage 3) T1D trials (Protege, AbATE, Study 1, others)
- **Role:** supportive/confirmatory evidence (FDA reanalysis)
- **Model family:** other - study-level two-stage random-effects meta-analysis (FDA); Applicant used one-stage fixed-effects IPD ANCOVA after originally planning random effects
- **Response:** log(mean C-peptide AUC+1) change, after MI within study
- **Fixed effects:** Per-study ANCOVA: treatment, log baseline C-peptide AUC, age; Applicant one-stage adds study and study*treatment
- **Random effects:** Between-study random effect (FDA two-stage)
- **Covariance:** Not applicable
- **Covariance fallback:** Not stated
- **DF method:** Not stated
- **Estimation:** Inverse of within+between-study variance weights [StatR]
- **Time coding:** Not stated
- **Estimand / contrast:** Not stated
- **Missing data:** Not stated
- **MNAR sensitivity:** Not stated
- **Software:** Not stated
- **Result:** 1-year 0.09 (95% CI 0.01, 0.16); 2-year 0.09 (-0.04, 0.22) not significant; I2 89-90% [StatR]
- **FDA comments:** FDA rejected the fixed-effects assumption ('too strong an assumption that rarely holds') and ran random-effects meta-analysis; not a patient-level mixed model
- **Spec source:** StatR verbatim

#### Verbatim specification excerpts

##### Model 1: Immunologic and metabolic markers (e.g., C-peptide) over time up to diabetes onset (exploratory/secondary (longitudinal))

> "4. Longitudinal analyses will assess the effects of teplizumab versus control treatment on immunologic and metabolic markers over time up to the onset of diabetes. Differences between groups in the mean levels of quantitative factors over time will be assessed using a normal errors linear model for repeated measures. Differences between groups in the prevalence of qualitative factors over time will be assessed using generalized estimating equations for categorical measures. Generalized estimating equations may also be employed for the analysis of quantitative factors when the normal errors assumptions are violated (5)."
>
> — TN-10 SAP, item 4, p. 5 (https://cdn.clinicaltrials.gov/large-docs/61/NCT01030861/SAP_001.pdf)

> "The study was not designed to fully support these assessments, because C-peptide was not collected once a patient developed T1D, we performed exploratory analyses utilizing collected data and fully acknowledged restrictions on interpretation posed by the study design limitations. Therefore, we need to remind readers that analyses of C-peptide data collected in Study TN-10 are exploratory in nature. These design limitations caused informative censoring and rendered analysis results of available C-peptide data uninterpretable."
>
> — FDA Statistical Review, §3.2.1.2.2 Secondary Efficacy Endpoints, p. 24 (https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2023/761183Orig1s000StatR.pdf)

##### Model 2: Change from baseline in log(mean C-peptide AUC+1) at 1 and 2 years (supportive/confirmatory evidence (FDA reanalysis))

> "For each study, after multiple imputation (MI) was used to fill in missing values, an analysis of covariance (ANCOVA) was used to estimate the treatment effect. The dependent variable was the change from baseline in log (AUC+1) at the last study visit (2 years for Protégé, AbATE, Study 1 in one meta-analysis, and 1 year for all five studies in another meta-analysis). Covariates were treatment, log (baseline C-peptide AUC+1), and age."
>
> — FDA Statistical Review, §3.3.2.1 Individual Study Analyses, p. 38 (https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2023/761183Orig1s000StatR.pdf)

> "By pooling individual participant data from the five completed studies, a one-stage fixed-effects model that combined and re-analyzed all studies simultaneously was used by the Applicant. On the basis of the individual study analysis ANCOVA model, the meta-analysis model included two additional terms: a fixed-effect term indicating study identities, and a term for treatment-by- study interaction. In their original plan for the one-stage meta-analyses, the Applicant proposed a random-effects approach analysis. The Applicant explained, however, that because all five completed randomized studies to date were included in the meta-analyses, the purpose of the analyses was to assess the effect of these specific studies on the outcome, such that fixed-effects models would be more appropriate for the meta-analyses. The fixed-effects approach assumes that the between- study variance is zero, which is too strong an assumption that rarely holds. Instead, for each analysis time frame, FDA carried out a two-stage random-effects meta-analysis to estimate the overall treatment effect which accounts for the between-study variances."
>
> — FDA Statistical Review, §3.3.2.2 Meta-analyses, p. 38 (https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2023/761183Orig1s000StatR.pdf)

> "We observed high heterogeneity among the individual studies, in both the 1-year and 2-year analyses. The statistics I2, which is often used to measure heterogeneity, was 89% for the 1-year meta-analysis; and 90% for the 2-year meta-analysis. To account for this unignorable between- study variability, for each analysis time frame, we performed a two-stage random-effects meta- analysis to estimate the overall treatment effect. The two-stage random-effects meta-analyses calculated the weighted average of treatment effect estimates from the individual studies, where the weights were given by the inverses of the sum of within study and between-study variances components. At both 1-Year and 2-Year, the overall treatment effects were similar in size with the one-stage fixed effect model estimates; however, the associated confidence intervals were wider and the estimated overall treatment effect at 2-year was not statistically significant."
>
> — FDA Statistical Review, §3.3.4 Results and Conclusions, p. 41 (https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2023/761183Orig1s000StatR.pdf)

### Fezolinetant (Veozah) — NDA 216578

Therapeutic area: Endocrine/Women's health (menopausal VMS). Sponsor: Astellas. Approval year: 2023.

Note: README says no protocol/SAP posted and no multiplicity procedure; the posted SAP (v2.0, 30-Sep-2020) specifies Hochberg across the two doses, with all four co-primaries required per dose. README's p=0.09/0.501 severity values come from the per-protocol sensitivity table, not the primary FAS MMRM. Secondary PROs (PROMIS SD SF 8b, etc.) also used the same MMRM per SAP.

#### Model 1: Change from baseline in mean daily frequency of moderate-to-severe VMS at Weeks 4 and 12 (2 co-primaries) (primary (co-primary))

- **Trial:** SKYLIGHT 1 (NCT04003155) and SKYLIGHT 2 (NCT04003142)
- **Role:** primary (co-primary)
- **Model family:** MMRM
- **Response:** Change from baseline in daily frequency
- **Fixed effects:** treatment, week, smoking status (current vs former/never), treatment*week; baseline VMS measure and baseline weight covariates; baseline measurement*week [SAP; StatR]
- **Random effects:** none (covariance modeled via R-matrix only)
- **Covariance:** Unstructured shared across arms [SAP 6.4.1.1]
- **Covariance fallback:** Toeplitz if UN fails [SAP]
- **DF method:** Kenward-Roger [SAP verbatim]
- **Estimation:** REML [SAP: 'restricted maximum likelihood-based repeated-measures approach']
- **Time coding:** Categorical week (Weeks 1-12)
- **Estimand / contrast:** LS-mean difference vs placebo at Weeks 4 and 12 (LS means weighted by smoker proportion); hypothetical strategy (on-treatment data) for discontinuation [SAP]; Hochberg across 2 doses, all 4 co-primaries must succeed [SAP]
- **Missing data:** MAR, no explicit imputation [SAP]
- **MNAR sensitivity:** Discontinuation-reason-based MI: jump-to-reference (unconditional reference, baseline-only) for AE discontinuations, M=30, analyzed by primary MMRM, Rubin's rules [SAP]; results supported primary [StatR Tables 18-19]
- **Software:** SAS on Unix [SAP]
- **Result:** Week 12 diff vs placebo: SKYLIGHT 1 30 mg -2.39 (95% CI -3.25, -1.52), 45 mg -2.55 (-3.40, -1.70); SKYLIGHT 2 30 mg -1.86 (-2.94, -0.78), 45 mg -2.53 (-3.60, -1.46); all p<0.001. Baseline N 175/173/174 and 167/166/167 [StatR Table 7]
- **FDA comments:** FDA applied 'at least 2 per day / 14 per week' clinical-meaningfulness threshold alongside significance; no MMRM disagreement

- **Trial:** SKYLIGHT 1 (NCT04003155) and SKYLIGHT 2 (NCT04003142)
- **Role:** primary (co-primary)
- **Model family:** MMRM

#### Verbatim specification excerpts

##### Model 1: Change from baseline in mean daily frequency of moderate-to-severe VMS at Weeks 4 and 12 (2 co-primaries) (primary (co-primary))

> "For each of the 4 co-primary efficacy endpoints, a mixed models repeated measures analysis of covariance (MMRM) will be used with treatment group, week (Week 1 through Week 12) and smoking status (current vs former/never) as factors, with baseline weight and baseline VMS as covariates, as well as an interaction of treatment by week and an interaction of baseline measurement by week. An unstructured covariance structure shared across treatment groups will be used to model the within-patient errors (and then Toeplitz if model does not converge). The Kenward-Roger approximation will be used to estimate denominator degrees of freedom and adjust standard errors. This analysis will use a restricted maximum likelihood–based repeated-measures approach. The treatment difference will be estimated at all study weeks (subtract placebo change from baseline from each fezolinetant response). MMRM will use all available on-treatment data to inform mean treatment effect estimates without requiring explicit imputation for missing data due to intercurrent events (i.e., for discontinued subjects). This approach is consistent with the hypothetical strategy used for the estimand, which is to compare subjects as though they had continued on the assigned treatment. Given the primary objective of the study, the analysis should describe the pharmacologic effect of the randomized treatments. The MMRM approach, and the missing at random (MAR) assumption, allows us to hypothesize that subjects had continued on assigned treatment while not being influenced by how subjects might have done without treatment or with alternative treatment(s)."
>
> — 2693-CL-0301 SAP v2.0, §6.4.1.1 Primary Analysis for Primary Efficacy Endpoints, p. 49 (https://cdn.clinicaltrials.gov/large-docs/55/NCT04003155/SAP_001.pdf)

> "Comparisons between the fezolinetant and placebo at Week 4 and Week 12 will be calculated based on least-squares mean contrasts using a 2-tailed 95% confidence interval (CI) and p-values. The LS Means will be estimated using weights proportional to the percentage of women who were randomized as current smokers."
>
> — 2693-CL-0301 SAP v2.0, §6.4.1.1, p. 49 (https://cdn.clinicaltrials.gov/large-docs/55/NCT04003155/SAP_001.pdf)

> "For each of the 4 co-primary efficacy endpoints, a mixed models repeated measures analysis of covariance (MMRM) will be used with treatment group, week (Week 1 through Week 12) and smoking status (current vs former/never) as factors, with baseline weight and baseline VMS as covariates, as well as an interaction of treatment by week and an interaction of baseline measurement by week. An unstructured covariance structure shared across treatment groups will be used to model the within-patient errors (and then Toeplitz if model does not converge). The Kenward-Roger approximation will be used to estimate denominator degrees of freedom and adjust standard errors."
>
> — 2693-CL-0302 SAP v2.0, §6.4.1.1 (same text in the second trial's SAP), p. 49 (https://cdn.clinicaltrials.gov/large-docs/42/NCT04003142/SAP_001.pdf)

> "The MMRM analysis that will be used to perform the primary analysis of the primary endpoint assumes that missingness is at random. That is, the model assumes that the trajectory of VMS events over time for subjects who prematurely discontinue is similar to the trajectory for those observed in their own treatment arm which is valid so long as that assumption is reasonable. Discontinuation-reason based multiple imputation (MI) will be used to examine the sensitivity of the primary analysis results to departures from that underlying assumption and will assess a situation where data for subjects who discontinue early follow a pattern which is missing not at random. Specifically, MI will be used for imputation of missing data, using “Jump to Reference” algorithm (where placebo is the reference group) [Carpenter et al. 2013] for subjects who discontinue active treatment due to AEs (AE reported as primary study drug treatment status in the End of Treatment eCRF). The analysis will be implemented using the general three-step process (imputation phase, followed by analysis phase, followed by pooling phase) described in O’Kelly and Ratitch, 2014. 1. The imputation phase will implement MI via sequential modelling for the “Jump to Reference” algorithm. In particular, when implementing the “Jump to Reference” algorithm via sequential modelling, this means that only baseline values are used in the imputation of missing values for subjects in the fezolinetant 30 mg or 45 mg groups who discontinue due to AEs (this variation of the “Jump to Reference” algorithm is also referred to as the “Unconditional Reference” approach). The imputation phase will generate M imputed datasets, where M=30. 2. The analysis phase will perform the primary MMRM analysis model of the primary efficacy endpoint as described in Section 6.4.1.1 for each of the M imputed datasets. 3. Rubin’s rules will be used to generate an overall set of pooled results which combines the analysis results from the M imputed datasets."
>
> — 2693-CL-0301 SAP v2.0, §6.4.1.2 Discontinuation-reason based multiple imputation, p. 50 (https://cdn.clinicaltrials.gov/large-docs/55/NCT04003155/SAP_001.pdf)

> "In general, the mechanism of missing data due to COVID-19 will be assumed to be missing at random (MAR)."

### Elinzanetant (Lynkuet) — NDA 219469

Therapeutic area: Endocrine/Women's health (menopausal VMS). Sponsor: Bayer. Approval year: 2025.

Note: Unusual fallback: if UN fails, AR(1) plus a random subject intercept, then CS. MMRM was applied to each of 500 MI datasets (treatment-policy retrieved-dropout-style imputation), not as a likelihood-based MAR analysis. The Phase 2b SWITCH-1 trial also used MMRM (IR, supportive).

#### Model 1: Change from baseline in mean daily frequency of moderate-to-severe hot flashes at Weeks 4 and 12 (primary (co-primary; OASIS 3 single primary at Week 12))

- **Trial:** OASIS 1 (NCT05042362) and OASIS 2 (NCT05099159); OASIS 3 (NCT05030584) for frequency
- **Role:** primary (co-primary; OASIS 3 single primary at Week 12)
- **Model family:** MMRM
- **Response:** Change from baseline in daily frequency
- **Fixed effects:** treatment, week, region (US/North America vs rest of world), treatment*week; baseline value covariate; baseline*week [SAP Table 5-3; IR]
- **Random effects:** None under UN; random subject intercept added only if AR(1) fallback used [SAP Table 5-3: 'If AR(1) structure is used, a random subject intercept will also be included in the model']
- **Covariance:** Unstructured shared across arms [SAP; IR]
- **Covariance fallback:** UN -> AR(1) (+ random subject intercept) -> CS; applied per imputed dataset [SAP]
- **DF method:** Kenward-Roger (ddfm=KR) [SAP PROC MIXED code; IR]
- **Estimation:** Not stated (PROC MIXED default REML)
- **Time coding:** Categorical week (1, 4, 8, 12)
- **Estimand / contrast:** LS-mean difference at Weeks 4 and 12, one-sided alpha 0.025; all four co-primaries must succeed; treatment-policy strategy
- **Missing data:** Treatment policy: all data used; intermittent missing imputed by MCMC MI (MAR); post-discontinuation missing imputed by MI regression including on-treatment indicator auxiliaries (retrieved-dropout style, Guizzaro 2021); 500 imputations, each analyzed by MMRM, Rubin's rules [SAP; IR]
- **MNAR sensitivity:** SA2 tipping point: delta 1-10 (frequency) added to elinzanetant-arm imputed values only; also supplementary estimands with censoring + MMRM implicit imputation or baseline imputation (treatment failure) [IR]
- **Software:** SAS 9.4+ PROC MIXED / PROC MI / PROC MIANALYZE; ValidR 3.5.2+ [SAP]
- **Result:** OASIS 1 (N=199/197): Week 4 -3.29 (95% CI -4.47, -2.10); Week 12 -3.22 (-4.81, -1.63). OASIS 2 (N=200/200): Week 4 -3.04 (-4.40, -1.68); Week 12 -3.24 (-4.60, -1.88); all one-sided p<0.0001. OASIS 3 (N=313/315) Week 12 -1.55 (-2.04, -1.05) [IR Tables 18-19]
- **FDA comments:** SA1 (MMRM without imputation, weekly data Weeks 1-12) run post hoc at FDA request; consistent (OASIS 1 Week 12 -2.96, OASIS 2 -2.97) [IR Table 216]; FDA judged Applicant's MI approach reasonable given low dropout
- **Spec source:** SAP verbatim (model table + SAS code) + IR verbatim

- **Random effects:** None under UN; random subject intercept added only if AR(1) fallback used [SAP Table 5-3: 'If AR(1) structure is used, a random subject intercept will also be included in the model']
- **Covariance:** Unstructured shared across arms [SAP; IR]

#### Verbatim specification excerpts

##### Model 1: Change from baseline in mean daily frequency of moderate-to-severe hot flashes at Weeks 4 and 12 (primary (co-primary; OASIS 3 single primary at Week 12))

> "Inference about the primary endpoints will be done based on a mixed model for repeated measures (MMRM). Prior to performing modeling with the MMRM, missing data will be handled in alignment with the estimand strategies for ICEs (described in Section 1.1). Table 5—3 provides a detailed overview of the MMRM model for the change from baseline in frequency of HF. A similar analysis model will be conducted for the change from baseline in severity of HF endpoints."
>
> — OASIS 1 (21651) SAP v3.0, §5.3.2 Main Analytical Approach, p. 30 (https://cdn.clinicaltrials.gov/large-docs/62/NCT05042362/SAP_001.pdf)

> "Dependent variable: Change from baseline in frequency of moderate to severe HF at Week 1, Week 4, Week 8 and Week 12 [...] Factors (class variables): Treatment, Week, Region (stratification factor) Interaction terms: Baseline*Week Treatment*Week Covariance structure: Unstructured (UN) If the convergence cannot be attained with the unstructured correlation matrix, the following alternative structures will be attempted in the specified order: autoregressive(1) (AR(1)), and compound symmetry (CS). The first structure in this list with which the model converges will be used. If AR(1) structure is used, a random subject intercept will also be included in the model. This will need to be applied for each imputed dataset."
>
> — OASIS 1 (21651) SAP v3.0, Table 5—3 Model description, p. 30 (https://cdn.clinicaltrials.gov/large-docs/62/NCT05042362/SAP_001.pdf)

_Table 5—3 covariates row (two-column layout interleaved in the text layer): 'Covariates (continuous variables): Baseline mean daily frequency of HF'._

```sas
PROC MIXED data=DATA;
CLASS subject treatment region Week;
MODEL change = baseline treatment region Week
treatment*Week baseline*Week /ddfm=KR outp=resid s;
REPEATED Week / subject=subject type=un;
RANDOM subject; /* only if AR(1) covariance structure is
used */
LSMEANS treatment*Week /cl diff;
ESTIMATE 'Elinzanetant - Placebo at Week 1' treatment 1 -1
treatment*Week 1 0 0 0 -1 0 0 0 /cl;
ESTIMATE 'Elinzanetant - Placebo at Week 4' treatment 1 -1
treatment*Week 0 1 0 0 0 -1 0 0 /cl;
ESTIMATE 'Elinzanetant - Placebo at Week 12' treatment 1 -1
treatment*Week 0 0 0 1 0 0 0 -1 /cl;
ODS OUTPUT TESTS3=TYPE3_eff LSMeans=LSMEAN ESTIMATES=ESTIM;
RUN;
```

— OASIS 1 (21651) SAP v3.0, Table 5—3 SAS code, p. 31 (https://cdn.clinicaltrials.gov/large-docs/62/NCT05042362/SAP_001.pdf)

> "A treatment policy strategy will be applied to handle all of the specified ICEs in the main estimand. According to this strategy, all collected data should be utilized in the analysis irrespective of occurrence of the ICEs. Although all study participants are expected to be followed after ICEs, some missing data may occur. Missing values that occur while participants continue on their randomized treatment and simply represent missed assessments will be assumed missing at random (MAR). Such missing values are likely to be intermittent and will be imputed using a Monte Carlo Markov Chain (MCMC) multiple imputation (MI) method for imputation of non- monotone missing data. For the baseline value to be imputed, at least 2 post-baseline values out of the 4 post-baseline values (i.e., Week 1, 4, 8 & 12) need to be available. Possible missing baseline values will be imputed together with other intermittent missing values. Absolute values will be used for imputation steps. Missing values that occur after the discontinuation of randomized treatment will be imputed using a MI model (Rubin 1987) such that it aligns with the treatment policy estimand. The MI regression model will include auxiliary variables indicating (yes/no) whether the participant continued on randomized treatment at each visit (i.e., Week 1, 4, 8 & 12). These variables will be included in the imputation model to account for the occurrence of permanent discontinuation of randomized treatment (Guizzaro et al. 2021). In addition to the indicator variables, baseline HF, region and treatment as specified in Table 5—3 as well as previous post-baseline endpoint values will also be included in the imputation model. In case there are less than 10 participants (who permanently discontinued the randomized treatment) across both treatment groups with available post-discontinuation data at any intermediate time point, the indicator variable will not be included in the imputation model for that time point."
>
> — OASIS 1 (21651) SAP v3.0, §5.3.2, p. 31 (https://cdn.clinicaltrials.gov/large-docs/62/NCT05042362/SAP_001.pdf)

> "After the completion of imputation step, change from baseline values will be calculated and each imputed dataset will be analyzed using the MMRM model specified in Table 5—3 to obtain an estimate of the mean change from baseline and of the treatment effect. The results [...] will be combined using the Rubin’s rule (Rubin, 1987) to obtain an overall estimated mean change from baseline and an overall estimated treatment effect. A total of 500 multiple imputation steps will be used."
>
> — OASIS 1 (21651) SAP v3.0, §5.3.2, pp. 31–32 (https://cdn.clinicaltrials.gov/large-docs/62/NCT05042362/SAP_001.pdf)

> "The statistical evaluation will be performed by using the software SAS (release 9.4 or higher; SAS Institute Inc., Cary, NC, USA) and ValidR (version 3.5.2 or higher; Mango Solutions Ltd., UK)."
>
> — OASIS 1 (21651) SAP v3.0, §5.1 General Considerations, p. 21 (https://cdn.clinicaltrials.gov/large-docs/62/NCT05042362/SAP_001.pdf)

> "The prespecified primary analysis to evaluate the superiority of elinzanetant 120 mg to placebo in the four coprimary efficacy endpoints was performed using MMRM analysis including all randomized subjects, even if they stopped treatment temporarily or permanently, or took prohibited medications, following a treatment policy strategy. The MMRM model included treatment group, week (Weeks 1, 4, 8, and 12), and region (United States and the rest of the world) as factors, baseline VMS as covariate, and the interaction effects of treatment by week and baseline measurement by week. An unstructured covariance structure shared across treatment groups was used to model the within-patient errors. The Kenward-Roger approximation was used to estimate denominator degrees of freedom and to adjust standard errors."
>
> — FDA Integrated Review, §6.2.4.2 Analysis of Coprimary Efficacy Endpoints, p. 62 (https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2025/219469Orig1s000IntegratedR.pdf)

> "In the primary efficacy analyses in OASIS 1, OASIS 2, and OASIS 3, the Applicant imputed nonmonotone (intermittent) and monotone missing data using Monte Carlo Markov Chain multiple imputation (MI) method under a missing at random missing data mechanism."
>
> — FDA Integrated Review, §6.2.4.2 Handling of Missing Data, p. 62 (https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2025/219469Orig1s000IntegratedR.pdf)

> "Given the minimal dropout rates and limited missing data within each study (Table 14), the Applicant’s approach to handling missing data in the primary efficacy analysis appears reasonable."
>
> — FDA Integrated Review, §6.2.4.2, p. 63 (https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2025/219469Orig1s000IntegratedR.pdf)

> "Sensitivity analysis 1 (SA1): MMRM analysis without any missing data imputation. The MMRM model used in SA1 was the same as those used in the primary analyses except that SA1 used all data from Weeks 1 to 12 while the primary analyses used data only from Weeks 1, 4, 8, and 12. This sensitivity analysis was conducted by the Applicant post hoc per FDA’s request."
>
> — FDA Integrated Review, §6.2.4.2 Sensitivity Analyses, p. 63 (https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2025/219469Orig1s000IntegratedR.pdf)

> "Sensitivity analysis 2 (SA2): A tipping point analysis was used to assess the sensitivity of the main analysis results to violations of missing at random assumptions used in the primary analyses. In the tipping point analysis, delta adjustments were applied only to the MI values in the elinzanetant arm. For the two coprimary endpoints of VMS frequency, the adjustments were applied with delta values from 1 to 10 with an increase of 1 in each successive tipping point iteration. For the endpoints related to severity of hot flashes, the adjustments were applied with delta values of 0.2 to 2 with an increase of 0.2 in each successive tipping point iteration."
>
> — FDA Integrated Review, §6.2.4.2 Sensitivity Analyses, p. 63 (https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2025/219469Orig1s000IntegratedR.pdf)

##### Model 2: Change from baseline in mean daily severity of moderate-to-severe hot flashes at Weeks 4 and 12 (primary (co-primary))

_Same SAP and IR passages as Model 1: the SAP states 'A similar analysis model will be conducted for the change from baseline in severity of HF endpoints' (quoted in Model 1), and the SA2 tipping-point quote under Model 1 gives the severity deltas (0.2 to 2)._

##### Model 3: Key secondaries: frequency at Week 1; PROMIS SD SF 8b total T-score at Week 12; MENQOL total at Week 12 (key secondary)

> "Three key secondary endpoints in OASIS 1 and OASIS 2 were analyzed similarly to the primary analysis for the coprimary efficacy endpoints. For PROMIS SD SF 8b, the MMRM model used data from Weeks 1, 4, 8, and 12. For MENQOL, the MMRM model used data from Weeks 4, 8, and 12 since Week 1 data were not collected for MENQOL. In the analysis of PROMIS SD SF 8b total T-score and MENQOL total score, score-level missing data were handled by multiple imputation."
>
> — FDA Integrated Review, §6.2.4.3 Analysis of Key Secondary Endpoints, p. 64 (https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2025/219469Orig1s000IntegratedR.pdf)

#### Verbatim specification excerpts

##### Model 1: Mean IOP at 9 timepoints (8AM/12PM/4PM x Week 2, Week 6, Month 3) (sensitivity (FDA reviewer analysis))

> "The reviewer conducted an ANCOVA analysis using the population of all randomized and treated subjects (referred to as FDA-ITT). Additionally, a repeated measures ANCOVA accounting for possible correlation between IOP measurements was conducted. Both analyses provided results which were consistent with the applicant’s findings."
>
> — FDA Statistical Review, Executive Summary, p. 6 (https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2017/207795Orig1s000StatR.pdf)

> "The ANCOVA analysis performed at each time point of each visit separately does not take the possible correlation between IOP measurements taken from the same subject. The reviewer thus performed a repeated measure analysis of covariance that accounted for correlated IOP measurements as part of the sensitivity analyses. The model used an unstructured covariance matrix and included the fixed effects for treatment, visit, time, baseline IOP values, and the interaction of treatment by visit by time. Time was included in the model as a categorical variable. Treatment differences in the mean IOP at each time point of each visit was determined based on least squares means using the above model."
>
> — FDA Statistical Review, §3.2.4.1.2 Sensitivity Analyses, D. Repeated Measures ANCOVA, p. 23 (https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2017/207795Orig1s000StatR.pdf)

> "The results of the analysis of the primary efficacy endpoint using the repeated measures ANCOVA on all randomized and treated subjects with missing data imputed using the hybrid LOCF best/worst approach, on Bausch-ITT with LOCF, and the analysis on all randomized and treated subjects with available data only provided results that are in agreement with the non- inferiority conclusion of the primary efficacy analysis. In all analyses results, Vyzulta was non- inferior to Timolol at all nine post-baseline time points for both studies. However, there was at least one time point at which Vyzulta was not superior to Timolol (Figure 25- Figure 30)."
>
> — FDA Statistical Review, §3.2.4.1.2 D., p. 23 (https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2017/207795Orig1s000StatR.pdf)

##### Model 2: 24-hour supine IOP after 4 weeks (primary of supportive crossover study)

> "The primary efficacy analysis was conducted on all randomized and treated subjects with baseline and at least one post baseline IOP (ITT) using the mixed effects model for repeated measures. The model included fixed effects for baseline, treatment, time (relative to 1st IOP assessment), period, baseline-by-time and treatment-by-time interactions and a random subject effect. The least squares mean difference for treatment and 95% confidence interval was derived from this model. Based on the above model, the applicant reported the mean IOP in the Vyzulta and Timolol arms respectively as 21.77 mm Hg and 23.55 mm Hg leading to a treatment difference of -1.78 (95% CI -2.38, 1.12)."
>
> — FDA Statistical Review, §6.4 Summary results: Study 803, p. 54 (https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2017/207795Orig1s000StatR.pdf)

### Brolucizumab-dbll (Beovu) — BLA 761125

Therapeutic area: Ophthalmology (nAMD). Sponsor: Novartis. Approval year: 2019.

Note: The primary analysis is ANOVA with LOCF (fit in PROC MIXED, without repeated measures). MMRM is supportive only.

#### Model 1: BCVA change from baseline at Week 48 (primary) and average over Weeks 36-48 (first key secondary) (supportive/sensitivity)

- **Trial:** HAWK (NCT02307682) and HARRIER (NCT02434328)
- **Role:** supportive/sensitivity
- **Model family:** MMRM
- **Response:** Change from baseline in BCVA (ETDRS letters)
- **Fixed effects:** treatment, visit, baseline BCVA category, age category, treatment*visit [SAP; StatR]
- **Random effects:** none (covariance modeled via R-matrix only)
- **Covariance:** Unstructured [SAP; StatR]
- **Covariance fallback:** UN -> VC -> CS -> AR(1) -> Toeplitz [SAP verbatim]
- **DF method:** Kenward-Roger (DDFM=KENWARDROGER in SAP pseudo-code)
- **Estimation:** Not stated (PROC MIXED default REML)
- **Time coding:** Categorical visit
- **Estimand / contrast:** LS-mean difference at Week 48 (ESTIMATE statement for Weeks 36-48 average); NI margin 4 letters
- **Missing data:** Observed data, no imputation; BCVA censored after start of alternative anti-VEGF treatment (implicit MAR) [SAP; StatR]
- **MNAR sensitivity:** Not stated
- **Software:** SAS 9.4 or above, PROC MIXED [SAP]
- **Result:** FAS observed, Week 48 brolucizumab 6 mg vs aflibercept: HAWK -0.72 (95% CI -2.74, 1.30), N=360/360; HARRIER -0.45 (-2.14, 1.25), N=370/369; NI p<=0.0008. HAWK 3 mg -0.92 (-2.83, 0.98) [StatR Table 29]
- **FDA comments:** Reviewer disagreed with Applicant viewing post-anti-VEGF censored data as 'missing' (treats censoring/LOCF as a while-on-treatment ICE strategy); MMRM results 'consistent with the primary efficacy results'
- **Spec source:** SAP verbatim (incl. SAS code) + StatR verbatim

#### Verbatim specification excerpts

##### Model 1: BCVA change from baseline at Week 48 (primary) and average over Weeks 36-48 (first key secondary) (supportive/sensitivity)

> "3. Mixed model repeated measures (MMRM) using the FAS and PPS with observed data (including censoring). The MMRM will include treatment, visit, baseline BCVA category, age category and treatment by visit interactions as fixed-effect terms and visit as a repeated measure. An unstructured covariance matrix will be used to model the within-subject error. For the MMRM analysis: a. The treatment difference at Week 48 will be estimated using the LSM and 95% percent confidence interval. b. For the endpoint of average change from Baseline over the period Week 36 through Week 48, a SAS code utilizing the ESTIMATE statement in PROC MIXED will be provided in the programming specification document to obtain the LSM estimate for the corresponding treatment difference and 95% confidence interval. c. If an MMRM model with unstructured covariance matrix does not converge, a more restricted covariance matrix can be considered in the following order until convergence is reached: variance components (VC), compound symmetry (CS), first-order autoregressive (AR) and Toeplitz (TOEP)."
>
> — HAWK (RTH258-A2301) SAP v2.0, §2.5.4 Supportive analyses, p. 19 (https://cdn.clinicaltrials.gov/large-docs/82/NCT02307682/SAP_001.pdf)

> "The following MMRM model will be used for the supportive analysis of the primary and first key secondary efficacy variables: <change from Baseline in BCVA at Week 48> <average change from Baseline in BCVA from Week 36 to Week 48> = intercept + treatment + Baseline BCVA category + age category + visit + treatment*visit + error."
>
> — HAWK (RTH258-A2301) SAP v2.0, §5.2.1 Primary and first key secondary analysis, p. 49 (https://cdn.clinicaltrials.gov/large-docs/82/NCT02307682/SAP_001.pdf)

```sas
PROC MIXED DATA=<Dataset> order=Internal;
               CLASS USUBJID <Treatment> <VISIT> <BCVA CAT> <AGE CAT>;
            MODEL <Chg_VA> = <Treatment> <VISIT> <BCVA CAT> <AGE CAT>
           <VISIT>*<Treatment>
                           / solution DDFM=KENWARDROGER ALPHA=0.05;
               REPEATED <VISIT>/type=UN subject=USUBJID;
               LSMEANS <VISIT>*<Treatment> / DIFF CL ALPHA = 0.05 om;
               ODS OUTPUT LSMEANS=outLsm DIFFS=Diffs;
RUN;
```

— HAWK (RTH258-A2301) SAP v2.0, §5.2.1 pseudo SAS code (MMRM), p. 49 (https://cdn.clinicaltrials.gov/large-docs/82/NCT02307682/SAP_001.pdf)

> "For the above MMRM analysis, the data structure is one record per FAS subject per scheduled visit. The data will include all subjects and have records for all scheduled visits, regardless of whether the assessment was missed or not at a given visit. Missing values will NOT be imputed using LOCF. Instead, the value will be passed to the model as missing."
>
> — HAWK (RTH258-A2301) SAP v2.0, §5.2.1 Note, p. 50 (https://cdn.clinicaltrials.gov/large-docs/82/NCT02307682/SAP_001.pdf)

> "For subjects who discontinue treatment but continue in the study, the efficacy data will be censored at the time the subject started alternative anti-VEGF treatment in the study eye. No other censoring is applied within the FAS analysis of the primary and first key secondary endpoints. Censored or missing data will be imputed by the last observation prior to receiving alternative anti-VEGF treatment."
>
> — HAWK (RTH258-A2301) SAP v2.0, §2.5.3 Handling of missing values/censoring/discontinuations, p. 18 (https://cdn.clinicaltrials.gov/large-docs/82/NCT02307682/SAP_001.pdf)

> "The prima1y analysis at Week 48 and the final analysis after all subjects completed / te1minated the study will be performed by the Biostatistics and statistical programming groups of Nova1tis using SAS 9.4 or above."
>
> — HAWK (RTH258-A2301) SAP v2.0, §2.1 Data analysis general information, p. 12 (https://cdn.clinicaltrials.gov/large-docs/82/NCT02307682/SAP_001.pdf)

> "3. Mixed model repeated measures (MMRM) using the FAS and PPS with observed data (including censoring for alternative anti-VEGF). The MMRM will include treatment, visit, baseline BCVA category, age category and treatment by visit interactions as fixed-effect terms and visit as a repeated measure. An unstructured covariance matrix will be used to model the within-subject error."
>
> — HARRIER (RTH258-A2302) SAP v2.0, §2.5.4 Supportive analyses, p. 18 (https://cdn.clinicaltrials.gov/large-docs/28/NCT02434328/SAP_001.pdf)

> "Mixed model repeated measures (MMRM) using the FAS or PPS: the MMRM model includes treatment, visit, baseline BCVA category, age category, and treatment by visit interactions as factors. An unstructured covariance matrix is used to model the within- subject error. For subjects who discontinued treatment but continued the study, the BCVA values are censored at the time the subjects started alternative anti-VEGF treatments. Censored or missing data are not imputed."
>
> — FDA Statistical Review, §3.2.2 Statistical Methodologies (supportive analyses), p. 18 (https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2019/761125Orig1s000StatR.pdf)

> "1. The SAPs states that the censored data are “imputed” by the observations prior to receiving alternative anti-VEGF treatments. It appears that the Applicant views the censored data as missing data. However, the reviewer does not agree with this perspective. Censoring and using the last observation prior to censoring is one way of handling the intercurrent event of receiving alternative anti-VEGF treatments. The reviewer does not consider the censored data as missing data."
>
> — FDA Statistical Review, §3.2.2 reviewer comment, p. 17 (https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2019/761125Orig1s000StatR.pdf)

> "Further supportive results by the MMRM models can be found in Table 29 and Table 30 of Appendix D. The supportive results by the MMRM models are also consistent with the primary efficacy results."
>
> — FDA Statistical Review, §3.2.4 Results, p. 26 (https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2019/761125Orig1s000StatR.pdf)

> "[2] MMRM model with treatment, visit, baseline BCVA categories, and age categories, and treatment by visit interaction."
>
> — FDA Statistical Review, Table 29 footnote [2], p. 49 (https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2019/761125Orig1s000StatR.pdf)

#### Verbatim specification excerpts

##### Model 1: Change from baseline in BCVA averaged over Weeks 40/44/48 (primary)

> "The primary estimand is defined as follows:  Population: Adult treatment-naive patients with nAMD, as defined by the inclusion / exclusion criteria (see Section 4.1.1) (ITT Population)  Variable: Change in BCVA score from baseline averaged over Weeks 40, 44, and 48. BCVA score is based on the ETDRS VA chart assessed at a starting distance of 4 meters  Intercurrent events: – Discontinuation of study treatment due to adverse events (AEs) or lack of efficacy not due to COVID-19: A treatment policy strategy will be applied where all observed values will be used regardless of the occurrence of the intercurrent event – Use of any prohibited systemic treatment or prohibited therapy in the Study eye (Section 4.4.3 of Protocol Version 3) not due to COVID-19: A treatment policy strategy will be applied where all observed values will be used regardless of the occurrence of the intercurrent event – Discontinuation of study treatment due to COVID-19: A hypothetical strategy will be applied where all values will be censored after the intercurrent event – Use of any prohibited systemic treatment or prohibited therapy in the study eye due to COVID-19: A hypothetical strategy will be applied where all values will be censored after the intercurrent event – Missed dose(s) with potentially major impact on efficacy due to COVID-19: A hypothetical strategy will be applied where all values will be censored after the intercurrent event – COVID-19 death: A hypothetical strategy will be applied  Population-level summary: Difference in adjusted mean between faricimab (up to Q16W) and aflibercept (Q8W) arms"
>
> — TENAYA/LUCERNE (GR40306/GR40844) SAP, §4.4.1 Primary Efficacy Endpoint (estimand), p. 17 (https://cdn.clinicaltrials.gov/large-docs/87/NCT03823287/SAP_001.pdf)

> "The primary analysis will be performed using a MMRM. The model will include the change from baseline at Weeks 448 as the response variable and will include the categorical covariates of treatment group, visit, visit-by-treatment group interaction, baseline BCVA (continuous), as well as randomization stratification factors as fixed effects. Comparisons between the two treatment arms will be made using a composite contrast over Weeks 40, 44, and 48. The MMRM model will assume an unstructured covariance structure. If there are convergence problems with the model, then a heterogeneous compound symmetry or an AR (1) covariance structure may be fitted. Missing data will be implicitly imputed by the MMRM model, assuming a missing at random (MAR) missing data mechanism."
>
> — TENAYA/LUCERNE (GR40306/GR40844) SAP, §4.4.1.2 Analysis Methods, p. 18 (https://cdn.clinicaltrials.gov/large-docs/87/NCT03823287/SAP_001.pdf)

_'Weeks 448' appears to be a dropped range dash in the PDF text layer (presumably Weeks 4–48); quoted as extracted._

> "a) Last observation carried forward: The estimand and analysis method will be the same as the primary analysis (Section 4.4.1), with the exception that any missing BCVA assessments due to any reason will be imputed using the last available post-baseline observation prior to the occurrence of missing data. Additionally, BCVA assessments after the COVID-19 related intercurrent event will be censored and will be imputed using the last available post- baseline observation prior to the COVID-19 intercurrent event."
>
> — TENAYA/LUCERNE (GR40306/GR40844) SAP, §4.4.1.3 Sensitivity Analyses, p. 18 (https://cdn.clinicaltrials.gov/large-docs/87/NCT03823287/SAP_001.pdf)

> "In both studies, the primary efficacy analysis for the primary estimand of interest was an evaluation of noninferiority of faricimab to aflibercept in the mean change in BCVA from baseline at Week 40/44/48 using a mixed model repeated measure analysis (MMRM). The model included the categorical covariates of treatment group, visit, visit-by-treatment group interaction, the continuous covariate of baseline BCVA, and randomization stratification factors as fixed effects. The model assumed an unstructured covariance structure to account for within-subject correlation."
>
> — FDA Statistical Review, §3.2.1.2 Statistical Methodologies, p. 19 (https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2022/761235Orig1s000StatR.pdf)

> "The primary efficacy analysis was based on the ITT population including all randomized subjects. In the Applicant’s primary efficacy analysis, subjects with intermittent missing data due to missed visit (due to COVID-19 or other reasons) and/or subjects whose data post-occurrence of IEs due to COVID-19 were censored were implicitly imputed using the MMRM model assuming a missing at random (MAR) missing data mechanism."
>
> — FDA Statistical Review, §3.2.1.2, p. 19 (https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2022/761235Orig1s000StatR.pdf)

> "As additional sensitivity analyses, the reviewer also performed the primary and the sensitivity analyses for the primary estimand by imputing intermittent missing data and data after occurrence of IEs using multiple imputation (MI) strategy and the last observation carried forward (LOCF) imputation approach."
>
> — FDA Statistical Review, §3.2.1.2 Sensitivity Analyses, p. 20 (https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2022/761235Orig1s000StatR.pdf)

> "Reviewer’s Remark: In the Applicant’s primary estimand strategy, data for subjects with IEs not related to COVID-19 were used in the analysis but data for subjects with IEs due to COVID-19 were censored and imputed using the MMRM model assuming MAR missing data mechanism. Considering that the number of subjects with IEs not related to COVID-19 were minimal in the studies, and due to COVID-19 appeared not to be treatment-related (Table 1), the reviewer considered the treatment policy estimand strategy (i.e., including all data regardless of IEs), as the primary estimand. Analysis based on the Applicant’s primary estimand of interest was used as supporting."
>
> — FDA Statistical Review, §3.2.1.2 Reviewer’s Remark, p. 20 (https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2022/761235Orig1s000StatR.pdf)

> "As shown, in TENAYA, the adjusted mean change in BCVA from baseline at Week 40/44/48 in the faricimab group was +5.7 letters and in the aflibercept group was +5.1 letters with a treatment difference of +0.6 (95% CI: -1.2 to 2.4). Similarly, in LUCERNE, the adjusted mean change in the faricimab [...] group was +6.4 letters and in the aflibercept group was +6.6 letters with a treatment difference of -0.1 (95% CI: -1.9 to 1.6)."
>
> — FDA Statistical Review, Executive Summary (results), pp. 7–8 (https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2022/761235Orig1s000StatR.pdf)

##### Model 2: Change from baseline in BCVA averaged over Weeks 48/52/56 (primary)

> "The change from baseline averaged over Weeks 48, 52, and 56 will be compared between each faricimab arm and the aflibercept Q8W arm using a mixed-model repeated measures (MMRM) model. The model will include the change from baseline at Weeks 456 as the response variables and will include the categorical covariates of treatment group, visit, visit-by-treatment group interaction, the continuous baseline value for the response variable (in this case, baseline BCVA), as well as randomization stratification factors as fixed effects. Comparisons between each faricimab arm and the aflibercept Q8W arm will be made using a composite contrast over Weeks 48, 52, and 56. The MMRM model will assume an unstructured covariance structure. If there are convergence problems with the model, then a heterogeneous compound symmetry or an AR(1) covariance structure may be fitted. Missing data will be implicitly imputed using the MMRM model, assuming a missing at random missing data mechanism (i.e., the probability that missing data are dependent on other observed variables but not on the missing data). Data for patients who receive prohibited therapy will be censored at the timing of use of prohibited therapy. Data for patients who discontinue from study drug and do not receive any prohibited therapy after discontinuation of study drug will be included in the analysis."
>
> — YOSEMITE/RHINE (GR40349/GR40398) SAP, Appended protocol text (primary analysis), p. 52 (https://cdn.clinicaltrials.gov/large-docs/80/NCT03622580/SAP_001.pdf)

> "In both studies, the primary efficacy analysis for the primary estimand of interest was an evaluation of noninferiority of each dose of faricimab to aflibercept in the mean change in BCVA from baseline at Week 48/52/56 using a mixed model repeated measure analysis (MMRM). The model included the categorical covariates of treatment group, visit, visit-by- treatment group interaction, the continuous covariate of baseline BCVA, and randomization stratification factors as fixed effects. The model assumed an unstructured covariance structure to account for within-subject correlation. The noninferiority margin was set at -4.0 letters."
>
> — FDA Statistical Review, §3.2.2.2 Statistical Methodologies, p. 42 (https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2022/761235Orig1s000StatR.pdf)

> "Considering that the number of subjects with IEs due to none-COVID-19 were minimal in both studies and due to COVID-19 appeared not to be treatment-related (Table 17), the reviewer considered the treatment policy estimand strategy outlined in item (ii) above as the primary estimand. In this strategy, all data regardless of occurrence of IEs were used in the analysis. The Applicant’s primary estimand of interest where all data after occurrence of IEs due to COVID- 19 were censored was used as supporting."
>
> — FDA Statistical Review, §3.2.2.2 Reviewer’s Remark, p. 43 (https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2022/761235Orig1s000StatR.pdf)

> "As shown, in YOSEMITE, the adjusted mean change in BCVA from baseline at Week 48/52/56 in the ITT population was +10.6 letters in faricimab Q8W, +11.5 letters in faricimab PTI, and +10.8 letters in aflibercept with a treatment difference of -0.3 (97.5% CI: -2.0 to 1.5) between faricimab Q8W and aflibercept and +0.6 (97.5% CI: -1.1 to 2.4) between faricimab PTI and aflibercept. Similarly, in RHINE, the adjusted mean change was +11.7 letters in faricimab Q8W, +10.7 letters in faricimab PTI, and +10.2 letters in aflibercept with a treatment difference of +1.5 (97.5% CI: -0.2 to 3.1) between faricimab Q8W and aflibercept and +0.5 (97.5% CI: -1.2 to 2.1) between faricimab PTI and aflibercept."
>
> — FDA Statistical Review, Executive Summary (results), p. 10 (https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2022/761235Orig1s000StatR.pdf)

### Omidenepag isopropyl (Omlonti) — NDA 215092

Therapeutic area: Ophthalmology. Sponsor: Santen Inc. Approved: 2022-09-22.

#### Model 1: IOP at 9 timepoints (primary, non-inferiority)

- Trials: 011709IN/Spectrum 3 (NCT03691649), 011710IN/Spectrum 4 (NCT03691662), 01171505/AYAME (NCT02981446).
- Model family: MMRM. Verbatim [StatR p.15]: "The FDA required primary efficacy analyses in all the three studies provided the treatment difference in the mean IOP at each of the 9 time points and the corresponding 2-sided 95% confidence interval using a mixed effects model for repeated measure (MMRM). The model was fitted for each time of the day separately, and included time-matched baseline IOP, treatment, visit (Week 1, 6 and Month 3) and treatment by visits interaction. The within-subject correlation was captured via an unstructured covariance matrix. Missing IOP data was assumed to follow the missing at random (MAR) mechanism and was not explicitly imputed."
- Response: raw IOP (mmHg), with time-matched baseline IOP as a covariate.
- Fixed effects: time-matched baseline IOP, treatment, visit, treatment × visit. There are 3 separate models, one per time of day (08:00, 10:00, 16:00).
- Random effects: none (R-matrix only).
- Covariance: UN. Fallback: Not stated. df method: Not stated. Estimation: Not stated. Time: categorical (3 visits).
- Estimand/contrast: LS-mean difference (DE-117 minus comparator) with 95% CI at each of the 9 timepoints. Non-inferiority required UCL < 1.5 mmHg at all 9 timepoints and UCL < 1.0 mmHg at 5 or more of the 9. The reviewer said no estimand was pre-specified and that the MMRM "is likely an evaluation of the 'hypothetical estimand'" [StatR p.26].
- Missing data: MAR. IOP after rescue was treated as missing. Data collected after treatment discontinuation but before rescue were included.
- MNAR sensitivity (Applicant): a PMM delta-adjustment. Missing data were first imputed by MI under MAR. A shift of +1 to +5 mmHg was then added for subjects who discontinued for AE or lack of efficacy, or who used rescue. The same MMRM was used for analysis. Tipping points were shift = 1 for 011710IN and shift = 2 for 01171505. 011709IN already failed at shift 0 [StatR Table 6].
- Software: Not stated.
- Results: 011710IN and 01171505 met both NI criteria. 011709IN failed: UCL > 1.5 mmHg at Week 6 08:00, Month 3 08:00 and Month 3 10:00. The per-timepoint LS-mean numbers are only in figures (images) and could not be extracted. FAS N: 011709IN 212/213, 011710IN 204/205, 01171505 184/185.
- FDA comments: see Model 2. The reviewer also ran:
  - a "fully hypothetical" MMRM, with post-discontinuation data set to missing
  - a treatment-policy MMRM that included post-rescue data

  Neither changed the conclusions.

#### Model 2: IOP, all 9 measurements jointly (FDA reviewer sensitivity analysis)

- The reviewer criticized the per-time-of-day models. Verbatim: "This analysis ignores the possible correlation among IOP measurements taken from the same subject on a given visit. This could potentially result in biased estimates, as well as incorrect standard errors". The reviewer refit a single MMRM with "Fully Unstructured Correlation" across measurements within a day and across visits [StatR p.25-26, Figs 7-9].
- Result: generally consistent with the primary analysis. However, one timepoint each in 011710IN and 01171505 had UCL > 1.5 mmHg.

#### Model 3: mean diurnal IOP and change-from-baseline IOP (key secondary/secondary)

- Same MMRM as the primary analysis [StatR p.16].
- Mean diurnal IOP difference at Month 3 (95% CI): 011709IN 1.0 (0.5, 1.6), 011710IN 0.3 (-0.2, 0.8), 01171505 0.6 (0.0, 1.2) mmHg [StatR Tables 7-9].

#### Verbatim specification excerpts

##### Model 1: IOP at 9 timepoints (primary, non-inferiority)

> "The FDA required primary efficacy analyses in all the three studies provided the treatment difference in the mean IOP at each of the 9 time points and the corresponding 2-sided 95% confidence interval using a mixed effects model for repeated measure (MMRM). The model was fitted for each time of the day separately, and included time-matched baseline IOP, treatment, visit (Week 1, 6 and Month 3) and treatment by visits interaction. The within-subject correlation was captured via an unstructured covariance matrix. Missing IOP data was assumed to follow the missing at random (MAR) mechanism and was not explicitly imputed."
>
> — FDA Statistical Review §3.2.2.3.A, p. 16 (https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2022/215092Orig1s000StatR.pdf)

> "To assess the sensitivity to departure from the MAR assumption, based on which the MMRM approach is valid, the Applicant used a pattern-mixture model (PMM) with delta-adjustment. In this approach, first, all missing data is imputed using a multiple imputation approach under the MAR assumption. Second, for subjects who had missing data because they discontinued the study due to adverse events or lack of efficacy and those who received rescue medication prior to the evaluation of the efficacy outcome, the imputed IOP values were shifted by a magnitude of 1 to 5. Missing data due to other reasons is still assumed MAR and hence no shift is added. The [...] analysis of the imputed data for each shift parameter was conducted using the MMRM approach used for the primary efficacy analysis."
>
> — FDA Statistical Review §3.2.2.3.B, pp. 16-17 (https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2022/215092Orig1s000StatR.pdf)

> "IOP values measured after study drug discontinuation, but prior to administration rescue medication, were included in the primary efficacy analysis. However, all IOP values collected after rescue medication use were treated as missing."
>
> — FDA Statistical Review §3.2.3 (Reviewer's remark), p. 22 (https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2022/215092Orig1s000StatR.pdf)

> "Recall, in the primary efficacy analyses, data after treatment discontinuation and data collected after the receipt of IOP lowering medication (rescue therapy) was treated as missing and assumed to follow the missing at random (MAR) mechanism. To assess the impact of deviation from this assumption, which is the basis for the MMRM approach, the Applicant performed a pattern mixture modeling approach in which a positive shift parameter between 1 mm Hg and 5 mm Hg were added to the imputed values for subjects in both arms who received a rescue medication or discontinued the study due to either adverse events or lack of efficacy."
>
> — FDA Statistical Review §3.2.4.1.2.A, p. 25 (https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2022/215092Orig1s000StatR.pdf)

> "As shown in Table 6, the tipping points for studies 011710IN and 01171505 are 1 and 2, respectively. However, in these studies, the upper limit of the 95% CI is ≤1.5 in at least 7 out of 9 timepoints for shift parameters of 3-5mm Hg. Furthermore, for Study 011709IN, the upper limit of the 95% CI is ≤1.5 in 6 of the 9 timepoints for a shift parameter of 2mm Hg and in 5 of the 9 timepoints for the shift parameters of 3-5mm Hg."
>
> — FDA Statistical Review §3.2.4.1.2 (Reviewer's remark), p. 26 (https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2022/215092Orig1s000StatR.pdf)

> "Neither the protocols nor the statistical analysis plans for the three Phase 3 studies specified the primary estimand of interest. The primary analysis with the MMRM is likely an evaluation of the “hypothetical estimand”, that is, the difference in mean IOP in a hypothetical scenario where the intercurrent events of treatment discontinuation and rescue medication use had not occurred. For non-inferiority studies in IOP indications, the Agency has accepted this estimand in the past."
>
> — FDA Statistical Review §3.2.4.1.2.B.ii, p. 27 (https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2022/215092Orig1s000StatR.pdf)

> "Note, studies 011709IN and 011710IN allowed subjects who discontinued the study treatment to remain in the study and provide data. In the Applicant’s primary efficacy analysis, data collected post-treatment discontinuation (prior to recue medication use) is used in the analysis. To evaluate the effect of including data from these subjects on the hypothetical estimand (which is evaluated under the scenario that treatment discontinuation had not occurred), the reviewer conducted the analysis of the primary efficacy endpoints by treating post-treatment discontinuation data as missing. The analysis is done using the same MMRM model used for the primary efficacy analysis (Figure 10-Figure 11)."
>
> — FDA Statistical Review §3.2.4.1.2.B.ii, p. 27 (https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2022/215092Orig1s000StatR.pdf)

> "For some subjects, data post-rescue medication was collected. However, the data was not used in the primary efficacy analyses. This reviewer conducted the analysis of the primary efficacy endpoint by using all observed data including data collected following a rescue medication use (Figure 13 and Figure 14) as an estimate of this estimand. Apart from a slightly improved effect for the DE-117 arm, the overall conclusion of non-inferiority has not changed in this analysis."
>
> — FDA Statistical Review §3.2.4.1.2.B.ii, p. 27 (https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2022/215092Orig1s000StatR.pdf)

##### Model 2: IOP, all 9 measurements jointly (FDA reviewer sensitivity analysis)

> "The primary efficacy analysis was conducted based on an MMRM model for each time of the day separately. This analysis ignores the possible correlation among IOP measurements taken [...] from the same subject on a given visit. This could potentially result in biased estimates, as well as incorrect standard errors of the estimated treatment differences. To this end, this reviewer performed the analysis of the primary endpoint accounting for the within visit and across visit correlations. The results of this analysis are generally consistent with the primary efficacy analyses results. However, there was one time point each in Study 011710IN and Study 01171505 at which the upper limit of the 95% confidence interval crossed the pre-specified non-inferiority margin of 1.5 mm Hg (Figure 7-Figure 9)."
>
> — FDA Statistical Review §3.2.4.1.2.B.i, pp. 26-27 (https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2022/215092Orig1s000StatR.pdf)

> "Reviewer’s analysis: An MMRM model accounting for correlations among IOP measurements within a day and across measurement visits is accounted for."
>
> — FDA Statistical Review Appendix Figure 7 source note, p. 34 (https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2022/215092Orig1s000StatR.pdf)

##### Model 3: mean diurnal IOP and change-from-baseline IOP (key secondary/secondary)

> "The analyses of the key secondary efficacy endpoints were conducted using the MMRM approach that was used for the analysis of the primary efficacy endpoint."
>
> — FDA Statistical Review §3.2.2.3.C, p. 17 (https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2022/215092Orig1s000StatR.pdf)
